author: Sophia Cope
title: DHS Inspector General Finds That TSA is Not Properly Safeguarding Passenger Facial Recognition Data
content:
EFF legal intern Gabrielle Ladun was the principal author of this post.

The Department of Homeland Security Office of Inspector General (DHS OIG) has published a summary of findings from its audit of the Transportation Security Administration’s (TSA) facial recognition technology. While the detailed findings are classified, the summary states that the OIG’s audit uncovered a “significant weakness” in the technology’s ability to protect the privacy of passenger data. This has massive privacy implications for the millions of passengers who travel and don’t opt out of the TSA’s biometric surveillance technology verification process.

TSA uses facial comparison technology for identity verification of airline passengers. A camera takes a photo of passengers to verify that their provided identification matches their live photo. Although TSA states that it is “committed to protecting traveler privacy,” the audit highlights that this has not been the case.

The OIG found that TSA’s Credential Authentication Technology 2’s (CAT-2) vendor “was able to access and extract sensitive passenger information, including driver’s license and passport images, during system troubleshooting and enhancements, without TSA’s knowledge.”

The OIG further admonished the agency:

TSA lacked clear policies, did not track when this data was extracted, could not verify that extracted information was properly deleted, and did not notify passengers when their biometric and biographic information may have been stored. As a result, although passenger information was generally protected during routine operations, weaknesses in vendor oversight created a risk that sensitive personal information could be retained or exposed.

We hope the TSA will fix these issues. The OIG summary states:

We issued one finding and three recommendations to strengthen controls, improve oversight, and ensure transparency and the proper handling of passenger data. TSA concurred with all three recommendations. Two recommendations are open and resolved, and one remains open and unresolved.

EFF has a long history of opposing governmental use of facial recognition technology. As the OIG’s audit underscores, this technology presents privacy risks associated with unsecured data, unauthorized access, and data breaches. The government’s use of this technology also creates a mass surveillance system and facilitates the creation of warrantless biometric records for unconsenting parties.

The biometric data captured by this technology is not without errors. There have been multiple instances of law enforcement agencies using facial recognition technology to misidentify and arrest innocent individuals.

Given that facial recognition technology is prone to mistakes, combined with the OIG’s audit revealing significant privacy weaknesses, it is imperative that travelers remember that opting out is possible. TSA’s own website emphasizes that travelers who wish to decline to have their photo taken for facial comparison can do so without any delay, disruption, or recourse.

Considering the data protection weaknesses exposed by the OIG’s audit, EFF will continue to oppose this governmental system of mass surveillance and spread awareness to ensure that no one is forced to relinquish their biometric data without consent.

title: Indigenous Just Transition in The Arctic
content:
This is going to be a collaborative event between Ungeirr Umkveraasenaar, or the Icelandic Young Environmentalists, and the Indigenous Environmental Network. Maybe we can go around and you guys can give a little introduction about yourselves. Sure.

Huang’a a’ka, pang’a’anang naka pang’a’u yu, huang’a a’taka, a’anatirma, naka kirstinuga pás, huang’a sivunga rumi. I come from St. Lawrence Island. I’ve been with IEN since 2021, and I work on organizing against climate geoengineering.

Kweyanaipaplusi maunga, huang’a a’akaluk, ungelaksirmiu runga, angayukang maktaklu Charlie. I a’anukwa’apu’a makigaklu anaktiyuk asii, janililu Charlie, chinirmiu, ungelaksirmiu. Thank you everyone for welcoming us here today.

I’m Adrienne A’akaluk Blatchford. I’m from Unalakleet, Alaska, which is up on the Northwest Coast in the passageway to the Arctic. We’re right on the coast of the Bering Sea in the heart of the Norton Sound.

And I work with Indigenous Environmental Network as a geoengineering outreach organizer with a focus on Alaska and the Arctic. Hello, thank you for having us as the host.

My name is Thomas Joseph. I’m a Hoopa Valley tribal member from the Six Rivers National Forest in Northern California. I am also Shoshone Paiute from the Sierra Nevadas. Paiute is what we call it, the land of flowing water.

I’m down there by Yosemite and the Half Dome area. I am here with the Indigenous Environmental Network as their carbon pricing educator. And again, thanks for having us.

Yá’át’ééh. My name is Talia Boyd. Older women from my community who love to have the time of their lives shared with me.

Greetings, everyone. My name is Talia Boyd. I’m the mining organizer for IEN.

I’m based in New Mexico, originally from Arizona, and I hail from the Navajo Nation in the Southwest. And I’m very honored to be here with y’all and share this space and time. Thank you.

Awesome. And a little bit about me for any of you who don’t know me. My name is Isla.

I’m originally from Wales and I’ve been living here in Iceland for over five years and I’m the education representative for the Icelandic Young Environmentalists. So how about we just go straight into things and you guys can give us a little bit of an oral presentation about your work and everything that you do and then we’ll get started with the panel Q&A afterwards. Sounds good.

Thank you. So I want to kind of do a little bit of an introduction on who is the Indigenous Environmental Network. Over 30 years ago the United States, we’re kind of seeing that return back to that, was having a really hard time addressing the mining operations of uranium in the southwest and the Indigenous people came together as they were the ones that were being directly affected by these mining operations that was being used for the production of uranium for the purpose of war.

And so the Indigenous peoples from that region rallied together to try to protect their communities against the high rates of cancers and other issues that was plaguing their communities to no avail. The state governments wouldn’t listen to them. The national governments wouldn’t listen to them and so they seen that it was in their best interest to take this fight to the international space of the United Nations and that’s when the Indigenous Environmental Network was formed with the purpose and intent of taking the struggles of the mining and the struggles of the health impacts of mining to a global positioning.

The Indigenous Environmental Network has been active in the United Nations space since then and in various different causes pertaining to the Paris Climate Agreement, water issues, mining issues, also very active in the Convention on Biological Diversity and we continue to play a role of Indigenous networks across Turtle Island. So we come from impacted communities of Indigenous peoples. Frontline community is another term that’s often used from across Turtle Island of communities that are faced with deforestation, faced with dams, faced with any type of harm that we see against our Mother Earth.

In these past 30 years IEN has now expanded its network to be globally and so we have Indigenous organizations that we work with across the globe and in North America we have a strong positioning on mining operations which is Talia Leeds and geoengineering and carbon pricing which I do but we also do a lot of other work pertaining to just transition and many other things that you can find on our website at IENEarth.org. author: labor4pal
title: Universities fire dozens amid pressure from Zionist billionaires (Electronic Intifada)
content:
Ali Abunimah Rights and Accountability 14 October 2026

Universities in the United States and Canada have fired, suspended and harassed employees for speaking out against Israel’s genocide in Gaza, often using ostensibly neutral disciplinary procedures to conceal politically motivated retaliation.

That is the finding of a new report from the Academic Freedom Initiative, a project of the Middle East Studies Association (MESA).

“Lessons in Repression: Silencing Campus Workers on Palestine Since October 7, 2023” is the first systematic study of retaliation against university employees for their Palestine-related speech and activism in the two countries.

The report draws on a database of 196 incidents recorded through 20 August 2026 and in-depth interviews with 31 targeted employees.

Of those incidents, 76 – nearly 40 percent – resulted in termination, while 59 involved suspension or campus bans.

Both tenured professors and precariously employed instructors and staff have been targeted. Of 134 cases in which racial or ethnic identity was known, nearly two-thirds involved people of color. Some 16.5 percent of those targeted identified as Jewish.

Most retaliation had nothing to do with classroom teaching. More than half the incidents stemmed from other on-campus activities, including protests, while only 11 percent concerned alleged classroom interactions.

Another 16 percent of cases arose from off-campus speech and 12 percent from social media posts, “suggesting that teaching is a relatively less common context provoking punishment.”

Major drivers of the repression include pressure from wealthy pro-Israel donors, government interference and the political loyalties of university administrators and trustees, the report says.

Growing financial dependence of universities on wealthy benefactors, alongside austerity and the widespread use of precariously employed workers, also makes institutions more vulnerable to political pressure.

At the University of Pennsylvania, for example, trustee Cheryl Peisach is married to the treasurer of a family foundation that donated $100,000 to Canary Mission in 2023.

The notorious pro-Israel blacklisting website publishes dossiers attacking students and academics who support Palestinian rights.

US immigration authorities have admitted to using its dossiers to target Palestine activists.

In another case at Penn, a tenured professor faced a vicious online harassment campaign over her support for Palestine, including hundreds of messages containing rape and death threats.

The donor funding her endowed chair withdrew support. According to the professor, a dean told her that donor pressure had led the university to encourage her retirement. She retired in June 2026.

Billionaire Bill Ackman demanded a blacklist of Harvard students who disagreed with his views, while billionaire Leon Cooperman threatened to stop donating to Columbia University following a Palestine solidarity walkout.

Pressure from the Trump administration has reinforced the crackdown.

During the last two months of 2023, the US government opened more federal “anti-Semitism” investigations against universities than in all previous years combined.

Dozens of institutions agreed to government monitoring, including sharing the names of students and employees accused of anti-Semitism, to close investigations.

Harvard provided a notable example of such cowardice. Even as it fought a Trump administration lawsuit falsely portraying Gaza solidarity protests as anti-Jewish terror, the university boasted of its own crackdown on alleged anti-Semitism rather than defend its students’ right to protest Israel’s genocide.

A federal judge dismissed the lawsuit in August, finding that the government had failed to plausibly allege any ongoing violation of civil rights law.

Six congressional hearings between December 2023 and July 2025 subjected university leaders to McCarthyite interrogations over alleged failures to combat anti-Semitism.

In Illinois, Northwestern University journalism professor Steven Thrasher was suspended shortly after being singled out during one of these hearings and was later denied tenure and terminated. He is currently suing the university for discrimination and violations of his First Amendment rights.

РБ: Йоханнес, первое слово как от собрата по оружию к собрату по оружию (1) – после измельчания протестного движения шестидесятых годов, и с тех пор как марксизм в ФРГ овладел не массами, а завоевал профессуру – ты остался среди тех, кто, как и прежде, преследует цели эмансипации своим теоретизированием. Т.е. теx, кто не видит своей задачи в «продуктивном» обогащении актуальной науки посредством «марксистской теории» – а остался контрапродуктивным элементом, и в своей области, в «критике политики», проявляет себя как решительного врага государства. Я правильно говорю?

Аньоли: Я предпочитаю определение Штернберга. Он утверждал, что я не являюсь «другом государству», и я тем более предпочитаю так говорить, скажем, по полицейско-правовым причинам, ибо враги государства, как известно, преследуются и не имеют права быть профессорами. Я xотел бы совсем коротко сказать о, скажем так, научно-теоретической позиции, которую я представляю. Я как-то раз на мероприятии Института имени Отто Зура о смысле и целях политологии сформулировал это так: по моему мнению, единственно верной задачей политологического исследования сегодня является субверсивная (подрывная) наука. Большего не предвидится пред лицом всеобщего политического отступления левых. Всё прочее, что в нашей науке не является подрывным, в принципе, в конечном итоге – аффирмативно. Я не хочу сказать, что я единственный, кто развивает эту субверсивную науку. Я думаю, к примеру, об Эккхарте Криппендорфе: он хотя и не марксист, но со своей позиции вступил в борьбу с милитаристским государством, и последовательно ведёт её дальше. Вопрос в том, что другие левые профессора, я не хочу сказать, что они подались к правым, вынуждаются объективными условиями «печь булочки поменьше». С другой стороны, мне хотелось бы, чтобы они всё же выказывали – не хочу сказать «мужества» – но больше критической решительности. Речь о том, чтобы – не важно, марксист или нет – подвергнуть основания политической формы критике; в то время как во время так называемого кризиса марксизма, который является на самом деле кризисом многих марксистов, и больше ничего, многие товарищи, профессора, которых я всё ещё рассматриваю как товарищей, перешли к критике неблагоприятных условий и денунциации превышения полномочий, в то время как, по моему мнению, заниматься нужно именно критикой условий (вообще) и денунциацией нормального «использования» политики. Неблагоприятные условия и превышения полномочий являются, так сказать, побочными эффектами всякой системы и не столь важны; важно то, что условия фальшивы, а применение политики – правильно в том смысле, что политика воспринимается серьёзно как метод применения власти и эффективно используется. То, что политика – это захват и применение власти, вот это должно критиковаться в политической науке.РБ: С другой стороны, нужно ведь замечать, что с 70-х годов довольно большое количество называющих себя левыми людей пошло в университеты. Но большинство из них остановились на весьма обобщённом сорте критики, занимались, к примеру, «определением государства», имеют левые претензии, но когда они выступают вне семинаров, то выказывают либеральную…

Аньоли: …либеральную протестную позицию. Немецкий народ – это не народ революционеров, он стал народом «резолюционеров», левым народом, левым профессорским народом. Это та причина, по которой я отказываюсь иногда, иногда это надо делать, подписывать какие-нибудь резолюции. Резолюции обладают как раз противоположным действием, чем то, каким они должны обладать: они служат выражением протеста, т.е. доказательством того, что мы живём в приличном государстве, где каждый может протестовать так долгo, сколько ему угодно.

РБ: Откуда идёт это явление именно у левых профессоров …

author: socialmedia
title: Newcomers to Trail Hunting Week: A Very Awkward Recruitment Drive.
content:
After last year’s embarrassing

Farcical Friday

, the pro-blood sports lobby group, the British Hound Sports Association (BHSA), has somehow managed to surpass itself in the ridiculousness stakes – and it’s not even

Smokescreen Saturday

 yet!


By now, you might have thought the hunting fraternity would have learned to exercise a little more care when selecting which hunts to showcase in its desperate attempt to maintain the smokescreen of trail hunting.


But no, you actually couldn’t make this up if you tried.


Erm, awkward. Trail Hunting is banned in Scotland.


Just days after a

Lauderdale Hunt huntswoman

 was convicted of illegally hunting a fox with hounds, the Lauderdale is advertising an event encouraging newcomers to discover the joys of ‘trail hunting’. The event poster was uploaded onto the Lauderdale Hunt’s social media and quickly spotted by Glasgow Hunt Saboteurs.


In Scotland. Where trail hunting is banned.


The Lauderdale’s joint meet with the Berwickshire Hounds is seemingly delighted to support

Newcomers to Trail Hunting Week

 in Wedderlie, Gordon, on Saturday 17 October.


Saturday also happens to be the annual smokescreen performance day, when a carefully selected (or perhaps a not-so carefully selected) handful of hunts are wheeled out to put on a display for Tory MP’s and other indignitaries. If they are lucky, GBeebies and the Torygraph might even dispatch a tea-boy masquerading as a journalist to cover the spectacle.


The since-deleted poster promises a warm-welcome courtesy of the Tilson family, a chance to meet the hounds and follow on horseback or foot. No previous experience is necessary.


Clearly, no previous knowledge of Scottish hunting legislation is needed either.


So-called trail hunting has been banned in Scotland since 2023.  Under the Hunting with Dogs (Scotland) Act 2023, following an animal-based scent laid for hounds is prohibited.


As if that weren’t awkward enough, the Lauderdale Hunt was in the news recently for illegal hunting. 


On 05 October 2026, Claire Bellamy, former master and huntswoman of the Lauderdale Hunt, was convicted in Paisley Sheriff Court of deliberately hunting a fox with dogs outside the area permitted by a NatureScot licence.


In fact, it was reported that she wasn’t even named on the NatureScot licence in any case!


Convicted huntswoman Claire Bellamy wasn’t even named on the licence.

 Image: Glasgow Hunt Saboteurs


The poster invites the public to “Come and discover more about trail hunting and our community”.


Perhaps they first ought to discover what the law says.


The poster forms part of the wider campaign organised and promoted by the Countryside Alliance’s propaganda wing,

Future for Hunting

 and the British Hound Sports Association (BHSA) – itself a rebrand of the disgraced Hunting Office.


As if that wasn’t farcical enough, another participating hunt has managed to make this public relations disaster even more awkward.


Three Counties Hunt Saboteurs reported this week that The Worcestershire Hunt – one of the four hunts selected to put on a trail demo on Saturday – was filmed by a member of the West Midlands Badger group in an incident involving a fox and a badger sett.


The incident was said to have occurred in the Wilmcote/Aston Cantlow area of Warwickshire. Sabs say that an officer from the Badger Group who had been in the area in relation to a swan rescue, witnessed the hunted fox run past them near a canal.


She noticed two men in the corner of a nearby wood and approached them telling them that police were on their way. The men scarpered and the large badger sett where they had been was discovered to have freshly blocked entrances.


One of the two men by the freshly blocked badger sett at the Worcestershire Hunt meet.


After last year’s Farcical Friday, you might have expected the BHSA to be a little more selective, but then again, finding a hunt that actually lays a trail must certainly be quite a challenge for hunting’s propaganda unit.


A HSA spokesperson said


“It is no surprise to see this poster advertising what is essentially an illegal activity, made even worse by the Launderdale’s recent conviction. Sometimes they drop the ball and tell us exactly who they are, whereas other times they put up the smokescreen and invite pro-hunt MP’s and media to report on it once a year.

author: Unknown
title: Ephéméride des luttes : 15 octobre
content:
Le 15 octobre de l'éphéméride des luttes est le genre de journée où nos mort-e-s passé-e-s continuent à vivre dans les flammes des révoltes d'aujourd'hui et de celles à venir.


1840 :

 A Paris, l'ouvrier Marius Darmès, proche des idées de ce qui deviendra l'anarchisme, tire au pistolet sur la voiture du roi Louis-Philippe sur le quai des Tuileries, mais le pistolet lui explose dans la main, sauvant la vie du roi. Darmès sera condamné à mort le

29 mai

 de l'année suivante.


1920 :

 A Milan, la police perquisitionne les locaux du journal anarchiste L'Umanità Nova et arrête les personnes présentes.


1940 :

 En Espagne, le président républicain de Catalogne Lluís Companys est exécuté par Franco et son régime fasciste.


1965 :

 Aux USA, la première carte d'appel pour le service militaire est brûlée en public, ce qui donnera lieu à un grand mouvement antimilitariste.


1966 :

 Aux États-Unis, première parution du

programme en 10 points

 du Black Panther Party.


1971 :

 A Belfast, l'IRA abat deux membres des troupes armées Irlandaises loyales à la couronne d'Angleterre et qui collabore avec son armée d'occupation.


1974 :

 En Irlande du Nord, une révolte a lieu dans la prison de Maze, où des prisonniers de l'IRA incendient plusieurs cellules.


1977 :

 A Lucca en Toscane, le groupe 'Lutte Armée pour le Communisme' fait sauter des explosifs contre le palais de justice de la ville.


1979 :

 En Irlande du Nord, un sondage révèle que près de 22% des Irlandais-es soutiennent l'action de l'IRA (ce qui est deux fois plus élevé que le taux d'approbation porté en ce moment à François Hollande ou Manuel Valls).


1981 :

 Au Salvador, la guérilla du FMLN fait sauter le pont Puente de Oro.


1984 :

 A Ixelles, près de Bruxelles, les Cellules Communistes Combattantes (CCC) font sauter la Fondation Internationale Jean Rey / Centre Paul Hymans. Il s'agit de l'institut de recherche politique et idéologique de l'Internationale Libérale (dont le Centre Paul Hymans est la section belge). Lire le communiqué conjoint avec leur action deux jours plus tard

ici

.


1987 :

 Au Burkina Faso, assassinat de Thomas Sankara, qui avait donné un nouveau souffle au pays en prenant toute une série de mesure économiques et politiques socialistes et très largement dirigées vers les classes les plus populaires du pays.


2005 :

 A Toledo, en Ohio, des antifascistes (composés en grande partie des anarchistes et des militant-e-s antiracistes locaux) organisent une contre-réunion contre un rassemblement néonazi. Cette situation débouche sur quatre heures d'affrontements entre les antifascistes et la police, qui arrêtent plusieurs douzaines de personnes. Un bar de policiers est incendié.


2008 :

 En Val Susa en Italie, plus de 400 pneus sont incendiés, provoquant le blocage de l'autoroute pour plus de trois heures.


2011 :

 A Rome, grande journée d'affrontements au cours de la 'journée mondiale des indignés'. Une annexe du ministère de l'Intérieur, des voitures de luxe et une fourgonnette de police sont incendiées ('Carlo Vive') et des banques et agences d'intérim attaquées sur tout le parcours.


2016 :

 Près de Des Moines dans l'Iowa, une pelleteuse et trois bulldozers

sont incendiés

 pour protester contre la construction du pipeline du Dakota Access, faisant 2 millions de dollars de dégâts. L'entreprise offre 100.000$ à qui balancera les auteurs de l'attaque. Espérons que ça n'arrive jamais.


2018 :

 A Besançon, huit véhicules d'Enedis (ex-Edf), qui promeut largement le développement de l'industrie nucléaire,

sont incendiés

 en pleine rue.


Voir

l'éphéméride anarchiste

 du 15 octobre.

title: Sağanakla perişan olan İstanbul'da ikinci ölüm: Ayazağa'da selde bir kişi hayatını kaybetti
content: İstanbul'da etkili olan sağanak sonrası Ayazağa'da meydana gelen selde 1 kişi hayatını kaybetti.

author: Unknown
title: İstanbul'u sel aldı: 1.277 su baskını, bir ölüm, 15 heyelan, binlerce yardım çağrısı
content:
İstanbul Valiliği, 14 Ekim günü sabah 06:00 ile 20:00 arasında kesintisiz süren olağanüstü yağışların 1.277 su baskınına yol açtığını, kentte 15 heyelan, 47 mahsur kalma, 13 ağaç devrilmesi ve iki çatı uçması kaydedildiğini bildirdi. Ayrıca 808 konut, 280 iş yeri ve 76 araçla ilgili ihbarlar alındı. 


Valilik açıklamasında şu bilgilere yer verdi:


“AFAD, İBB, İlçe Belediyeleri başta olmak üzere tüm kurumlar 8 bin personel, 2 bin araç ve iş makinası ile sahada yağış nedeniyle oluşan olumsuzluklara müdahale etmektedir.”


Kent genelinden alınan 2 bin 518 ihbarın ilgili müdahale ekiplerine yönlendirildiği bildirildi. 


Beykoz'da metrekareye 194 kilogram yağmur


İstanbul'un ilçeleri arasında yağış miktarı farklılık gösterdi.


Valiliğin verilerine göre Beykoz-Ömerli'de metrekareye 193,84 kilogram; Arnavutköy'de 125,9, Sarıyer-İTÜ Maslak istasyonunda 124,72, Çatalca'da 75,2 kilogram yağış kaydedildi.


Buna karşılık Kartal'da 14,3, Bakırköy'de yalnızca 6,8 kilogram yağış ölçüldü.


Yağış özellikle İstanbul'un bazı kuzey ve batı ilçelerinde yoğunlaştı. 


Yollar ve alt geçitler sular altında kaldı


Sağanak, özellikle Esenyurt, Başakşehir, Sultangazi ve Bayrampaşa'da ciddi su baskınlarına yol açtı.


Esenyurt Haramidere Sanayi Bölgesi'nde iş yerlerini su bastı. Başakşehir İkitelli'de araçlar suyla dolan yollarda ve alt geçitlerde mahsur kaldı.


Sultangazi'de yolların göle dönmesi nedeniyle yayalar yürümekte zorlandı. Bayrampaşa'da iş yerlerini korumaya çalışan esnaf, biriken suları kendi imkânlarıyla tahliye etmeye çalıştı.


Alt geçitlere ve bazı metro istasyonlarına su girmesi ulaşımda aksamalara neden oldu. Trafikte kalan araçlar ve toplu taşıma duraklarında biriken yolcular, yağışın günlük yaşam üzerindeki etkisini artırdı. 


Fatih'te 14 yaşındaki çocuk elektrik akımına kapıldı 


Sel felaketinin ilk ölüm haberi akşam saatlerinde geldi. Fatih'in Balat Mahallesi'ndeki Çukurbostan Parkı'nda 14 yaşındaki M.I., bir su birikintisine bastığı sırada elektrik akımına kapıldı. Bilinci kapalı olarak hastaneye kaldırılan çocuk, tüm müdahalelere rağmen kurtarılamadı.


İstanbul Valiliği olayla ilgili soruşturma başlatıldığını açıkladı. 


Sel sularında sürüklenen kadın kurtarıldı


Esenyurt'un Dereyolu Hürriyet Mahallesi'nde suya kapılan bir kadın, metrelerce sürüklendikten sonra çevredekilerin yardımıyla kurtarıldı. 


Sarıyer Ayazağa'da ise saat 19.00 sıralarında bir İETT otobüsü sel sularında sürüklendi. Mahsur kalan yolcular otobüsün tepesine çıkarak yardım bekledi. 


Perşembe günü okullar tatil, motosikletler trafikten men edildi


İstanbul Valiliği, 15 Ekim Perşembe günü kent genelindeki resmi ve özel eğitim kurumlarında yüz yüze eğitime bir gün ara verildiğini duyurdu.


Valilik ayrıca kamu kurumlarında çalışan hamile ve engelli personelin, gazilerin ve belirli koşullarda sekiz yaşından küçük çocuğu bulunan kadın çalışanların idari izinli sayılacağını açıkladı.


Motosiklet ve benzeri iki tekerlekli araçların trafiğe çıkışı da 14 Ekim saat 21.00'den başlayarak ikinci bir talimata kadar yasaklandı.


İstanbul Valiliğinin 19.49'da yayımladığı resmi açıklamada özellikle bodrum katlarında oturan yurttaşların su baskını tehlikesine karşı önlem almalarını ve zorunlu olmadıkça dışarı çıkmamalarını istendi. 


Felaketin boyutları


İstanbul'da birkaç saat içinde felaket boyutlarına bürünen olağanüstü yağışın etkisi, yalnızca su baskınlarıyla sınırlı değildi. Heyelanlar, elektrik çarpması tehlikesi, sürüklenen araçlar ve toplu taşıma sistemindeki aksamalar kent altyapısının farklı kesimlerinde sorunlara yol açtı. 


İstanbul'un sel tarihinde yeni bir felaket


14 Ekim'de Beykoz-Ömerli'de metrekareye düşen 193,84 kilogram yağış, İstanbul'un ekim ayı ortalaması olan 66,3 kilogramın yaklaşık üç katı. Bu miktar, kentin tarihsel yağış rekorlarına yaklaşırken bazı istasyonlarda kaydedilen en yüksek günlük değerleri de aşıyor.


İstanbul daha önce de benzer felaketler yaşadı. Eylül 2009'da Ayamama Deresi ve çevresindeki selde 31 kişi hayatını kaybetti. Temmuz 2017'de Silivri'de 2 saat içinde 118 kilogram yağış ölçüldü. Eylül 2023'te Arnavutköy ve Başakşehir'de 125 kilograma ulaşan sağanakta 2 kişi yaşamını yitirdi. 2026 felaketi, şiddetli yağış açısından istisnai boyutlara ulaşmış olsa da, İstanbul'un sel geçmişinde benzer felaketler yaşanmıştı.

title: Situation des forces antirep de la LT Paris IDF et rappels stratégiques pour la suite du mouvement lycéen
content:
En début de semaine, nous avons partagé sur Paris Lutte Infos un compte rendu de la répression de ces dernières semaines. Nous pensons qu'il est important de compléter ce compte rendu par une proposition stratégique pour la suite. En effet, la répression ne va sûrement pas diminuer car la lutte non plus

 

!!!


Depuis 2 semaines la legal team de Paris

IDF

 est aux côtés des lycéens.ne.s qui subissent la répression policière, judiciaire et administrative. 


Selon nous ces répressions ont un objectif commun : traumatiser les jeunes et les isoler pour les empêcher de recommencer. Pourquoi

 

? Car la justesse de leur engagement et sa spontanéité inquiète le pouvoir.


Pour éviter que cet isolement ne fonctionne la Legal Team Paris

IDF

 utilise la défense collective. Qu'est ce que c'est

 

? Tout simplement le fait qu'on ne laisse personne solo face à la répression (caisse de solidarité qui prend en charge les frais d'avocat.e) et qu'on ne se tape pas entre nous pour se défendre (principe de non différenciation, autrement dit on fait pas de différence entre un.e «

 

gentil/le manifestant.e pacifique

 

» et un.e «

 

grand méchant black bloc

 

» pour reprendre les termes du pouvoir

 

;)

 

!) 


Depuis la création de la Legal Team Paris

IDF

 en 2016 nous soutenons que la défense collective doit impérativement désacraliser le rôle des professionnel.le.s du droit dans sa pensée et son application. C'est la raison pour laquelle des militant.e.s sont présent.e.s tout au long de la procédure pour que les stratégies de défense soient pensées collectivement avec la personne réprimée, lae militant.e et l'avocat.e. 


La situation actuelle nous rappelle cette nécessité de ne pas dépendre des professionnel.le.s du droit. 


En effet, depuis deux semaines les avocat.e/s de confiance avec lesquel.le.s on travaille donnent tout ce qu'iels peuvent pour accompagner judiciairement les personnes réprimées et nous sommes très heureux.se.s de militer à leurs côtés. Iels se sont déplacé.es dans toute l'Ile-de-France pour des gardes à vue et des déferrements.


Mais aujourd'hui, compte tenu de l'ampleur de la répression et du nombre historique d'interpellations, iels ne sont pas suffisamment pour être présent.e.s sur chaque

GAV

 et chaque déferrement pour lesquel.le.s le numéro de téléphone de la Legal Team est appelé. 


Nous sommes à chaque fois honnêtes sur nos forces numériques. Nous informons les proches qui appellent si aucun.e avocat.e ne pourra se déplacer et nous conseillons de tenter auprès d'autres collectifs qui appliquent la non différenciation et les mêmes principes de base (le silence) si iels veulent absolument désigner un.e avocat.e pour la

GAV

. 


Cette situation de fait nous pousse donc à rappeler que l'antirépression n'est pas conditionnée aux professionnel.le.s du droit et qu'il est impératif de se former collectivement pour s'autonomiser en la matière.

author: newsroom
title: Παρέμβαση Γιάννη Μάγγου: «Αμετανόητοι οι κατηγορούμενοι»
content:
Σύνδεσμος δημοσίευσης:

Παρέμβαση Γιάννη Μάγγου: «Αμετανόητοι οι κατηγορούμενοι»


Ο Γιάννης Μάγγος, πατέρας του Βασίλειου Μάγγου, μετά την ολοκλήρωση των απολογιών

των κατηγορουμένων αστυνομικών για τον βασανισμό του γιού του

 στο Μικτό Ορκωτό Δικαστήριο της Καρδίτσας, παρεμβαίνει με δημόσια ανάρτησή του στην οποία θέτει ερωτήματα και προς τον υπουργό Μιχάλη Χρυσοχοΐδη.


Υπενθυμίζεται ότι το δικαστήριο δεν έχει επιτρέψει την παράσταση προς υποστήριξη της κατηγορίας για την οικογένεια του Β. Μάγγου.


Ολόκληρο το κείμενο της παρέμβασης που δημοσίευσε ο Γιάννης Μάγγος:


Αμετανόητοι οι κατηγορούμενοι


Ολοκληρώθηκαν στις 12.10.2026 οι απολογίες των έξι κατηγορούμενων αστυνομικών, βασανιστών του Βασίλειου Μάγγου. Όσον αφορά για το συνολικό περιστατικό, παραδέχτηκαν ότι «έγινε σωρεία λαθών και παραλείψεων» για τα οποία ευθύνονται και οι ίδιοι. «Έπραξα λάθος» είπαν.


Κανένας τους όμως δεν ζήτησε συγγνώμη από εμάς τους γονείς του για την προσβλητική, κακοποιητική και ανάρμοστη συμπεριφορά τους.


Είναι αδίστακτοι και αμετανόητοι.


Στην ερώτηση για την κινητικότητά του, απάντησαν πως, όταν κατέβηκε από το αυτοκίνητο, περπάτησε κανονικά, ανέβηκε τις σκάλες και έφτασε στον πρώτο όροφο της Υποδιεύθυνσης Ασφάλειας Βόλου χωρίς δυσκολία.


Ακριβώς! Επειδή τα πιο σφοδρά χτυπήματα και η πιο βάναυση συμπεριφορά επακολούθησαν κατόπιν μέσα στην Ασφάλεια.


Και σε άλλη ερώτηση του δικαστηρίου, πώς δικαιολογούνται τα έξι σπασμένα πλευρά και η θλάση στο ήπαρ, η απάντηση όλων των κατηγορούμενων ήταν ότι αυτοί μέσα στην Υ/Α δεν έκαναν τίποτα, ότι ο Βασίλειος Μάγγος δεν είχε τίποτα, δεν παραπονέθηκε για τίποτα…


– Και γιατί ο Μάγγος δεν πονούσε μόνο κατά το διάστημα από 4 μέχρι 5 μ.μ. που τον είχαν στην Ασφάλεια;


– …


Οι μάρτυρες που τον βρήκαν κατέθεσαν ότι πονούσε φρικτά και δεν μπορούσε να σηκωθεί να περπατήσει. Όλα αυτά επιβεβαιώθηκαν από τις καταθέσεις των γιατρών και την αξονική τομογραφία. Και γιατί δεν τον πήγαν στο νοσοκομείο; «Δεν το ζήτησε»…


Ούτε τους ζήτησε νερό: «Αν ζητούσε κάτι, μέχρι και ελικόπτερο θα κατεβάζαμε για να του το δώσουμε»… Κανένας όμως δεν είπε ότι του έδωσαν, έστω, ένα ποτήρι νερό.


Όπως κατήγγειλε ο ίδιος, τον παρέπεμψαν να πιει νερό από ένα χαλασμένο ψύκτη, σύρθηκε μέχρι εκεί και προσπάθησε να πάρει λίγες σταγόνες νερού στο στόμα του για να ανακουφίσει το σωματικό και ψυχικό του μαρτύριο. Και αυτοί τον χλεύαζαν και γελούσαν εις βάρος του για την προσπάθεια που κατέβαλλε. Αυτό του κόστισε ανυπολόγιστα, ακύρωσε την ύπαρξή του, όπως διαπιστώσαμε κι εμείς οι γονείς του.


– Και σαν προσαχθείς, σε ποιον ήταν χρεωμένος;


– …


Και ενώ δεν επρόκειτο παρά για μία «απλή προσαγωγή» κι ο Βασίλειος Μάγγος ήταν «ήσυχος και ήρεμος» (όπως είπαν), γιατί απαιτούνταν η συνδρομή έξι αστυνομικών; Τέσσερις της ΟΠΚΕ και δύο της Υ/Α Βόλου;


Πάλι απάντησαν ανεύθυνα, λέγοντας ψέμματα ότι δεν παρείχαν συνδρομή. Στην προανάκριση όμως άλλα κατέθεσαν.


Π.χ. κατηγορούμενος της ΟΠΚΕ: «..προσήλθαν και όλοι οι υπόλοιποι μηνυόμενοι. Παρείχαμε επιτήρηση στον Μάγγο Β.» (έγγραφα 1,2,6).


Κάποιος, σε σχετική ερώτηση του δικαστηρίου, γιατί άλλα έλεγαν πριν και άλλα τώρα, είχε την αφέλεια να απαντήσει ότι «άλλαξε η υπερασπιστική γραμμή»… Παρατήρηση του δικαστηρίου: «η αλήθεια δεν αλλάζει».


Όπως ακριβώς με την ιατροδικαστή και τους γιατρούς τους. Οι τρεις γνωμάτευσαν ότι τα πλευρά τα είχε σπασμένα, πριν τον χτυπήσουν μπροστά στα δικαστήρια και ο τέταρτος υποστήριξε ότι του τα έσπασαν μπροστά στα δικαστήρια.


Και τί ώρα αποχώρησαν από την υπηρεσία τους;


Οι αστυνομικοί της ΟΠΚΕ απάντησαν ότι αποχώρησαν πριν τις 5 μ.μ. Όμως στον Πίνακα Διάταξης της Υπηρεσίας και σε δεύτερο έγγραφο αναφέρεται ότι η υπηρεσία τους ήταν από 10π.μ. έως 6 μ.μ. (έγγραφα 3, 4, 5). Και ο σκοπός πύλης κατηγορηματικά κατέθεσε ότι τους είδε να αποχωρούν στις 6μ.μ.


Και ποιοι αποχώρησαν πρώτοι; Όλοι ισχυρίστηκαν ότι οι κατηγορούμενοι της ΟΠΚΕ αποχώρησαν πρώτοι. Όμως στην προδικασία ένας κατηγορούμενος ισχυρίστηκε το αντίθετο (έγγραφο 6 – βλ. παραπάνω).


Αντιφάσεις, αντιφάσεις και ψέμματα…


Γιατί τον κράτησαν σχεδόν δύο ώρες και τον άφησαν αβοήθητο, ενώ ήταν ήδη χτυπημένος;


Του έκαναν σωματική έρευνα, (δεν του βρήκαν τίποτα) αλλά δεν αντιλήφθηκαν να πάσχει από κάτι: «Ηταν μια χαρά!».


Έκθεση σωματικής έρευνας, όμως, δεν συνέταξαν.

author: Unknown
title: Carcere di Torino: cimici dei letti e condizioni degradanti. Il diario di un detenuto racconta la realtà del carcere
content:
Ieri è stato sollevato in Consiglio Regionale il problema delle cimici dei letti all’interno della sezione maschile del carcere di Torino. La questione è uscita grazie a dei fogli di diario, alcuni passaggi sono stati letti anche in seduta di Consiglio.


Noi li abbiamo ricevuti da alcuni detenuti e di seguito li ripubblichiamo integralmente.


diario cimici

Download


Ne avevamo già parlato

qui

 quando, a seguito di racconti di detenuti, abbiamo avuto la possibilità di fare uscire il tema. Erano coinvolti sicuramente il Blocco B e la decima sezione in particolare. Ma, stando alle ricostruzioni, sembra molto probabile un’infestazione del magazzino dei materassi del carcere, oltre che delle celle.


Da allora non è stata fatta alcuna azione per migliorare le condizioni.


In questa intervista su

Radio Blackout

 Giorgio, da poco uscito dal carcere per termine di sconto della pena, racconta in maniera dettagliata la situazione.


Giorgio Rossetto

, militante di lunga data dell’Autonomia torinese e della resistenza No Tav, è recentemente uscito dall’ennesimo periodo di detenzione, scattato il 22 agosto 2026 con la revoca degli arresti domiciliari.


Grazie al suo contributo cerchiamo di osservare la situazione attuale all’interno del carcere delle Vallette a Torino, tra processi di deumanizzazione, autolesionismo e suicidi, disperazione dilagante e sofferenza sociale:


Qui il video in cui la consigliera regionale Alice Ravinale solleva la questione


Anche al Tg Regionale di martedì 13 ottobre è passato un servizio sulle condizioni del carcere di Torino.


Ciò che già scrivevamo qualche settimana fa “Chissà se il Sindaco Lo Russo, il Presidente della Regione Cirio o il ministro della Giustizia Nordio se ne fregheranno altamente anche questa volta. Certo è che i detenuti e le detenute devono aver riconosciuta la loro dignità e molte volte trovano anche da soli il modo per farla rispettare, come successo nei giorni scorsi nel carcere Don Bosco di Pisa” possiamo riproporlo senza modifiche a riprova dell’inerzia e totale disinteresse delle istituzioni a fronte di una situazione gravissima.

author: PETA-Team
title: Tote Rehe für Wortwitz verhöhnt: „Speziesismus des Monats“ an smile Versicherungen
content:
Speziesismus ist in unserer heutigen Gesellschaft noch weit verbreitet, aber ethisch nicht gerechtfertigt: Bei diesem Denkmuster unterscheiden wir Menschen andere 

fühlende Tiere

 nach ihrem vermeintlichen Wert und Nutzen für uns – wir stellen uns über andere Spezies: Wir diskriminieren sie, beuten sie milliardenfach aus, lassen sie leiden und töten sie. Wir von PETA Deutschland vergeben regelmäßig den „Speziesismus des Monats“ als Negativpreis für Unternehmen, Prominente und Behörden, die mit speziesistischen und tierfeindlichen Aussagen und Aktionen auffallen.


Eine Werbekampagne der Versicherungsfirma

smile

 mit Sitz in Österreich und der Schweiz nimmt Wildunfälle zum Anlass, einen Wortwitz auf Kosten von Rehen als Slogan zu verwenden: „Reh umgefahren. Halb so wild.“ Aus unserer Sicht werden Rehe damit zu bloßen Hindernissen degradiert und ihr Tod für eine Werbebotschaft bagatellisiert. Für diese speziesistische Darstellung verleihen wir smile Versicherungen den Negativpreis „Speziesismus des Monats“ im Oktober 2026. Denn Speziesismus ist die Diskriminierung von Lebewesen aufgrund ihrer Artzugehörigkeit.


„Reh umgefahren. Halb so wild.“: Negativpreis für smile Versicherungen

 


Wildunfälle

 können für Tiere und auch für Menschen tödlich enden oder schwere Verletzungen verursachen. Die Werbekampagne von smile macht aus diesem Leid einen Wortwitz: „Reh umgefahren. Halb so wild.“ Aus unserer Sicht wird der Tod von Rehen damit verharmlost und für Werbezwecke instrumentalisiert. Die Tiere werden in diesem Zusammenhang zweitrangig als Objekte hinter dem finanziellen Schaden dargestellt – und ihr Tod als nicht so schlimm, weil der finanzielle Schaden ausgeglichen wird. Dass es sich um fühlende Lebewesen handelt, die durch einen Unfall ein schweres Schicksal erleiden, wird ausgeblendet.  


Für diese Darstellung verleihen wir smile Versicherungen den Negativpreis „Speziesismus des Monats“. 


„Die Kampagne von smile verharmlost das Leid der unzähligen Rehe, die jedes Jahr im Straßenverkehr auf grausame Art ums Leben kommen. Ihren Tod als vermeintliche Pointe eines Witzes zu benutzen, ist geschmacklos und hinterlässt den Eindruck, dass sie von den Verantwortlichen als reine Objekte angesehen werden. Es ist bedauerlich, dass die Texter:innen der Werbekampagne keinen Slogan gefunden haben, der sich für Mensch und Tier einsetzt.“

Peter Höffken, Fachreferent bei PETA Deutschland 


In einer von PETA angefragten Stellungnahme erklärt das Unternehmen, dass sie mit dem Slogan „halb so Wild“ ausschließlich den finanziellen Schaden am Fahrzeug darstellen wollten, der durch eine Versicherung reguliert werden kann. Ausdrücklich nicht gemeint sei das Tier selbst oder das Unfallgeschehen. Man empfinde Wildunfälle ebenso als schreckliche Ereignisse. Die Werbekampagne sei nun beendet.    


Millionen Wildtiere sterben jährlich im Straßenverkehr

 


Unter den größeren Tierarten fallen in Deutschland

Rehe

 besonders

häufig Wildunfällen zum Opfer. Im Jagdjahr 2023/24 waren es über 204.000 Tiere. Hinzu kamen unter anderem mehr als 15.000 Wildschweine. [1, 2] 


Doch die erfassten größeren Wildtiere sind nur ein Teil der Opfer des Straßenverkehrs. Jedes Jahr sterben auch unzählige kleinere Wildtiere wie Igel, Marder, Kaninchen, Vögel oder Kröten auf deutschen Straßen. Allein bei

Igeln

 wird die Zahl der jährlich überfahrenen Tiere auf 500.000 bis eine Million geschätzt. [3] 


In der Schweiz sterben jedes Jahr Hundertausende Wildtiere im Straßenverkehr.

Unter den größeren Tierarten fallen auch dort Rehe am häufigsten Wildunfällen zum Opfer. Im Jahr 2025 waren es 7651 Tiere. [3] Auf Schweizer Straßen sterben jedes Jahr schätzungsweise Hunderttausende weitere Wildtiere bei Wildunfällen, beispielsweise über 6000 Füchse im vergangenen Jahr. Besonders häufig sind Kleintiere wie Igel, Marder, Kaninchen, Vögel oder Kröten betroffen, von denen viele statistisch nicht erfasst werden. 


Wildtiere brauchen sichere und unberührte Lebensräume

 


Inmitten von Kulturlandschaften, Straßen und dicht bebauten Siedlungsbereichen wird der

Lebensraum für Wildtiere

 immer knapper. Dort, wo einst Rast- und Nahrungsgebiete waren, gibt es heute vielerorts kaum noch Platz. Insbesondere die auf Profitmaximierung ausgerichtete industrielle Land- und Forstwirtschaft trägt zum Verlust von Lebensräumen bei. 


Tierarten, die versuchen, in Koexistenz mit Menschen zu leben, werden vertrieben,

gejagt

 oder zu sogenannten „Schädlingen“ degradiert.  …

title: Γιάννης Μάγγος: “Αμετανόητοι οι κατηγορούμενοι”
content:
Γιάννης Μάγγος: “Αμετανόητοι οι κατηγορούμενοι”


Κοινοποιούμε αλληλέγγυα την σημερινή δημοσίευση που μας απέστειλε ο κύριος Γιάννης Μάγγος σχετικά με την ολοκλήρωση των απολογιών των έξι κατηγορούμενων αστυνομικών, βασανιστών του Βασίλειου Μάγγου:


ΑΜΕΤΑΝΟΗΤΟΙ ΟΙ ΚΑΤΗΓΟΡΟΥΜΕΝΟΙ


Ολοκληρώθηκαν στις 12.10.2026 οι απολογίες των έξι κατηγορούμενων αστυνομικών, βασανιστών του Βασίλειου Μάγγου. Όσον αφορά για το συνολικό περιστατικό, παραδέχτηκαν ότι “έγινε σωρεία λαθών και παραλείψεων” για τα οποία ευθύνονται και οι ίδιοι. “Έπραξα λάθος” είπαν.


Κανένας τους όμως δεν ζήτησε συγγνώμη από εμάς τους γονείς του για την προσβλητική,


κακοποιητική και ανάρμοστη συμπεριφορά τους.


Είναι αδίστακτοι και αμετανόητοι.


-Στην ερώτηση για την κινητικότητά του, απάντησαν πως, όταν κατέβηκε από το αυτοκίνητο, περπάτησε κανονικά, ανέβηκε τις σκάλες και έφτασε στον πρώτο όροφο της Υ/Α Βόλου χωρίς δυσκολία.


*Ακριβώς! Επειδή τα πιο σφοδρά χτυπήματα και η πιο βάναυση συμπεριφορά επακολούθησαν κατόπιν μέσα στην Ασφάλεια.


-Και σε άλλη ερώτηση του δικαστηρίου, πώς δικαιολογούνται τα έξι σπασμένα πλευρά και η θλάση στο ήπαρ, η απάντηση όλων των κατηγορούμενων ήταν ότι αυτοί μέσα στην Υ/Α δεν έκαναν τίποτα, ότι ο Βασίλειος Μάγγος δεν είχε τίποτα, δεν παραπονέθηκε για τίποτα…


-Και γιατί ο Μάγγος δεν πονούσε μόνο κατά το διάστημα από 4 μέχρι 5 μ.μ. που τον είχαν στην Ασφάλεια;


– …..


*Οι μάρτυρες που τον βρήκαν κατέθεσαν ότι πονούσε φρικτά και δεν μπορούσε να σηκωθεί να περπατήσει. Όλα αυτά επιβεβαιώθηκαν από τις καταθέσεις των γιατρών και την αξονική τομογραφία.


-Και γιατί δεν τον πήγαν στο νοσοκομείο; -“Δεν το ζήτησε”…


-Ούτε τους ζήτησε νερό.


“Αν ζητούσε κάτι, μέχρι και ελικόπτερο θα κατεβάζαμε για να του το δώσουμε”…


*Κανένας όμως δεν είπε ότι του έδωσαν, έστω, ένα ποτήρι νερό.


Όπως κατήγγειλε ο ίδιος, τον παρέπεμψαν να πιει νερό από ένα χαλασμένο ψύκτη, σύρθηκε μέχρι εκεί και προσπάθησε να πάρει λίγες σταγόνες νερού στο στόμα του για να ανακουφίσει το σωματικό και ψυχικό του μαρτύριο. Και αυτοί τον χλεύαζαν και γελούσαν εις βάρος του για την προσπάθεια που κατέβαλλε. Αυτό του κόστισε ανυπολόγιστα, ακύρωσε την ύπαρξή του, όπως διαπιστώσαμε κι εμείς οι γονείς του.


-Και σαν προσαχθείς, σε ποιον ήταν χρεωμένος;


– …..


-Και ενώ δεν επρόκειτο παρά για μία απλή προσαγωγή κι ο Βασίλειος Μάγγος ήταν ήσυχος και ήρεμος (όπως είπαν), γιατί απαιτούνταν η συνδρομή έξι αστυνομικών; Τέσσερις της οπκε και δύο της Υ/Α Βόλου.


Πάλι απάντησαν ανεύθυνα, λέγοντας ψέμματα ότι δεν παρείχαν συνδρομή. Στην προανάκριση όμως άλλα κατέθεσαν. π.χ. κατηγορούμενος της οπκε: “..προσήλθαν και όλοι οι υπόλοιποι μηνυόμενοι. Παρείχαμε επιτήρηση στον Μάγγο Β.” (έγγραφα 1,2,6).


Κάποιος, σε σχετική ερώτηση του δικαστηρίου, γιατί άλλα έλεγαν πριν και άλλα τώρα, είχε την αφέλεια να απαντήσει ότι άλλαξε η υπερασπιστική γραμμή…


Παρατήρηση του δικαστηρίου: “η αλήθεια δεν αλλάζει”.


*Όπως ακριβώς με την ιατροδικαστή και τους γιατρούς τους. Οι τρεις γνωμάτευσαν ότι τα πλευρά τα είχε σπασμένα, πριν τον χτυπήσουν μπροστά στα δικαστήρια και ο τέταρτος υποστήριξε ότι του τα έσπασαν μπροστά στα δικαστήρια…


-Και τί ώρα αποχώρησαν από την υπηρεσία τους;


Οι αστυνομικοί της οπκε απάντησαν ότι αποχώρησαν πριν τις πέντε μ.μ. Όμως στον Πίνακα Διάταξης της Υπηρεσίας και σε δεύτερο έγγραφο αναφέρεται ότι η υπηρεσία τους ήταν από 10π.μ. έως 6 μ.μ. (έγγραφα 3,4,5). Και ο σκοπός πύλης κατηγορηματικά κατέθεσε ότι τους είδε να αποχωρούν στις 6μ.μ.


Και ποιοι αποχώρησαν πρώτοι; Όλοι ισχυρίστηκαν ότι οι κατηγορούμενοι της οπκε


αποχώρησαν πρώτοι. Όμως στην προδικασία ένας κατηγορούμενος ισχυρίστηκε το


αντίθετο (έγγραφο 6).


Αντιφάσεις, αντιφάσεις και ψέμματα…


-Γιατί τον κράτησαν σχεδόν δύο ώρες και τον άφησαν αβοήθητο, ενώ ήταν ήδη χτυπημένος;


Του έκαναν σωματική έρευνα, (δεν του βρήκαν τίποτα) αλλά δεν αντιλήφθηκαν να πάσχει από κάτι:


“Ηταν μια χαρά!”.


*Έκθεση σωματικής έρευνας, όμως, δεν συνέταξαν. Ούτε ενημέρωσαν τον εισαγγελέα. Κι ενώ έπρεπε, όπως ισχυρίστηκαν, να τον συλλάβουν για τα υποτιθέμενα αδικήματα αντίστασης κατά της αρχής και απόπειρα απελευθέρωσης κρατουμένου, παρ΄όλα αυτά δεν το έκαναν, ούτε σχημάτισαν δικογραφία εις βάρος του…


Όμως “αυτοί δεν ευθύνονται για τίποτα”, οι ανώτεροί τους φταίνε που έδωσαν προφορικές εντολές να μη σχηματιστεί δικογραφία και να τον ελευθερώσουν…


“Φταίει ο διοικητής της Υ/Α”… “Ήταν εντολή άνωθεν να μη γίνει σύλληψη και δικογραφία”… “Ο διοικητής της Υ/Α δεν ενημέρωσε τον εισαγγελέα και βρισκόμαστε εμείς στο …

author: AfricanFeminism
title: Morocco’s First Woman Prime Minister and the Terms of Freedom
content:
Something changes when a woman occupies an office men have treated as their natural inheritance. Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri’s

appointment

 on 29 September 2026 makes that change visible in Morocco. For women whose competence is routinely scrutinised, the pleasure is neither naïve nor trivial.


But the woman forming a government and the woman labouring in the fields, raising children without pay and denied an equal share of her inheritance encounter power differently. Representation changes who governs; emancipation changes what all women have the power to do. That distinction shifts our attention from PM Mansouri’s gender to the politics of the centre-right

 Party of Authenticity and Modernity (PAM

)

, which she leads. Will its programme redistribute the resources and rights on which women’s freedom depends?


The history beneath the headline


Calling women’s leadership foreign to Morocco requires forgetting its history. Historian Osire Glacier

documents

 women’s authority long before the contemporary premiership. Kenza al Awrabiya, the Amazigh mother of Idris II, helped secure the Idrisid dynasty, founded in the late eighth century in what is now Morocco. Zaynab al Nafzawiyya influenced eleventh-century Almoravid politics around Aghmat, near Marrakech. Sayyida al Hurra governed Tétouan, a city in northern Morocco, during the sixteenth century. Khnata bint Bakkar intervened in eighteenth-century dynastic politics.


Across the region,

Dihya

 is remembered as an Amazigh queen who led resistance to the Arab conquest in the Aurès, in present-day Algeria, during the late seventh century. Tuareg oral tradition remembers

Tin Hinan

 as a queen and founding ancestress of noble lineages in the Ahaggar, in present-day southern Algeria.


These histories expose how male authority is made to appear natural. Fatima Mernissi’s

The Forgotten Queens of Islam


challenges that selective memory. Colonialism also reorganised authority: French Protectorate administrators

reshaped

 customary courts around imperial priorities. What survives as tradition can carry the history of political intervention. 


Religious interpretation can give exclusion another claim to permanence. Islamist and other conservative opponents invoke this

hadith

 against women’s political authority:


«لَنْ يُفْلِحَ قَوْمٌ وَلَّوْا أَمْرَهُمُ امْرَأَةً»


Usually translated as saying that a people governed by a woman will not prosper, it becomes a prohibition irrespective of her competence. Asma Lamrabet, a

Moroccan Islamic feminist thinker

, questions turning a

narration linked

 to Persia’s dynastic succession into a universal ban. She reads it against the Qur’anic Queen of Sheba, whose judgement demonstrates capable leadership. Her argument contests male authority’s claim to divine necessity.


PAM’s promises and its record


Women have long contested how authority is distributed within the family. Fatima Sadiqi

documents

the Union de l’Action Féminine’s 1992 million-signature campaign to reform the Moudawana, Morocco’s family code. The 2004 reform abolished wives’ duty of obedience but retained unequal inheritance and exceptions to the marriage age of eighteen. Proposals announced in December 2024 left fundamental equality demands unresolved. In October 2025, more than sixty civil society organisations and public figures

joined to call for comprehensive reform

. Rights in Morocco have advanced through organised demands, not the gender of an officeholder.


PAM, a centre-right party founded in 2008,

advocates

 social modernisation and positions itself against the Islamist Justice and Development Party (PJD). It entered government in 2021 alongside the National Rally of Independents and conservative nationalist Istiqlal. Opposition to Islamist conservatism, however, does not itself entail reforming the laws and economic conditions that subordinate women.


PAM’s

2026 programme

 promises improved widow pensions, childcare, safe transport, a women’s enterprise fund and labour inspection. The commitments leave inheritance equality, abortion reform and decriminalisation of consensual same sex relations unaddressed. Mansouri called for

banning child marriage

 without exceptions in 2024, yet PAM’s electoral programme

omits that commitment

author: Hassan Alnaser, Mohamed Alagra, Ehsan Salah
title: Sudan, Egypt to pursue joint border security, as public tensions flare after deadly mine bombing
content:
In the aftermath of the bombing of a mine in the

Halayeb Triangle

 that left scores of Sudanese miners dead, Egypt and Sudan are discussing a new security framework along the countries’ shared eastern border.

 


That framework would provide for joint coordination to pursue what both sides regard as security risks arising from organized crime, Sudanese and Egyptian officials

told

 Mada Masr.


The push toward closer coordination comes amid public outcry in Sudan and diplomatic concern in international quarters over the killing of scores of artisanal miners in the disputed

Halayeb Triangle

 on Saturday.

 


That public outcry was accentuated on Monday when a gunman killed two Egyptians in a main market in southern Khartoum in what Sudanese security officials involved in the investigations told Mada Masr was a retaliatory attack.


The shooting took place at around 2 pm near the

Export Development Bank in the Local Market

, a security source in

Khartoum State police

 told Mada Masr.

 Three Egyptians were targeted in the market’s commercial area.

Two died at the scene, while the third was taken to the

Omdurman Medical Corps Hospital

for treatment.


Ali al-Laouta, a vegetable seller at the market, witnessed Monday’s shooting.

He told Mada Masr that he noticed a man wearing a

military uniform bearing the badge of the joint force of military-allied armed movements buying some items in the market.

 


He then suddenly pointed his weapon at the three Egyptians shopping nearby, opened fire and fled the scene, Laouta adds.


Police patrols and security units responded to the scene and tracked down the suspect, a source in the Khartoum police’s criminal investigations department told Mada Masr. The suspect initially resisted arrest, opening fire on security forces, but officers eventually subdued him, seized the weapon used in the attack and took him into custody, the source said.


One member of the arrest unit was shot in the leg during the exchange of fire, a security officer involved in the operation said. The injured officer was hospitalized and is in stable condition, he added.


The suspect is a member of the “support forces” — a wide range of armed formations that fight alongside the Sudanese military in the current war — a source informed of the preliminary investigation told Mada Masr.


Sudan’s military-led government adopted a wartime policy that put the joint force, its main battlefield ally, in charge of protecting state institutions and supporting security operations in cities under military control. That has left the alliance with a heavy presence in urban areas.

But a

string

 of violent incidents involving joint force members in recent months has stoked public concerns and prompted authorities to review the policy and seek to curb the allied group’s urban presence.


The source informed of the preliminary investigation told Mada Masr that the suspect was subjected to intensive questioning about his military affiliation and how he had obtained the weapon used in the attack.


The interrogating officer told Mada Masr that, in his initial statement, the suspect said he had shot the Egyptian men in retaliation for his brother’s death in Saturday’s strikes.


The shooting comes amid a wave of polarization in Sudanese public opinion following the deadly airstrike near the Sudanese-Egyptian border that killed scores of Sudanese people.


The shooting adds more complexity to an already charged public sphere.


Sudanese lawyer Oweis Salah Eddin al-Iraqi urged authorities to disclose the facts related to the miners’ deaths directly to the public, saying the case had become a matter of public concern and that any mishandling could provoke backlash.


Many in the public and political arena are viewing the shooting in the context of wider accountability for the miners’ deaths.


Viewing the market shooting in isolation from the attack on the miners would offer an incomplete assessment of the situation, said Adel Ibrahim Hamad, the head of

Sudan’s Ashigga Party.


The party was re-established by former members of the Democratic Unionist Party, drawing inspiration from an earlier party of the same name that called for union with Egypt.

 The revived party focuses on national issues, paying particular attention to Sudanese-Egyptian relations.


Discussion of Monday’s shooting, Hamad argued, must begin with the original incident, saying Egypt’s response was disproportionate to the violation, “if any.” …

author: Eliel Peterson
title: Death as liberation
content:
Death as liberation is hardly a comfortable political proposition to digest. In a world where Black death is often the common condition, there is a well-established insistence on our living. So what do we make of two of Africa’s greatest filmmakers, Ousmane Sembène and Souleymane Cissé, whose earliest cinematic visions, expressed through their respective debut features

Black Girl

 (1966) and

Den Muso

 (1975), center on the suffering, alienation, and eventual deaths of Black women?

Sembène’s

Black Girl

 is preoccupied with racial violence and the economic exploitation that continues to structure relations between Senegal and France. The film follows Diouana, a young Senegalese woman who accepts employment with a white French family and travels to Antibes believing she is embarking on a new life. While Cissé’s

Den Muso

, turns inward, examining interpersonal violence and the ways patriarchal power consumes family life and communities, weakening the broader social fabric of a nation. The film follows Tenin, a mute young woman who becomes pregnant after being raped, exposing the brutal underbelly of the patriarchal violence imposed upon her. Despite the differences in their circumstances, both films position death as a troubling possibility of liberation for their central characters.

Tenin (Dounamba Dany Coulibaly) in a still from Souleymane Cissé’s

Den Muso

 (1975).

The history of Black resistance has not solely been confined to the preservation of life. From enslaved Africans who leapt from ships during the Middle Passage, to those who faced death in the fight against their oppression,

It is true

 that to rather die than to endure is not a popular or digestible form of liberation. Although these acts are not equivalent, nor do they carry the same weight as the deaths of these fictional characters, Sembène and Cissé, raise an uncomfortable question: what does life mean for a person stripped of agency, recognition, and self-determination?

For Diouana and Tenin, freedom remains out of reach because of the structures governing their everyday lives that continually deny these women full humanity: Tenin’s father and her rapist, Diouana’s white employers. This sustained stripping of humanity produces what I would argue is already a death, albeit a social one, that precedes their physical endings. Sembène and Cissé challenge audiences by asking what is living for the dehumanized. Diouana travels to France only to find her livelihood replaced by isolation and unpaid, alienated labor, while Tenin’s body becomes a site upon which familial and communal shame, punishment, and control are dumped. Death, therefore, is at the core of both films from the outset, existing not only as a shocking culminating event, but as a condition of violence. By the end of each film, Sembène and Cissé are not arguing over whether death is a worthy or noble choice for self-liberation; rather, they position the act of self-annihilation as the only remaining form of control available to their characters, and as an indictment of a society in which death is the only option. 

It is understandable to recoil at the self-inflicted violence that ultimately claims both Diouana and Tenin. One might ask why their rage is not directed solely towards those who harmed them. Why does Tenin’s retaliation extend beyond her rapist? Why doesn’t Diouana exact revenge on her employers and flee France? These questions linger because death feels like an unsatisfying conclusion, one that denies us, as audiences, the catharsis of resistance. We want these women to fight back and survive. We want their suffering to lead somewhere other than death. Yet perhaps the more daunting question is not why these women die, but whether we find their deaths more difficult to accept than the suffering that precedes them. What is ultimately more uncomfortable to confront: their deaths, or the conditions that made life itself unbearable?

Neither film offers an uncomplicated answer. To read Diouana’s and Tenin’s deaths as acts of liberation is not to suggest that their deaths resolve the violence they endure, or that self-annihilation is freedom in any complete sense. Their deaths do not dismantle the structures that dehumanized them. What death offers these women, perhaps then, is not freedom but a final assertion of agency within those systems. This is what makes their endings so devastating: the possibility of control emerges only when the possibility of living on their …

author: WoMin
title: Press Release | Women’s Climate Assembly strengthens Pan African solidarity, women-led resistance and the struggle for a just future
content:
“

Empowering women is a radical way to transform the world!

” –

Ivorian activist


The fourth regional

Women’s Climate Assembly

 (WCA), held in Yaoundé, Cameroon, from 5–8 October 2026, concluded with a powerful reaffirmation of African women’s determination to defend their lands, territories, livelihoods and communities, and to demand climate justice and reparations.


Under the theme, “

Our lands, our voices: African women united for climate justice and reparations!

”, the Assembly convened over 75 women community leaders, activists, feminist organisations, civil society groups and allies from twelve countries including Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Côte d’Ivoire, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Guinea-Conakry, Liberia, Namibia, Niger, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Senegal and Zambia.


The gathering provided a vital space for women on the frontlines of the climate crisis, extractive industries, land dispossession and environmental destruction to share their experiences, strengthen relationships across borders and build collective strategies for change.


As the Assembly closed, one message rang clear: African women are not merely bearing the costs of the climate crisis. They are leading the struggle for solutions, defending their communities and shaping the future they want.


“

There’s an adage in my village that women cannot build a nation. The Women’s Climate Assembly has proved that women build nations. We counter this adage with the unity and solidarity of African women!”

 –

DRC activist-participant


Turning shared struggles into collective power


From communities confronting oil and gas expansion and destructive mining to women defending forests, seeds, water sources and ancestral lands, participants brought forward the lived realities of communities too often excluded from decisions about their territories and futures.


Through collective reflection, popular education and movement-building, women connected struggles that may take place in different countries but are rooted in common systems of exploitation, inequality and environmental destruction.


Designed by women activists and members of the WCA Steering Committee, the thematic teach-ins explored a range of political concepts, questions and practices, including:


The erosion of farmers’ seeds

: A challenge for building resilient and sustainable food systems. What solutions are there for preserving our seed heritage?  


Nature Commons

: The defence of the Congo Basin’s forests.


Counting the Costs of Mal/Bad Development and Demanding reparations

: The case of the African Development Bank campaign.


Fighting some of the false solutions to the climate crisis

: Gas extraction, enclosure of our forests and lands for carbon trading, green conservation and more.


Building democratic, accountable, ‘loving’ leadership

: Why are these principles so important to feminist leadership? What else do we feel is critical to leading as feminists?


Lessons on organising and movement building

: Growing National/sub-regional grassroots movements.


Building knowledge from what we know

: Building feminist popular knowledge as the basis for Building Women’s Power. How can we go about doing this locally in our communities and beyond that.


The WCA celebrated the knowledge, resistance and organising power of rural, Indigenous, peasant and working-class women. The

Each One, Teach One

 sessions embodied this spirit of knowledge-sharing, collective learning and liberation. On Day Two, participants exchanged practical skills, crafts and tools, sharing techniques for making baobab candies, producing eco-briquettes from cassava and creating seed bricks to cultivate and protect Indigenous seeds. Weaving, cloth-dyeing, beadwork and other practices also featured, affirming the value of knowledge held, practised and passed down through generations of women.


The gathering reaffirmed the importance of strengthening a Pan African ecofeminist movement that recognises the connections between the climate crisis, extractivism, gender injustice, food insecurity and the loss of community control over natural resources.


It also reinforced a fundamental principle: communities must have the power to determine their own futures, including the right to say NO to destructive development projects that threaten their lands, livelihoods and ways of life.


Climate justice means reparations, not empty promises

author: ROAPE
title: African Labour and Liberation
content:
African Labour and Liberation

 brings together the experiences of workers, trade unions and labour movements across the continent to ask what they can tell us about work, power and liberation today. We assembled this collection because of the surprisingly few recent accounts of the emergence of a class politics on the continent. Labour is central to understanding the present political economy of Africa.  More than 90 percent of Africa’s 500 million workers work in informal and precarious jobs in a labour force that will grow rapidly in the next three decades.


The social and political mobilization of workers in multifarious contexts across the continent is imperative to improving their socio-economic conditions. It is necessary to situate Africa’s workers at the centre. This collection starts from the premise that labour struggles are essential to improving the conditions of work and stamping out poverty and inequality that the confronts most African workers today and form the basis for building new forms of collective power.


This heterodox collec­tion finds six primary patterns prevalent in the struggle for the working class liberation in the post-independence era.


1. Most governments in Africa are comprador-bureaucratic regimes beholden to foreign capital and imperialists’ interests to protect and maintain unequal exchange of trade and the attenuation of demands by the masses for national control over natural resources and production. Comprador-bureaucratic regimes remain loyal to their post-colonial powers and pay fleeting attention to national sustainability, the rights of women, natu­ral ecology, and the ever-growing needs of the masses for health care, education, housing, infrastructure, water, and electricity.


Government legislation to defend popular interests that have been enacted by national assemblies are rarely fully implemented and are likely to be opposed by international banks and lenders, predominantly from the West through structural adjustment programs that undermine evanescent attempts to ameliorate the most significant challenges.


2. Diverse workers’ movements form to resist t the comprador-bureaucratic political economies which formed in the colonial era which most often extract surplus value from workers and natural resources from the continent  through what  Arghiri Emmanuel  identified as

unequal exchange of trade

, and despoiling, and plundering African nations. Control is maintained by local elites attached to state power who are beneficiaries of rentier capitalism. These national elites have welcomed Western powers to establish military bases osten­sibly to establish peace and order.


In most instances, the emergence of violence and disorder were generated by Western military intervention. However, as Samir Amin shows, workers and peasants drive the enduring imperative for the formation of national projects for popular sovereignty, which are often imperfect and challenged by imperialists seeking to maintain the unequal exchange of trade.


3. African states are ruled by comprador state-centric bureaucratic elites who maintain rentier capitalism as the primary source of revenue rather than investing in productive technology. The historical pattern is opposition to the redistribution of wealth and income to the masses.


This process, in which bureaucratic elements seek to transform themselves – sometimes successful sometimes not, but nearly always drawing links to imperial­ism and thereby fusing the bureaucratic and comprador elements – can be seen nearly everywhere. Unquestionably, compliant and often corrupt political elites provide the patina of legitimacy for all practical purposes, for the expansion of inequality.


4. In Africa, racial justice must include an anti-imperialist per­spective which acknowledges the legacy of European colonialism and the protracted nature of imperialism which sustains racial subordina­tion. Markedly, South Africa, a semi-peripheral mineral-rich state, did not redistribute wealth and property with the end of political apartheid and the development of a superficially democratic state. Black South Africans, composing over 80 percent of the country’s 65 million popu­lation, remain marginalized through the 1994 accords, which did not include a redistribution of wealth and resources – causing higher levels of poverty and inequality and impeding the working class from improv­ing its living standards.

author: Reem Aljeally
title: Class, Creativity, and Cultural Production in Africa
content:
Artistic freedom and expression has long been shaped and constrained by many factors, including power, economic hierarchies, and class. In Africa, the right to create and distribute art without censorship has always been a contested terrain. Artists’ realities in the African region are directly influenced by both their geographical and societal positions; class plays a big role in how the art world runs. What does society consider as art?  Who gets to buy, collect, or even witness art?  Who has access to exhibition spaces or international residencies? These questions are not abstract; they define the careers of many artists, including my own.


Since 2011, we have seen youth-led movements harness creativity as a tool for political resistance, from the Arab Spring uprisings to #FeesMustFall in South Africa, #EndSARS in Nigeria, and, most recently, Kenya’s Gen Z protests. In Sudan, where I was born and raised, the December Revolution was marked not only by chants in the streets but also by murals, poems, songs, and performances that transformed the cityscape into a living archive of resistance. Yet, even within such moments of collective creativity, class distinctions determined who could participate, whose voices were amplified, and whose remained unheard.


In this article, I reflect on how class shapes artistic and cultural production in Africa: how it has defined access to creativity, how it limits cultural consumption, and what mechanisms – grassroots, digital, and transnational – have begun to narrow these divides. My reflections are grounded in personal experience as an artist and curator working between Khartoum and Cairo, as the founder of The Muse multi-studios and the Sudan Art Archive, and as a participant in regional and international networks of cultural production.


Social hierarchy and access to creativity


In Khartoum, where I first studied architecture before turning to painting and curation, access to art education was already limited to two art schools at the Sudan University for Science and Technology and the newly founded Art programme at the Al-Nileen University. Access to these institutions was competitive, and while not restricted in principle, in practice it was shaped by social status and community expectations. Families in Sudan often encouraged more “practical” fields like engineering, medicine, or architecture – disciplines seen as more secure.


Many young Sudanese who aspired to become artists may have had their educational background shaped by these community views, yet it has not stopped them from pursuing a career in the field upon completing their studies. Those who came from upper-class families had a better chance of accessing educational institutions abroad, while the majority were funnelled into informal workshops or self-taught practices because institutions were either non-existent or insufficiently resourced.


German curator and researcher Larissa-Diana Fuhrmann observes that the development of art education in Sudan has been deeply influenced by colonial legacies. Institutions such as the College of Fine and Applied Arts in Khartoum (originally established under British colonial rule) implemented curricula modelled on Western art academies. These frameworks introduced formalist, Eurocentric paradigms that continue to shape artistic discourse, pedagogy, and aesthetic hierarchies in the postcolonial context.


Access to these institutions, and to international art education more broadly, has historically been mediated by class intersecting with gender and racial categories. During both the late colonial and early post-independence periods, educational and cultural policies enabled a small elite (predominantly from Khartoum’s middle- and upper-class families) to study abroad. Upon their return, these artists occupied influential positions in Sudan’s cultural institutions and helped define national artistic narratives. As Fuhrmann notes, the stratification becomes evident when examining how some of these artists categorize work produced outside formal institutions or urban centres as “folkloric”, thereby reinforcing classed and spatial distinctions in cultural valuation.


This dynamic illustrates the broader relationship between class, cultural capital, and aesthetic authority. Artists with international training and transnational visibility have historically been more likely to receive institutional recognition and access to resources such as galleries, collectors, and …

author: Bhavya Johari
title: The Congo and Rwanda Peace Agreement: The Accountability Clause That Cannot Be Applied
content:
The

peace agreement

 between Congo and Rwanda contains one promise about justice: that no fighter will be taken into the Congolese army until someone has checked whether they committed atrocities. The last time Congo skipped that check, the soldiers it absorbed went on to start the war now being negotiated. The check is not happening this time either.


Two meetings in Geneva, seventeen days apart, show why. On 29 June 2026, Arnauld Akodjenou, who chairs the United Nations commission set up to establish who committed which atrocities in eastern Congo,

told the Human Rights Council

 that his investigators had finished their first mission without reaching Goma, and that United Nations budget constraints had cut into their investigative capacity and their ability to stay in the field. On 16 July, at the United States Mission across the city, officials from Congo and Rwanda

agreed to explore ways

 of verifying that troops were pulling back. Both meetings used the word accountability. Only one is being equipped.


A Peace That Made a War


The fighting escalated in January 2025, when the

March 23 Movement

, an armed group backed by the Rwanda Defence Force,

captured Goma

, the main city in Congo’s east. The response split in two. The Human Rights Council established a commission of inquiry; the United States brought the two governments together and brokered a

peace agreement

, signed on 27 June 2025 and later packaged as the Washington Accords.


That agreement says nothing about prosecutions, victims or reparations. It contains one sentence that attaches any consequence to having committed atrocities. Section 2. iii says that any reintegration of fighters into the Congolese army or police ‘shall be carried out in a rigorous, individualized, and conditional manner, on a case-by-case basis’, on criteria including ‘respect for and absence of serious violations of international humanitarian law’.


That sentence matters because of what came before. On 23 March 2009, Congo signed a

peace agreement

 at Goma with the National Congress for the Defence of the People, an earlier Rwandan-backed rebel group. Article 1.1 folded its fighters into the army and police. Article 12.8 let them keep the ranks they had held as rebels. Article 3.1 promised an amnesty. Nothing in it required anyone to find out what any individual had done. Bosco Ntaganda, publicly

wanted by the International Criminal Court

 since the year before, was

taken into the army and made a general

. In April 2012, several hundred of those soldiers mutinied and named their new movement after the date of the agreement they said had been broken: the March 23 Movement.


The war now being negotiated grew out of an army intake that nobody screened. Section 2. iii reverses every one of the 2009 choices.


Nobody to Do the Checking


Section 2. iii is a vetting clause, and vetting is not a loose word. The United Nations’ own

operational framework

 describes it as a formal process for identifying and removing individuals responsible for abuses, in three stages: registering those to be assessed, screening them against the criteria, and certifying those who pass. Registration is easy and produces a list roughly equivalent to that of 2009. Screening is the hard part: it needs a record that can tell one fighter from another, and that means investigators, witnesses, archives and time.


Nothing in the peace process produces such a record. The only body charged with naming individuals is the

commission of inquiry

 created in February 2025, which the Council told to preserve evidence for future legal proceedings and to identify those responsible. An earlier United Nations mission had already found

reasonable grounds to believe

 that members of the March 23 Movement committed murder, torture, rape and sexual slavery, and that Congolese forces and allied militia committed grave violations too. Those findings name a movement. Screening needs findings that name people.


The commission is in no position to supply them.

Resolution 60/22

 pushed its full report back to early 2027, citing the United Nations’ financial situation. Its first mission

got no further than Kinshasa

, kept out of Goma by insecurity and an Ebola outbreak. The taking in of fighters, meanwhile, is being arranged now. A condition that cannot be assessed is not broken; it is met by default. On the available record, every candidate for the army is someone against whom no finding exists …
