title: Aynur Sarıca: Women must play a founding role in the peace process
content:
Aynur Sarıca of the Jineolojî Academy drew attention to the role women must play in the Peace and Democratic Society Process, saying that pressure and attacks against the women's movement in Kurdistan were continuing.


Sarıca said women must not be confined to following the process or being represented on monitoring commissions, stressing that their participation in decision-making mechanisms was crucial to building a democratic society.


Sarıca said women had played an important role in shaping social life throughout history, but that the nation-state mentality and patriarchal structures continued to attack women's labour, identity and lives. She added that women's historical role had been pushed into the background in dominant narratives.


 


Sarıca said women had often been treated as spoils of war or as instruments for ensuring the continuation of a lineage during periods of war and conflict, but had fought throughout history to defend their existence against such attacks.


She said attacks on women's identity, children, labour and social life had continued through different methods as conflicts intensified in Kurdistan. She added that operations and detentions targeting the women's movement were intended to prevent the struggle for women's freedom from taking root throughout society.


Sarıca said: “Women have asserted their struggle for existence in every period by declaring, ‘We existed, we exist, and we will continue to exist.’ They have carried on this struggle through their identity, labour, way of life and social relationships. In the context of Kurdistan, as conflicts have intensified, we have seen attacks on women's identity, social life, children and labour increase through special warfare methods. The targeting of the women's movement, attempts to undermine its social foundations and attacks driven by a patriarchal mentality were intended to create a barrier preventing the struggle for women's freedom from spreading throughout society.”


‘Women must be active participants in commissions’


Aynur Sarıca said women's role in the Peace and Democratic Society Process needed to be reconsidered, stressing that women could not be confined to positions on monitoring commissions.


Sarıca emphasised that women were founding subjects of a democratic, ethical and political society.


Sarıca said: “The women's struggle and women's freedom are among the fundamental areas around which we organise. Drawing on this paradigm and ideology, we have organised, and continue to organise, around how women's existence, lives and struggles should take shape within society. In the course of a democratic struggle, women cannot simply remain observers or be limited to positions on monitoring commissions. On the contrary, women are the founding subjects of a democratic, ethical and political society. For this reason, we continue to insist that women establish commissions, participate in them and take an active role in decision-making mechanisms.”


Sarıca said commissions composed exclusively of men would lead to social problems being addressed once again through a patriarchal approach. She stressed that women's commissions needed to be considered in their legal, political and social dimensions.


Sarıca continued: “If the commissions to be established consist only of men, society will once again be shaped by codes that impose sexism. This would mean that provisions and laws concerning women, labour, children and society as a whole would once again serve the dominant mentality. This is why we insist and struggle for women to participate in commissions as active decision-makers. We approach this not merely as a legal or political issue, but as a whole, including its dimension of building social life. We do not adopt a fragmented approach; instead, we act on the basis of a comprehensive model of governance and democratic life.”


‘A democratic model of life must be developed as a whole’


Aynur Sarıca argued that addressing social problems in isolation created conditions for massacres, deaths and sexism, stressing the need to build a comprehensive democratic model of life.


Sarıca said women's role in the peace process should also be considered from this perspective and added: “We have seen that fragmented approaches lead to massacres, deaths, sexism and all forms of fascism. The logic of ‘divide and rule’ has prevailed. Our criticism is aimed at presenting an alternative that is the complete opposite of this approach. We …

author: Fareeha Ali Yahya
title: Beyond legislation: What does it take to make child marriage laws work?
content:
13th October 2026


Beyond legislation: What does it take to make child marriage laws work?


8 min read


Policy & Practice


End harmful practices


Global


Every year,

12 million girls are married before the age of 18

. While progress towards ending child marriage remains too slow, legal and policy reforms around the world offer important lessons about what works and how change can happen.


This

International Day of the Girl Child

, we are looking at what it takes to turn legal commitments into meaningful protection for girls.

Setting 18 as the minimum age of marriage without exceptions is critical, but it is only the beginning.


Ending child marriage requires comprehensive laws and policies that prevent marriages from happening, protect girls at risk and support their rights to education, bodily autonomy and a future of their own choosing.


Learning from legal reform around the world


In the United States,

California’s recent ban on child marriage

 offers a timely example of progress, following years of advocacy.


“California’s ban demonstrates that progress is possible, even after years of advocacy. The next step is to build on that momentum. With child marriage still legal in 32 states, we need to learn from reforms that have worked and ensure that strong legal protections reach every child,” says

Anastasia Law

, Equality Now’s Legal Advisor for North America.


Understanding why some reforms succeed, how they are achieved and what makes them effective is essential to strengthening legal protections elsewhere.


Working with the

 UNFPA-UNICEF Global Programme to End Child Marriage

, our legal experts set out to identify good practices from across the globe and examine how these approaches could inform future law and policy reform.


The resulting report,


Towards effective laws: An analytical framework and compendium of good practices on laws and policies to address child marriage

, draws on legal analysis, lived experiences and consultations with experts, practitioners, lawmakers and civil society.


Rather than presenting a single model for countries to replicate, it brings together practical examples that can be adapted to different national contexts, while recognising gaps in implementation and contradictions that may remain.


What can we learn from the research?


The compendium

 examines how countries can move beyond setting a minimum age of marriage to develop comprehensive legal and policy responses. It offers practical learning on:


Why setting 18 as the minimum age of marriage without exceptions must be accompanied by harmonisation

 across related laws and legal frameworks.


How prevention, protection and response measures can be built into child marriage laws and policies

 to address risks before harm occurs and support those already affected.


How accountability mechanisms, clear responsibilities and multi-sectoral coordination

 can support effective implementation.


What meaningful routes to remedies

 can protect and support children already in marriages.


How criminal provisions can be designed and applied

 without unintentionally harming survivors and children.


How legal reform can strengthen access

 to education, sexual and reproductive health and rights and other essential services.


These lessons are particularly relevant for lawmakers, legislative drafters, government ministries, legal practitioners and advocates seeking to strengthen legal protections and ensure they work in practice.


What successful reform processes can teach us


Two recent reforms in Latin America illustrate how the process of changing a law can be just as important as the legal provisions themselves.


A non-punitive, root causes approach helped advance legal reform in Colombia


After 17 years and eight unsuccessful attempts,

Colombia raised the minimum age of marriage to 18 without exceptions in 2024

.


The reform rejected a punitive approach, focusing instead on children’s rights and the root causes of child marriage. Strategic alliances between legislators, government and civil society, alongside public campaigning and efforts to challenge misconceptions, helped build broad support for reform.


The lesson:

 Legal reform can be strengthened by combining strong legal protections with approaches that address the drivers of child marriage and build support across sectors and communities.

author: JoEllen Chernow
title: What If We Organized Survivors of Sexual Violence?
content:
Every few months America discovers another “monster.” A celebrity. A billionaire. A politician. A religious leader. A professor. A CEO.

The details differ, but the story doesn’t: rape survivors risk everything revealing years of abuse, followed by a burst of public outrage and demands for accountability.

Survivors of Jeffrey Epstein told us about a global rape and sex-trafficking network in which young people were abused and exploited by some of the world’s wealthiest and most influential men. For decades, survivors were ignored, disbelieved, and failed by the institutions around them. Newly released files corroborating their horror stories have resulted in zero US criminal arrests and little tangible accountability.

The #MeToo movement was supposed to interrupt this cycle. For a brief moment in 2017, it seemed possible that we could stop treating each “scandal” as an isolated incident and confront the systems connecting them. Instead, less than three months after the hashtag went viral, the press was full of opinion pieces about how it had all “gone too far.” The backlash flipped #MeToo into #NotAllMen. Outrage faded into fatalism, denial, and eventually business as usual.

As a rape survivor, community activist, and labor organizer, I call bullshit.

The problem isn’t that we keep “discovering” abusive men. It’s that we keep refusing to look at the underlying systems that reproduce sexual violence. Instead, we focus on finding, exposing, and punishing the monster du jour (or not) and then wait for the next one.

What we haven’t built is survivor power. Survivors are a constituency with the potential to change the social, political, and material conditions that enable violence and produce abuses of power.

Survivor power is not simply inviting us to the table or ensuring we are represented in leadership. It begins when we invite survivors to bring their full selves. Survivor power is built in the movement by moving from isolation to connection, from private shame to shared analysis, and from shared analysis to collective action. And because sexual violence is enabled by unequal distributions of power, survivor power means changing the basic conditions that make people vulnerable to violence in the first place: economic precarity, workplace exploitation, racism, misogyny, housing insecurity, and isolation.

We use the term power-based violence more than gender-based or sexual violence with survivors. It shifts our focus from seemingly separate forms of harm toward the throughline that links rape and domestic violence to workplace sexual harassment and coercion to the daily intimidation of strangers shouting obscenities and catcalls.

Survivor power is the power to imagine and build what does not yet exist.

More than 90 percent of adult rape victims are women and over 80 percent of survivors under the age of 18 are girls. Of every 100 survivors, 98 of them are raped by men. The vast majority of male survivors are also assaulted by men. Abusers are almost never strangers.

Sexual abuse and harassment aren’t isolated incidents just because they happen behind closed doors (or on private islands). They are expressions of ideology–a structural pattern of male power and control that reproduces itself from the intimate to the institutional and beyond.

Violence–and the ever-present threat of it–shapes where women go, whom they trust, what jobs they take, how they move through public space, and hundreds of other daily micro-calculations about their bodies and lives. Criminalized survivor and Chicago abolitionist organizer Monica Cosby maps out these similarities in the reframing of State Power and Control Wheel tracing how dynamics familiar from domestic violence–coercion, isolation, surveillance, economic control, threats, and violence–are also wielded through institutions and the state.

Yet we continue funding systems designed primarily to (inadequately) respond to violence while dramatically underinvesting in the people and strategies capable of changing the conditions that produce it. In 2026, the Violence Against Women Act and related sexual and gender-based violence programs received roughly $720 million–less than the cost of the White House renovation. Within these limited resources, funding overwhelmingly flows toward what happens after the harm is done.

The state’s narrow mandate to identify, prosecute and remove the “monster” has failed to make us safe. Only a tiny fraction of sexual assaults result in …

author: Unknown
title: Hande Ortaç ile ‘Sus’ üzerine: ‘Yazı benim mücadele alanım’
content:
Yasemin Seven Erangin [email protected]

Hande Ortaç’ın İletişim Yayınlarından çıkan “Sus” romanı, bir polis operasyonuyla başlayan hikayesi üzerinden şiddet, güç ilişkileri, adalet ve suskunlukla yüzleşiyor. Biri şiddeti iktidar kurmanın aracı olarak kullanan, diğeri ise maruz kaldığı sistematik şiddetin ardından öz savunmaya başvuran iki karakterin hikayesini karşı karşıya getiren roman, suçun yalnızca sonucuna değil, onu doğuran koşullara da bakıyor.

Romanın ilk cümlesinden itibaren güçlü bir “av” metaforu kuruyorsunuz: “Bir av partisinin en masumu avın ta kendisi değil midir?” Sus’u yazarken bu metafor sizin için ne ifade ediyordu?

Roman, tüm İstanbul’u etkisi altına alan bir polis operasyonuyla başlıyor. Avcılar kolluk kuvvetini temsil ediyor. Toplum için tehlikeli olduğuna inandırıldığımız bir katili kovalıyorlar. Roman ilerledikçe ortada iki katil olduğunu anlıyoruz. Hikayeler derinleşirken dışarıdaki av devam ediyor ve günün sonunda sadece biri yakalanacak.

Bu metaforda ısrar ediyorum çünkü söylemi kurma ayrıcalığına sahip olanların peşine düştükleri genellikle en güçsüzler oluyor. Güç sahibinin, iktidar yakınının işlediği suçların çoğunlukla cezalandırılmadığını, hatta alkışlandığını görüyoruz. Gerçek suçlu eğer erkten yanaysa avcıların cephesinde yer alıyor. Romanı yazarken bir avın sonunda mutlaka en masumun öldürüldüğünü hep aklımda tuttum.

Sus, suçun kendisinden çok suçu doğuran koşullarla yüzleştiriyor. Sizce adalet her zaman eşitlik demek midir? Bir insanı suça götüren koşullar, o suçun değerlendirilmesinde ne kadar belirleyici olmalı?

Adaletin eşitlikle değil hakkaniyetle daha sıkı bir ilişkisi olduğunu düşünüyorum. Kadın ve erkek benzer koşullarda, şiddet sarmalında büyümüş iki karakter. Fakat biri eril gücü ve şiddeti iktidar kurmanın aracı olarak görüyor, diğeri ise hayatının her aşamasında şiddet mağduru olmasına rağmen şiddeti araçsallaştırmıyor.

İkisi de birini öldürüyor ama eylemlerinin sebepleri arasında dağlar kadar fark var. Sonuç benzer olsa da iki olayı bağlamlarından bağımsız değerlendirmek mümkün değil. Hayat siyah ve beyazdan ibaret değil, aradaki tüm tonlar da vicdan ve akıl muhasebesi için.

Kadın karakteri, kendisine şiddet uygulayan kocasını öldürüyor. Bir kadının hayatta kalma mücadelesi hangi noktada öz savunmaya dönüşür?

“Öz savunma” kavramını indirgemeden verebilmek için olayları bağlamından koparmadan anlatmaya gayret ettim. Ataerkil şiddetin, karşısındakinin cezayı hak ettiğini düşünüp had bildirmeyi kendinde hak gören yaklaşımını deşifre etmeye çalıştım.

Sistematik şiddetin ve tacizin görünmeyen, konuşulmayan taraflarına yer vermek istedim. “Öz savunma”nın tek bir neden-sonuç düzlemine indirgenemeyecek kadar derin psikolojik bağları olduğunu düşünüyorum. Tek bir anı değil, tüm süreci anlatarak bunu görünür kılmak en büyük amacımdı.

Romanda şiddeti evde, iş yerinde, ilişkilerde ve dijital dünyada farklı biçimleriyle gösteriyorsunuz. Bu şiddet biçimleri aynı toplumsal kaynaktan mı besleniyor?

Dezavantajlı kesimlerin ve hassas kimliklerin sınırları hemen her karşılaşmada aşılabiliyor. Bu gruplara kadınlar ve LGBTİ+’nın yanında engellenen bireyler, çocuklar ve hayvanlar da dahil.

Genç bir kadın okulda, otobüste, sosyal medyada ya da iş yerinde tacize uğrayabiliyor. Medeni olduğunu düşündüğünüz sevgilinizden ya da iş için iletişim kurduğunuz birinden bile beklenmedik bir anda sınır ihlaliyle karşılaşmak mümkün. Bu hadsizliklerin, kontrol etme açlığının ve sınır ihlallerinin en büyük sebebinin güç ilişkilerinde olduğuna inanıyorum. Roman boyunca bu kuşatılmışlığı hissettirmeye gayret ettim.

Erkek karakteri üzerinden sosyal medya trollerini ve dijital dünyadaki kadın düşmanlığını da anlatıyorsunuz. Anonimlik şiddeti artırıyor mu?

Sosyal medya, avatarların ardına sığınarak insana sonsuz bir özgürlük ve hesapsız bir varoluş fırsatı sunuyor. Erkeklik de sıkı kurallara tabi. Makbul bir erkek olursan, oyunu kurallarına göre oynarsan ödülünü alacağın söyleniyor.

Erkeklikten pay alma itkisiyle sosyal medyanın sağladığı güvenli alan birleştiğinde şiddet artıyor. Yüz yüze olmamanın verdiği rahatlıkla şiddet kontrolsüz biçimde büyüyor. Romandaki erkek karakter de erkeklik normlarına uymadığı için zorbalanıyor, ardından şiddeti araçsallaştırmayı seçiyor. Sosyal medya onun için gizlenebileceği ve iktidar kurabileceği bir alan haline geliyor.

Romanın parçalı anlatım biçimi en başından beri tasarladığınız bir yöntem miydi?

“Sus” benim için bu dönemin yaralarıyla yüzleşme …

title: Mor Çatı’nın uluslararası konferansında kadın dayanışması öne çıktı
content:
Mor Çatı Kadın Sığınağı Vakfı, İstanbul Beyoğlu’nda “Kadına Yönelik Şiddetle Mücadelede Dayanışma Merkezleri - Uluslararası Deneyimler” başlıklı bir konferans düzenledi.


MA'nın haberine göre, Konferansın “Dayanışma Merkezleri: Kadına Yönelik Şiddetle Mücadelede Nasıl Bir Dönüşüm Yaşanıyor?” başlıklı ilk oturumunda Avrupa Şiddete Karşı Kadınlar Ağı (WAVE) temsilcisi Elena Floriani, Danimarka’daki Danner kadın örgütünden Ditte Specht ve Mor Çatı’dan Leyla Soydiç konuştu. Oturumu Mor Çatı gönüllüsü Elif Ege yönetti.


“Kadın örgütleri değişimin aktörleri”


WAVE temsilcisi Elena Floriani, kadınlara ve kız çocuklarına yönelik şiddetle mücadelede uzman destek hizmetlerinin önemine dikkat çekti. Bu hizmetlerin kadınların ihtiyaçlarını merkeze aldığını ve kendi yaşamlarına ilişkin kararlarını desteklediğini söyledi.


Kadın örgütlerinin tarihsel mücadelesine değinen Floriani, 1970’lerde feminist aktivistlerin ilk kadın sığınaklarını açarak şiddeti siyasi gündeme taşıdığını hatırlattı.


Kadın örgütlerinin yalnızca destek hizmeti sunmadığını, toplumsal değişime de öncülük ettiğini belirten Floriani, şöyle konuştu:


“Kadın örgütlerinin kadına yönelik şiddetle mücadele politikalarının oluşmasında en önemli itici güç olduğunu araştırmalar gösteriyor. Bu nedenle kadınlara yönelik uzman destek hizmetlerini yalnızca hizmet sağlayıcılar olarak değil, değişimin aktörleri olarak ele alıyoruz.”


WAVE’nin bu yıl yayımladığı

Değişimin Aktörleri

 (Agents of Change) başlıklı raporun bulgularını da paylaşan Floriani, kadın örgütlerinin kadınların güçlenmesinden yasal düzenlemelere ve kurumlar arası işbirliğine kadar birçok alanda etkili olduğunu söyledi.


Şiddete maruz bırakılan kadınlara destek vermenin yalnızca sığınakta bir yatak sağlamaktan ibaret olmadığını vurgulayan Floriani, “Kadınlara özgü bir yaklaşımı olmayan genel hizmetler, uzman destek hizmetlerinin yerini alamaz. Kadına ve kız çocuklarına yönelik şiddetle anlamlı bir mücadele için bu hizmetler vazgeçilmezdir” dedi.


Kadın haklarına yönelik tepkilerin, toplumsal cinsiyet karşıtı hareketlerin ve finansman kısıtlamalarının kadın örgütlerinin çalışmalarını zorlaştırdığını belirten Floriani, uzman destek hizmetlerinin korunması ve güçlendirilmesi çağrısı yaptı.


“Sığınaktan ayrılmakla mücadele sona ermiyor”


Danimarka’daki Danner kadın örgütünden Ditte Specht, kadına yönelik şiddetle mücadelede farklı sektörlerin ve meslek gruplarının işbirliği yapması gerektiğini söyledi.


Kadın sığınaklarında sunulan desteğin, kadınların sığınaktan ayrılmasıyla sona ermediğini vurgulayan Specht, şiddetten uzak bir yaşam kurmanın uzun bir süreç olduğunu belirtti.


Specht, “Kadın sığınaktan ayrıldığında da desteğimiz sona ermiyor; şiddetten uzak bir yaşama giden yol sığınaktan çıkmakla tamamlanmıyor. Hatta gerçek mücadelenin o zaman başladığını söyleyebiliriz” diye konuştu.


“Kadınlar kendi hayatlarının uzmanıdır”


Mor Çatı gönüllüsü Leyla Soydiç, şiddetin kadınların yaşamında uzun yıllar süren sosyal, ekonomik ve ruhsal sonuçlar yarattığını belirterek dayanışma merkezlerinin bu süreçte kadınlara eşlik ettiğini söyledi.


Erkek şiddetini yalnızca bireysel sorunlarla açıklamanın patriyarkayı ve güç ilişkilerini görünmez kıldığını ifade eden Soydiç, kadınların kendi yaşamlarına ilişkin kararları kendilerinin alması gerektiğini vurguladı.


“Zehirli ilişki” şiddeti görünmez kılıyor


Konferansın “Dayanışma Merkezlerini Çeşitlilikle Sürdürmek” başlıklı ikinci oturumunda Fransa, İspanya ve İtalya’dan kadın örgütlerinin temsilcileri deneyimlerini paylaştı. Oturumu Mor Çatı gönüllüsü Selime Büyükgöze yönetti.


Fransa Ulusal Kadın Dayanışma Federasyonu (FNSF) İletişim Birimi Sorumlusu Camille Lextray, kadınların maruz bırakıldığı şiddetin resmi istatistiklere bütünüyle yansımadığına dikkat çekti. Federasyonun Fransa genelinde 80’den fazla derneği bir araya getirdiğini belirten Lextray, yardım hatlarına başvuran kadınların ortalama üç farklı şiddet biçimi bildirdiğini, psikolojik şiddetin yüzde 85 ile ilk sırada yer aldığını söyledi.


Fransa’da aile içi şiddetin giderek “zehirli ilişki” olarak tanımlanmasına karşı çıkan Lextray, bu ifadenin şiddet uygulayan kişinin sorumluluğunu ve ilişkideki tahakkümü görünmez kıldığını belirtti.


Lextray, “Resmi istatistikler yaşananların yalnızca bir bölümünü gösteriyor. Biz resmi kayıtlarda görünmeyenleri ortaya çıkarmak istiyoruz” dedi.

author: Victoria Law
title: Mississippi Is in Danger of Executing Woman on Death Row, Despite Key Evidence
content:
Lisa Jo Chamberlin’s co-defendant confessed to coercing her into their crime. Will that be enough to stop her execution?

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Lisa Jo Chamberlin’s life has always been a tangle of drug use, abuse, and extreme violence. Her mother drank and used Sudafed heavily during her pregnancy. As a result, Chamberlin was born with Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder (FASD), a group of medical conditions, including poor reasoning and judgment skills, learning disabilities, and intellectual disability, that occur when a fetus is exposed to alcohol.People with FASD are more vulnerable to manipulation by others. For Chamberlin, that vulnerability led to a death sentence.

The 45 women on death row across the country make up 2 percent of the total number of Americans sentenced to death. The vast majority of women behind bars have experienced abuse before arrest. Ninety-six percent of women on death row had experienced gender-based violence before arrest, 80 percenthave intellectual or psychosocial disabilities, and 90 percent have no prior conviction for a violent felony. Chamberlin checked all of these boxes.

As a child, she suffered constant physical and sexual abuse from her father, her mother, her stepfather, her brother, and even her fourth-grade teacher. Her mother beat her with whatever was on hand, sometimes whipping her with a wooden spoon until it broke. When she was six, her 11-year-old brother put her into a closet with three neighborhood children, instructing them to touch her sexually. He also sexually abused her for years. Chamberlin told her mother, who dismissed her complaints.

When she was 12, Chamberlin began using drugs to numb the constant violence and abuse.

As an adult, her boyfriends used her substance dependency to exert control. They also physically and sexually abused her. Roger Gillett, who would become her co-defendant, strangled her, attempted to drown her, and raped her. He ordered her to move with him from Oregon, where her family lived, first to Kansas and then Mississippi in 2004. That was where Gillett killed two people.

Now 53, Chamberlin is the sole woman on Mississippi’s death row. If her appeals fail, she will be the first woman the state executes since 1944.

“In capital cases, women who have experienced some of the most extreme forms of gender-based violence and oppression are also among those who have received the least support from the legal system, from their communities, from their families, and from society,” Sandra Babcock, founder and director of the Cornell Center on the Death Penalty Worldwide, told Truthout. “There are two dynamics: One is that these women are among the most damaged and vulnerable survivors to become involved in the criminal legal system. But their experiences of violence and trauma go unrecognized by the legal system when they are charged with a capital crime.”

In Mississippi, Chamberlin and Gillett stayed with Gillett’s cousin, Vernon Hulett, and his cousin’s girlfriend, Linda Heintzelman. At first, they all got along. Then, after an auto accident between the two couples, they hatched a plan for Heintzelman to report the accident, collect insurance, and split it with Gillett and Chamberlin.

Heintzelman never filed the insurance claim, leading to tension between the two couples. When their hosts suggested that they move out, Gillett tortured and killed them. He and Chamberlin then placed their bodies into a freezer, loaded it into Heintzelman’s truck, and drove to an abandoned Kansas farm owned by Gillett’s grandfather.

There, police conducted a drug raid, arresting both. They later found the freezer and charged the couple with the deaths of Hulett and Heintzelman.

The pair were tried separately. Both were convicted and sentenced to death.

Chamberlin’s trial was marked by demonizing gender stereotypes. The prosecutor painted her as the mastermind behind the murders. He introduced testimony about Chamberlin’s sex life, including testimony from two jailhouse informants. Jailhouse informants’ testimonies, commonly motivated by law enforcement, are inherently unreliable and have been the leading cause in 46 percent of death row exonerations. Even the Mississippi Supreme Court recognized the problematic nature of relying on jailhouse informants, stating in 1989, “The testimony of jail-house informants, or ‘snitches,’ is becoming an increasing problem in …

content:
Projection du documentaire Le jeu vidéo, une affaire d'hommes

Je ne peux pas m'identifier au protagoniste de ce jeu car c'est une femme et je suis un homme. 

 

» Est‐ce que ce genre de déclaration ne cache pas quelque part des soucis un brin plus profonds

 

?


Le jeu vidéo — comme le cinéma, la

BD

, la littérature… — peut servir de support à des idées politiques de tous bords. Ce court métrage s'attaque plus spécifiquement au sexisme 

 

; mais, de façon plus générale, existe‐t‐il des jeux luttant contre toutes les formes de discrimination, contre le capitalisme, l'État, la religion 

 

? Des jeux vidéo anarchistes 

 

?


Le sexisme dans le milieu du jeu vidéo


Les femmes travaillant dans l'industrie vidéoludique constatent une différence de salaire (25,3 % d'écart au bénéfice des hommes). Certains rejettent les designs de personnages féminins non hyper‐sexualisés. Dans les studios de développement français, les femmes représentent 24 % des effectifs alors qu'elles n'en constituaient que 10,6 % il y a 10 ans. Depuis 2018, nous constatons toujours la même disparité selon les catégories de métier, avec une sous‐représentation des femmes dans les métiers techniques (programmation, data). La question du harcèlement au bureau est également régulièrement soulevée. D'autres formes de sexisme évoquées sont le manque de volonté d'inclure des personnages féminins bien représentés dans les jeux vidéo.


Les jeux qui cherchent à mettre en avant des personnes non hommes peuvent entraîner un harcèlement de leurs scénaristes et développeurs : c'est le cas de Amber Scott, scénariste du jeu Baldur's Gate : Siege of Dragonspear, harcelée en 2016. Elle a en effet inclus un personnage principal féminin et un personnage secondaire transgenre dans le jeu, en plus de se moquer du Gamergate

 [

1

]

 dans une réplique. En réponse à ces actions, elle est la cible d'une campagne de harcèlement et le jeu reçoit des retours négatifs en masse.


En juillet 2021, suite à son harcèlement par un manager, une employée du studio américain de jeux vidéo Activision Blizzard se suicide. Deux mille de ses collègues signent alors une pétition protestant contre des méthodes de management, et organisent un mouvement de grève. De manière plus générale, c'est la «

 

 culture Bro 

 

», culture sexiste répandue dans les milieux de la tech, qui est mise en accusation.


Sur les 152 major games publiés en 2022, 61 % des personnages sont des hommes, 39 % des femmes, et 31,7 % des jeux vidéo mettent en scène des personnages exclusivement masculins. Dans les 50 RPGs les plus joués ces 30 dernières années, les hommes parlent en moyenne 2 fois plus que les femmes.


67 % des françaises jouent aux jeux vidéo, elles ont 39 ans en moyenne et représentent 48 % des personnes qui jouent au moins une fois par semaine. Mais 40 % d'entre elles affirment avoir déjà dû se résoudre à cacher leur genre dans des parties en ligne, 46 % des gameuses jugent les contenus qu'elles voient en ligne trop sexistes ou misogynes, et elles sont aussi 40 % à avoir déjà vécu des situations de harcèlement en ligne.


Il n'y a sans doute pas plus de sexistes dans le jeu vidéo que dans le reste de la société : ce triste constat n'est que le reflet de l'état des lieux en général. Mais, comme dans la littérature ou le cinéma, changer le contenu ne devrait‐il pas participer à changer les mentalités 

 

?


Dimanche 18 octobre 2026 à partir de 16 heures


Entrée libre (accueil dès 15 heures)


Librairie du Monde Libertaire, 145 rue Amelot, Paris 11

]

author: Unknown
title: Childfree – Ein pro-choice Rollenspiel
content:
Childfree ist ein LARP darüber, dass dein Körper nur dir gehört. Darüber, sich zu ermächtigen, lebensverändernde Entscheidungen zu treffen und den eigenen Träumen und Projekten zu folgen. Es ist ein LARP über die Entscheidung, eine Schwangerschaft abzubrechen.


Es ist uns eine große Freude, unsere Ausgabe des Rollenspiels „childfree“ von Axiel Cazeneuve vorstellen zu dürfen. Wir hatten dieses Spiel im Jahr 2023 auf Französisch und Englisch herausgebracht. Zwei Jahre später haben unsere Freund*innen von

LarpPunk

 es ins Polnische übersetzt, und nun hat das autonome Gesundheitskollektiv Geko aus Bern es ins Deutsche übersetzt.


Die Möglichkeit, frei über den eigenen Körper zu verfügen, ist nach wie vor ein umkämpftes Thema – und wird es wahrscheinlich auch bleiben, solange Einzelpersonen, Institutionen oder Nationen sich die Macht über andere anmaßen. Mit dieser Neuauflage möchten wir uns solidarisch mit all jenen zeigen, die für den freien Zugang zu Schwangerschaftsabbrüchen kämpfen, sei es durch den Kampf gegen

Abtreibungsgesetze in Polen

 oder durch die Entwicklung von I

T-Sicherheitstools zum Schutz von Pro-Choice-Aktivist*innen in Brasilien

.


Wie alle unsere anderen Produktionen kann „Childfree“ zum freien Preis bestellt werden, und eine PDF-Version steht auf unserer Website kostenlos zur Verfügung. Um das Spiel in gedruckter Form zu bestellen oder bei der Verbreitung und Übersetzung dieses Spiels mitzuhelfen, kontaktiere uns bitte unter evasions@riseup.net.


Einleitung Von Axiel


„Childfree“ ist ein Live-Action-Rollenspiel – die Teilnehmenden schlüpfen physisch in Rollen, um gemeinsam eine Geschichte zu erzählen, ohne dass ein Publikum anwesend ist – für 5 bis 7 Personen, das in insgesamt vier Stunden gespielt wird. Es befasst sich mit Abtreibung, genauer gesagt mit dem freiwilligen Schwangerschaftsabbruch und bietet den Spielerinnen die Möglichkeit, einerseits die gesellschaftlichen Zwänge im Zusammenhang mit Schwangerschaft oder Abtreibung und andererseits die Individualität der schwangeren Person zu verkörpern. Der flexible und nicht-direktive Rahmen des Spiels ermöglicht es den Spielerinnen, verschiedene Situationen zu entwerfen und vorzuschlagen. Das Geschlecht der schwangeren Person, die Details ihres Lebens, der rechtliche Kontext … all dies bleibt ganz den Spielenden überlassen, die dabei durch die Spielunterlagen unterstützt werden, die so klar und einfach wie möglich gehalten sind. Die Entscheidung, die Schwangerschaft abzubrechen oder fortzusetzen, liegt natürlich ebenfalls bei der schwangeren Rolle (und somit bei der Person, die sie spielt). Indem ich eine Erfahrung biete, die vollständig von den Teilnehmenden gemeinsam gestaltet wird, wollte ich ein wenig von dem weitergeben, was ich durch einen freiwilligen Schwangerschaftsabbruch gelernt habe, sowie das Gefühl der Befreiung, das damit einherging.


Ich habe dieses Spiel 2018 geschrieben: Anlässlich der Veröffentlichung der Ausgabe durch Projet Évasions möchte ich auf meine persönliche Erfahrung zurückblicken und darauf, was mich zum Schreiben motiviert hat.


Ein Spiel mit wunderschönen Illustrationen von Nemo


Erfahrungen mit einer freiwilligen Schwangerschaftsunterbrechung in Frankreich im Jahr 2017


Anfang 2017 blieb meine Periode eine Woche aus. Da das ungewöhnlich war und ich zudem starke Schmerzen im unteren Rücken und in der Brust hatte, ging ich los, um einen Schwangerschaftstest zu kaufen. (Auf dem Weg dorthin machte ich einen Abstecher in den Laden um die Ecke, weil ich Heißhunger auf Fruchtgelee hatte. Als ich die einsame Pappschachtel auf dem Förderband vorbeiziehen sah, fragte ich mich, ob es sich wirklich lohnte, den Test zu machen).


Natürlich war das Testergebnis positiv. Als ich die beiden Striche erscheinen sah, versuchte ich zu weinen. Ähm … Nein, das klappt nicht. Ich versuchte zu lachen. Nein. Also griff ich zum Telefon – es war, glaube ich, ein Montag, gegen Mittag – und rief beim „Planning Familial“ an (ein Netzwerk aus Vereinen und aktivistischen Gruppen, das in Frankreich Dienstleistungen im Bereich der sexuellen Gesundheit anbietet). Folgendes habe ich wörtlich gesagt:


– „Hallo, ich habe mir vor neun Monaten bei Ihnen eine Spirale einsetzen lassen, ich habe gerade einen Schwangerschaftstest gemacht und er ist positiv.


Stille.


– Oh Scheiße. Können Sie in zwanzig Minuten vorbeikommen?“


Ich sprang in mein Auto, das mein Partner fuhr, und innerhalb einer halben Stunde waren wir im Planing-Familial 31 …

author: Unknown
title: There’s probably some weird corner of the internet where “marginalized people need to have…
content:
I really, really don’t think “My turbo-principled position is that because marginalized groups are sometimes maligned as sexual predators, marginalized people need to have solidarity with confessed actual sexual predators!” is a good hill to die on for anybody.

Guys who use their privilege to actually do this stuff don’t need any more people standing up for them. They’ve already got mainstream society making excuses and ensuring that their rights are protected in ways that, say, for example, a trans woman accused of having a bit of a bad vibe could never even dream of.

As a person who’s considered guilty even when proven innocent, you aren’t going to reap any benefits from defending someone who’s already treated like he’s innocent despite being proven guilty.

There’s probably some weird corner of the internet where “marginalized people need to have solidarity with confessed actual sexual predators” is an actual opinion that some people have, but I’ve never really encountered that opinion ever.

What I have encountered far far more is

Because this marginalized group is so often maligned as sexual predators, they will sometimes be convicted as sexual predators, therefore our solidarity should include convicted sexual predators, as some are innocent and we can’t tell which ones they are.

Because this marginalized group is so often a victim of abuse and abuse is often cyclical, some will complete the cycle of abuse and will become abusers. Therefor our compassion should include people who have committed abuse because only with support can we break the cycle of abuse.

We should stand in solidarity with all incarcerated people, no matter how terrible their wrongdoings, because prison abolition and transformative justice for all is the only path to a truly free and just society.

And other variations of that, which then get twisted as “so you think we should have solidarity with confessed actual sexual predators?”, when like, that was not the point.

title: ExisTransInter 2026
content:
Appel de l'

interorga de l'ExisTransInter

 pour l'édition 2026 : rendez-vous vendredi 16 octobre à 19h devant Gare de l'Est à Paris


L'autodétermination au pouvoir


Vendredi 16 octobre à 19h à gare de l'Est

, l'ExisTransInter réunira

les personnes intersexes, les personnes trans, et leurs allié·es

. Notre histoire commune est faite d'entraide et de transmission, de lutte et de résistance, de victoires arrachées. En 2016, nous réclamions déjà le changement d'état civil libre et gratuit, le libre choix des parcours médicaux, l'arrêt des mutilations des enfants intersexes, la reconnaissance de droit pour les personnes migrantes et les travailleur·euses du sexe (

TDS

). Dix ans plus tard, et en l'absence affligeante d'avancées majeures sur ces sujets, notre détermination reste intacte et sans concession. Nous ne voulons plus d'une société où l'accès au droit, au soin, au logement, dépendent de notre conformité aux normes cis et dyadiques –- pas plus que de notre classe sociale, de notre pratique du

TDS

, de nos origines, de notre validité ou de nos titres de séjour.


Dans un contexte politique particulièrement menaçant, nous refusons plus que jamais la réduction de nos vies à des controverses médiatiques, à des paniques morales, à des cases administratives. Nous refusons d'être les boucs émissaires de cel·leux qui alimentent la peur et la haine des minorités.

Nos luttes sont antifascistes, anti-impérialistes, anti-coloniales

. Elle sont, en cela, indissociables de celles des peuples palestinien, congolais, soudanais et iranien.


Enfant·es ou adultes, nos corps nous appartiennent


Nos luttes sont indissociables des luttes féministes et enfantistes

. En ce sens, nous défendons l'autonomie corporelle de tous·tes les enfant·es, dont les droits fondamentaux ne commencent pas à la majorité. De la naissance à l'adolescence, les jeunes sont des personnes, et doivent être écouté·es avant tout.


Tout en prétendant protéger les enfants, les mouvements réactionnaires internationaux continuent les mutilations des enfant·es intersexes, dont le corps doit être “normalisé”. L'extrême-droite et ses lobbies alimentent ainsi un continuum de violences (familiales, sociales, physiques, sexuelles) qui doit absolument cesser. Ils privent les enfant·es trans de soin, violentent les enfants racisé·es, invisibilisent cel·leux qui, en ce moment même, meurent sous des génocides.


Peu importent les rapports, les promesses et les demi-mesures partisanes : les mutilations des enfants inters doivent cesser, et leurs droits doivent être protégés avant 2027. Nous soutenons, en cela, les

propositions de loi n° 1914 et n° 2286

. Un rassemblement pour le droit des personnes inters aura lieu

le 7 novembre à 15h, place Stravinsky

.


La Haute Autorité de Santé (

HAS

) a entamé, en 2026, l'élaboration de recommandations spécifiques sur l'accompagnement des mineur·es trans, dont la publication est prévue pour 2027. Nous condamnons fermement l'exclusion des associations d'auto-support, aux côtés des mineur·es trans et inters depuis des années, de ce processus. Nos savoirs expérientiels doivent être au centre de ces travaux, et le lobbying réactionnaire n'a rien à faire dans un travail scientifique.


Les personnes transinters existent

 

!


Les personnes intersexes représentent environ 13 000 naissances par an. Leurs corps sont en dehors de la binarité des sexes, mais on les assigne malgré tout à un sexe et à un genre à la naissance. Un récent rapport européen montre que 6

3% des personnes inters se déclarent sur le spectre trans/non-binaire

, donc en dehors du genre qui leur a été assigné à la naissance. La panique morale exercée par les réactionnaires à l'encontre des mouvements trans, qui “mutileraient des enfant·es” est hypocrite : ce sont el·leux qui mutilent les enfant·es inters. Les enfant·es transinters subissent ainsi une

double transition forcée

, dans leur chair et dans leur genre. Le rapport indique aussi que

44% des personnes inters estiment avoir subi une thérapie de conversion en France

. Ainsi, pour nombre d'entre nous, le parcours de transition, choisi à l'âge adulte, représente une forme de réparation de nos corps.


Le sexe, tout autant que le genre, est une construction sociale qui, factuellement, n'a rien de binaire. Un des piliers de la transphobie est la haine envers les personnes sortant de la binarité des sexes, d'où l'animosité féroce des réactionnaires, à international, envers la non-binarité. Nous …

author: TGEU
title: TGEU publishes Know Your Rights: How EU Directives Protect Trans People. Second Revised Version
content:
This guide provides a basic overview of EU directives in which trans people are protected from discrimination, including through the explicit inclusion of the grounds of ‘gender reassignment’, ‘gender identity’, or ‘gender expression’. As such, it helps trans people to better understand and claim their fundamental rights. It also helps legal professionals, equality bodies, and policymakers to understand their legal obligations to ensure equal protection. 


Get the guide


What are EU directives?


EU directives are a type of EU law that sets goals Member States must reach through their own legislation. However, EU directives do not prescribe how Member States should implement them. In other words, EU directives set a common minimum standard but leave Member States flexibility in how they achieve it.


All EU directives must be ‘transposed’, a process that incorporates an EU directive into national legislation. Once a directive is adopted, transposition begins, and the directive itself sets a deadline for completion.


Objective of the guide


Since TGEU published our first Know Your Rights guide in 2015, additional EU directives have been adopted and are entering into force. These newer directives, which extend protections for trans people across a broader range of areas, form the focus of this guide.


What does this guide cover?


Equality Bodies Directives: Standards on the mandate, independence, resources, tasks, and powers of Equality Bodies to prevent discrimination, promote equality, assist victims of discrimination, and promote equal treatment (Directive (EU) 2024/1500 and Directive (EU) 2024/1499)


Pay Transparency Directive: The principle of equal pay for equal work or work of equal value between men and women. Employers must be transparent about pay, and workers can enforce their rights if they are paid unequally (Directive (EU) 2023/970)


Directive on combating violence against women and domestic violence Directive (EU) 2024/1385)


Get the guide


Your support makes change possible


We work across Europe and Central Asia to advance trans rights, build strong communities, and drive change through research, advocacy, and community-building.


Your donation helps us continue this vital work — defending trans lives, amplifying trans voices, and advocating for justice every day.

author: anred
title: Histórico: Buenos Aires será la sede del 40° Encuentro Plurinacional en 2027
content:
Tras cuatro décadas de recorrido federal y de manera ininterrumpida, el máximo evento de los feminismos y las disidencias regresa al territorio donde nació en 1986. La elección se realizó mediante el tradicional «aplausómetro» durante el cierre de la edición número 39 en Córdoba.

Por ANRed

 


CÓRDOBA — En una jornada cargada de mística, debate y organización colectiva, la Comisión Organizadora del 39° Encuentro Plurinacional de Mujeres, Lesbianas, Travestis, Trans, Bisexuales, Intersexuales y No Binaries anunció que la Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires albergará la próxima edición del evento en 2027. La decisión se tomó a través del histórico sistema de «aplausómetro», el mecanismo asambleario y masivo con el que este espacio federal define democráticamente sus destinos año tras año. Tras la elección de la sede, se procedió a la lectura de las conclusiones de los más de 100 talleres que funcionaron durante el fin de semana.


Este regreso a las callee porteñas tiene una profunda carga simbólica y política. La última vez que el Encuentro se realizó en Buenos Aires fue en su edición fundacional de 1986. En aquel momento, apenas unas 600 mujeres provenientes de diferentes provincias y de diversas comunidades de pueblos originarios se congregaron para sembrar la semilla de una experiencia asamblearia y colectiva que terminaría transformando por completo la historia de los feminismos en la Argentina.


Cuarenta años después de aquella primera convocatoria, el espacio se ha masificado, transformado y complejizado. Con la única y lógica excepción del parate obligado por la pandemia de COVID-19, los Encuentros se sostuvieron de forma ininterrumpida durante cuatro décadas. Su persistencia en el tiempo consolida un formato único en el mundo: un espacio completamente autónomo de los gobiernos y los partidos, federal, plural, autofinanciado y autoconvocado que sirve como usina de organización, debate y posterior lucha en las calles.


De cara al próximo año, el desafío se traslada al centro político del país. En un contexto que demanda la articulación constante frente a las violencias y opresiones, el 40° Encuentro Plurinacional abrirá un nuevo capítulo en Buenos Aires con el objetivo de seguir reconociendo diversidades, compartiendo experiencias desde los territorios y fortaleciendo el tejido social hacia una comunidad más justa e igualitaria.


Todo en pleno año electoral, en el marco de una profunda crisis política social y cultural, en el gobierno de la Libertad Avanza. «Vamos a Buenos Aires a sacar a Milei, contra todos los fascismos. Seremos Nostres quienes les pongamos un freno a estas politicas de precarización de nuestras vidas» cerro una encuentrera.

author: Laura Guido
title: Mormon Church Donates $1 Million to Fight Idaho Abortion Rights Ballot Measure
content:
The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints is one of several religious institutions taking a stance on the initiative.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints has donated $1 million to an Idaho political action committee, or PAC, opposing the abortion rights initiative on the ballot this November.

The donation went to the Too Extreme for Idaho Political Action Committee, which opposes the initiative.

“While The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints remains neutral toward political candidates, it actively addresses ballot initiatives it believes carry significant moral consequences,” the church said in a statement. “Accordingly, the Church has joined a coalition of like-minded organizations and individuals in Idaho to dedicate resources toward defeating Proposition 1.”

If passed, the voter initiative would repeal Idaho’s abortion laws, enumerate rights related to reproductive health, and create liability protections for healthcare providers who provide abortion and other reproductive healthcare.

The Idaho Falls radio station NewsTalk 107.9 first reported the donation on Thursday. The Idaho Capital Sun confirmed the donation with a spokesperson for the church on Friday.

The large donation comes after Idaho Attorney General Raúl Labrador published an opinion in August that says churches are allowed to donate money to political campaigns — including for and against Proposition 1 — without disclosing their donors, as long as they don’t ask members to donate specifically for the campaign, Boise State Public Radio reported.

Leaders from the church, widely known as the Mormon church, issued a letter against Prop 1 in September, the Salt Lake Tribune reported. The letter was read to congregations last month, the church’s assistant communications director Brian Whitlock said in an email.

“Our long-held stance on abortion remains clear and unchanged,” the four-member U.S. Central Area Presidency of the LDS Church wrote in the letter.

The church, which opposes elective abortions, posted its stance on abortion online. It allows for possible exemptions in cases of rape and incest, if a “competent physician determines that the life or health of the mother is in serious jeopardy,” or a “competent physician determines that the fetus has severe defects that will not allow the baby to survive beyond birth.”

“Even these exceptions do not automatically justify abortion,” the statement said. “Abortion is a most serious matter. It should be considered only after the persons responsible have received confirmation through prayer.”

Idaho’s abortion ban allows the procedure to prevent the death of the mother and in cases of rape and incest in the first trimester with a police report. Doctors who provide abortions outside of those exemptions face felony penalties, including minimum prison time, and potential civil lawsuits brought by family members of the aborted fetus.

The LDS Church isn’t the first or only faith-based organization to contribute to the campaigns related to the ballot measure, but it is the largest reported donation from a church-affiliated group.

Groups attached to Catholic organizations have contributed $7,161 to the Too Extreme for Idaho PAC, campaign finance reporting shows. The Roman Catholic Diocese of Boise contributed $2,000, and Catholic fraternal groups, called Knights of Columbus Councils, contributed the rest, the Idaho Capital Sun previously reported.

The Catholic Diocese of Boise could not be reached for comment for this story after multiple emails and phone calls. The diocese has publicly opposed the initiative.

Bishop Peter Christensen in late July posted a statement in opposition to the ballot measure and encouraged other members of the church to voice their opposition.

“I strongly encourage you to vote NO this November. Our response must not be rooted in anger or fear, but in steadfast faith, charity, and an unwavering commitment to the truth about human life,” Christensen wrote.

He said the diocese will be encouraging parishes to offer “pro-life themed Masses” and pastors to communicate “awareness raising information in bulletins and parish communications provided by the Diocese.”

title: Terror das feministas: radicais, deputadas conservadoras disputam poder na extrema direita
content:
Investigamos o que importa para os brasileiros além do que passa na campanha eleitoral. Leia mais reportagens como essa clicando

aqui

O terror das feministas. É como se autointitulam Ana Caroline Campagnolo e Eduarda Campopiano, as deputadas estaduais mais votadas em Santa Catarina e São Paulo. Ambas do Partido Liberal (PL), elas se apresentam como amigas em posts nas redes sociais e se dizem admiradoras  de Olavo de Carvalho. Juntas, as duas somaram mais de 2,3 milhões de votos na eleição de 2026. Ao lado delas, ocupando o posto de deputada estadual mais votada do Estado, está Índia Armelau, também do PL, que conquistou 248.504 votos para a Assembleia Legislativa do Rio de Janeiro. 


São

mulheres que se unem ao clã de Michelle Bolsonaro (PL-DF), Damares Alves (Republicanos-DF), Bia Kicis (PL-DF) e Celina Leão (PP-DF) pela pauta anti-identitária e antiaborto

, mas que, segundo especialistas ouvidas pela

Agência Pública

, não pertencem ao mesmo grupo de suas antecessoras, inclusive considerando a construção de narrativas para o eleitorado. 


Na visão de Lívia Reis, coordenadora de Religião e Política no Instituto de Estudos da Religião (ISER), a extrema-direita conquistou uma pluralidade de candidaturas femininas nesta eleição, o que pode criar uma disputa pelo poder de influência entre as próprias eleitas. 


“O Valdemar [Costa Neto, presidente do PL] não está preocupado com o alinhamento ideológico de uma influenciadora, ele quer que ela seja eleita e vote com ele”, argumenta a antropóloga em referência a eleição de Eduarda Campopiano, atualmente com mais de 2,5 milhões de seguidores do Instagram.

 “Vejo que talvez isso seja também um dos atritos que a própria Michelle vai ter com ele, porque ela quer centralizar o PL Mulheres

 e as candidaturas femininas, mas o próprio PL vai apostar em quem quiser”, explica Reis. 


Vereadora de Praia Grande, no litoral paulista, Eduarda Campopiano foi eleita para a Assembleia Legislativa de São Paulo como uma espécie de discípula de Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG), deputado federal mais votado da história do país, com mais de 22 milhões de seguidores no Instagram. Outro aliado é o vereador paulistano Lucas Pavanato (PL), que detém mais de 5 milhões de seguidores na rede social da Meta e foi eleito para deputado federal com mais de 3 milhões de votos. 


“O PL sabe o poder das redes sociais. Todas as candidaturas se forjam ali, eles estão elegendo influenciadores há muito tempo e agora chegaram ao ápice dos candidatos mais votados serem os influenciadores. Por isso, eu diria que a Eduarda chega [ao partido] com tanto poder quanto a Michelle. E vai disputar isso”, explica Reis. 


A esposa do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, preso por tentativa de golpe de Estado, protagonizou em junho deste ano o seu primeiro embate público com o Partido. Após a rejeição da sigla ao nome indicado por ela ao Senado pelo Ceará, o da deputada Priscila Costa (PL-CE), Michelle publicou um vídeo contando que Flávio Bolsonaro a havia desrespeitado durante a formação dos arranjos partidários nos estados. “Ele disse que seria melhor eu ficar fora das decisões do partido. Disse que eu havia chegado ontem e não entendia nada de política”, afirmou a ex-primeira dama.


No vídeo, ela exaltou sua atuação à frente do PL Mulher, ala de mulheres conservadoras do partido: “[em 2024] elegemos 45,8% mais mulheres que em 2020. Foram 1.005 mulheres eleitas”, disse. Com a instauração da crise, que abalou a campanha à presidência de Flávio Bolsonaro, e após se reunir com Costa Neto, Michelle anunciou sua saída da presidência do PL Mulher. 


Na visão de parlamentares próximos ao PL, Campopiano representa um discurso mais radical da extrema-direita, capitaneado por Olavo de Carvalho

, conhecido como o “guru” do bolsonarismo. “Eu acho que ela [Eduarda] vem muito daquela linha do Olavo de Carvalho, que é essa juventude conservadora formada. Mas creio que com a maturidade ela vai entender que a pauta feminina não é uma pauta feminista. A gente vai ter ainda um tempo para fazer esse convencimento”, disse à

Pública

 a senadora Damares Alves, que também afirmou que irá dialogar nesse sentido com a deputada Índia Armelau.

author: Karen Gullo
title: Turkish Crackdown On LGBTQ+ Organizations Threatens Freedom of Expression and Association
content:
EFF strongly condemns Turkey’s state-led discriminatory, oppressive attacks on feminist and LGBTQ+ organisations, media platforms, student groups, and rights defenders and activists within the country.

Since mid-September, access to the websites and social media accounts of a dozen organizations have been blocked by court order, while over 60 members and activists have been detained, their offices and homes raided, mobile phones, laptops and other digital devices seized, and judicial proceedings launched against them.

These actions threaten the very existence of the LGBTQ+ organizations targeted, limiting their ability to carry out legitimate human rights work, deterring participation and support, and chilling the free speech rights of not just these groups, but any organization that even reports on LGBTQ+ oppression.

A little over a week ago, an Istanbul court shut down the website and social media accounts of T24, Turkey’s longest running independent digital news organization—which has covered government-backed campaigns against and earlier crackdowns on gay rights groups—alleging it had aired “LGBT propaganda” over the past year.

It’s all part of Turkey’s efforts to portray LGBTQ+ groups and support networks for those living with HIV as criminal organizations that must be suppressed, purportedly to protect family values. Homosexuality is not illegal in Turkey (unlike Uganda, Nigeria, and Egypt, where it is criminalized), but LGBTQ+ organizations and activists have in recent years faced increased government oppression, including criminal proceedings on allegations related to obscenity and violations of Turkey’s Law on Associations, which regulates the activities of nonprofits.

In its new crackdown, the government is targeting LGBTQ+ groups’ websites and social media channels for alleged obscene posts accessible to children. Kaos GL, Turkey’s oldest gay rights organization, said investigations are being led by the Cyber Crimes Bureau of the Ankara Chief Public Prosecutor’s Office, which took members of its Board of Directors into custody, raided their homes, and searched the organization’s offices, where electronic devices were seized.

According to Human Rights Watch, prosecutors in Istanbul said those targeted were suspected of “founding, leading, or being a member of a criminal organization,” as well as sex work and drug-related offenses. Publicly available law enforcement and judicial documents about the investigation reportedly don’t say which publications or posts are alleged to be obscene.

The prosecutor’s office launched an investigation of the organization and others under Article 226 of the Turkish Penal Code, which regulates the offense of “obscenity” (without clearly defining it), while the overall operation, dubbed “My Family is Safe” and launched as part of President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan’s “Decade of the Family” program, is being brought under Article 220 of the code. Justifying the crackdown by invoking family values and child safety suggests that the government is trying to enforce a moral code on society based on intolerance of and discrimination against LGBTQ+ people.

Framing the activities of LGBTQ+ rights organizations as violations of organized crime provisions is a new low for Turkey, where free speech and press freedoms have long been under attack. The implication from these raids and investigations is that the organizations’ legitimate civil society work advocating for the rights of queer people—monitoring human rights violations, offering legal aid, running news portals, sponsoring cultural events such as symposiums and film screenings, publishing an online magazine and supporting LGBTQ+ refugees—is suspected of being criminal threatens the basic human rights of the LGBTQ+ community in Turkey.

These actions send a dangerous message to people and organizations exercising freedom of speech and association in support of queer people. Under the penal code, directing a criminal organization is punishable by five to ten years in prison, while merely being a member carries a sentence of two to five years.

EFF joins hundreds of human, civil, LGBTQ+, and digital rights organizations around the world in calling for the immediate release of all those detained for exercising their rights to freedom of expression, association and legitimate human rights work, and the unblocking of all websites and social media accounts of affected organizations.

author: Hamilton Nolan
title: We Infiltrated a Police Union Convention in Las Vegas
content:
The gruff man at the microphone on the stage in the front of the meeting room in the Paris casino in Las Vegas was complaining about Las Vegas. How it’s hot. How it’s expensive. And how, having come here hoping for a thriving and successful convention, his organization now found itself thwarted by a straitjacket of absurd institutional rules.

“You can’t even move a box from left to right without contacting someone to do that,” he grumbled.

Could you blame him for being peevish? There were only about 50 people in the room. Not really an attendance to brag about. It was 109 degrees outside on this late August day. The big water bottles in the rooms’ minibars went for $15 each. And these convention contracts with big Vegas resorts did, in fact, come with lots of rules—no doubt due to the fact that every single property on the Vegas strip is fully unionized. These unions, with their crazy regulations and sky high prices! It was enough to drive any convention planner mad.

The weird thing was: we were at a union convention.

Technically, at least. This was the 23rd Annual Convention of the International Union of Police Associations (IUPA), which represents tens of thousands of cops in local departments from coast to coast. Though not the largest police union in America, IUPA has the distinction of being the only police union that is a member of the AFL-CIO. It joined the labor federation in 1979, making it a formal but uncomfortable partner to every progressive labor union that has ever had its striking workers arrested by cops who may well have been IUPA members. You wouldn’t know it from the subdued convention crowd, but that half-empty Concord Ballroom at the Paris Casino—down the hall from the X Rocks Sexy Topless Revue, past the fake Eiffel Tower and the Dominique Ansel restaurant, past the Monte Cristo cigar bar where middle aged men sipped whisky served by young cocktail waitresses trying to conceal their revulsion, surrounded by rich burgundy carpets, flanked by fake oil portraits of Louis XV and Marie Antoinette—was effectively the epicenter of the ongoing, seething debate over what the proper relationship of the labor movement and the police should be.

That grouchy, plainspoken man on stage, with white hair and a thin goatee, was Sam Cabral, who has been IUPA’s president for more than 30 years. Cabral sets the right wing edge of the AFL-CIO’s unions. In 2014, when racial justice protests wracked Ferguson, Missouri following the killing of Michael Brown by police, the AFL-CIO’s then-president, Richard Trumka, joined calls for police reform and an end to police militarization. Cabral responded with a letter saying that police “are not the cause of the problems facing the black communities in America.

“They are not responsible for the single parent families, the unemployment, the school dropout rate or its attendant unacceptable literacy rate among black youth. They are not responsible for the gangs, black on black crime or the infant mortality rate,” his letter said. He also wrote that “we have not ever seen racism or systematic exclusion of minorities” in police department staffing.

When IUPA endorsed Donald Trump’s reelection bid five years later, Cabral was still miffed. “Every top Democrat currently running for this office has vilified the police and made criminals out to be victims. They seem to take any union’s support for granted,” he wrote. “Many of them still refer to the tragedy in Ferguson as a murder, despite the conclusions of every investigative inquiry to the contrary.”

In 2020, as Black Lives Matter protests swept the nation following the killing of George Floyd, Cabral played his role once again. Parts of the labor movement (including my own union, the Writers Guild, East) renewed their push for the AFL-CIO to disaffiliate from IUPA, on the grounds that police unions have interests that are irreconcilable with their alleged comrades in other unions. The AFL-CIO defended IUPA’s membership, saying in a statement that “We believe the best way to use our influence on the issue of police brutality is to engage our police affiliates rather than isolate them.” Yet the federation’s support for police reform in general was too much for Cabral, who sent another furious letter to Trumka, saying that criticizing police over what happened to George Floyd was “reprehensible” and an act of “profiling.”

People are always like “rice and beans and vegetables are super healthy” but then decide that burritos are unhealthy. Did the rice and beans and vegetables become bad when I wrapped them up. Do they think tortillas cause cancer. What’s happening here.

Oh, it’s racism, actually. Usually is, but definitely is in this scenario.

Racism with just a dash of protestant ‘if it’s hard work to prepare and unsatisfying to eat, it’s good for you. If it’s easy and you enjoy it and feel satisfied, it’s bad for you’ mixed in there.

Guys… its because 99.9% of burritos made in the US are made by a fast food joint or meant for bachelors to heat up while drunk.

I’m willing to bet lots of people make burritos at home, because that’s a cheap, easy and delicious way to use leftover veggies.

Bachelors can eat healthy or unhealthy foods while drunk. Heating up food instead of preparing it does not make it unhealthy.

Location, demographic and convenience are all cultural markers that we associate with 'unhealthy food’, not actual unhealthy ingredients. So you’re kind of proving the point here.

It’s because they’re Mexican.

Everything in a burrito and everything in a subway sandwich is entirely interchangeable other than the carb around it. But one is made by a white Italian and one by a brown Mexican.

Have you seen all those clean eating diet fads? Notice how they never feature any spices or ethnic ingredients?

Have you noticed that every non-white food family is regularly accused of causing diarrhea? Mexican, Chinese Indian, Vietnamese, Arab.

During Covid everyone immediately jumped to making jokes about bat soup. Those haven’t stopped, even though by now we know enough about Covid to know better.

beginning

actually

author: Amy Goodman
title: Nobel Peace Prize Awarded to Jurist Who Led UN Inquiry Into Genocide in Gaza
content:
South African human rights lawyer Navanethem “Navi” Pillay began her career defending anti-apartheid activists.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

The 2026 Nobel Peace Prize has been awarded to Navanethem “Navi” Pillay, the South African jurist who led the United Nations commission of inquiry that concluded that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza. Pillay’s long career in international human rights law includes work as a defense attorney for anti-apartheid activists, president of the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, a former judge at the International Criminal Court and the U.N.’s high commissioner for human rights from 2008 to 2014.

“Everybody in the human rights movement reveres Navi Pillay,” says war crimes prosecutor Reed Brody, who calls the award “a stinging rebuke to Donald Trump.” Brody, a member of the United Nations Group of Human Rights Experts on Nicaragua, also comments on the Trump administration’s decision to deport a Nicaraguan opposition activist, Jeffrey Jarquín, from the United States, where he was in the process of seeking asylum. Upon his return to Nicaragua, Jarquín was immediately imprisoned at the same facility in which he was once tortured.

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org, The War and Peace Report. I’m Amy Goodman, with Juan González.

The Norwegian Nobel Committee has announced the winner of the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize. This is the chair of the Nobel Committee speaking in Oslo this morning.

JØRGEN WATNE FRYDNES: The Nobel Peace Prize for 2026 goes to a person who, with exceptional courage and integrity, has led the way towards a more comprehensive global legal order. This year’s laureate has been instrumental in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide are prosecuted. The Norwegian Nobel Committee has decided to award the Nobel Peace Prize for 2026 to Navanethem “Navi” Pillay for her efforts to promote peace and international law.

AMY GOODMAN: The South African human rights lawyer and international jurist Navi Pillay has been the United Nations high commissioner for human rights and a judge at both the International Criminal Court and at an international tribunal investigating the 1994 genocide in Rwanda. Most recently, she led the U.N. Independent International Commission of Inquiry that concluded that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza.

Navi Pillay is now 85 years old. She was born into an Indian Tamil family in apartheid South Africa. The first woman to start a law practice in Natal, South Africa, in 1967, she began her legal career defending anti-apartheid activists, including Nelson Mandela, exposing torture and helping establish key rights for prisoners on Robben Island. The Nobel Committee also praised her work in South Africa.

JØRGEN WATNE FRYDNES: A common thread runs from her early work, defending Nelson Mandela and others who stood up against apartheid, to her service as a judge in some of the key international court cases of our time.

AMY GOODMAN: Navi Pillay was in Nuremberg, Germany, at an annual conference of human rights lawyers and judges when she got the news this morning.

NAVI PILLAY: Thank you very much. Thank you very much. If you clap a little bit more, I may share this prize with Trump. … The last thing I did is the delivery of the report on Gaza naming what’s happening there as genocide.

AMY GOODMAN: Meanwhile, Israel’s Foreign Ministry took to X to denounce the awarding of the Nobel Peace Prize to Navi Pillay, calling it a, quote, “grotesque weaponization of an award to legitimize anti-Israel hatred and prejudice,” unquote.

This is Navi Pillay speaking to Reuters last year about her genocide findings as the chair of the U.N. Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territories.

author: Marcelo Oliveira
title: Mulheres são maioria das vítimas de violência política, mesmo sendo minoria das candidatas
content:
O primeiro turno da campanha eleitoral de 2026 durou 50 dias e registrou 134 episódios de violência política contra candidatos e candidatas, além de agentes políticos.

Um aumento de 11% em relação aos 121 casos registrados no mesmo período da eleição municipal de 2022.


Os 134 episódios representam um caso de violência política a cada nove horas de campanha.

 E apesar das mulheres serem apenas 35% do total de candidatos, elas foram a maioria (52%) das vítimas do primeiro turno, segundo o levantamento.


Os dados integram a 4ª edição da pesquisa Violência Política e Eleitoral no Brasil, realizada pelas organizações de direitos humanos Terra de Direitos e Justiça Global, que pesquisa o tema desde 2016. O levantamento foi divulgado nesta quarta, dia 7 de outubro.


A porcentagem de

vítimas mulheres aumenta

 mais ainda quando a pesquisa separa apenas os casos envolvendo candidatas e candidatos. Dos 134 episódios de violência política durante o primeiro turno, 102 foram dirigidos a pessoas que disputavam o pleito. Desse total, 60 eram mulheres, quase 59% do total.


Para a coordenadora do Setor de Incidência da Terra de Direitos, Gisele Barbieri, “os dados trazem importantes achados para identificar os ambientes em que agentes políticos estão mais vulneráveis e pensar medidas de proteção. Quando eleitas, essas pessoas passam a ser vítimas de violências nos seus locais de atuação, seja no Parlamento ou no Executivo”, afirma.


Machismo e misoginia se misturam nos casos de violência política


A pesquisa mostra que a violência política é marcada pela discriminação de gênero e raça.

Quando se considera o universo completo de 70 casos de violência política contra mulheres, 45 casos envolveram machismo ou misoginia, nove envolveram racismo e cinco envolveram transfobia. Mulheres pretas foram vítimas de 25% dos casos de violência política medidos nesse primeiro turno.


A ameaça foi o tipo de violência política mais recorrente no período, com 64 casos registrados. Na sequência, aparecem 33 episódios de ofensa e 19 de agressão física. Também foram registrados 11 atentados, cinco casos de criminalização e dois assassinatos.


Mais da metade dos casos (71 ocorrências) aconteceu nas ruas, durante atividades públicas de campanha. O ambiente virtual concentrou 31,3% dos episódios.


Além disso, apenas candidatas sofreram ameaças de violência sexual. Em todos os sete casos, as vítimas eram mulheres.


“Enquanto os homens são atacados por sua atuação política, mulheres, pessoas negras e pessoas trans enfrentam também o racismo, o machismo e a transfobia que estruturam a sociedade brasileira”, afirmou em nota Glaucia Marinho, diretora-executiva da Justiça Global.


Policiais e outros agentes públicos foram a maioria dos autores


Em quase 20% dos casos o autor identificado da violência política era um agente público, incluindo parlamentares e forças de segurança.

Até o encerramento da coleta de dados pelas organizações autoras da pesquisa, nenhum dos 134 episódios havia resultado em alguma punição efetiva, limitando-se a medidas cautelares de urgência determinadas pela Justiça Eleitoral.


A região Nordeste liderou o número de casos (48), seguido pelo Sudeste (38). Entre os estados, São Paulo lidera com 16 casos, seguido por Rio Grande do Norte (13), Minas Gerais (12) e Rio Grande do Sul (10).


A presença de policiais entre os autores de violência política já havia sido detectada também em

levantamento

 realizado pela

Agência Pública

 durante o primeiro turno.

title: Los sepultureros de Gaza de Norman Finkelstein es una obra maestra
content:
Hay hechos sin consecuencias, libros sin seguimiento. ¿Qué haremos de esta monumental investigación y razonamiento que apela a nuestra conciencia y debería impulsarnos a la acción? Lo que está en juego es la esencia misma de la existencia civilizada, los valores de la Declaración Universal de los Derechos Humanos, los propósitos y principios de las Naciones Unidas. El genocidio en Gaza no es solo otro Holocausto monstruoso, es un espectáculo público.

[1]

 El fracaso de las Naciones Unidas para detenerlo y la inacción de la mayoría de los estadounidenses y europeos nos hacen a todos cómplices del crimen, porque

qui tacet consentire videtur

. Si solo somos

voyeurs

de esta masacre en curso, tenemos, como mínimo, responsabilidad moral. Por Alfred de Zayas 


En los últimos 30 años, Norman Finkelstein nos ha brindado muchos libros brillantes, entre ellos

Método y locura, Acuso, Saber demasiado,

Gaza

,

Más allá de la desfachatez

y

La industria del Holocausto.


Este libro de más de 400 páginas documenta el colapso civilizatorio de las clases dominantes en Occidente, la traición a todos los valores humanistas, el rechazo demasiado público por parte de Israel del derecho internacional y la moral, con la complicidad,

entre otros

, de Estados Unidos, Reino Unido, Francia, Alemania y la Unión Europea.


Todo esto se ve acompañado por la cacofonía de los medios de comunicación convencionales orwellianos, que difunden noticias falsas, historia falsa y leyes falsas, especialmente con respecto a los palestinos como pueblo, a quienes se les representa erróneamente como “terroristas”, cuando poseen el derecho, reconocido en el derecho internacional, a resistir la colonización y la ocupación.

[2]


Nelson Mandela también fue tildado de «terrorista», pero fue fundamental en la lucha por la liberación de su pueblo. Hoy todos reconocen que el fin del apartheid en Sudáfrica era algo que debió haberse hecho hace mucho tiempo. ¿Cuándo veremos el fin del apartheid en Israel y los Territorios Ocupados? Esto es lo que Jimmy Carter exigió en su libro

Palestina: Paz, no apartheid

.

[3]


Los políticos occidentales y los principales medios de comunicación han invertido los papeles y han culpado a la víctima de su desgracia. Israel es el terrorista que practica el terrorismo de Estado y coloca trampas explosivas en los buscapersonas, como demostró de forma obscena el primer ministro israelí Benjamin Netanyahu durante su diatriba en la Asamblea General de la ONU el 24 de septiembre de 2026.

[4]


Israel nació del terrorismo

[5]

 contra británicos y palestinos, ha sido un Estado agresor desde su creación, en un sentido muy real un

Estado fallido

, porque no ha aprendido a vivir en paz con sus vecinos.


Israel ha atacado Líbano, Siria, Irak, Irán, Egipto, etc. En una infame operación de falsa bandera, incluso atacó el buque de inteligencia de la Armada de los Estados Unidos USS

Liberty

[6]

 en junio de 1967, matando a 34 marineros estadounidenses, en un intento fallido de involucrar a los Estados Unidos en la guerra de agresión de Israel.


Israel ha sido un estado paria desde su creación en 1948, e incluso antes.


El genocidio de Gaza no es más que una continuación de la intención criminal de establecer un «Gran Israel» anacrónico e imperialista en medio del mundo árabe y musulmán.


[Fuente:

cartooningforpeace.org

]


Sin duda, los gobiernos de Israel, Estados Unidos y la UE están moralmente en bancarrota.

[7]


Lamentablemente, la

percepción

de la realidad es más determinante que la realidad misma. Dado que nuestras acciones están condicionadas por la información de la que disponemos, nuestro juicio se ve influenciado —e incluso subvertido— por las narrativas odiosas que recibimos de los principales medios de comunicación, y nuestras opiniones se distorsionan por el incesante discurso de odio y la propaganda contra los palestinos. Esto constituye una incitación al odio y a la violencia, en contravención del artículo 20 del Pacto Internacional de Derechos Civiles y Políticos.

[8]


Los principales medios de comunicación difunden la versión israelí y suprimen las opiniones disidentes. No solo nos mienten, sino que nos privan de información crucial que cambia radicalmente la situación.


El público es manipulado, pero muchos se dejan manipular. Como escribió Julio César en

De Bello Civili (II, 27, 2): «quae volumus, ea credimus libenter»

(Creemos lo que queremos creer). O peor aún, como decían los romanos …
