Part One: The Bolshevik Counterrevolution

Lenin: Butcher of the Working Class

Timeline: A Revolution Derailed

The USSR: Force for Global Counterrevolution, Accomplice of Fascism

The Relevance of the Communist Counterrevolution

Part Two: Restless Specters of the Anarchist Dead

Golos Truda, The Voice of Labor

Since the mid-19th century, anarchists have maintained that the key to liberation is not to seize the state but to abolish it. From Paris to St. Petersburg, from Barcelona to Beijing, one generation of revolutionaries after another has had to learn this lesson the hard way. Shuffling politicians in and out of power changes nothing. What matters are the instruments of rule — the police, the military, the courts, the prison system, the bureaucracy. Whether it is a king, a dictator, or a Congress that directs these instruments, the experience on the receiving end remains roughly the same.

This explains why the outcome of the Egyptian revolution of 2011–2013 was not all that different from the outcome of the Russian Revolution of 1917–1921 or the French Revolution of 1848–1851. In each case, as soon as the people who made the revolution stopped attempting to carry out social change directly and shifted to investing their hopes in political representatives, power consolidated in the hands of a new autocracy. Whether the new tyrants hailed from the military, the aristocracy, or the underclass, whether they promised to restore order or to incarnate the power of the proletariat, the end result was roughly the same.

Government itself is a class relation. You can’t abolish class society without abolishing the asymmetry between ruler and ruled . The first condition for any government is that it must achieve a monopoly on coercive force. In struggling to achieve this monopoly, fascist despotisms, communist dictatorships, and liberal democracies come to resemble each other. And in order to achieve it, even the most ostensibly radical party must ultimately collude with other power players. This explains why the Bolsheviks employed tsarist officers and counterinsurgency methods, why they repeatedly took the side of the petite bourgeoisie against anarchists, first in Russia and later in Spain and elsewhere. History gives the lie to the old alibi that Bolshevik repression was necessary to abolish capitalism. The problem with Bolshevism was not that it used brutal force to push through a revolutionary agenda, but that it used brutal force to crush it.

It’s not particularly popular to acknowledge any of this today, when the flag of the Soviet Union has become a dim, receding screen onto which people can project whatever they wish. A generation that grew up after the fall of the Soviet Union has renewed the pipe dream that the state could solve all our problems if the right people were in charge. title: TEV-DEM condemns racist provocation in Hesekê
content:
Following a demonstration featuring anti-Kurdish demands in Hesekê, the Democratic Society Movement (TEV-DEM) warned against attempts to fuel ethnic tensions in the multi-ethnic city. At Friday’s rally in the predominantly Arab neighborhood of Xiwêran (Ghweiran), around 200 people called, among other things, for Kurds to be removed from institutions in Hesekê province.


During the demonstration, in which a particularly large number of children and young people participated, slogans were also chanted against Kurdish national symbols and flags. Kurdish flags were also reportedly burned following Friday prayers. In a statement on Sunday, TEV-DEM described the action as a racist provocation by a limited group and explicitly rejected attempts to portray it as reflecting the views or demands of the Arab population.


“Limited to a particular group”


According to TEV-DEM, the slogans voiced during the demonstration were aimed at inciting racism against the Kurdish population and other sections of society. The position expressed there was limited to a particular group, TEV-DEM stated. “Some of the rhetoric directly targeted the legitimate national and political rights of the Kurds. At the same time, rhetoric was used that fueled social discord and thereby served the enemies of Syria.”


TEV-DEM emphasized that the anti-Kurdish demands must not be attributed to the Arab population of Hesekê. The movement also rejected attempts to portray the provocation as an ethnic conflict between Kurds and Arabs.


Call for an investigation into the incidents


TEV-DEM called on the relevant authorities to launch a transparent and responsible investigation into the incidents, demanding that those who spread hatred and racist incitement be held accountable. At the same time, the movement warned against allowing Hesekê province to become a scene of ethnic conflict.


TEV-DEM said that Kurds, Arabs, Syriacs and other communities should not allow hate speech to turn them against one another but should instead remain committed to dialogue and peaceful coexistence.

author: Sonali Kolhatkar
title: An Abolitionist Vision for the World We Want
content:
A recent New York Times editorial by Tim Wu, a former antitrust adviser for the Biden administration, caught my eye for the criticism it leveled at Democrats for making affordability a central issue ahead of the midterm elections. Wu contends that the party needs to go further and focus not merely on the high price tags of necessities, but on the unfairness of the entire economic system.

While this is a refreshing shift in the right direction, it doesn’t go nearly far enough. It’s true that a majority of Americans across the political spectrum believe our economy is rigged in favor of the rich. But merely pointing out the obvious is unlikely to attract a huge shift in voting toward the Democratic Party.

Moreover, Wu says nothing about the racist rage that has defined President Donald Trump and the Republican Party’s decimation of our democracy, about the devastation to communities of color, immigrants, women, LGBTQ+ people, and other marginalized members of our society. Nor does he acknowledge the corporate harms that Democrats failed to tackle when they were in power and are now being accelerated under Republicans: fossil fuel emissions, tech domination, and AI, harms that disproportionately impactpoor people and people of color.

To Wu and most Democratic Party consultants, these issues are distinct and, depending on the cultural tides, are either worth tackling or anathema.

In fact, they are intimately linked. White supremacy feeds capitalism by distracting poor whites from billionaire-fueled inequality and climate devastation using immigrants and people of color as scapegoats. To take on an unfair economy without addressing the systematically racist impacts of policing, immigration, corporate oligarchy, and the climate crisis does us all a disservice. Moreover, there is an absence of a radical vision for tackling economic and racial justice risks to prevent repeating the same crises in the future.

Democratic Party leaders are falling deeply short by offering little more than undoing Trump’s worst excesses. It is a conservative position to seek a return to the “good old days,” when a predatory capitalist system was overseen by articulate, sensible-sounding statesmen who didn’t embarrass the nation on the global stage, who championed police and prisons as tools of safety, who echoed Trump’s rhetoric on “border security,” who preserved corporate profiteering in healthcare, who embraced endless war as long as it was their party’s doing, and so on.

The Democratic Party is essentially a modern-day conservative party, while Republicans are the extremist, fascist party.

No wonder Americans in general dislike both major parties at roughly the same rate. And while the Democrats’ chances of taking control of Congress appear to be surging ahead of the midterm elections, it is likely because the pendulum is swinging away from Republicans, rather than towardDemocrats and their milquetoast agenda.

So, what can Democrats do to ensure victory?

Frankly, it is not our job as voters—or for that matter, the job of newspaper editorialists—to offer advice to political parties.

Our job as voters, especially in this moment, is to seize power in a system that has rendered us powerless and articulate our demands loudly and clearly. Politicians win our votes by acceding to our agenda. Not the other way around.

Therefore, the far more important question is, what do we, the voters, want?

If we agree that the economic system is rigged against the majority of Americans, then how do we unrig it? Is it as basic as “a promise to level out a lopsided economy,” as Wu advises, while ignoring other issues? Is it as simple as a rallying cry to “tax the rich,” as some Democratic-leaning states are doing?

If we want to end the wild pendulum swings of American politics, which are veering us further into the abyss of authoritarianism with each election, we need a complete reset on all fronts, not merely a return to a more balanced economy.

We require, I would argue, an “abolitionist mindset.”

Black abolitionists, who are better versed than the rest of us on what it’s like to be on the receiving end of systemic harms, have long articulated a vision for a better world where we all can thrive: a world where we reverse the equations of how our collective wealth is spent and where we refuse to let our needs be continually defunded.

Black abolitionists like Angela Davis, Ruth Wilson Gilmore, Mariame Kaba, and Andrea J. Ritchie have already shown …

author: Harriet Williamson
title: Anti-Migrant, Anti-Muslim Extremists Drive UK Terror Threat Level Increase
content:
Anti-migrant and anti-Muslim extremists are becoming increasingly likely to attempt terrorist attacks against mosques and asylum seeker accommodation, Britain’s spy chief has warned.


MI5 director general Sir Ken McCallum said cases where anti-immigration and anti-Muslim views had tipped into “terrorist intent” were the “most marked trend” of the past year. 


In comments made as part of

his annual threat update

delivered on Tuesday, McCallum also said the recent upgrade of the UK terrorism level to “severe” (which means an attack is highly likely) was “driven in significant part by extreme rightwing terrorism”. 


The MI5 boss noted the case of a teenager who

planned to set fire to Inverclyde Muslim Centre

 in a racially-motivated terror attack, and described the demographics most likely to be drawn into extreme rightwing terrorism as skewing young and “driven by the internet”.


One mosque in Britain is

attacked every five days

, according to data released in July by the British Muslim Trust, the government’s partner for monitoring anti-Muslim hatred. It had tracked and verified 78 attacks and incidents at Muslim places of worship in the last year. 


The UK has seen a spate of protests and violent disorder outside hotels and addresses  believed to house asylum seekers since the Southport riots in the summer of 2024. 


August saw

attacks on addresses believed to house asylum seekers

 in Thetford, Norfolk, with a senior police officer

 telling the i Paper

 that such disorder is becoming harder to predict due to a “growing narrative” that all asylum seekers are a threat.


Last month,

anti-migrant protesters targeted

 the Marriott in Portsmouth, believing migrants were inside. In reality, a visiting Pakistani cricket team was staying at the hotel. 


McCallum’s wide-ranging speech on threats to UK national security included a warning about the risks posed by AI’s potential to produce new bioweapons, along with individually tailored propaganda and radicalising material. 


He named Russia as “aggressor number one” and the most serious foreign state threat to UK security.

title: Migrationspakt und GEAS: Neuer Anlauf in der EU-Flüchtlingspolitik (???)
content:
Dossier

Beitrag von Phillipp Saure vom 19. Juni 2020 im Migazin


, siehe dazu nachfolgend:


GEAS-Verschärfungswelle der EU: Rückführungsverordnung mit Return-Hubs in Afrika, Abschiebungen ohne Asylverfahren und bald die Aussetzung des Rechts auf Asyl?


[GEAS-Verschärfungswelle der EU] 38 Organisationen fordern: Bundesregierung muss im Europäischen Rat die Aussetzung des Asylrechts in der EU verhindern


„

Vor der Tagung des Europäischen Rats am 15. und 16. Oktober warnen 38 Organisationen, darunter PRO ASYL eindringlich davor, das Recht auf Asyl in bestimmten Situationen auszusetzen. Gemeinsam appellieren sie an die Bundesregierung, den diskutierten Vorschlägen entschieden entgegenzutreten und auf europäischer Ebene für den Schutz des individuellen Asylrechts einzustehen: „Eine von der EU genehmigte Aussetzung des Asylrechts wäre ein folgenschwerer Bruch mit den europäischen Grundrechten.“

Erstmals wird der Europäische Rat über Ideen diskutieren, wonach das Asylrecht vorübergehend ausgesetzt werden kann, wenn zum Beispiel sehr viele Menschen auf einmal an einer Grenze ankommen und vermutet wird, dass ihre Ankunft von einem Drittstaat instrumentalisiert werden könnte. Das würde bedeuten: Schutzsuchende könnten an europäischen Grenzen zurückgewiesen werden, ohne dass überhaupt geprüft wird, ob ihnen Verfolgung, Krieg, Folter oder andere schwere Menschenrechtsverletzungen drohen

…“ gemeinsame

Pressemitteilung vom 14.10.2026 bei Pro Asyl

 


Weniger Asylsuchende, noch weniger Schutz: GEAS verschärft den Trend

Die Zahl der Asylerstanträge ist im ersten Halbjahr 2026 erneut gesunken, während die Schutzquote weiterhin erschreckend niedrig ist. Das reformierte GEAS verstärkt diese Tendenz, wie erste Zahlen zeigen. PRO ASYL befürchtet einen Einbruch der Schutzquote. Denn mehr beschleunigte Verfahren bedeuten auch: mehr Menschen, die durch das Raster fallen

…“

Meldung vom 02.10.2026 von Pro Asyl

 


Ein Fundament, auf das gebaut werden soll: Der Migrationspakt ist erst wenige Monate alt, doch die EU-Innenminister wollen es noch verschärfen. Sogar über die Aussetzung des Asylrechts wird nachgedacht


„Den ganzen Tag hatten die EU-Innenminister am Donnerstag in Luxemburg beraten, am Abend trat EU-Innenkommissar Magnus Brunner mit Jubelmeldungen vor die Presse. Es gebe ein „Rekordtief“ bei den Asylanträgen in Europa, die Zahl der irregulären Grenzübertritte sei in den vergangenen zwei Jahren um 55 Prozent gesunken, verkündete er strahlend. (…) „Das ist eine wirkliche Veränderung, die zeigt: Unsere Reformen funktionieren“, sagte der aus Österreich stammende Brunner. Mit den Reformen meinte er das von ihm „Pakt“ genannte EU-Asylsystem Geas, das nach neunjährigen Verhandlungen am 12. Juni in Kraft getreten war. Aus Innenministersicht also alles in Ordnung? Von wegen. Der Pakt sei natürlich nur das „Fundament“, meinte Brunner. Und mit einem Fundament „hört man nicht auf, man baut darauf“. Und deshalb standen bei der Innenministerrunde gleich drei neue Reformen auf der Tagesordnung, mit denen die EU-Grenzen noch stärker geschützt werden sollen. Zum einen nahm die Runde die neue EU-Rückführungsverordnung formal an. Dieses neue Abschiebegesetz gibt unter anderem den Behörden weite Spielräume für Razzien in Privatwohnungen und anderen „relevanten Räumlichkeiten“ bei der Suche nach Ausreisepflichtigen. Abschiebehaft ist für mehr als 24 Monate möglich. Vor allem aber ermöglicht sie den EU-Staaten, nach eigenem Ermessen Abschiebezentren in Drittstaaten einzurichten. In die sollen Ausreisepflichtige gebracht werden können, wenn die EU sie nicht in ihre eigenen Länder abschieben kann. (…) …

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Trump’s Mass Deportation Push May Cut Retirees’ Social Security By $2k Annually
content:
The program’s insolvency date was already pushed up to 2032, partly as a result of mass deportations.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

The average retiree will soon see average cuts of over $2,000 to their annual Social Security benefits if the Trump administration’s mass deportation campaign is continued, according to a new report on the widespread economic consequences of the president’s inhumane agenda.

By 2034, retirees’ benefits may be cut by 8.6 percent, or an average of $2,152 per year, as a result of the loss of tax revenue caused by the deportation campaign. This would be a massive cut for retirees, who on average receive $25,000 a year from Social Security, which is the U.S.’s top anti-poverty program. The projected insolvency date for the program was already pushed up a year, to 2032, by the program’s trustees earlier this year, due in part to President Donald Trump’s anti-immigrant policies.

These findings were included in a report by Economic Insights and Research Consulting released by immigrant advocacy group America’s Voice and first reported by The Guardian.

This cut would compound existing poverty concerns for the elderly amid impacts on industries that rely heavily on immigrant labor. Costs for goods like groceries and housing — and services like elderly care — are rising as a result of the mass deportation policies, according to the report; immigrant labor makes up roughly 48 percent of agricultural occupations and 32 percent of construction jobs, the report finds.

The Trump administration has repeatedly claimed that their deportation agenda serves U.S.-born workers by deporting foreign-born workers and freeing up their job posts. In reality, on top of the massive harms to immigrant workers — including the deportations of tens of thousands of children — the deportation campaign is set to wreak havoc on the U.S. economy, which could lead to hundreds of thousands of job cuts for U.S.-born workers as well.

The report references a study on the effects of the deportation policies between January and September of 2025, which found that 668,000 jobs were lost in that time, with between 51,000 and 297,000 jobs lost by U.S.-born workers.

Meanwhile, even as Congress neglects to pass legislation to stave off Social Security insolvency, they have helped to balloon ICE’s budget, which is now larger than that of every other federal law enforcement agency combined. Previous research has found that federal officials have spent or have committed $269 billion to the mass deportation agenda through 2029, costing roughly $2,358 per taxpayer.

Social Security solvency issues seem to be of little concern to the Trump administration. Last week, Trump expressed a desire to privatize the program, saying that he “wanted to do it so badly” during his first term. Experts have warned against such an idea, saying that similar attempts in the past to privatize Social Security-like programs in other countries have led to major cuts to benefits.

author: Joel Mukisa
title: Jumuiya’s Arts Censorship and Resistance in East Africa
content:
Introduction | Coordinated Jumuiya transnational repression 


In the recent past, our Jumuiya’s democracy scales have been trembling with the impunity of human rights abuses and a worrying trend of

transnational repression

. One incident that chilled the conscience of all freedom-loving East Africans was the

brazen abduction

 of Ugandan opposition politician, Kizza Besigye, on 16 November 2024 in Kenya by unidentified assailants who bundled him into a vehicle together with FDC (Forum for Democratic Change) member Haji Obeid Lutale, and drove him across the border to Uganda without any formal extradition process. After suffering the ordeal of being held in incommunicado detention, Besigye was arraigned before the General Court Martial and charged with offences relating to security and the unlawful possession of firearms and ammunition, which could attract the death penalty. In July of the same year, 36 other members of the FDC party had been

arrested in Kisumu, Kenya,

 and forcibly deported to Uganda where they were charged with terrorism despite having lawfully entered Kenya with the necessary immigration permissions. 


The Boniface Mwangi and Agather Atuhaire Torture and Deportation


Six months after the kidnapping of Kizza Besigye from Kenya,

Boniface Mwangi and Agather Atuhaire

, who are prominent Kenyan and Ugandan human rights activists respectively, were abducted in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, while expressing solidarity with opposition leader Tundu Lissu. There is a thread of consistency in the way all these major East African nations (mis)treat their opposition politicians and Activists. Like Besigye, Tundu Lissu faces treason charges ahead of contentious elections in Tanzania. Agather and Boniface not only endured days of incommunicado detention just like Besigye, but also reported suffering

severe sexual torture

, including rape and beatings by Tanzanian security forces. 


Since the cross-border snatch-and-transfer operation happened almost a year ago, Besigye and his counterpart Haji Obeid have not received due process contrary to the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights. Similarly, the enforced disappearances and ill-treatment of Agather and Boniface breached the human rights protocols of the East African Community and the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, to which all three countries are signatories.


There is a complex historical origin of artistic censorship in Africa, partly stemming from colonial policy. The post-independence African states did not shake off the institutional legacy of colonialism, including the suppression of critical artistic expression.  Through the use of draconian laws, censorship boards, and internet restrictions, more East African countries have registered excesses against the freedom of artists. 


Across the region, from the early 2000s to the mid-2010s, there was a fusion of different forms of art, from graffiti and mural paintings to subversive visuals and performances by creative artists who defied authoritarianism. 


Art Meets Gen Z Maandamano


 In April 2025, the

Kenyan police fired tear gas

 to disperse the audience that had gathered to watch Kenya’s national high-school drama competition. This followed the staging of a play,

Echoes of War,

 by Butere Girls High School. Kenyan authorities could not stomach a play, produced by students, set in a fictional kingdom where the youth have lost faith in their leaders. The play’s author, Cleophas Malala, was also briefly detained by police. 


Additionally, Kenya published the 

Statute Law (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill 2020

 in June 2020, with proposed amendments to the

 

Film and Stage Plays Act 1962 (Cap 222)

. The intention behind this move is to increase the reach and grasp of the 

Kenya Films and Classification Board (KFCB)

 to bolster its capacity for censorship of artistic works deemed critical of the regime. The following month in the same year, Tanzania passed a new law, the 

Electronic and Postal Communications Act (EPOCA), on Online Content Regulations 2020

, to tighten state restrictions on freedom of expression under the pretext of “morality” and national security. What the foregoing laws do is impose criminal prosecutions against grassroots satirists and online artists, further curbing dissent.

political participation

 and democratic expression in the recent #GenZ protests in Kenya, when young people …

title: Global day of action vs IMF-WB
content:
Photo courtesy of Asia Pacific Forum on Women Law and Development

We are really delegitimizing the IMF-WB.

BANGKOK – The People’s Global Campaign (PGC) against the International Monetary Fund and World Bank (IMF-WB) marked October 12 as the Global Day of Action against the two Bretton Woods institutions.

The Bretton Woods Institutions or the IMF-WB are financial institutions established in 1944 at a conference in Bretton Woods, New Hampshire in the United States. The goal was to establish a stable international economic system after the devastation of World War II. The IMF and World Bank have been criticized for imposing loan conditions that push governments to adopt liberalization policies, including deregulation and privatization.

In a press conference on October 12, representatives from the women, indigenous peoples, migrant workers as well as leaders in local organizations in Thailand spoke how the IMF-WB destroyed people’s lives through neoliberal policies implemented around the world.

“Today marks the start of the Annual Meetings of the IMF-WB, and for the next several days, behind closed doors, they will be deliberating on the next major neoliberal scheme as the world economy plummets into further crisis and the people slip into further destitution,” said Donna Denina, spokesperson from the PGC.

The press conference was also joined by the Thai People’s Movement (TPM) against IMF-WB.

October 12 was the first day of the Annual Meeting of the IMF-WB which ends on October 18. Thailand is the host of the said event which will be attended by more than 15,000 participants from 191 countries, including central bank governors, economic policy makers and business leaders to discuss the world economy.

Denina said that the Global Day of Action protests also happened in different parts of the world, including the Philippines.

In its 80 years of existence, the IMF-WB plundered land, exploited the people and destroyed the environment, said Emily during the press conference.

“Since 1970, the number of migrants has continued to surge. In 2026, the number of migrants reached 304 million or 3.7% of the world’s population. Meanwhile, the number of refugees reached 117.8 million. This number will continue to rise alongside the plundering of natural resources and repression,” said Emily of International Migrants Alliance (IMA).

She lamented how governments have failed to address the root cause of migration and have only complied with the IMF-WB’s labor migration and labor export policies. “In this scenario, migrants become the new commodity for export,” Emily said.

Now with the aging population in the developed countries, Emily stressed that more migrant workers would be further exploited. “Under the slogan ‘migration for development,’ the World Bank frames labor migration as a way to address labor shortages in developed countries caused by aging populations so the business will not lose profit. To generate super profits, migrants are exploited to an even greater extent and treated like modern-day slaves.”

She said that migrant workers are often granted fewer rights and they enjoy less protection than local workers. They also face discriminatory and degrading conditions, including extremely low wages, restricted residency rights, quota systems, and the denial of other labor rights. They would tend to be isolated through “live-in” arrangements, requiring them to live in their employers’ homes or on company or plantation premises.

“Restrictions on their freedom to settle, move, or change jobs further limit their autonomy. They are also stigmatized, prevented from organizing or speaking out, and made scapegoats during crises, as seen during the 2008 global financial crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020,” she said.

Indigenous People leader Celestine AkpoBari represented the Ogoni people of Nigeria and the International Indigenous Peoples Movement for Self-Determination and Liberation (IPMSDL) said that Indigenous People are the primary caretakers of the world’s last frontiers “and are more often than not sidelined in the political and economic conversations of our countries.”

“We have every reason to join the resounding call of the peoples of the world: ‘Shut down the IMF and the World Bank!’ Indigenous Peoples are among those most affected by these traps, loan conditionalities, and other forms of deceit,” he said. “Our lands, forests, and waters are first to be targeted for plunder, while we face displacement …

author: Kodao Productions
title: Migrant leader urges evacuation plan for OFWs in Riyadh
content:
A veteran migrant leader called on the Ferdinand Marcos Jr. government to immediately craft an evacuation plan for overseas Filipino workers (OFW) caught in the escalating war between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis of Yemen.


Migrante International chairperson emeritus Garry Martinez said the Philippine government must ensure that all the needs of the victims—as well as those of their families in the Philippines—are fully met.


Martinez issued the demand after the Houthis hit King Khalid International Airport with missiles since Friday, killing 12 and injuring at least 300 passengers and airport staff, including four Filipinos.


Three of the Filipinos sustained serious injuries requiring intensive hospital care, various media reports said.


“We urge Marcos to make public the evacuation blueprint in the event that the situation in the Middle East escalates,” Martinez said.


The leader said a comprehensive plan by the government is needed as the situation shows no sign of de-escalation.


“The government should stop thinking of potential remittance loss in this situation. The lives of OFWs are most important,” he said.


Philippine carriers suspend flights to Saudi


Meanwhile, Philippine Airlines (PAL) has extended its cancellation of flights between Manila and Riyadh until November 29, the country’s flag carrier announced on Monday, citing the “evolving security situation at Riyadh’s airport.”


PAL first canceled flights PR654 and PR655 last week. “(We) continue to closely monitor developments and assess conditions affecting the safe operation of its flights. Further updates will be provided as necessary,” PAL noted.


Josh Vasquez, PAL Middle East regional head, said Monday that flights from Manila to Dubai and Doha are operating as scheduled.


Budget airline Cebu Pacific (CEB) also extended flight suspensions between Manila and Riyadh as King Khalid International Airport announced operation stoppages until October 17.


“As this is a developing situation, some flight changes may take place in the next few days. We encourage passengers to regularly check their flight status and to update their contact details via the manage booking portal to receive timely flight notifications. We will continue to assess our Middle East flight operations and provide updates as necessary,” CEB added. #

(Raymund B. Villanueva)

author: By Camilla Donzelli, Contributor
title: Greek Trials Turn Migrants Into ‘Smugglers’ and Minors Into Adults
content:
Crete, Greece — Crete’s courts are convicting shipwrecked people on the move as “smugglers” in trials lasting minutes, with lawyers documenting minors registered as adults and sentences reaching hundreds of years.


Eleftheria Iatraki lets her gaze wander along the walls of the room as she tells the story of Thalassa of Solidarity. The shelves are crowded with books, sewing machines, toys, and other objects. “We created this place as a space to meet each other through learning activities — sewing classes, language classes, computer classes,” she explains. She wears a black T-shirt reading “no one is illegal,” her elbows resting on the table that fills the small room where the collective carries out its activities.


Eleftheria Iatraki speaks with Unicorn Riot in the space where Thalassa of Solidarity holds its activities. Photo contributed by Romanos Lioutas.


Through the glass door facing the street, the white facades of the buildings in central Heraklion, Crete’s regional capital, are visible.


Thalassa of Solidarity was founded in 2019 by local activists as an independent, self-funded space. Even then, Crete was a secondary destination for people on the move and refugees who had arrived in Greece

through Turkey

, but there were no real spaces where local residents and communities on the move could meet each other. “The idea was to create situations where people could communicate with one another and identify common problems and struggles,” continues Eleftheria — a name that, fittingly, means “freedom” in Greek.


The collective has always provided social and legal support too, helping people navigate an often labyrinthine bureaucratic system. Consequently, as the migration route that has progressively made Crete Greece’s

main entry point

 since

2023

 became established, Thalassa of Solidarity expanded its scope of work.


The entrance to the Thalassa of Solidarity collective’s headquarters in central Heraklion, Crete. Photo contributed by Romanos Lioutas.


Faced with the

lack of adequate reception facilities

 on the island and authorities’ often repressive handling of arrivals, the collective began monitoring the informal centers where people are effectively detained upon landing. This work has brought into focus increasingly troubling mechanisms of criminalization.


“From the moment they arrive, people are isolated and all contact with the outside world is blocked,” Eleftheria says. “Everything is under the control of the police and the Coast Guard. Human needs, basic rights, and asylum requests are all completely subordinated to one absolute priority: finding the boat drivers, and charging them as smugglers.”


Eleftheria Iatraki, Michalis Markodimitrakis, and two other activists from the Thalassa of Solidarity collective speak with Unicorn Riot. Photo contributed by Romanos Lioutas.


Activists from the collective Steki Metanaston, who are monitoring the situation in Chania, a city in the western part of the island, confirm this pattern. They describe how the search for boat drivers takes place during the custody phase at Agya, a former exhibition center used as a first-reception site.


“The very first step is the confiscation of cell phones,” they explain. “After that comes the so-called preliminary investigation, which consists of interrogations almost always conducted without interpreters and with extremely rough methods of communication.”


In this context, stripped of legal safeguards, police ultimately make an arbitrary designation: anyone who so much as touched the tiller or held a map is labeled a “smuggler,” with no verification of whether they drove the boat under threat or simply in an attempt to bring the group to safety — a charge that, once filed, can carry sentences of years or even decades in Greek courts.

People on the move who landed in Crete are transferred by the authorities to camps on mainland Greece for checks and registration in October 2025. On the ferry, they are cordoned off by police. Photo contributed by Romanos Lioutas.


People on the move are transferred by the authorities from Crete to camps on mainland Greece in October 2025. On the ferry, they are surrounded by police and wear identification wristbands. Photo contributed by Romanos Lioutas.

author: labor4pal
title: CUNY for Palestine Demands Accountability and Action on Palestine from Mayor Zohran Mamdani
content:
A post shared by Labor4Palestine (@labor4palestine)

New York, New York—On Wednesday, October 7, 2026, CUNY for Palestine and NYC-wide Students for Justice in Palestine (SJP) organizers held a rally at City Hall, endorsed by various Palestine solidarity and community organizations, in support of the Palestinian national liberation struggle. Students joined the protest downtown after walking out of class at several of CUNY’s 26 campuses, including the flagship City College of New York (CCNY). Despite Meta’s attempts to censor organizers’ social media, removing posts from across movement accounts in the lead-up to the event, the protest drew hundreds of students, academic workers and community members from across the city to mark three years of ongoing genocide and resistance in Palestine. The protest also attracted international media attention as the principled demands resonated so deeply across the globe. As one student organizer put it: “We’re glad our rally exposed every normalizer, traitor, and hypocrite, when it comes to the Palestinian cause, but the truth is, the resistance and city of Gaza exposed these realities early on.”

Building on the work of the CUNY Divestment Coalition, student organizers’ demands were expressed clearly in the chants that reverberated across Lower Manhattan: “One: We are the students, Two: We won’t stop fighting, Three: We want divestment now, now, now!”

In the wake of the 2024 Student Intifada, students and educators across the country united behind a campaign targeting their universities’ Boards of Trustees (widely referred to by students as “Boards of Butchers”). These boards are the universities’ financiers and oversee university endowments, making them key pressure points for campaigns aiming to divest funds from “Israel”. As one City University of New York (CUNY) student explained, “CUNY claims to be a people’s university, yet it is governed by a body whose interests are completely at odds with the daily realities and solidarity commitments of our majority working class, Black and Brown student body and the communities they belong to.

Last year, CUNY students won a landmark lawsuit forcing CUNY to disclose all financial records from the last five years. The records, released last month, reveal investments made with New York taxpayer money and CUNY student tuition into weapons manufacturers arming “Israel”; tech companies providing security infrastructure to “Israel” and the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS); private prison contractors including CoreCivic and GEO Group, which operates the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) concentration camp Delaney Hall; and corporations profiting directly from US prison labor, such as 3M, a company that has supplied raw materials to prison labor programs in at least 13 states.

In the opening speech made by a representative of CUNY Law Students for Justice in Palestine (SJP), the speaker emphasized that Palestine is the moral compass of all revolutionaries and that this was in fact the reason why divestment has been a key demand of the national student movement for Palestine and a central focus for NYC student organizers as well. Universities are materially complicit in the genocide through their investments in weapon manufacturing companies such as Lockheed Martin, Elbit, and General Dynamics. The speaker emphasized that students’ push for divestment is therefore the most material form that their solidarity with Palestine can take. “It is our duty to resist [the settler colonial genocide in Palestine], and as students, the least we can possibly do is to demand and push for our universities to divest from death.” In another speech, a representative of the Young Democratic Socialists of America (YDSA) called out CUNY’s investments in Caterpillar, Boeing, Raytheon, and Palantir, emphasizing that they are at the top of the CUNY Divestment Coalition’s list of targets for divestment.

On October 7th, protesters turned their attention to New York City’s Mayor. They disrupted Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s attendance at a vigil hosted by “Israelis for Peace,” a front for “Standing Together,” which the BDS Movement has denounced as “an Israeli normalization outfit that seeks to distract from and whitewash Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza.” The event, held in Union Square, parroted rhetoric used by Western media to slander the Palestinian resistance and manufacture consent for the ongoing genocide in Gaza. Most press on the matter outside of social media, that I can find, has died down, but they continue providing on the ground footage and documentation of what is happening at the US/Mexico “border” wall.

And they are making a difference.


View this post on Instagram


The Tohono O'odham Nation also had set up a prayer camp in resistance to border wall expansion, having had the buried remains of their ancestors at sacred sites blown apart by border wall expansion.


View this post on Instagram


Some quotes from an

 article on the Tohono O'odham’s experience with the efforts of expansion:

“I have been here because of this border wall that’s going up and the Trump administration,” he said.  “I really dislike it because it’s dividing our people and that really hurts,” he told ICT. “They can’t see their families, they can’t visit their families, they can’t go home. Just the other day, we went to our neighbors right across (the border) to invite them over for breakfast and we got stopped … and we got carded and they never did that before. They wouldn’t let us cross until we gave them our tribal IDs.”

- Davy Cross, Tohono O’odham

Later in the article:

The chairman [of the Tohono O'odham Nation, Verlon Jose] explained that Tohono O’odam citizens in Mexico would have to apply for a special permit to come into the United States for a day or a couple of days.

But he said there would be real problems with those.

“The

president of the United States put out an executive order and they said that anybody with those permits would have to pay $1,000 for it

,” he said while standing this month at one of the traditional tribal border gates.

“

We don’t have $1,000

,” he said, shaking his head.

“It is even hard for our members … in Mexico, to even have $100. So it’s very difficult.”

Since many tribal members wouldn’t be able to pay for a visa, they would lose the ability to access Indian Health Service and other tribal benefits on the U.S. side of the border, he said.

“As it is right now,

they won’t have health care. The public health care in Mexico is zero-to-none. People die in the waiting rooms,”

title: Yδρογονοενέργεια. Κοινωνική απελευθέρωση και κοινωνική ισότητα σημαίνει ενεργειακή απελευθέρωση και ενεργειακή ισότητα
content:
Γράφει ο

Κώστας Λάμπος


Διδάκτωρ οικονομικών επιστημών

 του

FREIE UNIVERSITAET BERLIN


«Ανώτερο πράγμα κι’ από την αλήθεια είναι


το θάρρος να την πεις και να την γράψεις»


Αριστομένης


 

«Μπορεί να ανήκετε σ’ εκείνους τους ανθρώπους που νομίζουν ότι η ενέργεια του υδρογόνου είναι μια φαντασίωση κάποιων μελλοντολόγων ή κάποιων άλλων συγγραφέων επιστημονικής φαντασίας.


Ή, στην καλύτερη περίπτωση, μπορεί να την θεωρείτε ως μια πολλά υποσχόμενη μελλοντική τεχνολογία που, αν κάποτε εφαρμοστεί, αυτό θα γίνει στο μακρινό μέλλον. Εάν όντως σκέφτεστε μ’ αυτόν τον τρόπο, ξανασκεφτείτε το σοβαρά… Φανταστείτε έναν κόσμο στον οποίο η … (ανθρωπότητα) κέρδισε την ελευθερία της από το πετρέλαιο…


Μπορούμε να χτίσουμε αυτόν τον κόσμο μέσα σε δέκα χρόνια με την υπάρχουσα τεχνολογία… Φανταστείτε έναν κόσμο στον οποίο η (ανθρωπότητα) αποφάσισε να ξεπεράσει την ενεργειακή και την κλιματική κρίση που απειλεί την… (ύπαρξή) της. Μπορούμε να χτίσουμε αυτόν τον κόσμο σήμερα με συνειδητές επιλογές και πολιτική βούληση»

, αναφέρεται στο: 

Jerry Brown, Rinaldo Brutoco

και

 James Cusumano, Freedom From Mid-East Oil, Edition of World Business Academy, 2007


Καθημερινά ακούμε για το ενεργειακό πρόβλημα, από πολιτικούς, ‘ειδικούς ενεργειολόγους’, δημοσιογράφους, παπαγαλάκια της εξουσίας και λοιπούς ινστρούχτορες, χωρίς ωστόσο να τολμούν

να αναζητήσουν λύσεις, παρ’ ότι όλοι γνωρίζουμε πως ενέργεια από ορυκτά καύσιμα και απάνθρωποι και καταστροφικοί πόλεμοι αποτελούν την όψη του ίδιου νομίσματος, με το οποίο οι πλούσιοι γίνονται πλουσιότεροι και οι φτωχοί φτωχότεροι. Ανυπότακτοι, όμως επιστήμονες με ακέραιη την κοινωνική και επιστημονική τους συνείδηση έχουν εδώ και δεκαετίες δημιουργήσει την εναλλακτική μορφή ενέργειας με την συνδυασμένη συμπληρωματική συνεργασία των ανανεώσιμων πηγών ενέργειας, (ΑΠΕ), όπως ο ήλιος, ο άνεμος, η γεωθερμία, η δύναμη των κυμάτων κ.λπ κλπ. Αυτές οι πηγές ενέργειας μπορούν σε αποκεντρωμένη σε επίπεδο καταναλωτή ενέργειας να παράξουν φτηνή ηλεκτρική ενέργεια, με την οποία μπορεί, όπως λ.χ. με την ηλεκτρόλυση του νερού, να αποσπαστεί το υδρογόνο που είναι ανεξάντλητο στο περιβάλλον μας και στο Σύμπαν και ως καύσιμη πρώτη ύλη να δώσουν, καταργώντας τα πανάκριβα συγκεντρωτικά ενεργειακά μονοπώλια, να εξασφαλίσουν, στον κάθε αυτοπαραγωγό και ταυτόχρονα καταναλωτή ενέργειας, άφθονη, φτηνή, καθαρή και ασφαλή ηλεκτρική ενέργεια, με την οποία θα μπορεί να ευημερούν άτομα, κοινωνίες, χώρες και ανθρωπότητα χωρίς να αναγκάζονται να υποτάσσονται στα συγκεντρωτικά ενεργειακά μονοπώλια και στους πολιτικούς τους υπαλλήλους. Αυτός άλλωστε είναι και ο λόγος που κανένα κόμμα, όπως και κανένας ακαδημαϊκός, ή συστημικός διανοούμενος που σιτίζεται στο Πρυτανείο της εξουσίας του Κεφαλαίου δεν τολμάει να καταγγείλει τα ορυκτά καύσιμα και τα συγκεντρωτικά ενεργειακά δίκτυα που ελέγχουν τις οικονομίες των επιμέρους κοινωνιών και της ανθρωπότητας συνολικά. Γι’ αυτό κανένας δεν αναφέρεται στην υδρογονοενέργεια και κανένας δεν μιλάει για κοινωνική αλλαγή, αλλά όλοι μιλούν για ‘πολιτική αλλαγή’, που σημαίνει πως όλοι βάζουν υποψηφιότητα για διαχειριστές του κεφαλαίου, κι’ ας τάζουν λαγούς με πετραχήλια. Όμως όλο και περισσότερο, όλο και περισσότεροι αντιλαμβάνονται πως την λύση θα την δώσει η Ενιαία Κινηματική Κοινωνία και όχι τα δημιουργήματα της τακτικής του κεφαλαίου με το divinede et impera, δηλαδή τα νόθα συστημικά μικροκινήματα.


*


Το είδος και η ποσότητα των πηγών ενέργειας που κάθε φορά μπορούσαν και μπορούν να αξιοποιούν οι άνθρωποι καθόριζαν και καθορίζουν ακόμα την ποιότητα και την επάρκεια-ανεπάρκεια των μορφών ενέργειας που χρησιμοποιούν και σε συνδυασμό με το είδος και τον τρόπο κοινωνίας και επικοινωνίας των ανθρώπων καθόριζαν την εξέλιξη των επιμέρους κοινωνιών και διαμόρφωναν πάντα και συνεχίζουν να διαμορφώνουν το αποτύπωμα του ανθρώπινου πολιτισμού. Αυτή η διαδικασία βρίσκεται σήμερα σε κρίσιμη φάση.


Το κρισιμότερο πρόβλημα της εποχής μας είναι, χωρίς καμιά αμφιβολία, το ενεργειακό. Κι αυτό, γιατί το υφιστάμενο ενεργειακό σύστημα των ορυκτών καυσίμων δεν μπορεί να καλύψει ούτε τις βασικές ανάγκες της ανθρωπότητας, επειδή η ενέργεια αυτή:


Είναι πολύ ακριβή, με αποτέλεσμα να την στερείται απόλυτα ή σχετικά το μεγαλύτερο μέρος του ανθρώπινου πληθυσμού.


 

Ρυπαίνει επικίνδυνα το περιβάλλον και υποβαθμίζει τους όρους ζωής στον πλανήτη.

author: LCM-Redaktion
title: Die Bedeutung revolutionärer Kultur
content:
Im Folgenden veröffentlichen wir ein zweiteiliges Interview, das vom

Radio Résistance

 mit Carlos Manangan, einem Revolutionär der Nationalen Demokratischen Front der Philippinen (NDF) und der philippinischen Diaspora-Organisation „Compatriots-NDF“, geführt wurde. Manangan ist selbst Künstler und schafft revolutionäre Kunst in verschiedenen Formaten, darunter Video, Musik, Theater und Puppenspiel. In dem Interview geht es um nichts Geringeres als die Frage, was revolutionäre Kommunisten auszeichnen sollte

. Dies

 bettet Carlos Manangan in seinen Ausführungen zur Geschichte und Strategie der revolutionären Bewegung auf den Philippinen ein. Da er selbst viele Jahre als Migrant in den imperialistischen Zentren gelebt hat, stellt er zudem seine Sichtweise auf die Entwicklungen der kommunistischen Bewegung an diesen Orten wieder.


Wer bist du und welche Rolle spielst du in der revolutionären Bewegung auf den Philippinen?


Mein Name ist June. In den sozialen Medien bin ich unter dem Namen John bekannt. Ich bin ein politischer Flüchtling und Organisator von Migrant:innen. Ich habe einen Hintergrund als politischer Flüchtling. Ich bin Künstler – nicht von Beruf, aber ich nutze die Kunst als Mittel zur Organisation und auch als meinen persönlichen Ausdruck des Widerstands gegen Ausbeutung und Unterdrückung, insbesondere gegenüber der Arbeiter:innenklasse und speziell gegenüber philippinischen Wanderarbeiter:innen. Aber natürlich bin ich stets solidarisch mit der Bewegung der arbeitenden Menschen weltweit.


Zunächst wollen wir mit dir über die Kultur aus der Perspektive der revolutionären Strategie sprechen, damit wir Einblicke in die theoretischen Grundlagen deiner Arbeit gewinnen können. Welche Rolle spielt Kultur in revolutionären Bewegungen im Allgemeinen?


Als Erstes müssen wir natürlich definieren, was Kultur ist, und dann darauf eingehen, was reaktionäre Kultur und revolutionäre Kultur sind. In meiner Praxis betrachte ich Kultur als Spiegelbild der Interessen und Werte in der Gesellschaft. Aber natürlich ist die Gesellschaft keine homogene Gesellschaft. Insbesondere gibt es verschiedene Klassen. Es gibt unterdrückte und ausgebeutete Klassen, und es gibt diejenigen, die andere Klassen beherrschen, unterdrücken und ausbeuten. Sie sind die herrschende Klasse. Die vorherrschende Kultur wäre also ein Spiegelbild der Interessen und Werte der herrschenden Klasse. Und in der heutigen Zeit sind die vorherrschenden Werte der bürgerliche Individualismus und dieses wahnsinnige Verlangen nach Privateigentum, denn wir leben im Zeitalter des Kapitalismus. Und die Kultur des Kapitalismus spiegelt die Gier nach Profit wider. Und diese lässt sich nur durch Unterdrückung und Ausbeutung erreichen, insbesondere der Arbeiter:innenklasse. Wenn wir also von revolutionärer Kultur sprechen, ist dies das Gegenteil der derzeit vorherrschenden Kultur. Sie ist der Ausdruck des Strebens der Arbeiter:innenklasse nach Freiheit. Freiheit von Ausbeutung und Unterdrückung. Wir wollen also eine Gesellschaft schaffen, die frei von Ausbeutung und Unterdrückung einer Klasse durch eine andere ist. Das ist die revolutionäre Kultur: Unsere Bestrebungen und Werte, die wir vertreten, um Revolutionär:innen zu werden.


Gibt es eurer Meinung nach universelle Aspekte revolutionärer Kultur, die in jedem konkreten kulturellen Kontext gleich sind, insbesondere im Hinblick der Unterschiede zwischen imperialistischen Zentren und halbkolonialen Ländern?


Um unsere politische Arbeit zu leisten, ist es notwendig, tiefgreifend zu verstehen, was wir als Revolutionär:innen erreichen wollen. Es mag zwar einen globalen Traum von uns geben, aber es gibt auch lokale Realitäten, denen wir uns stellen müssen, sowie Probleme, die wir lösen müssen. Wir müssen wissen, wer unsere Feinde und wer unsere Freunde, unsere Verbündeten sind. Deshalb müssen wir eine umfassende soziale Analyse und Klassenanalyse durchführen und die Gesellschaft untersuchen, sei es auf globaler oder lokaler Ebene, unter Berücksichtigung der nationalen Gegebenheiten. Nur so können wir einen Speer zu haben, der wirklich scharf genug ist, die Rüstung unserer Feinde zu durchdringen. Er muss sehr scharf und nicht allgemein gehalten sein, und er muss im Bereich des Verständnisses der Massen liegen, die wir in eine revolutionäre Kraft verwandeln wollen.


Wir haben unterschiedliche Kontexte. Ob in der Schweiz, in den Vereinigten Staaten oder in anderen Ländern Europas – wir arbeiten in einem anderen …

author: Unknown
title: Beyond Polarity: For a Marxist Theory of the World Order
content:
Collage by Tricontinental: Institute for Social Research drawing from a Dymaxion map projection and Islamic, Mesoamerican, Ethiopian, and Chinese maps made between the twelfth and seventeenth centuries.


Images sourced from: Muhammad al-Idrisi, Tabula Rogeriana, 1154, 1929 reconstruction and transliteration by Konrad Miller via Wikimedia Commons; Matteo Ricci and Li Zhizao, Kunyu Wanguo Quantu (坤輿萬國全圖), 1602, Library of Congress Geography and Map Division via Wikimedia Commons; Códice Xólotl, Lámina 1, Tetzcoco, Mexico, c. 1541 via Wikimedia Commons; Tigrayan circular map from the Māshafā Aksum (Book of Aksum), pre-eighteenth century, Bibliothèque nationale de France, Collection Antoine d’Abbadie, via Wikimedia Commons; and Justinkunimune,

Blank World Map, Dymaxion Projection

, 2023, Wikimedia Commons, CC0 1.0.


The maps in this dossier trace how the hegemonic world order has organised and represented the world, from colonialism, the post-World War II international order, and Cold War bipolarity to internationalised capital, the North–South divide, and US unipolarity. More than representations, they distil concepts imperial and colonial powers have used to exercise power. Every dot of ink is a choice: what sits at the centre, which countries appear at the top, and which distortions are considered acceptable. The cover gathers cartographic traditions with different centres, orientations, and cosmologies, asking how, beyond poles and blocs, we might understand the unequal social relations that constitute the world order itself.


The Mercator projection was developed in 1569 for European navigation during the colonial period. During imperial expansion, it became the standard map projection, still used today.

This map, which shows the spheres of influence of the ‘great powers’ and their ‘possessions’, was created by H.E.C. Robinson in 1908. Sourced from the National Library of Australia via Wikimedia Commons.


The language of ‘unipolarity’ and ‘multipolarity’ – whether global power is concentrated in one dominant state or distributed among several major states – has become almost unavoidable in political debates. US and allied policymakers have often described the post-Cold War international system as a ‘liberal international order’ increasingly threatened by ‘revisionist powers’ such as China and Russia. Many governments and movements in the Global South, by contrast, welcome what they see as the emergence of a multipolar world in which Washington can no longer dictate the terms of international life. This aspiration is understandable. Any weakening of the United States’ capacity to impose blockades and unilateral sanctions, organise coups, and wage wars can open political space for sovereign development and for class struggles to advance.


‘Multipolarity’ may function as a slogan of resistance to US primacy and offer a rough description of how certain forms of state power are distributed. Its political appeal, however, should not be confused with explanatory power. The number of powerful states tells us little about the social relations that produce their power, the class interests organised within them, or the imperialist hierarchies that connect them. Multipolarity does not, by itself, provide a Marxist account of the world; when treated as such, it can mislead us into believing that a wider distribution of state power is inherently progressive.

1


Venezuela’s former President Hugo Chávez, who had every reason to welcome a world of many centres, was dissatisfied enough with the term ‘multipolarity’ to coin ‘pluripolarity’ against it – insisting that what mattered was not the number of centres but whether popular subjects were the agents of transformation.

2

 The need to specify this political content was itself revealing: the number of poles alone tells us nothing about the class forces or popular subjects shaping the resulting order.


A Marxist analysis must therefore replace the arithmetic of poles with the analysis of a chain: an unevenly developed system of social formations, each internally constituted by class struggle and externally bound to the others by relations of exploitation and dependence. The question is not how many poles there are but how the chain is held together and where it is most susceptible to being broken.


The problem, then, lies in the image of the pole itself. It asks us to picture the international system as a set of sovereign states treated as its decisive units, each …

author: dev
title: Effleurer l'avenir. Notes sur le technofascisme
content:
« L'avenir appartient à ceux qui savent perforer le présent »

 [

1

]

, écrit Cindy Coutant au début de son excellent

Pénétration terminale

, dernière publication des éditions Audimat. Perforer, c'est traverser ; mais traverser d'une façon bien particulière : traverser en vue d'atteindre, d'arriver – traverser

pour

 arriver. Perforer semble être cet impératif de l'époque que, il y a presque trente ans, un groupe d'auteurs anonymes décrivait ainsi « il faut supprimer le trajet ; il est impératif d'

arriver

 seulement »

 [

2

]

.


Perforer, c'est donc performer afin d'atteindre le plus rapidement, le plus efficacement possible, c'est trouer tout ce qui sépare de la fin, c'est performer l'atteinte. Cette performance ne va pas sans force, sans efficience, sans vigueur, elle est la promesse de la technologie, et des discours qui la sous-tendent relevant d'une « grammaire rigide de la perforation »

 [

3

]

. Il est question partout dans l'ouvrage de cette rigidité érectile comme imaginaire et cap du technofascisme. Seul un être rigide peut, en effet, « tout défoncer sur son passage »

 [

4

]

 – c'est-à-dire arriver à ses fins. Mais ce passage n'est pas infini, il ne peut être une dérive, liquide ou molle, un détour à jamais inachevé, figures du looser – de l'échoué – qui ne parvient pas. La perforation, la pénétration doivent être terminales. Coutant reprend l'expression à la balistique (une science des balles, une science

des projectiles

, donc,

une

science

 du projet

) :


La

pénétration terminale

 désigne la capacité opérationnelle de pénétration d'un projectile durant l'ultime phase de sa trajectoire : précision d'impact, capacité de percée, étendue des dommages selon sa nature anti-personnelle ou anti-matérielle. Si la balistique étudie les trajectoires sous tous leurs aspects, la balistique terminale est la branche scientifique qui étudie le moment où le projectile n'a plus d'options ; lorsqu'il ne corrige plus sa course, ne négocie plus sa vitesse, ne compose plus avec l'espace traversé. La trajectoire est verrouillée, l'horizon se referme en ligne d'impact : le projectile doit défoncer, et qu'il atteigne exactement sa cible ou qu'il la manque, il va le faire. La terminalité est tout à la fois une fin de parcours et le moment où l'action quitte le champ des possibles pour devenir exécutoire

 [

5

]


La balistique terminale s'intéresse donc au point de non-retour

 [

6

]

, qui porte mal son nom dans la mesure où ce moment est celui de l'impact, c'est-à-dire de l'arrivée : dans le projet, toute arrivée est un retour, puisqu'il s'agit d'atteindre ce qui a déjà été projeté au préalable, de parvenir là où on s'était imaginé aller,

de

retourner

 à

ce qui avait été projeté

. Et c'est ce qui explique, aussi, pourquoi l'imaginaire du technofascisme, qui est l'imaginaire de la projection par excellence, est un imaginaire nostalgique, réactionnaire : car, d'une certaine manière, tout projet est nostalgique, tout projet est une façon de retourner, retour en forme d'aller vers ce qui avait été prévu. La terminalité est le moment du passage à l'acte, en même temps que la preuve de la capacité à passer à l'acte, à être davantage qu'une pure puissance n'ayant pas éprouvé sa bravoure. La terminalité performe donc cette capacité à passer à l'acte – performance de son actualité en tant que, on va le voir, sujet masculin blanc occidental. La performativité/perforativité, que l'on pourrait à présent désigner par le syntagme perfor(m)ativité, peut apparaître alors comme une forme d'agentivité qui expliquerait certaines violences faites à tout ce qui est hors-norme, comme l'imaginent Véronica Gago et Luci Cavallero :


les féminicides, travesticides, transféminicides, lesbicides répandent l'idée d'un pouvoir absolu au niveau de la quotidienneté. Il n'est pas nécessaire d'avoir du « pouvoir institutionnel », il n'est pas nécessaire d'« être un grand homme », pour exercer ce pouvoir de tuer. Et, pour cela même, cet accès au pouvoir devient si attractif entre pairs. L'accès au gouvernement – au plus grand pouvoir institutionnel démocratique – d'une personne comme Milei, qui revendique de manière sinistre et efficace le pouvoir brutal de « ceux qui n'ont pas de pouvoir » (ceux qui ne sont pas la caste), « libère » un mode d'exercice du pouvoir que nous caractérisons comme passage à l'acte des « discours de haine » émis par l'État

 [

7

]


Perfor(m)er sa virilité, sa capacité à atteindre, sa rigidité …

While these words originally come from Social Anarchism and Organisation by the FARJ, this edited and abridged version represents our organizational understanding of this text which has been essential to the development of the Center for Especifismo Studies and the continuation of Militant Kindergarten. We have composed, numbered, and subtitled the following paragraphs by adapting our “Reading Guide” without page numbers or ellipsis to make for a smoother reading:

By especifismo, we refer to a conception of anarchist organization that has two fundamental axes: organization and social work/insertion. These two axes are based on the classical concepts of differentiated actuation of anarchism in the social and political levels (Bakuninist concept) and specific anarchist organization (Malatestan concept).

Synthesis advocates a model of anarchist organization in which are all the anarchists (anarcho-communists, anarchosyndicalists, anarcho-individualists etc.). So, it presents many of the characteristics that we criticize. We recognize that within synthesist organizations there are also serious militants committed to social anarchism, so we do not want the criticisms to seem generalized. Although we never question whether these organizations are anarchist (for us, they all are), they do not, in most cases, converge with our way of conceiving anarchist organization. There are diverse anarchist organizations that do not come out of the especifismo current. So, especifismo implies much more than to advocate anarchist organization. We understand anarchism as an ideology, that is, a “set of ideas, motivations, aspirations, values, a structure or system of concepts that have a direct connection with action – that which we call political practice”. title: La Crique, un futur lieu anti-autoritaire pour partir à l'abordage
content:
Appel à contributions pour acheter un local dans l'est parisien 💰


Difficile de rester insensible face au fonctionnement insensé du monde dans lequel on vit. L'argent est roi, les puissants s'enrichissent sur le dos de milliards d'autres personnes, sur le pillage et la destruction du vivant. Leur soif de pouvoir s'accompagne de conquêtes, de colonisations et de guerres.


Des murs sont érigés, les frontières renforcées, les indésirables chassé-es ou enfermé-es.


Les discours réactionnaires pullulent, légitimant le passage à l'acte des racistes, transphobes et homophobes de tous poils.


Pour que ça passe et que chacun ferme sa gueule, on nous vend des smartphones et la démocratie. Les caméras et les flics partout viennent compléter un contrôle de plus en plus large, optimiser la gestion intéressée de nos vies et empêcher toute rébellion.


Mais partout, des gens tentent de briser le cours des choses, rompre la normalité, résister à ce qui nous est imposé. C'est dans ces brèches que nous nous sommes rencontré-es ces dernières années : squats, manifestations et blocages en tous genres, mouvements, assemblées, collectifs, espaces de débrouille…


Sans être d'accord sur tout, nous partageons l'envie d'en découdre avec ce monde.


Pourtant, ces derniers temps, nous avons aussi constaté qu'il y a de moins en moins de lieux pour se rencontrer, débattre, et s'organiser. Pour qui aspire à un bouleversement de l'ordre social, cette question est primordiale. D'autant plus face à une vague autoritaire mondiale qui paraît inexorable.


C'est de là que vient l'envie de dénicher une Crique entre deux immeubles pour y ancrer sa barque. Un espace de débats, de partage de savoirs, de convivialité, de contre-information, de diffusion d'idées mutines et de pratiques de luttes offensives.


La Crique sera ouverte à toutes celles et ceux qui se retrouvent sincèrement dans le constat que ce monde est à saborder dans une perspective émancipatrice pour tou-tes, et qui veulent s'organiser sans capitaine, de manière anti-autoritaire et autonome.


Anti-autoritaire ça veut dire de manière horizontale, d'égale à égale, sans chef ni politicard.


Autonome ça veut dire agir par nous-mêmes. Le lieu n'est pas l'organe de transmission d'un parti ou d'un syndicat. Les voies qu'il explore sont donc anti-électorales.


Il ne s'agit pas de constituer un groupe politique avec une ligne précise. Mais dans cette période de confusion des idées, il semble important d'assumer une certaine base commune.


Ce futur lieu veut défendre une perspective révolutionnaire, c'est à dire la provocation d'un changement radical et l'avènement d'un monde libéré de toute autorité. Tous les combats doivent être menés de front contre les oppressions et les normes.


Combattre l'État, le capitalisme et la propriété privée. Combattre le racisme, le validisme, le genre, l'hétéronormativité et le patriarcat.


Combattre l'industrie et la technologie qui saccagent la planète et nous dépossèdent toujours plus de nos moyens de subsistance.


Combattre la démocratie dont l'objectif est de pacifier et de faire accepter l'ordre des choses. Les partis vendant un changement radical viennent simplement récupérer la colère et aménager l'existant.


Combattre les dominations partout où elles se trouvent que ce soit au niveau de l'État, de la famille, ou de nos assemblées.


Ce que nous imaginons faire dans la Crique est large et non exhaustif, ça dépendra des complicités et des idées que chacun-e amènera dans ses cales.


Lire des brochures sur le logement et la gentrification, organiser une manifestation sauvage après un énième meurtre policier, débattre sur les méthodes pour se débarrasser du nucléaire, imaginer une action contre la construction d'une nouvelle prison, chiller autour d'un café, rêver d'un blackout de l'économie, faire l'arpentage d'un livre sur l'histoire coloniale de la Kanaky, planifier la perturbation d'une conférence transphobe, faire un événement de solidarité autour de la guerre au Soudan, débriefer après une opération répressive, discuter pour faire écho à des révoltes ailleurs, accueillir une assemblée de mobilisation contre la guerre, se réunir avant d'aller recouvrir la ville de slogans contre le patriarcat, mater un film où à la fin on gagne, et aussi des ateliers pratiques, affiches, anonymat numérique, débrouille pour l'élec... et si on a assez d'oseille : aménager l'espace pour des concerts, des cantines, une piscine anti-olympique. 🏊


Concrètement, on …

title: AKP’li yıllarda TOKİ: İhale rejimi ve arsa düzeni
content:
Bugün milyonlarca emekçiyi girdaba sürükleyen barınma krizi, AKP iktidarı boyunca TOKİ ile Emlak Konut eliyle kurulan düzenin içinde mayalandı. Konut krizinin sermaye çevrelerinde, menkul simsarlarında ve onların sözcülüğünü yapanlarda nasıl anlatıldığı bellidir: “Yeterince konut üretilmiyor, arz talebi karşılamıyor, fiyatlar ve kiralar bu yüzden yükseliyor”. Uydurulan çözüm ise “daha çok inşaat, daha çok imar, daha çok kredi”. Bu kesime göre konut içinde yaşanacak bir yer değil, arzı ve talebi olan bir metadır. Kriz de ancak daha fazla meta üretilerek giderilecek bir piyasa aksaklığı olarak görülür. Aynı dil iktidarın da dilidir: Bakan Kurum 500 bin konutluk kampanyayı "hem konut fiyatları hem kira fiyatları düşsün diye" başlattıklarını kaydetmişti.

Oysa TOKİ ve Emlak Konut'un yirmi yılı bu reçeteyi sınayan büyük bir deney gibi duruyor. TOKİ Başkanı Ömer Bulut'a göre idare 2003-2022 arasında 1 milyon 170 bin konut üretti. Emlak Konut da kendi verisine göre 2003'ten bu yana 260 bin bağımsız birim geliştirdi. Yalnızca 2020-2022 arasında 247 bin TOKİ konutu yapıldı. Ev sahipliği oranı tam da bu yıllarda geriledi. Simsarların reçetesi devlet eliyle uygulandı, ama emekçinin barınma sorunu çözülmedi.

Demek ki mesele kaç konut yapıldığı değil, konutun kimin için ve neye göre üretildiğidir. Emekçi için konut başını sokacağı bir dam, ailesiyle birlikte ertesi güne hazırlandığı bir barınaktır. Sermaye için ise satıldığında kâr, elde tutulduğunda değer artışı getiren bir varlıktır. Birincisinin ölçüsü ihtiyaç, ikincisininki satış fiyatıdır. TOKİ ile Emlak Konut'un kurduğu düzen ağırlığı açıkça ikincisine verdi. Kamu, konut üretimini barınma hakkına göre değil, sermaye kriterlerince göre örgütledi.

Bunun en açık itirafı, 2003-2011 arasında TOKİ Başkanı, ardından Çevre ve Şehircilik Bakanı olan Erdoğan Bayraktar'dan geldi. Bayraktar 2012'de TBMM kürsüsünde, devletin Ataşehir, Ataköy, Bahçeşehir, Kayabaşı, Mavişehir ve Eryaman'daki arazilerini gelir paylaşımı modeliyle "1,5 misli, 2 misli, 5 misli değerle değerlendirdik" diyordu. Nitekim bakanın gurur kaynağı, kamu arazisinin emekçiye konut olması değil, satış değerinin katlanmasıydı. Kamu toprağı, devletin eliyle rant aracına dönüştürülüyordu.

Bu dönüşüm bir iş bölümüyle hayata geçti. TOKİ kamu arazisini topladı ve imara açtı; Emlak Konut bu araziyi müteahhide bağladı. Kamunun imar kararıyla değerlenen toprağı, inşaat sermayesinin hasılatına dönüştü. TOKİ'nin 500 bin konutluk kampanyasına 8 milyon 840 bin kişi başvurdu. Kentin merkezindeki kamu toprağı sermayeye satılacak projelere bağlandı. Emekçiye ise çeperde, kurayla dağıtılan ve taksitleri memur maaş artışına endeksli bir borç kaldı. Nüfusun yüzde 27'sini oluşturan kiracılar bu düzenin hesabına neredeyse hiç girmedi.

Elbette barınma krizinin başkaca nedenleri de var: Ücretlerin baskılanması, enflasyon, faiz politikası, depremin enkazı ve iç göç... Ancak devletin kentsel toprak ve konut üzerindeki “en güçlü aracı” TOKİ, yirmi yılı aşkın süre boyunca konutu emekçinin barınma ihtiyacına göre değil, sermayenin satış değerine göre düzenlemek için kullandı. Krize karşı kamunun elinde olması gereken kaldıraç, krizi üreten mantığın içinde çalıştı.

2001: Tasfiye halindeki Emlak Bankası'nın varlıkları TOKİ'ye devredildi. Bakanlar Kurulu kararıyla 7 bin 852 konut TOKİ'ye geçti.

2001-2002: Emlak Bankası'nın Emlak Konut'taki payları TOKİ'ye devredildi. Şirket gayrimenkul yatırım ortaklığı statüsü aldı ve TOKİ, Emlak Konut'un ana hissedarı oldu.

31 Temmuz 2003: 4966 sayılı Kanun, Toplu Konut Kanunu'nu değiştirerek TOKİ'ye konut sektörüyle ilgili şirketler kurma ve kurulmuş şirketlere ve finans kurumlarına ortak olma yetkisi verdi. Aynı düzenleme, kâr amaçlı projeler yapmanın da yolunu açtı.

2003: 4734 sayılı Kamu İhale Kanunu'na eklenen bir hüküm, TOKİ'ye kamulaştırma, mülkiyet, arsa temini ve uygulama projesi şartları aranmadan yapım ihalesine çıkma imkânı tanıdı.

5 Mayıs 2004: 5162 sayılı Kanun, Toplu Konut Kanunu'nun TOKİ'nin plan yetkisini düzenleyen 4. maddesini değiştirdi. TOKİ, gecekondu dönüşüm alanlarında ve kendi arsalarında her ölçekte imar planı yapma yetkisi aldı. Belediyece üç ay içinde onaylanmayan planları kendisi onaylayabilir hale geldi.

title: Geschichte von unten: Jeden Monat ein neues, faires T-Shirt von „Working Class History“ – für LeserInnen des LabourNet Germany zum reduzierten Preis, der zudem auch uns unterstützt!
content:
Dossier


Seit November 2021 ist das neue Projekt „T-Shirt of the Month“ von

dna merch


 in Zusammenarbeit mit der Bildungsinitiative

Working Class History


 online. LabourNet ist Teil des Projekts und kann die Shirts Euch daher mit dem Discount-Code etwas günstiger anbieten. Jeden Monat gibt es ein faires, genossenschaftlich genähtes T-Shirt, das einer Geschichte oder einer Persönlichkeit aus dem Archiv von Working Class History gewidmet ist. Es kann einen Monat lang weltweit vorbestellt werden und wird dann in der jeweiligen Auflage produziert und verschickt. Mit den Shirts werden die Forschungs- und Bildungsarbeit von Working Class History, eine Näherinnen-Kooperative in Kroatien sowie Basisgewerkschafter*innen in Südasien unterstützt. Die Designs kommen von Künstler*innen und Aktivist*innen aus der ganzen Welt. LabourNet-Leser*innen können beim Kauf der Shirts sparen und gleichzeitig unsere redaktionelle Arbeit unterstützen. Für jedes mit dem LabourNet-Discount-Code gekaufte Shirt bekommt ihr 5% Rabatt und wir eine Vermittlungsgebühr bzw. Spende. Siehe weitere Infos und die Shirts/Hoodies/Pullover:


[Mit dem LabourNet-Discount-Code] Das Oktober-2026-Shirt von Working Class History/dna: La Revolution Est Femme (Frankreich 1789)


„

Das Design dieses Monats ist den Tausenden von Frauen in Paris gewidmet, die am 5. Oktober 1789 einen entscheidenden Wendepunkt der Französischen Revolution herbeiführten. Verärgert über die hohen Brotpreise und den Brotmangel, plünderten sie das städtische Waffenlager und belagerten das Schloss von Versailles. Eine Augenzeugin hörte die Frauen sagen: „Die Männer hatten nicht genug Kraft, sich zu rächen, und sie würden beweisen, dass sie besser seien als die Männer.“ Die Frauen verlangten eine Zusammenkunft mit König Ludwig XVI., um Brot und Fortschritte bei der Ausarbeitung einer neuen, überarbeiteten Verfassung zu fordern, welche die Macht der Monarchie einschränken und neue Rechte für die Bevölkerung festschreiben sollte. (…) Wieder einmal hatten wir das Glück, die italienische Tätowierkünstlerin Fede Borgia für die Gestaltung eines Motivs zu gewinnen, das diese inspirierende Geschichte weiblicher Stärke einfängt. Sie gab ihrem Werk den französischen Titel „La Révolution est femme“, was auf Deutsch „Die Revolution ist weiblich“ bedeutet. Auf dem Schild im Hintergrund ist „Du Pain“ zu lesen – „Etwas Brot“, ein Verweis darauf, dass die hohen Brotpreise und der Brotmangel der Auslöser für die revolutionären Aktionen der Frauen waren

…“ Siehe mehr

Informationen und Bestellung in verschiedenen Versionen bei dna merch


 – den Code „LN20XX“ für 5 Prozent weniger und dennoch auch zur Unterstützung unserer Arbeit nicht vergessen!


[Mit dem LabourNet-Discount-Code] Das September-2026-Shirt von Working Class History/dna: Mehr Als 108 (Paraguay 1959)


„

In der Nacht zum 1. September 1959 stirbt der Radiomoderator und Tänzer Bernardo Aranda bei einem Brand in seinem Zimmer im Asunción Stadtteil Barrio Obrero. Der Fall wird nie aufgeklärt. Die von den USA unterstützte Militärdiktatur Alfredo Stroessners zieht trotzdem einen Schluss: Weil auch schwule Männer bei Aranda verkehrten, muss einer von ihnen verantwortlich sein. In den folgenden Tagen verhaftet und foltert die Polizei gezielt Männer, die als homosexuell gelten. Die regierungstreue Zeitung El País nennt schließlich die Zahl der Festgenommenen: 108. Angeklagt wird niemand, weder für Arandas Tod noch für das, was den Verhafteten angetan wurde. Bis heute wird „108″ in Paraguay als abwertender Begriff für queere Menschen verwendet. Zugleich entstand aus dieser Geschichte auch Widerstand. : Bereits Ende September 1959 erschien ein anonymer Protestbrief in derselben Zeitung, heute anerkannt als erster dokumentierter Akt queeren Widerstands im Land. Sein Jahrestag, der 30. September, wird inzwischen als Tag des queeren Gedenkens in Paraguay begangen

title: Cagnard prend fin, la lutte continue
content:
En cette rentrée, Cagnard a décidé de clôturer ses activités politiques. Dans ce texte, nous nous retrouvons à quelques-un·e·s pour tirer le bilan de l'existence du collectif et situons sa trajectoire dans la séquence politique que nous traversons. Nous exprimons là notre avis sur la tenue et fermeture de cet espace d'organisation alors que le groupe voit la fin de ses activités comme un constat qui s'impose à lui-même. Diverses lectures découlent de la situation parmi les membres restants.


Il est ainsi à noter que, pour certain·es d'entre nous, ce sont le manque d'effectifs et de motivation qui bloquent aujourd'hui le groupe.


Cette ligne identifie l'impossibilité de l'action future du groupe dans les tensions inter-personnelles qui ont pu apparaître au fil de notre activité et dans un manque de renouvellement de nos effectifs. L'accueil de nouveaux membres aurait alors pu permettre de diluer les divergences politiques, de mettre une distance entre les susceptibilités inter-personnelles ou de voir partir des camarades tout en laissant de nouvelles forces assumer les tâches organisationnelles laissées vacantes.


D'autres camarades voient poindre des problématiques liées à notre fonctionnement, notre ouverture et notre composition. C'est afin de préciser cette lecture que nous écrivons ce texte.


En premier lieu, nous détaillons les enjeux qui ont motivé la création du collectif. Puis, nous revenons sur l'actualité politique du groupe et livrons des éléments d'analyse du contexte. De nouveaux impératifs se dessinent constamment dans la lutte : notre réflexivité doit servir à ajuster nos perspectives politiques à l'aune des obstacles que nous traversons et des tâches qui émergent.


Cagnard, sa création et ses objectifs


Cagnard a été créé en mars 2025 avec pour ambition de former un groupe autonome et ouvert sur Marseille. À rebours des logiques affinitaires et de cooptation, des camarades ont souhaité initier un projet de rupture avec les institutions traditionnelles du mouvement – partis et syndicats – qui assume dans le même temps la nécessité et l'accessibilité de l'organisation politique. Dans un cadre de composition, des personnes de sensibilités politiques diverses se sont organisées sur la base de perspectives communes, à commencer par l'intensification des mouvements sociaux et leur défense face à la répression.


Nous avons œuvré à la diffusion de pratiques de défense, soutenu les inculpé·es face à la Justice et animé des ateliers de formation politique. Il est crucial de battre en brèche les dynamiques de spécialisation lorsqu'elles entravent la participation effective des camarades à l'organisation politique. L'action de rue se doit d'être massive et ne doit pas être l'apanage d'une élite éclairée. Quant à la défense juridique, elle ne doit pas être abandonnée à des spécialistes du droit. Ces deux pendants du renforcement d'un mouvement doivent se trouver aux mains du plus grand nombre de camarades.


Nous entendions défendre ces lignes, ce qui entraînait parfois de porter la rupture au sein du mouvement social, dans la rue et au sein des espaces d'organisation. Plus largement, nous cherchions à soutenir le débordement face à la répression, le dépassement des mots d'ordre défensifs, sectoriels et des cadres de lutte institués, et à exacerber les contradictions en leur sein.


La théorie n'étant qu'un moment de la pratique, la tenue d'ateliers de formation politique et culturelle devait servir à affûter nos perspectives d'intervention dans les mobilisations naissantes et celles à venir. La composition devait nourrir l'intelligence collective : loin de penser que la contradiction affaiblit le mouvement révolutionnaire, nous sommes convaincu·es qu'elle le renforce et qu'elle doit être entretenue. Au-delà du dogmatisme et du sectarisme, l'ouverture de nos espaces visait un objectif clair : défendre et construire l'autonomie politique, dans le prolongement de ce que ce champ a su porter d'anti-capitalisme, d'anti-étatisme et d'indépendance vis-à-vis des partis et organisations syndicales. Il s'agissait aussi d'accroître nos forces de lutte, de propager l'auto-organisation pour gagner en puissance collective.


Tout au long de son existence, le collectif a fait preuve d'une activité politique constante. Toutefois, ces derniers mois, ses membres ont éprouvé des contradictions dans la mise en œuvre de ces objectifs. Notre modèle politique éprouve des limites certaines.
