author: Rodrigo Acuña
title: Cubans See Hope in Reforms But Worry Over How the US May Thwart Them
content:
Residents of Havana discuss the obstacles facing the revival of the Cuban economy amid the US fuel blockade.

Residents of Havana discuss the obstacles facing the revival of the Cuban economy amid the US fuel blockade.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Last month, Cuban Prime Minister Manuel Marrero Cruz declared that 158 new economic and social measures, out of an original package of 176 approved in July by the Cuba’s National Assembly, were being implemented and backed by 197 legal decrees. The measures include allowing private business to import medicines and other goods, loosening restrictions on private tourism, and authorising privately owned banks — under Central Bank supervision — on a regulatory basis equivalent to state banks. Adding to these measures, the National Assembly for the first time permitted foreign capital to invest directly in Cuban private businesses instead of having to operate exclusively through state-controlled structures. Private companies also will no longer be restricted to a maximum of 100 employees.

According to Daniel Torralbas, a London-based Cuban economist, the National Assembly’s new measures are “the most profound economic reform programme … since the 1959 revolution.” Headed by Fidel Castro, the government in Havana between the mid and late 1960s nationalized a vast array of U.S.-owned businesses that controlled major shares in key industries such as public utilities, mining, railways and infrastructure, and land and agriculture.

Mauricio Alonso, a 68-year-old former nuclear engineer who lives in Havana and now runs an Airbnb rental, is embracing the government’s new economic measures.

“On a personal level this is going to benefit me,” says Alonso, “because it’s going to allow, for example, me — since I’m self-employed — to partner with foreigners, to team up, to be part of a larger organization, and to carry out actions with my lodging business, and so on.” Working with travel agencies, in Alonso’s view, will now be made easier with the lifting of restrictions. “If I qualify, if I get accredited as such,” says Alonso, “I can carry out the work of a tour guide without any kind of problem.”

During the 1980s, Alonso worked at the Central Electronuclear de Juraguá, near the city of Cienfuegos, which was being built with the aid of the Soviet Union to become Cuba’s first nuclear power station. Alonso says that, “when the Soviet Union collapsed in late 1991, work on the plant came to a halt in 1992.” Although Alonso continued working in the nuclear sector until 1995, he “realized that the project couldn’t go on — due in part to [the] intense pressure from the U.S. government.” At that point, he decided to “switch to the private sector and start renting out rooms” after inheriting a large apartment from his mother.

Had Cuba’s nuclear power station become operational, it is doubtful the island would be facing its current energy crisis.

Despite a small recovery between 2021 and 2022, after Cuba’s GDP in 2020 contracted by 10.9 percent as COVID-19 effectively shut down international tourism, the island’s economic crisis has been worsened by the Trump administration’s fuel embargo. When U.S. President Donald Trump began to take action against Venezuela’s oil shipments to Cuba in 2025, which approximated 26,500 barrels per day, Cubans saw a serious reduction of fuel on the island. On January 29, the Trump administration formalized the oil sanctions on Cuba by signing Executive Order 14380, which did not simply add another sanction on the island, but instead, created a mechanism to penalize third countries that supply oil to Cuba. Should a country provide crude oil or petroleum products, then the United States government can impose further tariffs on that country’s goods entering the U.S.

For Amalia Díaz Pérez, a 21-years old recent graduate in philosophy from the University of Havana, the Trump administration’s oil embargo disrupted her final year of study. Speaking to Truthout, she said:

The total blockade of fuel imports — with only one ship arriving in nine months — caused public transportation to disappear and reduced daily electricity availability to a minimum. Consequently, my study conditions and most of my daily recreational activities were affected. Compounding this situation, household chores became increasingly difficult due to the strain of the nationwide fuel shortage placed on water and …

author: anred
title: Flávio Bolsonaro y Lula van a segunda vuelta en Brasil
content:
Con casi el 100% de las mesas escrutadas, Flávio Bolsonaro se impone con el 47,05% de los votos y suma en total 56.082.216 votos. Este resultado no le alcanza para ganar la presidencias, por lo que se disputará una segunda vuelta con el actual presidente Lula Da Silva que consiguió 45,14% de los votos, que equivalen a 53.799.870. Las elecciones se dan en un contexto de extrema polarización, incertidumbre e injerencia del imperialismo yanqui. El resultado de las elecciones brasileñas tiene un especial peso en la balanza de las fuerzas políticas en Latino América. Tanto por el tamaño de la economía de Brasil como por la polarización entre el actual presidente Lula y el hijo de Bolsonaro subordinado al alineamiento del continente a Trump, el Escudo de las Américas y su doctrina de seguridad Donroe.

Por La Izquierda Diario.


Distintos analistas sostienen que el voto indeciso fue el que sorprendió en esta primera vuelta al volcarse a favor de Flavio Bolsonaro, que quedó dos puntos arriba de Lula. Este resultado refleja lo que las encuestas captaron días antes, una mejora de Bolsonaro quien capitalizó el voto útil de otras fuerzas conservadoras.


La presión del imperialismo parece haber surtido efecto como en la Argentina en las elecciones intermedias de 2027. Allí con el respaldo de dinero y la amenaza de retirar el apoyo y hundir las finanzas del Estado, de la mano del Secretario del Tesoro yanqui Scott Bessent. En Brasil, la amenaza se materializó con el cierre de consulados y la embajada por una supuesta cuestión de seguridad que la Policía Federal investigó y descartó. Además, está el antecedente de Venezuela y todas las acciones de presión con aranceles, y otras presiones diplomáticas sobre el gobierno de Lula.


Por otro lado, en todos estos años de gobierno petista no se cambió la estructura de la nación dependiente del imperialismo, así como tampoco se resolvieron las diferencias sociales, el racismo ni la concentración de tierras en manos de los latifundistas. Los salarios bajos y las familias endeudadas demuestran eso. No es solo el grave tema de las apuestas on line, son los ingresos de las familias, cada vez peores.


Cronología de este domingo 4 de octubre


22:41


«Brasil quiere un cambio»


Después del triunfo en primera vuelta, el candidato opositor Flávio Bolsonaro habló desde su bunker en Brasilia y aseguró que «Brasil quiere un cambio», sin hacer mención a la fallida presidencia de su padre.


También afirmó que este resultado muestra el fin del PT (Partido dos Trabalhadores) y dijo estar muy contento con los resultados regionales.


22:25


Un resultado inesperado


A poco de conocerse los resultados oficiales, Lula habló dió un discurso diciendo que el resultado lo había sorprendido y hasta aseguró que había confiado en que ganaba en primera vuelta.


Pensando en el próximo round, le dijo a sus seguidores que en la segunda vuelta «mostraremos la verdadera foto de Brasil.» También afirmó que su campaña se centrará en convencer a todos los que se ausentaron de las urnas de la importancia de ir a votar.


22:01


Segunda vuelta confirmada


Con casi el 100% de las mesas escrutadas, Flavio Bolsonaro se impone con el 47,05% de los votos y suma en total 56.082.216 votos. Este resultado no le alcanza para ganar la presidencia, por lo que se disputará una segunda vuelta con el actual presidente Lula Da Silva que consiguió 45,14% de los votos, que equivalen a 53.799.870.


Muy lejos se ubica el tercer candidato, Augusto Cury, con algo menos del 3%. Cury adelantó que no apoyará a ningún candidato en la segunda vuelta.


20:30


El Partido Liberal acumula gobernadores


Según resultados proyectados, los candidatos del partido de Bolsonaro fueron electos en Rio Grande do Sul, Rondonia, Roraima y Santa Catarina, donde reelige. Además, disputa en una segunda vuelta los estados de Paraná y Rio de Janeiro, donde actualmente gobierna, para un posible total de 6 estados.


San Pablo, el distrito electoral con mas peso y centro económico más importante del país, queda en manos del mismo gobernador de la ultraderecha, Tarcísio de Freitas, que no es del partido del Bolsonaro PL, sino de otro de la derecha, República. author: CMI Argentina
title: Claudio Katz: “Hay que construir la izquierda para derrotar a Milei”
content:
Tras la repercusión de la Marcha de la Bronca, Claudio Katz analizó el rol de la izquierda en la coyuntura actual, donde juegan cada vez más fuerte dos variables: el retroceso de Milei y un potencial estallido económico.


Las incógnitas sobre el peronismo, la apuesta del establishment a perpetuar el esquema de ajuste, explotación laboral y saqueo del país que logró establecer durante la actual gestión, la impunidad de la Corte Suprema y la agresividad del imperialismo estadounidense en la región son datos ineludibles del escenario presente ante los cuales la izquierda deberá plantearse nuevas tácticas y compromisos, consideró Katz, si quiere llegar al gobierno y disputar el poder.


Indymedia: – ¿Cómo ves el papel de la izquierda luego de la Marcha de la Bronca?


Claudio Katz:

 – Está cumpliendo un papel muy positivo ante todo en la acción callejera. La marcha fue un éxito

 por la

 concurrencia y el impacto de un acto político, que traspasó la resistencia social y democrática a los atropellos de Milei. Contrastó frontalmente con la capitulación de la CGT que deja pasar el ajuste.


La movilización alcanzó el nivel más alto de una convocatoria de

la izquierda. Superó lo conseguido con la “Plaza del No” en los años 90 y con las grandes concentraciones que en el pasado articulaba el

PC. Exhibió un nivel de politización muy superior a las marchas piqueteras e ilustró nuevamente cómo gravita la izquierda en las coyunturas de inmovilidad del peronismo.


Esa indefinición del justicialismo se vio por ejemplo cuando ganó Alfonsín, durante el neoliberalismo de Menem o en la época de Alianza. Actualmente, vuelve a aflorar por momentos y por eso hubo cierta presencia de militantes o simpatizantes del peronismo en la marcha. Igualmente te diría que el dato más significativo fue la centralidad de Myriam

Bregman. La movilización consolidó su protagonismo y la consiguiente incidencia de la izquierda en las próximas elecciones.


Indymedia: –

Pero cuál es la proyección electoral efectiva de Myriam, porque las encuestas resaltan una imagen muy positiva sin equivalencia en la intención de voto…


Claudio Katz: – Hay infinitas especulaciones sobre esa relación y no tiene mucho sentido obsesionarse con el tema, cuando falta más de un año para la elección. El número de votos que lograría el FIT-U depende de escenarios muy

abiertos con dos variables centrales: el retroceso de Milei y un potencial estallido económico, que podría repetir lo ocurrido tantas veces en la Argentina.


Foto:

Nicolas Solo ((i))


Nadie sabe si el gobierno podrá sostener el tipo de cambio hasta el 2027. La recesión, la pobreza y el endeudamiento podrían desencadenar el mismo tipo de rebelión que sepultó a De la Rúa o la protesta masiva que derrotó a Macri. No cabe duda que la izquierda estará en la primera línea de ese eventual estallido.


Pero en cualquier caso su crecimiento dependerá de lo que suceda con el peronismo y en ese campo hay varios cursos posibles de división o cohesión y de amoldamiento conservador o resurgimiento progresista.


Por el momento se verifica una gran fractura en el justicialismo, entre corrientes de adaptación y crítica al modelo que la clase dominante apuntala con Milei. En general predomina la postura de no decir nada a la espera de lo que más conviene. Pero mientras tanto, un fascista como Cúneo participa del espacio de Kicillof, que a su vez emite mensajes de adaptación tipo Alberto Fernández y elude comentarios básicos de denuncia del genocidio de Palestina. Pero lo que haría como presidente es un misterio. Conviene recordar que nadie imaginaba el giro progresista de Néstor y Cristina antes del 2001 y sería un error ignorar la recomposición que logró el peronismo al calor de la gestión kirchnerista.


Indymedia: –

 ¿Por qué importa ese dato?


Claudio Katz: – Porque conforma el escenario en el que actúa la izquierda. Desconociendo ese hecho es muy difícil desenvolver estrategias para derrotar a Milei, revertir el ajuste y reconquistar los derechos populares. Ese camino transita por llegar al gobierno y disputar el poder, mediante frentes comunes y acuerdos de lucha con los sectores dispuestos a reconstruir el país, apostando a un gobierno que en sus primeros días de gestión revierta de un plumazo todo lo hecho por Milei.

title: +++ Die Demo ohne Inhalt meldet sich zu Wort +++
content:
Gegen Ihre Repression


Am Sonntag, 11.10.2026, geht es wieder auf die Strasse. Und es hängt ein dunkler Schatten über dem Tag. Das war zu erwarten und wir möchten uns dazu nun positionieren. Klar ist, wir werden auf die Strasse gehen, denn die Berner Shitshow des letzten Jahres lassen wir so nicht stehen.


Zunächst eine erneute Einordung der aktuellen Lage


Die Schweiz ist eine Mörderin. Zum einen bietet sie ein ruhiges Hinterland für andere Mörder*innen wie UBS, Palantir, Glencore, Syngenta, die Weltbank oder Valcambi. Andererseits bringt sie als Teil des US-imperialen Blocks seit hunderten von Jahren unsere Geschwister auf der ganzen Welt um. Auch wenn gerade alle Augen dem seltsam faszinierenden Spektal der Trump-Administration zuschauen, fallen weiterhin echte Bomben, werden weiterhin echte Menschen verdrängt, sterben weiterhin echte Kinder. Kurz: die Lage hat sich nicht verbessert, sie ist nur nicht mehr so interessant für die bürgerliche Presse. Für uns heisst das nur, dass alle bereits bestehenden Analysen zu Krieg und Genozid weiterhin anzuwenden sind. Sie zu wiederholen, sparen wir uns an dieser Stelle. Wer es noch nicht kapiert hat, wird für den Moment wohl selbst dahinter kommen müssen (gäu Alec).


Zur Demo


Wir wissen, viele Menschen sind verunsichert und trauen sich aufgrund der Repression nicht mehr, an diesem Tag ihre Wut auf die Strassen zu tragen. Schöne neue Demokratie. Genau diese Menschen wollen wir mit diesem Communiqué ansprechen.


Wir nehmen an, ihr wollt euch grundsätzlich auch nicht von der Repression unterkriegen lassen. Aber das von Medien, Politik und Bullen kreirte Klima macht einfach keine Lust die "Demokratie" zu leben. Wir verstehen das und haben eine Antwort: Eine kreative Anti-Kessel-Demo. Ein Konzept, um am 11. Oktober auf die Strasse zu gehen und trotz Repression ein Ereignis zu schaffen, das uns im Widerstand gegen unseren mörderischen Staat und im Kampf für eine andere Welt zusammenbringt und unsere Banden stärkt. Um nichts über die aktuellen Entwicklungen zur Anti-Kessel-Demo zu verpassen und am Tag selbst optimal vorbereitet zu sein, ist es wichtig, dass du dem Demoticker beitrittst. Die Links dazu findest du unten im Beitrag.


Zur Frage der Bewilligung


Wir leisten Widerstand gegen den Schweizer Staat und lassen unser Handeln darum nicht von ihm bewilligen. Was wäre das auch für eine witzlose Logik.


Für die Repression ist die Bewilligung immer der erste Angriffspunkt. Und angegriffen wird, wenn es der Polizei beliebt. Oder was war das bitte am Smash WEF dieses Jahr? Einer bereits aufgelösten Demo in den Rücken prügeln?


Zum prophezeiten "Aufstand"


Die Herrschenden dominieren die Medien - wir sagen, sie kontrollieren den Diskurs - indem sie selektiv berichten und unsere Inhalte verschweigen. Diese Kontrolle des Diskurses erlaubt es dem Staat der Öffentlichkeit zu vermitteln, unser Widerstand sei nicht legitim, verwirrt, sinnfrei oder sonst irgendwie falsch. Und unser Aufruf vorallem eine Ansage zur totalen Eskalation. Das wurde einwandfrei klar aus den bereits veröffentlichten Beiträgen, siehe NZZ, BZ, Blick. Die Demo ist zur Projektionsfläche für alle möglichen Ängste und Unzufriedenheiten der Bürgerlichen geworden. Das ist bei linken Demonstrationen nicht ungewöhnlich, doch gerade der 11. Oktober 2025 wird immerwieder als Referenzpunkt verwendet, um die Verschärfung staatlicher Repression und Überwachung zu rechfertigen. Um verfassungswidrige Repression gegen uns zu legitimieren und unsere Inhalte unsichtbar zu machen. Der Staatsapparat will uns verunmöglichen, das "Recht" auf Protest auszuleben und zeigt damit im Endeffekt, was Rechte für diese "rechtsbasierte Ordnung" bedeuten - nichts.


Zum vergangenen "Aufstand"


Lassen wir letztes Jahr nochmal Revue passieren. Es waren locker 10 000 Menschen auf der Strasse. Es war friedlich, bis die Demo mehr wollte, als nur eine Platzkundgebung auf dem Bundesplatz. Zu laufen war legitimes Anliegen. Die Reaktion darauf unverhältnismässig. Die Eskalation danach verhältnissmässig. Zerstört wurden vor allem die Scheiben von Banken, ein legitimes Ziel, gerade die UBS. Warum das "de la Casa" angefangen hat zu brennen, ist nicht geklärt. Dass es neben den 18 Verletzten Polizist*innen über 300 verletzte Demonstrant*innen gab, wird von der Politik kaum erwähnt. Die Schmierereien in der Innenstadt - hört doch auf zu jammern... Nein, der wirkliche Skandal sollte das Vorgehen der Bullen sein. Und die Kompliz*innenschaft bei Krieg …

author: Javier Moreno Zacarés
title: Fifteen Years Later
content:
Fifteen years after the indignados occupied the Puerta del Sol, Madrid’s central plaza is once again the locus of a mass movement that has brought Spain to a political impasse. How are we back here again? The immediate trigger was the eviction of an elderly tenant. Maricarmen Abascal, who had occupied her rent-capped apartment in central Madrid since 1956, was expelled from her home on 23 September after the investment fund Urbagestión acquired the property and exploited a legal loophole to quintuple her rent. Maricarmen’s age and vulnerability – the 87-year-old was removed on a hospital bed and has since died – made it a particularly egregious breach of the moral economy. The case struck a nerve, prompting a political storm; the government has now announced a snap election. As protests spread nationwide, the encampment at Puerta del Sol consolidated under the leadership of the Sindicato de Inquilinas, Madrid’s tenant union. Media outlets are reporting on the motions passed at the open-air general assembly. One decision has been of particular public interest: a general strike for the right to housing, announced for 11 November, a few weeks before the election.

The political elite faces a reckoning. At the outset of the current parliamentary term in 2023, the progressive coalition headed by Sánchez’s centre-left Socialist Party (PSOE) placed housing at the top of the agenda. The promises were ambitious: the provision of mass social housing, the imposition of rent controls, the reassertion of the public interest against rentier logics. Yet these commitments yielded little. This was partly due to the obstruction of the right, both in parliament and in the regional governments under its control. But a share of the blame lies in the ambivalence of the Socialist Party itself, whose ministers have repeatedly expressed discomfort with what they regard as excessive regulation of housing. The junior coalition partner Sumar, a nebulous alliance of progressive parties, has proven feeble in holding the Socialists to account. They are now also a target of the protests, who charge the entire governing alliance of complicity with the rentiers. Amid the fury in the streets, Sumar’s cabinet members hastened to pressure the Socialist housing minister, Isabel Rodríguez – herself a landlord who owns multiple properties – to approve emergency measures to block evictions and institute permanent rolling contracts, both key demands of the tenant unions. Last Friday, both measures were struck down in parliament, to the anger of the masses gathered outside.

That a recalcitrant right-wing opposition – comprising the conservative People’s Party (PP) and the far-right Vox – would block the measures was entirely predictable. What was less so was that the deciding vote would be cast by an ally of the government: the centre-right Junts, party of the Catalan-nationalist bourgeoisie. The vote revealed a peculiarity of the Spanish conjuncture. Though the right-wing bloc is the largest in parliament, it is divided along nationalist lines, fractures the government has exploited – drawing support from the Catalan right to keep the Spanish unionist right out of power. It was always an unstable arrangement, premised on nation trumping class. On the housing question, the plurinational right voted in alignment with its shared interests (Junts has the largest proportion of landlords in parliament).

The Spanish right now enjoys a comfortable lead in the polls, which point to a PP–Vox coalition if elections were held tomorrow. But the wind is blowing in an uncomfortable direction for them. Over the past week, public opinion has swung massively in favour of regulating house prices, even among a slim majority of right-wing voters. In a matter of days, the protests have shifted the national conversation away from the right’s preferred talking points of crime and migration, overwriting a summer of hysteria around the border crisis in Ceuta. They have also deflected attention from the corruption scandals afflicting PSOE: only last June, a former minister in Sánchez’s cabinet was sentenced to twenty-four years in prison for influence-peddling related to substandard Covid-19 face masks. Ever the survivor, Sánchez has seized the moment with a characteristically audacious move. He has framed the election on 29 November as a plebiscite on the housing question, shifting the blame for it onto the right and boldly appealing to the electorate to ‘subdue the elites’ …

title: «12 de Octubre, nada que celebrar»: pueblos originarios marchan contra los desalojos y la extranjerización de la tierra
content:
Marcha del Contrafestejo del 12 de octubre de 2024. Foto: archivo Nicolás Parodi / Página 12


Bajo la consigna “¡Nada que celebrar, muchas luchas que sostener!”, la Organización de Comunidades y Pueblos Originarios (ORCOPO) convocó a una marcha y contrafestejo para este lunes 12 de octubre, a las 18, en Plaza de los Dos Congresos. La jornada de lucha denunciará el avance de los desalojos, la criminalización de las comunidades indígenas, la extranjerización de la tierra, los proyectos extractivistas, la entrega, el saqueo y el despojo, en un escenario de creciente conflictividad territorial luego del reciente fallo de la Corte Suprema. La convocatoria se da en el marco de la confirmación judicial del desalojo de la Lof Inalef, en Río Negro, y una nueva amenaza contra la Lof Melo, en Neuquén. Ambos casos se suman a otros conflictos territoriales que atraviesan comunidades originarias en distintas regiones del país y que, para las organizaciones indígenas, evidencian una ofensiva sobre sus territorios en paralelo con el desmantelamiento de herramientas de protección y la reactivación de la derogación de la Ley de Tierras Rurales. También exigen justicia por Rafael Nahuel y libertad para quienes permanecen detenidos por luchar.

Por ANRed.

author: Unknown
title: Çelik: No budget’ for students’ demands, yet 7.4 billion TL transferred to foundations
content:
As universities begin the autumn semester of the 2026–2027 academic year, a student at Istanbul Technical University (ITÜ) was expelled from a dormitory run by the Credit and Dormitories Institution (KYK) on the grounds that they had failed to pass the preparatory year in a single semester. With nowhere to stay, the student was forced to take refuge in the university library for days. They are now trying to continue their education while working to support themselves.


The experience of the ITÜ student is one example of the problems faced by thousands of students who are forced to work to continue their education, only to be labelled academically unsuccessful as a result and deprived of their right to housing.


Being a university student in Turkey is increasingly becoming less an educational experience and more a struggle for survival. The monthly scholarship or student loan of 4,000 TL (some 73 euros) provided to undergraduate students by the Ministry of Youth and Sports is not even enough to cover their basic needs, particularly in the face of rental prices and living costs in major cities.


Students forced working while studying


Rapidly rising rents for private dormitories and apartments in major cities have made KYK dormitories virtually the only housing option for students. Unable to receive sufficient financial support from their families due to the deepening economic crisis, students are forced to work in insecure and harsh conditions to make ends meet. When they cannot devote enough time to their studies as a result, the system labels them “unsuccessful”. This “failure” is then punished by depriving them of one of the most fundamental human rights: the right to housing.


ANF spoke with Senem Çelik of the

We Cannot Afford to Live Movement

, which has been working for days to bring the expulsion of an ITÜ student from a KYK dormitory to public attention, about the housing crisis and poverty experienced by students.


Referring to the mother who appealed for help on Instagram for her son, who had been expelled from his dormitory, saying, 'I don’t want my son to be left on the street. He hadn’t slept for two days, and neither have I,' Senem Çelik described what had happened: “Recently, we heard the desperate plea of a mother who explained that her child had been expelled from the dormitory for having to repeat a year. A fellow student at ITÜ has been trying to get through each day and continue their education since the semester began, sometimes staying in the library and sometimes at friends’ homes. The reason our fellow students have had to continue their education this way is that they have been forced to work while studying, which in turn has meant having to repeat the year.”


Stating that the

We Cannot Afford to Live Movemen

t has been working for years to bring the housing crisis facing young people to public attention and secure concrete gains for students, Senem Çelik said the housing problem could not be explained solely through economic indicators. She pointed out that the way university bureaucracies operate, treating students as secondary concerns, and their proposed solutions, which run counter to the ordinary realities of life, further deepen the injustices students experience.


Çelik said university students face not only housing difficulties and poverty but also declining educational quality, the failure of democratic mechanisms within universities to function, sexism in academia and harassment. She added that these problems cannot be considered separately from the deep poverty and the condition of being “excluded from citizenship” experienced by broad sections of society.


Senem Çelik said: “For example, struggles against the injustices experienced by students affected by earthquakes require us to connect with all citizens whose needs are ignored for the sake of profit and to support their struggles. Campaigns against poor living conditions in student dormitories bring together all students who cannot afford to heat their homes with natural gas or even pay for their meals.”


She added: “Alongside the exclusion of the public from all mechanisms of governance and oversight, students at universities, which should be centres of science and free thought, are increasingly being excluded from all decision-making and oversight mechanisms as universities are privatised and run like companies. Students do not even have a say in matters concerning their own living spaces in the dormitories …

author: Helmut Weiss
title: „Was wir nicht verdienen, zahlen wir nicht“ – eine landesweite Initiative in Spanien organisiert Mietstreik
content:
Dossier


„…

Es ist wahrlich kein Aprilscherz. Am 1. April 2020 treten nun viele Familien, Selbstständige sowie kleine und mittlere Firmen im ganzen spanischen Staat in den Mietenstreik. Mietergewerkschaften, wie sie ausgehend von Katalonien ab 2017 wie das „Sindicat de Llogaters i Llogateres“ gegründet haben, und soziale Organisation rufen zum Streik gegen fehlende Notmaßnahmen der sozialdemokratischen Regierung für die einfache Bevölkerung auf. Die 200 Initiativen schlagen vor, ab April die Miete nicht mehr zu bezahlen. (…) Eigentlich hatten sich die Mietergewerkschaften wegen explodierender Mieten gegründet. Sie forderten bisher vor allem stärkere Mieterrechte und eine Regulierung der explodierenden Mieten, vor denen spanische Gesetze praktisch nicht schützen. Einige der Aktivisten hatten Hoffnungen in die neue Regierung gesetzt, doch sie wurden massiv enttäuscht

…“ – aus dem

Beitrag „Mietenstreik wegen Coronavirus in Spanien“ von Ralf Streck am 01. April 2020 bei telepolis


 über die landesweite Initiative. Siehe dazu die weitere Entwicklung und Hintergründe:


„Ni una Maricarmen más“: Zwangsräumung der 87-jährigen Maricarmen Abascal treibt massive Proteste gegen Wohnungsnot und Mietwucher über Madrid hinaus an 


Die 87-jährige Maricarmen, deren Zwangsräumung die Bewegung in Spanien radikalisiert hat, ist vor der erkämpften Rückkehr in ihre Wohnung erschöpft gestorben 


„

Die 87-Jährige ist am Mittwoch im Krankenhaus Gregorio Marañón in Madrid verstorben, wie die Mietervereinigung in einer Erklärung bestätigte (…) In dieser Erklärung, die auch von ihrer Familie und ihrer Anwältin unterzeichnet wurde, erinnern sie daran, dass sie seit der Zwangsräumung im Krankenhaus lag. „Zwar wurde eine historische Einigung erzielt, die ihr die Rückkehr in ihre Wohnung ermöglicht hätte, doch diese Lösung kam viel zu spät“, bedauern sie. Die Unterzeichner sind der Ansicht, dass die Ereignisse nach ihrer Zwangsräumung – Massendemonstrationen, Zeltlager auf den Plätzen, vorgezogene Wahlen und der Aufruf zu einem Generalstreik – „einen Wendepunkt in der Geschichte dieses Landes“ darstellen, warnen jedoch, dass „der Preis, den wir dafür gezahlt haben, zu hoch war“. Und sie verabschieden sich mit der Bitte, die sie ihnen immer wieder gesagt hat: „Kämpft, kämpft weiter für das, was euch gehört.“


Dank des gesellschaftlichen Drucks stand zum ersten Mal in Spanien eine zwangsgeräumte Person kurz davor, in ihr Zuhause zurückzukehren, nachdem der Eigentümer bereit war, einen neuen Mietvertrag abzuschließen. Dennoch hatten die Zwangsräumung und die vorangegangenen Versuche Maricarmen körperlich stark mitgenommen, sodass sie sich in ihren letzten Lebensjahren nur noch im Rollstuhl fortbewegen konnte und bei den alltäglichen Verrichtungen auf Hilfe angewiesen war. Hinter ihr lagen fast sieben Jahre gerichtlicher Auseinandersetzungen, um in ihrem Zuhause bleiben zu können. In den letzten Monaten hatte sich ihr körperlicher Zustand verschlechtert. Sie hatte an Muskelmasse verloren, hatte Schwierigkeiten beim Essen und sagte, dass sich sogar ihre Stimme verändert habe. „Es hat mich in jeder Hinsicht beeinträchtigt. Ich bin jetzt nicht mehr ich selbst“, erzählte sie zwei Tage, bevor sie ihr Haus verließ

…“ span.

Artikel von Lucía Franco und Beatriz Olaizola vom 7.10.2026 in El Pais online


 (maschinenübersetzt) und auch:


Der Verband der Mieterinnengewerkschaften ruft zu einer Schweigeminute und einem Generalstreik für Maricarmen auf


„

Heute, Freitag, um 12 Uhr mittags an allen Arbeits- und Bildungseinrichtungen im ganzen Land. Der Aufruf des Verbandes der Mieterinnengewerkschaften erfolgt, nachdem sich die PP und Vox am Donnerstag geweigert hatten, in der Madrider Regionalversammlung eine Schweigeminute für Maricarmen einzulegen, mit der Begründung, sie wollten „nicht zu ihrer politischen Instrumentalisierung“ in einer „interessengeführten Kampagne“ beitragen, obwohl gerade die Verstorbene selbst dazu aufgerufen hatte, für die politische Sache gegen Zwangsräumungen und für menschenwürdigen Wohnraum zu kämpfen und sich zu mobilisieren. (…) Deshalb bitten wir dich, alle Arbeitnehmerinnen und Arbeitnehmer sowie die gesamte Gesellschaft, morgen, Freitag, um 12 Uhr mittags an allen Arbeits- und Bildungseinrichtungen des Staates eine Schweigeminute einzulegen. Außerdem bitten wir dich, dich darauf vorzubereiten, dass wir am 11. November einen historischen Generalstreik durchführen. Wir werden nicht aufhören, bis wir alles verändert …

author: Harriet Williamson
title: The Greens Are Still Relevant. They Just Need a Strategy
content:
Labour has held on in former prime minister Keir Starmer’s vacated seat of Holborn and St Pancras – a constituency the party has never lost since its creation in 1983 – with Green leader Zack Polanski coming in second. Camden council leader and Starmer ally Sagal Abdi-Wali won 45% of the vote, down 3.75% on Labour’s 2024 general election result, while the Greens more than tripled their vote share, taking 33%.


There are certainly some reasons for optimism among Green supporters this morning, while Polanski is asked on the mainstream media round if he’ll now be standing down as party leader until all our ears bleed. (Answer, no he won’t.)


The Cortado

Ash Sarkar

 and

Steven Methven

, every Monday and Friday morning.

The Greens took more of the vote last night than their combined 2024 vote share with Starmer’s nearest challenger, the independent and former South African MP Andrew Feinstein. The local campaign group born out of Feinstein’s challenge to Starmer on his record on Gaza, the Camden People’s Alliance, endorsed Polanski this time around.


While turnout was down on the last election – 2024’s “loveless landslide” – at 39% compared to 54%, we saw a 13% Labour to Green swing.


Ultimately, around 3,000 votes separated the victorious Abdi-Wali (12,292) and Polanski (8,928), and prime minister Andy Burnham can breathe a sigh of relief that the first major electoral test to his premiership is won.


There’s no doubt that Abdi-Wali benefitted from the ‘Burnham bounce’. She might be smiley and local, but her council carries

an appalling record on housing

 in the borough – a brief she was directly responsible for as Camden’s former housing lead – and she was tainted by her association with Starmer and the Starmite project that,

according to a valuable

 two-part

Tribune deep-dive

, birthed her candidacy.


There was something vaguely nauseating about Abdi-Wali campaigning on a message of “hope” for the people of Holborn and St Pancras when

on top of being council leader

 from May of this year, her party has always held the seat – including with a sitting prime minister. If Labour was going to bring hope to this constituency, it would’ve done it already.


But Abdi-Wali,

‘ming-vased’ by her party

, received remarkably little mainstream press scrutiny throughout the campaign (

remind you of anyone?

), as the – allow me a moment to adjust my chic tinfoil hat – political-media class closed ranks against the Greens.


The drop in last night’s

Lib Dem vote share

 alone can be taken as a suggestion of negative mobilisation against the Green party, who’ve weathered months of bad faith attacks after the political and media establishment swung back into action following

a Polanski tweet

 around the Golders Green stabbing.


Polanski’s personal approval ratings continue to show the strain, with the Green leader dipping four points below Nigel Farage on -28 in a

More in Common poll

 on Wednesday. The same pollster also has Westminster voting intention for the Greens

on 8%

, while

YouGov shows 11%

 – down from a March high of 21%. It’s unlikely that a deluge of

negative attention

 and the resurgence of an antisemitism narrative over the Greens’ recently-passed ‘Zionism is Racism’ conference motion will have helped matters, either.


While the result of this hotly-contested byelection was ultimately closer than the bookies’ odds (16/1 on Polanski yesterday) made out, Gorton and Denton this was not. The terrain has changed, and the Greens have not yet adapted quickly or robustly enough with it. Burnham in Number 10 requires a different approach for the party to

the one that worked

 under Starmer’s toxic premiership.


But

in her acceptance speech

 this morning, Abdi-Wali accepted key parts of the Greens’ electoral programme – public ownership of water and addressing the housing crisis. Polanski’s party is reshaping Labour in the face of everything the political and media elite can throw at it.


There’s no question of Green irrelevance, only of Green strategy. In my book, that’s a reason to be hopeful.

author: Brian Hioe
title: Xindian Eviction Case Illustrates Recurrent Dynamics
content:
A FORCED EVICTION case in Xindian has drawn concern from Taiwanese civil society, with long-term residents of a historic structure possibly forced to vacate it in the near future.

In particular, the eviction case revolves around the Tsai Jin-mu house, which has been inhabited by the Lai family for eighty years and was built by their grandfather, Tsai Jin-mu. The Lai family previously sought to seek cultural preservation status for the structure, as an example of architecture that dated to the Japanese colonial period. However, this was denied by the Cultural Bureau of the New Taipei City government in June, which concluded that the bricks used in the structure are similar in size to those that date from the Japanese colonial period, but that this could not prove that the structure indeed dated from then.

Other structures in the neighborhood have already been demolished, starting from 2006, because of the construction of the Liugong Canal. Nevertheless, the Lai family was unexpectedly sued in 2014, demanding the return of the land, having found out that the Irrigation Association had sold the land in 2012 to a developer for a low price without notifying. Although the Lai family had expressed a desire to purchase the land 60 years prior, at the time, the Irrigation Association had claimed that the land was government property that was hard to deal with.

Consequently, litigation over the property has been ongoing for over a decade. Though the Lai family has housing plates and taxation documents, and the house had a household registration and allowed for the payment of utility bills and taxes, the Lai family has lost many of the lawsuits it filed over the land. Among the justifications for the rulings were not filing applications for the land, though previously the Lai family had been ruled to have the rights to apply for the land.

In 2021, the Control Yuan published a report stating that the Irrigation Association had treated the land as unused in its auction process, which was procedurally incorrect. Experts on land use in Taiwan have highlighted the case as one that touches on issues of transitional justice, given that the dispute over the property rights stems from the various historical transitions Taiwan saw in the 20th century. Likewise, the International Tribunal on Evictions has raised concerns about the case.

The residents of the home have been successful in securing stays of demolition in the past. Nevertheless, it is possible that the Tsai Jin-mu House will prove to be a case similar to when other communities were forced out of their homes in Taipei, with examples in the past decade including the Huaguang Community and Daguan Community. Though the Lai family has hosted screenings and otherwise linked with Taiwanese civil society groups, there is not as much attention to cases of forced urban evictions as there was in the years prior to the Sunflower Movement, even with a KMT mayoral administration in charge of New Taipei. What comes next remains to be seen.

La comunidad universitaria vuelve a organizarse en las calles frente al incumplimiento de la Ley de Financiamiento Universitario por parte de Javier Milei. title: Les personnels du lycée Brossolette soutiennent leurs élèves dans la mobilisation
content:
Ce mardi 13 octobre est une nouvelle journée de mobilisation dans l'éducation, l'université et la recherche. normalement

author: Amy Goodman
title: Tens of Thousands Protest in India Against Modi Government’s Voter Roll Purges
content:
At least 7,000 people in New Delhi were detained on Saturday.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Tens of thousands of people in India have taken to the streets in recent days to protest the deletion of 130 million names from the voter rolls, a large majority of which are believed to be opposed to Narendra Modi’s ruling BJP party. The demonstrations, joined by leaders from India’s opposition parties, are being led by students and the youth-led “Cockroach” movement. Tens of thousands of security forces, including paramilitary and police, were out on the streets over the weekend cracking down on the uprising, detaining protesters en masse, including lawyers, journalists and protest leaders.

The demonstrations “represent an outpouring of anger, of frustration at what many Indians feel is the fact that their democracy has been taken away,” says Shoaib Daniyal, political editor of Scroll, who was arrested on Saturday along with 7,000 other protesters. He points out that “the deletions have affected Muslims far more than they have affected other Indians.”

On Monday, in one of largest recent protests in India’s capital of New Delhi, India’s main opposition leader, Rahul Gandhi of the Congress Party, led a march to the Supreme Court of India. “This march has become a people’s march, with all of them heading towards this constitutional authority, which they feel should safeguard the rights of Indian people, especially this very basic right to vote,” says Jahnavi Sen, managing editor of The Wire.

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

ANJALI KAMAT: In India, the right-wing government of Narendra Modi is facing its biggest challenge yet in 12 years in power, as tens of thousands of people have taken to the streets to protest what they call vote theft. At issue is the deletion of 130 million names from the voter rolls, and the vast majority of those deletions are believed to be opposed to Prime Minister Modi’s ruling BJP party.

The protests are being led by students and the youth Cockroach movement and joined by leaders from the opposition parties. They’re demanding the resignation of the chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, and an overhaul of the electoral system. The Cockroach movement started after the chief justice of India’s Supreme Court compared unemployed youth to cockroaches earlier this year.

Today, in one of largest recent protests in India’s capital of New Delhi, India’s main opposition leader, Rahul Gandhi of the Congress Party, is leading a march to the Supreme Court of India. Speaking to reporters earlier today, Gandhi reiterated the call for the election commissioner to resign.

RAHUL GANDHI: Narendra Modi is blocking the whole town, is putting 30,000-40,000 police people outside. For what? Because the opposition is asking one question: Prove to us that you have not cheated in the election. Prove to us that you’ve not cheated in the election.

AMY GOODMAN: The Modi government put New Delhi in lockdown ahead of Saturday’s protests, canceling trains to the city, shutting down metro stations, even suspending mobile internet in large parts of Delhi. Tens of thousands of security forces, including paramilitary and police, were mobilized across the city, and at least 7,000 people were detained Saturday alone, including protest leaders, lawyers and journalists. This is a protester speaking to reporters from inside a van where he was detained.

PROTESTER: [translated] The Modi government is scared of us. That is why we have been picked up from halfway. We didn’t even know where they were trying to bring us. [in English] This is just fear. And they are afraid of us because they have done something wrong, and you cannot do something wrong with the people of this country, man.

AMY GOODMAN: Several Cockroach movement leaders were also arrested right off the plane as they arrived in Delhi for the protest Saturday morning. After being released the next morning, Saurav Das, one of the leaders of the Cockroach People’s Party, vowed protests would continue.

SAURAV DAS: The protests are on. The protests will go on. [translated] The youth of the country have woken up. The youth of the country are asking for accountability. The peaceful protests will go on until they fix accountability. And now the protests will not only happen in Delhi, but in the whole country.

author: Ruhi Bhasin
title: How Gen Z Protests Are Reshaping Politics in Asia
content:
Asia has seen a surge of “Gen Z protests,” led by a generation tired of accepting the status quo and increasingly using social media to drive change in deeply entrenched political systems. In India, protests over the education system helped force the education minister’s resignation in 2026. Protests in Bangladesh and Nepal in 2024 and 2025, respectively, led to government changes. These protests have helped expose fractured political structures in these countries.

Governments in several South and Southeast Asian countries have done little to address the economic distress and corruption plaguing them. The Gen Z citizens, who are facing the brunt of these crumbling systems, are increasingly demanding accountability and justice, using social media to fight back, organize, document events, and press their demands. Despite efforts to suppress them, these protests have brought political change. Whether these movements can sustain solidarity and organize beyond immediate demands to pursue lasting reforms remains to be seen.

In India, the Bharatiya Janata Party-led government has been in power for more than 12 years, having first been elected in 2014. Press freedom and other democratic safeguards have come under pressure during its tenure; Sweden’s V-Dem Institute has classified India as an “electoral autocracy.” As stated by an August 2026 Time report, “Modi has consolidated his grip on all manner of national institutions in recent years: from the media, where pliant owners have repeatedly bent the knee to the administration, to election authorities, which in a recent state poll erased millions of names from voter rolls in a move widely seen as benefiting Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).”

India has been facing increasing unemployment among its educated youth, even though the government has consistently maintained these claims to be false. The country’s youth have also been contending with an education system marked by repeated paper leaks. In May 2026, the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test for undergraduate medical admissions was canceled over paper-leak allegations, fueling anger over the examination system.

Meanwhile, during the same month, the Supreme Court Chief Justice’s comparison of unemployed youth to “parasites” and “cockroaches” led to the formation of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) by Abhijeet Dipke, an Indian student from Boston University who graduated in 2025 with a master’s in public relations. The CJP’s Instagram account amassed 20 million followers within days, according to Time. Dipke eventually returned to India on June 6. Anger over the government’s mismanagement of the education system soon moved from social media to the streets as thousands of Gen Z showed up at Jantar Mantar, a popular protest site in India’s capital, New Delhi, with their main demand being the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

As the protest gained momentum and spread, authorities resorted to force against demonstrators. Young protesters used social media to document events on the ground and responded with “humor and grit.” For them, the protest wasn’t about any political party but rather about ensuring accountability for a broken education system. They finally succeeded in forcing Pradhan to resign on July 25, 2026.

“In the end, the young cockroaches proved so resilient because Modi’s regime of control had no punishment or humiliation to threaten them with beyond what the system already inflicts on them every day. These young men and women had reached a point where they felt they had no voice in the existing order—and nothing left to lose,” explains the Time report. Allegations of links to foreign funding were also made against the movement, but the Ministry of External Affairs said it had “no information” to confirm these allegations.

In July 2026, after the protest ended, the government introduced a bill to amend the public examinations law, and Modi announced an examination reform task force. Whether these actions succeed in reforming the education system and whether the CJP can keep pushing for their proper implementation remains to be seen.

The CJP announced another campaign in September 2026 demanding chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over alleged manipulation of voter rolls. Street protests followed in October, with opposition parties and civil society groups participating. The Election Commission denies the allegations. These protests will test the CJP’s ability …

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Journalists Arrested Under Terrorism Act at Protest Against Israeli Arms Company
content:
Police in Leicester arrested at least five journalists under the Terrorism Act while they were reporting on a protest outside a drone factory owned by an Israeli arms company.


The

journalists

 were detained for two hours last Thursday at a UAV Tactical Systems factory

owned by

 Elbit Systems, which makes weapons that are used in Israel’s genocide in Gaza.  


Those arrested included two reporters for the Leicester Gazette and three freelance photojournalists. Police only let them go once they shared information to prove they attended the protest in their capacity as journalists, Press Gazette reported. 


A photographer who goes by the name Just Barold on social media was

among those detained

. 


“Multiple journalists including myself were arrested under section 13 of the Terrorism Act for going to work,” he wrote. “An officer told me that I would be de-arrested as soon as I gave my details despite identifying myself as a journalist with a press card.


“Our arresting officer was unable to articulate what caused the suspicion but it did instantly vanish when they got my name, address and date of birth.” 


Press advocacy group Reporters Without Borders said in a statement that it was “deeply concerned to hear of the arrest of journalists covering a protest in Leicester, particularly given they had identified themselves as such to police.”


It added: “No journalist should have to weigh the risk of arrest against their duty to inform the public. If reporters cannot cover protests freely, the public is left in the dark about events it has a right to know about. Policing and government must ensure that journalists are free to do their jobs without interference.”


In total, police

arrested 35 people

 at the protest under section 13 of the Terrorism Act. Some of the protesters held signs reading, “I oppose genocide. I support Palestine Action”. The proscribed group has frequently targeted and damaged factories owned by Elbit Systems.

author: Akingbade Tope Olatidoye
title: Humor Is Not A Joke: A Situation Analysis of Artistic Freedoms in Nigeria – A Cartoon Draws Blood!
content:
In March 2025, I posted a single-panel cartoon on a civic WhatsApp group that caricatured the Supreme Court: a judge in full wig, a smiling, hulking anarchical figure beside a broken gavel. It was meant as a provocation — a civic jab that asked whether a court’s public trust can survive repeated, controversial decisions.  In this case, I was questioning the role Nigeria’s apex court had played in preparing the illegal grounds for the unconstitutional suspension of the elected governor of Rivers State in the oil-rich Niger Delta region which had been the scene of many conflicts around resource control and rival politics. The reaction was immediate. Group messages ranged from sarcasm to outright threats. One respondent typed,  “Go commit a crime and let your case get to the Supreme Court — I want to check something.”

The joke had not landed as a joke; it was a test. 


That exchange is not an isolated outrage; it’s a tiny weather vane. The barrage of abuse, the quick escalation from critique to menace, and the invocation of criminality as a retort reveal how fragile public satire has become. 


In Nigeria, mocking power — even in a small civic space — can trigger legal alarms, social shaming, and organized campaigns of trolling that function as a form of extra-judicial censorship. The cartoon and the reaction around it are a microcosm: creative dissent colliding with legal instruments, moral outrage, and digital mobs down the timeline of Nigeria’s nationhood.


From satire to statute: the long shadow of the law


Suppression of artistic expression first appeared against Nigerian theatre’s early pillars. Hubert Ogunde, a dramatist who frequently used ethnic Yoruba folklore and oral traditions in his plays to critique colonial rule and later government corruption, was one of the earliest targets of creative suppression His play

Yoruba Ronu

 (

Yorubas, Think!

), staged in 1964, was such a searing political statement that it was banned in the Western Region of Nigeria in the post-colonial era. The ban was lifted only in 1966 after a change of government. Ogunde’s other works —

Strike and Hunger, Otito Koro

 (

Truth is Bitter

) — similarly tackled political themes. 


Also, when Wole Soyinka – another leading dramatist who was imprisoned for his civic activism to prevent the escalation of the Nigerian Civil War in 1967 – published his experience in a memoir,

The Man Died

 (1972), one of the figures named in the book

brought a libel suit

 against him that was as much about silencing political memory as protecting reputations. Military regimes (which had governed the country for 29 years since its independence in 1960) largely suppressed and constrained artistic expression. One of the earliest and most vivid examples of suppression comes from the case of

Fela Anikulapo Kuti

, the pioneer of Afrobeat, a musical genre he used for strong social activism and commentary. In 1970, Fela Kuti founded the

Kalakuta Republic

, declaring it a space independent of Nigeria’s military regime. His music, increasingly political, exposed government brutality, corruption, and hypocrisy. The raid of Kalakuta in 1977 is infamous: approximately 1,000 soldiers stormed his compound, burned down Kalakuta, destroyed his recording studio, beat Fela up, and fatally injured his mother, Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti after throwing her from a second-floor window. Fela’s instruments, master tapes, and the infrastructure of his commune were destroyed. Fela channelled this atrocity into music, penning

Coffin for Head of State

 and

Unknown Soldier

. His 1977 album

Zombie

, in particular, used satire and metaphor to indict the military.


Censorship tightened under successive military regimes, targeting platforms that enabled artistic expression. In 1978, a special News Agency of Nigeria was created to

vet content

 to be broadcast on radio and television and, after the 1983 coup, the army itself took charge of monitoring information (Generals don’t read novels”, one writer

observed

). Set up in 1993, the National Film & Video Censors Board began banning movies

deemed indecent or subversive

.

author: Unknown
title: Gebze'de 10 Ekim anması: "Emek, barış ve demokrasi talebinde ısrarcıyız"
content:
Hasret Gültekin Kozan [email protected]

Gebze Emek ve Demokrasi Güçleri'nin çağrısıyla Kent Meydanı'nda yapılan anmada, 11 yıl önce Ankara Gar Katliamı'nda yaşamını yitirenler anıldı. Açıklamada asıl sorumluların korunduğu vurgulanırken adalet mücadelesinden vazgeçilmeyeceği belirtildi.

10 Ekim Ankara Gar Katliamı'nın 11'inci yılında Gebze Emek ve Demokrasi Güçleri'nin çağrısıyla Kent Meydanı'nda anma ve basın açıklaması gerçekleştirildi. Katliamda yaşamını yitiren 104 can için saygı duruşunda bulunuldu.

"10 Ekim'i unutma unutturma", "Katil IŞİD, işbirlikçi AKP" ve "Onlara sözümüz barış olacak" sloganlarının atıldığı anmada basın açıklamasını Eğitim Sen Kocaeli 2 No'lu Şube Başkanı Sinan Kaya okudu.

Kaya, 11 yıl önce ülkenin dört bir yanından savaşa karşı barışı, sömürüye karşı emeğin hakkını, baskıya karşı demokrasiyi savunmak için Ankara Garı önünde buluşulduğunu hatırlatarak, "IŞİD'in gerçekleştirdiği çifte bombalı saldırı sonucunda 104 arkadaşımızı, yoldaşımızı, canımızı yitirdik. 500'den fazla arkadaşımız yaralandı. Aradan 11 yıl geçti; acımız ilk günkü kadar taze, öfkemiz ilk günkü kadar diri" dedi.

Kaya, 10 Ekim'in yalnızca bir katliam değil, bu topraklarda barışı kalıcı kılmak isteyenlere yönelik alçakça bir saldırı olduğunu belirterek, "O gün katledilenler, savaşa karşı barışın sesini yükseltmek için oradaydı. Onlar biliyordu ki barış, yalnızca silahların sustuğu bir çatışmasızlık hâli değildir; adaletin, eşitliğin ve bir arada kardeşçe yaşama iradesinin adıdır" diye konuştu.

Açıklamada, ülkenin onlarca yıldır süren çatışmanın sona ermesi için yeniden tarihî bir eşiğin önünde olduğuna dikkat çekilerek, silahların bırakılması ve çatışmaların durması yönünde atılan adımların ülkenin demokratik geleceği açısından önemsendiği ifade edildi. Ancak gerçek ve kalıcı barışın yalnızca silahların susmasıyla kurulamayacağı vurgulanan açıklamada, "Evrensel ve kalıcı bir barış ancak sosyal adalet temeline dayanır" ilkesi hatırlatıldı.

Kürt sorununda kalıcı barışın, inkâr ve güvenlik politikalarıyla değil demokratik siyaset zemininde mümkün olduğunun savunulduğu açıklamada, barış sürecinin toplumun tüm kesimlerinin iradesine dayalı yürütülmesi gerektiği kaydedildi.

10 Ekim 2015'te katledilenlerin demokrasi, düşünce ve ifade özgürlüğü, örgütlenme ve toplanma hakkı için orada olduğuna dikkat çekilen açıklamada, halk hızla yoksullaşırken, gelir dağılımı adaletsizliği artarken itiraz eden herkesin terörle ve düşmanlıkla yaftalandığı bir düzen kurulmak istendiği belirtildi. Kayyım politikaları, seçilmiş belediye başkanlarının tutuklanması, grevlerin yasaklanması ve dijital sansürün yaygınlaşması bir aczin göstergesi olarak nitelendirildi.

Kaya, "11 yıldır adalet arıyoruz" diyerek yargılama süreçlerinde faillerin bir kısmının cezalandırılmış olsa da katliamın arkasındaki asıl sorumluların korunduğunu söyledi. Tüm istihbarat bilgilerine rağmen önlem almayanların, güvenlik bürokrasisindeki ihmallerin ortaya çıkarılmadığını ifade eden Kaya, "Devlet, başkentin ortasında, izinleri alınmış bir mitingde 104 insanın katledilmesinde dahi kendi sorumluluğunu kabul etmiyorsa, yarın herhangi bir kentte benzer bir katliam yaşanabilir ve yine 'bizim kusurumuz yok' diyebilir" diye konuştu.

Açıklamada, "Katliamın tüm sorumlularının açığa çıkarılması ve ihmali olan tüm kamu görevlilerinin yargılanması için yürüttüğümüz adalet mücadelemizden asla vazgeçmeyeceğiz. Emeğin, barışın ve demokrasinin egemen olduğu bir Türkiye'yi mutlaka kuracağız" ifadelerine yer verildi.

Açıklamanın ardından katliamda hayatını kaybedenlerin fotoğrafları yere serildi, üzerlerine karanfil bırakıldı ve oturma eylemi gerçekleştirildi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Amy Goodman
title: Israeli Forces Raid Palestinian NGOs in the West Bank Ahead of Israeli Elections
content:
The raids come four years after the forced closure of multiple NGOs that Israel designated as “terrorist” organizations.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Israeli forces have raided what they say are the offices of several Palestinian NGOs in the occupied West Bank. Palestinian officials say a child was injured from Israeli gunfire, while others suffered from tear gas inhalation. At least one journalist was reportedly detained in the raids, which come four years after the forced closure of multiple NGOs that the Israeli government designated as “terrorist” organizations.

“This is part of the whole propaganda show that this government is actually implementing just before the Israeli election,” says human rights lawyer Sahar Francis. “They just wanted to cause harassment, and this is the main message: the persecution and the collective punishment for the whole Palestinian community.” Francis was formerly the general director at Addameer Prisoner Support and Human Rights Association, one of the organizations that Israel claims to have raided this week despite the fact that it was already forced to close its West Bank offices in 2022.

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org. I’m Amy Goodman.

In the latest crackdown on human rights defenders in the occupied West Bank Tuesday, Israeli forces raided what they say are the offices of several Palestinian NGOs, confiscating legal files, court records, valuable equipment. Israeli forces also deployed snipers around the entrances to Ramallah’s Palestine Medical Complex, the largest government medical facility in the occupied West Bank. At least one journalist was reportedly detained. Palestinian officials say a child was injured from Israeli gunfire; others suffered from tear gas inhalation.

For more in these last few minutes, we go to Ramallah, where we’re joined by Sahar Francis, human rights lawyer, previous general director at Addameer Prisoner Support and Human Rights Association, which is one of the groups that Israel just raided.

Sahar Francis, welcome back to Democracy Now! We had you on when you were the head of Addameer, which is the prisoner support and human rights group in the West Bank. I was watching overnight when Israel was raiding, because Al Jazeera was showing the raid live. But these offices, in fact, of your group, your previous group, Addameer, and others, the Palestine Women’s Association, were already closed — is that right? — years ago, because the Israeli government classified these organizations as terrorist. So, what were they raiding?

SAHAR FRANCIS: Exactly. Good afternoon, and thanks for inviting me again to join you in this important discussion.

As you just said, these offices actually were raided in 2020. We were, too, forced closure after the decision to designate the six Palestinian organizations as terrorist organizations. They confiscated property and stole files and equipments at that time.

So, what happened yesterday, I would claim that this is part of the whole propaganda show that this government is actually implementing just before the Israeli election, couple of weeks before the Israeli election, to send a very clear message to the whole Palestinian society, and especially to the Palestinian Authority, because the offices they raided is very close to the official governmental offices and other ministries in Ramallah city, that “We are the masters. We decide what we will do. You cannot interfere. You cannot protect nothing to do with your sovereignty in even Ramallah city, that is supposed to be an Area A.”

And what happened yesterday, they were not confiscating property for illegal organization, claiming that this property is used to support terrorism. And I’m sure you all saw in the videos that were presented by the different media, local or international, that they mostly broke and destroyed the files and the equipment, even the windows. The refrigerator in this office that they claimed it belongs for Addameer, they were throwing it from the second floor down to the ground. They just wanted to cause harassment, and this is the main message: the persecution and the collective punishment for the whole Palestinian community. The raid onto the city center Ramallah is not a lonely activity. It happens every day that they raid different villages, different cities. They arrest …

author: Mada Masr
title: Protests at several prisons, detainee ‘banishments’ surround delay to Criminal Procedure Code
content:
A wave of protests has swept through several prisons over the last three weeks, as prisoners who were hopeful that the new Criminal Procedure Code would bring an end to their prolonged remand detention had their hopes dashed at the eleventh hour when the law’s implementation was postponed, according to several lawyers acting in defense of detainees held at different prisons who spoke separately to Mada Masr over the same time period.


The postponement pushed back what many detainees saw as a window of opportunity for authorities to release dozens of them held in remand after the law’s awaited implementation on October 1.


With that window now firmly shut until October 2027, a wave of demonstrations in detention centers has been met by security forces with measures that the lawyers say include the punitive transfer of detainees to prisons farther away from their families, a practice known as “

taghreeb”

 (banishment).


As cries and claims about the demonstrations and the security forces’ response made their way to social media, the Interior Ministry issued repeated denials that protests and abuses are taking place within prisons, most recently in an October 2

statement

. The Public Prosecution, meanwhile, was yet to issue a statement regarding the claims at the time of publishing.


The state’s National Council for Human Rights (NCHR) intends to pay visits to a number of prisons about which it has received complaints, the council’s deputy head, Mohamed Anwar al-Sadat, tells Mada Masr. Sadat adds, however, that the council has received “assurances” from the prosecution and the Interior Ministry that conditions inside prisons are “normal.”


But lawyers and human right defenders, who continue to hear from concerned families and document the incidents, have raised calls for an independent investigation into possible violations against detainees.


***


Among those subjected to “banishment,” is journalist and researcher Ismail al-Eskandarany, according to human rights lawyer Mahienour al-Massry.


Massry received information on October 1 that Eskandarany, whom she represents, and other detainees had been transferred from the 10th of Ramadan Correctional and Rehabilitation Center “violently, resulting in injuries to some detainees,” as per her

telegraph

 to the public prosecutor, in which she demanded the disclosure of Eskandarany’s place of detention.


Massry tells Mada Masr that Eskandarany’s family was able to confirm independently that he had been moved from 10th of Ramadan center’s prison 6 to the Wadi al-Natroun prison in what is known as a “banishment.”


Massry called, in her telegraph to the prosecution, for an urgent investigation into the circumstances of the transfer and any violations or assaults that may have been committed against Eskandarany or other detainees, noting the investigation should include their referral for forensic medical examination or to other relevant medical authorities to document their condition.


Another human rights lawyer representing prisoners in political cases says that some of his defendants, too, had been transferred from the 10th of Ramadan prison to the Gamasa prison against the backdrop of protests, according to information the lawyer received from three of his clients’ families. Demonstrations had taken place at 10th of Ramadan center’s prison 6, with large numbers of prisoners chanting slogans in protest against their detention conditions and refusing to return to their cells after their recreation time, according to the lawyer. Riot police intervened in an attempt to disperse the gatherings and return the prisoners to their cells, after which prison authorities began transferring a number of detainees to other facilities, the lawyer adds, citing accounts from detainees’ families. The lawyer says he was also informed of an incident in which a prisoner was placed in solitary confinement as a disciplinary measure after going on hunger strike.


The human rights lawyer, two other lawyers and a human rights source confirm to Mada Masr that detainees’ families have complained to them of security forces’ mistreatment of prisoners at the same facility following protests in several cells over recent days, including chanting and banging on cell doors, disabling surveillance cameras in several cells and refusing to leave their cells for recreation time. Prison authorities have also conducted extensive searches of cell contents, according to the lawyers.

author: Unknown
title: Release of two prisoners postponed again
content:
The release of Zeliha Ustabaş, who is held at Sincan Women’s Closed Prison, has been blocked for the fifth time by a decision of the Prison Administration and Observation Board.


Ustabaş’s release, which has been postponed four times since 18 July 2024, has now been delayed by a further nine months.


It was reported that Ustabaş’s current sentence period is due to end on 24 July 2027, and that 8 July 2027 has been set as the date for a reassessment of her case.


The release of Orhan Yakışır, who is held at Sincan No. 1 High-Security Prison, has also been postponed, for the third time.


Yakışır’s release was previously postponed by three months on the first occasion and eight months on the second. His release has now been delayed by a further 11 months.


It was stated that the board’s next review of Yakışır’s case will take place on 7 September 2027.

title: “Αμετανόητοι οι κατηγορούμενοι”, ανταπόκριση του Γιάννη Μάγγου από τη δίκη των 6 βασανιστών του Βασίλη Μάγγου
content:
Με ανάρτηση του, ο Γιάννης Μάγγος σχολιάζει τις εξελίξεις στη δίκη των 6 ένστολων βασανιστών του γιού του Βασίλη Μάγγου, αναφέροντας πως οι κατηγορούμενοι ένστολοι παρουσιάζονται αμετανόητοι και προσφέυγουν σε συνεχή ψέματα και αντιφάσεις στις απολογίες τους.


Παρακάτω η ανάρτηση του Γιάννη Μάγγου:


ΑΜΕΤΑΝΟΗΤΟΙ ΟΙ ΚΑΤΗΓΟΡΟΥΜΕΝΟΙ


Ολοκληρώθηκαν στις 12.10.2026 οι απολογίες των έξι κατηγορούμενων αστυνομικών, βασανιστών του Βασίλειου Μάγγου. Όσον αφορά για το συνολικό περιστατικό, παραδέχτηκαν ότι “έγινε σωρεία λαθών και παραλείψεων” για τα οποία ευθύνονται και οι ίδιοι. “Έπραξα λάθος” είπαν.


Κανένας τους όμως δεν ζήτησε συγγνώμη από εμάς τους γονείς του για την προσβλητική,


κακοποιητική και ανάρμοστη συμπεριφορά τους.


Είναι αδίστακτοι και αμετανόητοι.


-Στην ερώτηση για την κινητικότητά του, απάντησαν πως, όταν κατέβηκε από το αυτοκίνητο, περπάτησε κανονικά, ανέβηκε τις σκάλες και έφτασε στον πρώτο όροφο της Υ/Α Βόλου χωρίς δυσκολία.


*Ακριβώς! Επειδή τα πιο σφοδρά χτυπήματα και η πιο βάναυση συμπεριφορά επακολούθησαν κατόπιν μέσα στην Ασφάλεια.


-Και σε άλλη ερώτηση του δικαστηρίου, πώς δικαιολογούνται τα έξι σπασμένα πλευρά και η θλάση στο ήπαρ, η απάντηση όλων των κατηγορούμενων ήταν ότι αυτοί μέσα στην Υ/Α δεν έκαναν τίποτα, ότι ο Βασίλειος Μάγγος δεν είχε τίποτα, δεν παραπονέθηκε για τίποτα…


-Και γιατί ο Μάγγος δεν πονούσε μόνο κατά το διάστημα από 4 μέχρι 5 μ.μ. που τον είχαν στην Ασφάλεια;


– …..


*Οι μάρτυρες που τον βρήκαν κατέθεσαν ότι πονούσε φρικτά και δεν μπορούσε να σηκωθεί να περπατήσει. Όλα αυτά επιβεβαιώθηκαν από τις καταθέσεις των γιατρών και την αξονική τομογραφία.


-Και γιατί δεν τον πήγαν στο νοσοκομείο; -“Δεν το ζήτησε”…


-Ούτε τους ζήτησε νερό.


“Αν ζητούσε κάτι, μέχρι και ελικόπτερο θα κατεβάζαμε για να του το δώσουμε”…


*Κανένας όμως δεν είπε ότι του έδωσαν, έστω, ένα ποτήρι νερό.


Όπως κατήγγειλε ο ίδιος, τον παρέπεμψαν να πιει νερό από ένα χαλασμένο ψύκτη, σύρθηκε μέχρι εκεί και προσπάθησε να πάρει λίγες σταγόνες νερού στο στόμα του για να ανακουφίσει το σωματικό και ψυχικό του μαρτύριο. Και αυτοί τον χλεύαζαν και γελούσαν εις βάρος του για την προσπάθεια που κατέβαλλε. Αυτό του κόστισε ανυπολόγιστα, ακύρωσε την ύπαρξή του, όπως διαπιστώσαμε κι εμείς οι γονείς του.


-Και σαν προσαχθείς, σε ποιον ήταν χρεωμένος;


– …..


-Και ενώ δεν επρόκειτο παρά για μία απλή προσαγωγή κι ο Βασίλειος Μάγγος ήταν ήσυχος και ήρεμος (όπως είπαν), γιατί απαιτούνταν η συνδρομή έξι αστυνομικών; Τέσσερις της οπκε και δύο της Υ/Α Βόλου.


Πάλι απάντησαν ανεύθυνα, λέγοντας ψέμματα ότι δεν παρείχαν συνδρομή. Στην προανάκριση όμως άλλα κατέθεσαν. π.χ. κατηγορούμενος της οπκε: “..προσήλθαν και όλοι οι υπόλοιποι μηνυόμενοι. Παρείχαμε επιτήρηση στον Μάγγο Β.” (έγγραφα 1,2,6).


Κάποιος, σε σχετική ερώτηση του δικαστηρίου, γιατί άλλα έλεγαν πριν και άλλα τώρα, είχε την αφέλεια να απαντήσει ότι άλλαξε η υπερασπιστική γραμμή…


Παρατήρηση του δικαστηρίου: “η αλήθεια δεν αλλάζει”.


*Όπως ακριβώς με την ιατροδικαστή και τους γιατρούς τους. Οι τρεις γνωμάτευσαν ότι τα πλευρά τα είχε σπασμένα, πριν τον χτυπήσουν μπροστά στα δικαστήρια και ο τέταρτος υποστήριξε ότι του τα έσπασαν μπροστά στα δικαστήρια…


-Και τί ώρα αποχώρησαν από την υπηρεσία τους;


Οι αστυνομικοί της οπκε απάντησαν ότι αποχώρησαν πριν τις πέντε μ.μ. Όμως στον Πίνακα Διάταξης της Υπηρεσίας και σε δεύτερο έγγραφο αναφέρεται ότι η υπηρεσία τους ήταν από 10π.μ. έως 6 μ.μ. (έγγραφα 3,4,5). Και ο σκοπός πύλης κατηγορηματικά κατέθεσε ότι τους είδε να αποχωρούν στις 6μ.μ.


Και ποιοι αποχώρησαν πρώτοι; Όλοι ισχυρίστηκαν ότι οι κατηγορούμενοι της οπκε


αποχώρησαν πρώτοι. Όμως στην προδικασία ένας κατηγορούμενος ισχυρίστηκε το


αντίθετο (έγγραφο 6).


Αντιφάσεις, αντιφάσεις και ψέμματα…


-Γιατί τον κράτησαν σχεδόν δύο ώρες και τον άφησαν αβοήθητο, ενώ ήταν ήδη χτυπημένος;


Του έκαναν σωματική έρευνα, (δεν του βρήκαν τίποτα) αλλά δεν αντιλήφθηκαν να πάσχει από κάτι:


“Ηταν μια χαρά!”.


*Έκθεση σωματικής έρευνας, όμως, δεν συνέταξαν. Ούτε ενημέρωσαν τον εισαγγελέα. Κι ενώ έπρεπε, όπως ισχυρίστηκαν, να τον συλλάβουν για τα υποτιθέμενα αδικήματα αντίστασης κατά της αρχής και απόπειρα απελευθέρωσης κρατουμένου, παρ΄όλα αυτά δεν το έκαναν, ούτε σχημάτισαν δικογραφία εις βάρος του…


Όμως “αυτοί δεν ευθύνονται για τίποτα”, οι ανώτεροί τους φταίνε που έδωσαν προφορικές εντολές να μη σχηματιστεί δικογραφία και να τον ελευθερώσουν…


“Φταίει ο διοικητής της Υ/Α”… “Ήταν εντολή άνωθεν να μη γίνει σύλληψη και δικογραφία”… “Ο διοικητής της Υ/Α δεν …

author: Shireen Akram-Boshar
title: Netanyahu Orders Investigation and Prosecution of Israeli Soldiers in NAZA
content:
NAZA reveals how Israel’s AI-based systems have been used to execute remote killings of thousands in Israel’s genocide.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has ordered Israel’s attorney general and the heads of the Israeli military and Shin Bet security service to investigate the soldiers and officers interviewed anonymously in the documentary film NAZA.

Netanyahu called Sunday for the agencies to identify “all those who are involved or appear in the libel film” and to prosecute them for “serious information security offences, criminal defamation, and harming Israel’s diplomatic and security interests.”

In a letter to IDF Chief of Staff, the head of the Shin Bet, and Israel’s attorney general, Netanyahu decried the film for “present[ing] a false, misleading and biased narrative that defames the State of Israel and the IDF around the world and severely damages Israel’s standing.”

The film NAZA features anonymous interviews with 24 Israeli soldiers and officers involved in remote mass killings of Palestinians in Gaza over the past three years. The soldiers’ faces are obscured and voices are altered for anonymity as they speak with journalist and director Yuval Abraham on rooftops in Tel Aviv.

NAZA reveals how Israel’s AI-based surveillance systems have been used to facilitate and execute remote killings of thousands during Israel’s genocide in Gaza. The film’s title is a Hebrew military acronym for collateral damage – as in, the number of Palestinian civilians deemed acceptable to kill in a bombing with a military target. In one instance, a soldier tells director Yuval Abraham that the military approved the killing of 500 Gazans for one target.

The film and its directors have faced attacks by the Israeli government since its world premiere in September at the Venice Film Festival. Both the Israeli culture minister and Netanyahu have called for revoking the Israeli citizenship of the film’s directors, Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, while accusing them of treason and defamation. The IDF chief called the film a “blood libel” and “an attack on the State of Israel.”

Upon the film’s premiere in the U.S. in late September, Netanyahu compared NAZA to “launching dozens of ballistic missiles at Israel.”

Several Israeli civil society organizations, including human rights group B’Tselem, criticized the attacks on the filmmakers, and called for “an end to the wave of incitement and threats of violence against them.”

Abraham and Szor produced No Other Land, the 2024 documentary focused on Israel’s displacement of Palestinian villages in the West Bank, along with Palestinian activist and journalist Basel Adra and Palestinian researcher and photographer Hamdan Ballal. After the film won major international awards, including an Academy Award, members of the film’s Palestinian crew were attacked by both Israeli settlers and soldiers.

Earlier this month, Israel put forward a hastily-produced rival film to counter NAZA; last week, the Israeli government announced that it was awarding the filmmakers “for their contribution to Israeli public diplomacy.”

The Guardian, which produced the film, has pushed back on the Israeli government’s attempts to discredit NAZA. On October 1st, a Guardian spokesperson said that “The process of assessing the credibility of the testimonies was rigorous. It included leaked classified documents, detailed verification of specific strikes and corroboration via a wider pool of confidential journalistic sources who did not appear on camera in the film.”

The Guardian added that the team that produced the film interviewed “more than 100 sources familiar with IDF systems used in the war in Gaza, including senior-ranking commanders directly involved in the authorization of strikes.”

Much of the material in the film had already been published in reports at The Guardian, +972 Magazine, and Israel’s left-wing publication, Local Call.

In a 2024 piece co-published by +972 Magazine and Local Call, Yuval Abraham explained how AI systems like “Lavender” and “Where’s Daddy” identified low-ranking Hamas and Islamic Jihad operatives as military targets. After October 7, 2023, Israel’s military decided that these tens of thousands of people could be bombed inside their homes with their families – even tracking and monitoring their children in order to strike …
