title: YPJ Spokesperson: Any attack on the symbols of our martyrs constitutes an attack on every woman
content:
Ruksen Mohamed, spokesperson for the Women’s Protection Units (YPJ), made a statement regarding the attack that targeted the images of fallen female fighters in Hesekê.


The statement by Ruksen Mohamed reads as follows:


“In light of the recent events in Hesekê Governorate, which have witnessed acts of vandalism and grave assaults perpetrated by individuals operating outside the law, targeting the symbols and images of our fallen female martyrs, we strongly condemn and denounce these reprehensible acts, whether through tearing down their photographs, defacing them, or insulting their memory and sacrifices.


These unethical practices constitute a flagrant assault on our collective memory and conscience, as well as a violation of the humanitarian and national values embodied by our martyrs through their immense sacrifices.


Our female martyrs are symbols of struggle, dignity, and freedom. They gave their lives in defence of the land, justice, and gender equality, and their sacrifices will remain forever enshrined in the memory of our people.


We affirm that any attack on the symbols of our martyrs constitutes an attack on every woman who has struggled for freedom and legitimate rights. Such acts represent a grave moral and national offence that cannot be justified under any pretext. Accordingly, we call upon the Syrian government, represented by the Hesekê Governorate and its Internal Security Forces, to fulfil its responsibilities by holding those responsible for these assaults accountable and taking the necessary measures to prevent their recurrence.


We further emphasise that holding the perpetrators of these assaults accountable will serve as a genuine measure of the seriousness of the integration process, as well as the commitment to safeguarding rights, respecting shared values and principles, and upholding the dignity of women and the sacrifices of our fallen female martyrs.


We reiterate that these reprehensible assaults will not deter us from continuing our struggle to defend women’s rights, dignity, and freedom, or from preserving the legacy and sacrifices of our martyrs.”

title: Kongra Star holds Damascus responsible for provocations in Hesekê
content:
The Kongra Star Coordination has strongly condemned the recent attacks on Kurdish symbols and memorial portraits of fallen women in Hesekê. The women’s movement views these acts as deliberate provocations intended to fuel hostility between the Kurdish and Arab populations. It holds the Islamist transitional government in Damascus responsible for ensuring security in the city and preventing further attacks.


The statement follows an attack on an office of the Democratic Union Party (PYD) in the Xiwêran neighborhood on Tuesday. An individual entered the premises, damaged portraits of fallen women, and stole Kurdish symbols. Other memorial portraits taken from the office were subsequently desecrated in public. The perpetrator shared footage of these acts on social media. According to the ANHA news agency, the man has since been arrested by the Internal Security Forces.


Attacks target women’s struggle for freedom


Kongra Star placed the incident in the context of increasing attacks on Kurdish values, symbols, and fallen fighters since the mobilization of Arab groups from Deir ez-Zor, Raqqa, Tal Hamis, and al-Shaddadi. The women’s movement warned of attempts to divide the population along ethnic lines, saying: “Kurds, Arabs, and other communities have lived together in Hesekê for centuries. Their shared interest lies in peace and coexistence based on mutual respect, rather than renewed conflict.”


Denouncing the desecration of portraits of fallen fighters, Kongra Star stated: “This reflects a patriarchal and misogynistic attitude that attacks women’s struggle for freedom, their leadership role in society, and their political self-determination.”


The coordination recalled that the Women’s Protection Units (YPJ) played a decisive role in the fight against the Islamic State (ISIS). The women fighters, it said, drew inspiration from the ideas and resistance of the women whose memorial portraits are now being targeted. According to Kongra Star, these attacks are therefore directed not only against the achievements of the Kurdish population but also against the memory of the struggle against ISIS.


Damascus must take responsibility


Kongra Star called on the transitional government in Damascus to take concrete measures to prevent further attacks and ensure the safety of the population. These measures, it said, should include monitoring groups that have arrived in Hesekê from other regions. In particular, the incidents in the Xiwêran neighborhood must be thoroughly investigated, and those responsible must be held accountable, Kongra Star demanded.


“Accountability must not be limited to words. It must be implemented transparently and credibly to ensure public trust,” the statement said.


At the same time, the women’s movement criticized the handling of the integration process between the Autonomous Administration and the transitional government so far. It noted that the Kurdish side has approached this process sincerely and constructively, adding: “However, an integration process that fails to recognize the political will of the Kurdish population and tolerates attacks on its social values would jeopardize coexistence.”


Kongra Star called on women’s organizations, democratic forces, and the people of Rojava to jointly confront these provocations through democratic and legal means. It vowed to continue its democratic resistance and protest actions against attempts to incite hostility between Kurds and Arabs and plunge the region into another war.


In conclusion, Kongra Star called for an independent investigation into the attacks: “We hold the government in Damascus responsible for preventing the provocations that have occurred in Hesekê and any further provocations. We will not tolerate any attack targeting the coexistence of peoples.”

title: POV : Révolution
content:
Dimanche 4 octobre 2026, un premier ministre pince-sans-rire, Lecornu, annonce en catastrophe des chantiers pour «

 

préparer les lycées aux fortes chaleurs

 

». Depuis le 1

er

, rien ne semble arrêter les incendies de murs de poubelles, les assauts contre la police de la République, les déferlements suivis de pillages dans les centres-villes, les cris de joie quand on passe le portail de la captivité comme un lion saute à travers un cercle de feu. Plutôt que de lâcher des commentaires sur le fascisme, on met les slogans à jour : «

 

La jeunesse emmerde l'éducation nationale

 

».


Quand on veut qu'il se passe quelque chose, on a une chance de comprendre ce qui se passe dans les lycées. Les percées de ces derniers jours ont témoigné d'un niveau de courage, de détermination et d'euphorie qui apparaît de fait hostile à tout désir de réconciliation avec les forces du mépris, de l'humiliation et de l'enfermement. Si les revendications ne manquaient pas sur les premiers blocus, c'est en acte, dans tous les efforts déployés, que se traduit la profondeur des aspirations. Celui qui est humilié est vengé immédiatement. Lorsqu'un chef des

RG

, face à un lycéen, puise au ruisseau son inspiration de tortionnaire, la réponse est univoque : rapport de force inversé, chacun est libre de tirer son penalty. Comme le précise une vieille amie, «

 

un flic n'est jamais lynché gratos

 

».


Tous ceux dont la fonction ou le réflexe est de perpétuer l'enrôlement républicain sont niés, et s'ils se mettent en travers, ils seront pris comme un obstacle à affronter sur la voie de la libération. «

 

La République, c'est moi

 

», il faut le dire beaucoup moins fort. Tous les volontaires à l'Enseignement Moral et Civique s'exposent aux injures et aux coups. Ce qu'ils professent, les flics le font. On ne demande plus une hausse des moyens pour les bahuts, on fait un battle d'incendie. On ne demande plus de meilleures conditions de travail informel, on ravage la boîte. Le gouvernement tente de rétablir l'ordre avec les appareils du covid (on avait 8 ans mais on s'en souvient

 

!), les cours en ligne sont désertés, on appelle à des e-blocus et à se rejoindre dans la rue pour continuer. Par suite rigoureuse, mardi 6, même les boulevards parisiens retrouvent le grand air de l'émeute après des années empuanties. On ne prend pas les mêmes et on recommence. Oui, l'application des consignes de retenue est pour beaucoup dans ce changement d'ambiance. Mais la modération vient après une phase de répression ouvertement coloniale, où la force lycéenne est traitée comme une foule à disperser au casse-bouche. Le répresseur dit qu'il est divisé entre le père et le flic, on n'a rien à rajouter. Le rapport de force a toujours quelque chose de politique (voir le préfet de Paris de 68). Si le retrait des grenades explosives est effectif, croyez-bien que nous saurons quoi faire de cette décision qui a coûté un avant-bras à une personne de 15 ans.


On le sait bien, tenir cette vision des choses n'a rien d'une évidence et demande un combat dans la durée, qui a toujours son versant interne. Les médias n'ont pas besoin de mentir, il leur suffit de donner la parole aux trous du cul du mouvement. En attendant, jour 1, c'est panique à bord. «

 

Le mouvement des lycéens semble hors de contrôle

 

». Garder le contrôle : le cœur du propos ennemi se passe de plus amples développements. Cela témoigne du vide de ce qui règne. Cela relève aussi d'une simplification un peu rapide des enjeux. Une fois hors de contrôle, on devra aussi se mettre hors de fonctionnement, hors de valorisation, hors d'identification. Quand les «

 

citoyens en devenir

 

» commencent à devenir autre chose, c'est le flip. «

 

Casseurs

 

!

 

» «

 

Barbarie

 

!

 

». «

 

Entre des lycéens qui ont des choses à dire-de-manière-pacifique et les violences urbaines, il y a un monde

 

» (Maud Bregeon, porte-parole du gouvernement). Alors, si on n'est pas du bon côté, c'est comment

 

? Tir à vue «

 

proportionnel

 

»

 

? S'il y a encore de la place pour de si vieilles opérations de division, ce n'est pas que «

 

la violence empêche de parler du fond

 

», mais qu'on ne parle pas du fond de la violence.


Si l'on s'en tient à la vision amère-radicale du lycéen Tiktoké, embullé, sommet de l'aliénation, ce mouvement est juste impossible. On comprend d'où sort la détermination lycéenne quand on voit avec quoi elle rompt. Elle rompt avec le défaitisme et le …

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Trump Admin Killed Insider Trading Referral Probing Iran War-Related Oil Sales
content:
The incident raises alarm over officials’ moves to insulate insiders from anti-corruption enforcement.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

A Trump administration official intervened against an insider trading investigation into suspiciously timed oil sales made just minutes before a critical announcement by President Donald Trump related to the Iran war this March, new reporting finds.

Analysts within the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), the federal government’s regulator against abuses in derivatives markets, had made a referral to the agency’s Division of Enforcement on a series of advantageous large-volume trades made on March 23, Bloomberg reported this week.

These trades were highly profitable. That day, Trump announced that he was backing off, for now, on his threats to strike Iranian power plants — a move that would drastically escalate the war and undoubtedly cause Iran to double down on their closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Just 15 minutes before Trump’s announcement, traders made billions of dollars’ worth of transactions predicting that oil would fall and the S&P 500 would rise. These bets paid off nearly immediately.

CFTC workers in the Division of Enforcement are typically responsible for determining whether the agency would launch a full insider trading investigation that could potentially lead to an enforcement action. But, breaking with precedent, an official within the agency told the Division of Market Oversight to retract the referral. Instead, the official — Mel Gunewardena, a top adviser for Trump-appointed CFTC chair Michael Selig — said that further investigation into the incident would be done under his purview.

The incident, reported by Bloomberg on Wednesday, raises concerns about Trump administration insiders using non-public knowledge to make trades related to the Iran war. It also raises questions about whether the administration is installing Trump-friendly figures within agency watchdog roles in order to grant impunity for illegal activities like insider trading.

The trades were among a few of numerous well-timed trades made in March and April that agency officials have flagged, with a particular focus on the March 23 transactions. Analysts scrutinized those trades in particular because, in just two minutes, traders sold 8.5 times the volume of oil that had been traded in the same time over the prior week.

The forensic analysts are still looking into the trades, but they are siloed off from the rest of the agency as a result of Gunewardena’s intervention, Bloomberg found; the supervisor who Gunewardena ordered to retract the referral left the agency, and other members of that team resigned or were reassigned. Instead, Gunewardena “assembled his own team to conduct a new analysis of the trading,” the publication found.

The incident is another instance of the Trump administration’s interference in the CFTC’s regulatory role. The agency only carried out 13 enforcement actions in fiscal year 2025 — a major decline from 58 actions in 2024 and 96 in 2023.

author: David Venn
title: QIA funds $15M wellness centre in Igloolik
content:
A wellness centre planned for Igloolik’s core will be a positive addition to the community, says a hamlet leader.


Last week, the Qikiqtani Inuit Association announced $15 million for the Saviruut Building, which will house hamlet wellness initiatives and a federally funded early childhood development program.


“It’s good to see that we’re getting more infrastructure, because the need is there,” senior administrative officer John Ivey said in an interview with Nunatsiaq News.


The hamlet asked QIA to fund a wellness centre a few years before Ivey joined its administration.


The regional organization, responsible for just over 51 per cent of Nunavut’s Inuit population, allocated the money from its Indigenous Community Infrastructure Fund.


QIA selected Arctic Fresh Projects Inc. as the contractor and expects materials to ship to the hamlet next year, said a news release issued last week by the Inuit organization.


Once built, the facility will support “initiatives that promote healing and the transfer of Inuit traditional knowledge and worldview to future generations,” said QIA spokesperson Markoosie Qaunirq.


It will also be home to the Aboriginal Head Start early childhood program, to which the Public Health Agency of Canada provided $3.2 million.


Ivey said he’s unsure when Arctic Fresh plans to complete the building.


“The blueprints are very, very impressive,” he added.

author: The Canadian Press
title: Interim Indigenous languages commissioner’s term extended
content:
The interim commissioner of Indigenous languages will serve in the role for another month as the Canadian Heritage department continues to search for a permanent replacement.


Candice St-Aubin, a former senior assistant deputy minister of strategic policy with Indigenous Services Canada, was supposed to serve in the role for 90 days or until a new commissioner was appointed.


A cabinet order dated Oct. 7 extends her appointment for another 31 days, or until she is no longer needed in the role. The order is effective as of Oct. 12.


The term of Ron Ignace, the previous commissioner, ended in July, along with the terms of the office’s directors.


The Canadian Heritage Department has not yet replied to a question about when a permanent commissioner and directors will be appointed.


The Canadian Press reported earlier this year an audit is being conducted on the office, which is tasked with helping to preserve at-risk Indigenous languages.


Half a dozen sources, including former employees, told The Canadian Press that over the five years of its existence, the commissioner’s office has failed to move the needle on strengthening Indigenous languages and supporting research.


Instead, they said, the office has focused on extensive travel and hosting one big conference in Ottawa that cost $10 million. They also allege a toxic work environment, bullying and uncompleted projects, as well as staff quitting in frustration.


The Canadian Press agreed not to name the sources because they feared reprisals.


In a media statement at the time, Ignace said the office has faced challenges but “we succeeded in laying the foundation for an office capable of carrying forward this significant work.”


Canadian Heritage Minister Marc Miller described allegations against the office as serious.


“But part of holding people to account is giving people the benefit of the doubt, and that includes making sure the due process is respected,” he said earlier in June.


Read More: 


Landmark Indigenous languages office under audit, $10M spent hosting conference 


In a July interview with The Canadian Press, St-Aubin said she knows her office has work to do on rebuilding trust with Indigenous communities, and she is participating fully in the audit.


“Having seen the reporting coming in, my eyes were wide open. Financial stewardship is something that is ingrained in me, much like ethics and codes of conduct, but also managing people,” St-Aubin said.


St-Aubin said she wants the next commissioner and directors to start their mandates knowing the office is functioning.


She said Indigenous communities also want to see demonstrable results from the office’s work.


“We’ve got to build trust by showing [our work], by talking about it, by engaging in conversations, continued conversations, even if it’s uncomfortable,” St-Aubin said, adding she wants young people to have more of a say in the work the office does.


“There’s a whole lot of great innovation happening there. And I think if we can demonstrate that and show folks what’s going on, we’ll go a long way.”


Story by Alessia Passafiume

author: Stephen Prager
title: Mike Rogers’s Wealth Soared as His Wife’s Firm Won Billion-Dollar Contracts
content:
Despite concerns about conflicts of interest, Rogers was named chair of the House Intelligence Committee.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Former US Rep. Mike Rogers, the Republican Senate candidate in Michigan, saw his personal wealth soar after he was named chair of the House Intelligence Committee in 2011, thanks in large part to his marriage to the CEO of a powerful military contracting firm.

Financial disclosures reviewed by Drop Site News as part of an investigation published Tuesday show that Rogers had just $4,000-$60,000 worth of investment holdings in fiscal year 2008 after he divorced his first wife of 17 years.

But that all began to change in 2010, when he married Kristi Clemens, a senior executive for the British-founded private security contractor Aegis, which has a major US subsidiary that she helped to establish.

Mike Rogers did what? This is pretty crazy even by DC standards https://t.co/OJhYJuyf4j

During the 2000s, the company won multiple Pentagon contracts worth hundreds of millions of dollars to support US military operations in Iraq, where it was put in charge of coordinating other private contractors.

Less than a year after his marriage, Rogers was named chair of the House Intelligence Committee — one of the nation’s most powerful oversight posts, which gave him access to highly classified intelligence.

Within seven months — despite concerns about conflicts of interest — Aegis was awarded a contract worth more than $1 billion to protect the US embassy in Kabul, Afghanistan. In a since-deleted online biography for a law firm she joined after leaving Aegis, Kristi took credit for leading a “two-year pursuit and capture strategy” to secure the contract.

In the meantime, Rogers’ financial assets — now merged with Kristi’s — grew substantially. Up from between $136,000 and $391,000 during the first year of their marriage, the pair now held anywhere from $230,000 to $925,000 three years later.

Rogers’ potential conflicts of interest became a subject of scrutiny even among fellow Republicans, who accused him of slow-walking an investigation into the killing of four Americans at a US compound in Benghazi, Libya.

Aegis had been heavily active in Libya since 2011, when NATO launched its operation to overthrow President Muammar Gaddafi, which plunged the country into civil war in the following years.

Rogers’ handling of the Benghazi investigation would later draw a scathing rebuke from longtime right-wing operative Dick Morris, who accused him of “obstructing and delaying the Benghazi investigation in order to shield his wife, Kristi, from scrutiny.”

Amid this controversy, Rogers announced that he would not run for reelection. In 2015, after serving 14 years in Congress, he returned to the private sector.

Rogers went on to profit from the national security and surveillance industries he’d helped to oversee — taking board positions with military contractors and cybersecurity firms.

According to Business Insider, financial disclosures showed he received nearly $2 million in payments from technology and cybersecurity companies between January 2022 and late 2023.

When he left Congress in 2015, Mike and Kristi Rogers’ combined net worth was about $1.7 million. As of 2026, it is estimated to have climbed to between $7 million and $14 million.

Dr. Abdul El-Sayed blasts Mike Rogers: “He hasn't been serious about providing healthcare his entire career. What he has been serious about is monetizing his time in office.” $14 MILLION, two yachts, and a Florida McMansion. That's quite a payday! pic.twitter.com/X6XCsjaeKX

Rogers is currently in the midst of a battle to reenter Congress as Michigan’s US senator, in a close race that could decide whether Democrats retake the chamber next month.

His Democratic opponent, Abdul El-Sayed — a former Detroit public health official — has run as a staunch opponent of President Donald Trump’s aggressive wars abroad, including in Iran, and his support for Israel’s assaults on Gaza and Lebanon, which Rogers has backed.

With less than a month before polls close on November 3, El-Sayed has hammered on Rogers’ support for legislation that expanded government spying powers in the wake of the 9/11 attacks. He’s also zeroed in on the Republican’s lucrative personal ties to the military-industrial complex.

title: We Will Miss Denis J. Halliday
content:
Chapters, Culture of Peace, Europe, Ireland Chapter, Videos

By World BEYOND War, October 14, 2026

Here is a video of a WBW webinar with Denis Halliday:

Notice of death from this website:

Denis J. Halliday, son of the late Stanley and Kathleen of Terenure, Dublin 6 and Errislannan, Co. Galway, brother of the late Leo, died peacefully in the presence of his family on 11th October 2026.

Deeply loved and treasured by Fransisca, Keaton and Lena, Leo and Eileen, Orla, Niamh and Vincent, Paul, Aiden, Jasmine and Nichole.

Lovingly cherished by his extended family and friends, colleagues, his fellow Friends and many more around the world.

Remembered always for the courage of his convictions, his integrity and kindness. A sane voice in an insane world, and one needed now more than ever. A rare man who stood for what was right, even at personal cost.

With Denis’s departure, our consciences are quietened, yet awakened. May we keep a part of his voice alive in our own by speaking out when others stay silent.

Denis began a life of service as a Friends (Quaker) volunteer in Kenya, followed by 34 years with the United Nations, where he rose to Assistant Secretary-General and served as Humanitarian Coordinator in Iraq. His resignation in 1998, in protest of the Iraqi sanctions, marked not an end but a new chapter. Denis continued to devote himself to peace and human rights. His work was recognised with the Gandhi International Peace Award in 2003.

Denis was not only a voice for peace but an active participant, he sailed in 2010 on the MV Rachel Corrie, the Irish aid ship that sought to break the blockade of Gaza.

At home in Ireland Denis was a steadfast advocate of Irish neutrality, opposing the use of Shannon Airport by US military aircraft. He lent his voice to countless other causes, and through it all, his commitment to humanity and accountability never wavered.

Denis will be remembered at Churchtown Friend’s Meeting House, Religious Society of Friends, Dublin 14, D14 F620 on Tuesday (20th October) from 10.30am to 11.30am followed by private burial.

Family flowers only please. Donations, if desired, to Barnardos or the NSPCA.

Due to limited parking in the area, public transport is recommended to reach the Meeting House. Luas stop, Windy Arbour, located 200 metres away.

If you select to make a recurring contribution of at least $15 per month, you may select a thank-you gift. We thank our recurring donors on our website.

author: Chris Walker
title: Supreme Court to Hear Trump Arguments to Keep Musk’s DOGE Records Secret
content:
Elon Musk has spent over $360 million in support of Trump’s MAGA allies for this year’s midterm elections.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

On Tuesday, the United States Supreme Court agreed to hear an appeal from the Trump administration challenging a lawsuit that seeks access to records stemming from Elon Musk’s time leading the so-called “Department of Government Efficiency” (DOGE).

DOGE was responsible for ripping through the budgets of several federal agencies last year, ostensibly in the name of cutting wasteful spending but oftentimes targeting spending priorities opposed by President Donald Trump and Musk. The initiative operated without congressional oversight.

The U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID), which ran foreign aid projects around the world, faced the largest cuts. A former leading USAID administrator estimated over 700,000 deaths could be attributable to cuts made by DOGE from its beginning through July 2026.

Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington (CREW), a nonprofit watchdog group, filed a lawsuit to access records relating to DOGE’s work, arguing that the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) applied to DOGE. A federal judge agreed, and an appellate court confirmed the ruling. However, in June 2025, the Supreme Court intervened and sent the lawsuit back to the lower court to narrow the scope of open records requests.

After the lawsuit began to advance again, the Trump administration appealed to the Supreme Court to block it, arguing that the lower court decision “intrudes into the autonomy and confidentiality of presidential advisers and augurs time-consuming and burdensome discovery litigation.” The high court agreed to review the decision and to hear the case during this term, likely at the start of next year.

The Trump administration’s effort to keep information about DOGE hidden from the public is yet another example contradicting the president’s claims that he is “the most transparent” chief executive in U.S. history.

In a recent interview with The Economist, Musk said that he “got a little too involved in politics, got carried away, frankly.”

However, he appears to be back in the game: Musk has spent around $366 million in this year’s midterm election cycle in support of Republican candidates backing Trump’s MAGA agenda. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth has also brought him on board a three-person panel that will examine the future of technology for the U.S. military – a tremendous conflict of interest, given that Musk regularly seeks (and is often granted) billion-dollar contracts with the government.

Truthout is one of only a few platforms for justice-oriented, grassroots journalism. Today, we face an existential threat.

Due to Google’s launch of AI search, we’ve seen a drastic plunge in our site traffic and, as a result, our revenue. We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We are fundraising right now to meet our basic operating expenses. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference — we appreciate your support.

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: ‘Unacceptable’ for officer who killed Clyde River man to avoid inquest: Coroner
content:
A public inquest into an RCMP officer’s

fatal shooting

 of a Clyde River man in 2020 has been adjourned because the officer who fired the fatal shot in the incident has not confirmed he will participate.


Jerry Natanine wants the officer who killed his son Abraham Natatine to answer questions about the May 2020 incident that led to Abraham’s death. (Photo courtesy of Clara Noah)


Abraham Natanine was 31 when he died on May 6, 2020, after Cpl. Bryan Vaughan, shot him. The shooting happened after officers responded to a disturbance at a home at around 11 p.m. the evening prior.


In 2021, Ottawa police investigated and

concluded

 there were no grounds for charges. The police investigation also concluded Vaughan fired the fatal shot, said Andrew Morrison, the lawyer representing the Natanine family.


Nunavut law requires a public inquest into deaths involving an on-duty police officer. The inquest into Natanine’s death was scheduled to start on Oct. 5 and end on Oct. 9.


“I take their investigation at face value, but I still want to ask questions to the officer that was involved in the shooting,” said Jerry Natanine, Abraham’s father, in an interview.


Morrison asked a judge on Sept. 28 to adjourn the inquest after Nunavut Chief Coroner Marianna Cervantes informed him it would go ahead despite Vaughan’s presence being unconfirmed.


A judge granted that adjournment on Sept. 29.


The purpose of the inquest is to shine a light on what happened that night, which Morrison said can’t happen without each officer’s participation.


Cervantes declined to comment on the reason, when reached by Nunatsiaq News.


The Nunavut Coroner’s Act gives the chief coroner power to summon witnesses for inquests.


“The RCMP officer that was involved in the shooting hasn’t been summoned,” said Jerry Natanine.


“Summoning RCMP officers that are involved in shootings, that’s the norm. That’s normal for coroners inquests. It’s been done before in Nunavut.”


Natanine’s family wants to question Vaughan over discrepancies about what occurred on the day Abraham Natanine was killed, including Abraham’s words and conduct, the alleged weapon and the number of shots fired.


“Questions also remain about the officers’ actions after the shooting,” says the request for adjournment Morrison filed with the court.


The two other officers who were present when Natanine was shot had confirmed their attendance as of Sept. 18, according to court documents.


Nunatsiaq News reached out to Matthew Scott, the lawyer representing the involved RCMP officers. He declined to comment, redirecting requests for comment to RCMP.


Nunavut RCMP will participate in the inquest if called upon to provide evidence, said Sgt. George Henrie, spokesperson for Nunavut RCMP, although he said he had no information he could share about the participation of officers involved.


“Our family is not seeking to prevent the inquest from occurring,” Jerry Natanine said in an affidavit. “We seek a short adjournment so that reasonable steps can be taken to secure the meaningful participation of a witness whom the chief coroner has already described as central.”


Court documents also note RCMP’s reasons for Vaughan to not attend, which include concerns about his mental health and prior threats from community members. Vaughan is no longer employed with the RCMP, so he cannot be compelled by RCMP to attend, say the court documents.


“It is not acceptable for Cpl. Vaughan to avoid taking part in the inquest,” Cervantes noted in a Sept. 18 letter to RCMP’s counsel.


“Unless the RCMP provide adequate reasoning and evidence that Cpl. Vaughan cannot attend, initiating contempt proceedings is available under sec. 46 of the Coroner’s Act.”


Cervantes has offered various accommodations, such as a single-day attendance, a support person, and an advance hearing to set ground rules.


Natanine’s father also said does not believe enough evidence was brought forward to assess the validity of Vaughan’s mental health concerns, and suggested the inquest could be good for Vaughan, too.


“This can be a good closure, for the family, for all of us, and for the RCMP officer himself too,” he said. “If the officer is having issues psychologically, I would imagine he would want closure from this as well.”

title: Dene leaders push for education reform and greater control over child welfare
content:
Dene leaders passed resolutions on education and child welfare at the

56th Dene National Assembly

, calling for more stable school funding, stronger language and land-based learning programs, and greater First Nations involvement in decisions affecting Dene children and families.


The education resolution, presented by Chief Elizabeth Wright of the Tetlit Gwich’in Band Council, called for multi-year funding, additional student support, and improved teacher recruitment and retention.


“Education is a treaty right. That promise has never been fully kept,” Wright told delegates.


Figures presented at the assembly highlighted persistent and significant gaps in educational outcomes for Indigenous students in the Northwest Territories.


Wright said students in smaller communities face barriers that extend beyond the classroom, including overcrowded housing, inadequate teacher housing, limited course options and frequent teacher turnover.


“Our smaller communities are set up to fail and that’s a huge statement,” she said.


Some schools rely on multi-grade classrooms and online courses because of staffing shortages, Wright explained.


High teacher turnover also makes it harder for educators to build relationships with students and understand their backgrounds.


“Many of our students don’t have the curriculum or the funding to deliver real instruction in emerging for our language and our culture and our schools,” Wright said.


She said programs often receive funding for individual projects before having to apply again, rather than having the certainty of longer-term support making it difficult to provide critical on-the-land learning.


“What we are asking is that our schools receive multiple on the land immersion,” she said.


For Wright, passing the education resolution was only the first step. She urged leaders to bring the work back to their communities and collaborate with schools and education councils to identify needs and secure support.


“I want to, on my part, really support the education resolution going back into my community to work with the schools, to work with the education councils, and to ask them, how can we help?” she said.


Roy Erasmus Sr., a longtime counsellor and educator who spoke as a delegate with the Yellowknives Dene First Nation, said that problems arise long before students reach high school and that many children in smaller communities are already behind academically when they begin Grade 1.


Erasmus told delegates that figures presented at the assembly showed only about one in five students in smaller communities were meeting expected benchmarks by Grade 1.


He also cited attendance rates of about 60 per cent, meaning students were missing school roughly two days a week..


“Everybody gets pushed ahead with their same age kids to get moved up. The first time they have to pass something is in grade 10,” Erasmus said.


Margaret Ireland, an Elder from Tthets’ek’ehdeli – Jean Marie River spoke on behalf of Dehcho First Nation, and questioned whether teachers had the capacity to support students from remote communities.


“I don’t think there are teachers educated enough to deal with children who have all these challenges,” Ireland said. “I think they are just being pushed ahead to be pushed out.”


Chief Kele Antoine of Łı́ı́dlı̨ı̨ Kų́ę́ First Nation said education cannot be separated from health and wellness. He called for more qualified counsellors in schools to assess students’ needs and work alongside educators.


“Education, health and wellness are all interconnected, you know that is our Dene worldview everything is interconnected,” Antoine said. “Our schools need these qualified counsellors to help our youth and make these assessments for services and work along educators to help them to deal with the struggles they are facing because a lot of that burden is placed upon them and that is not fair.”


Throughout the three day assembly, conversations naturally flowed in and out of topics, but always came back to thinking about the next generation.


The issue of child welfare reform was another agenda item, with delegates calling for greater First Nations involvement in decisions about children taken into care and more support to keep families together.


Jennifer Drygeese, who heads the wellness division for the Yellowknives Dene First Nation, said Indigenous representatives need to be involved whenever children are apprehended by child and family services.

author: Daron Letts
title: Iqaluit crosswalk lights temporarily shut down
content:
Iqaluit’s only controlled

crosswalk


is disabled following a two-vehicle collision last week.


The lighted crossing is adjacent to the intersection of Niaqungusiariaq Road and Queen Elizabeth Way.


One of the crosswalk’s two light poles

fell Oct. 8

 after the incident, which halted

 early afternoon traffic for 90 minutes. No injuries were reported.


Residents should exercise caution while using the crosswalk, said acting city spokesperson Donna Keenainak in a public service announcement issued Wednesday morning.


Drivers are also asked to be cautious when approaching the intersection.


The busy intersection sits between the Qikiqtani General Hospital clinic entrance and the Sailijaaqvik Boarding Home, which sits at the southeast corner of the intersection. 


The city’s public works department did not immediately provide a timeline for repairs.


The crosswalk was installed in 2024.

author: Jai Dulani
title: The Tech Oligarchs Have Captured Washington — Now They’re Pivoting to the States
content:
AI and crypto firms have spent record amounts on the 2026 midterms.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Late last month, the wealthiest tech executives on the planet smiled next to President Donald Trump after essentially pinky-swearing they would voluntarily adopt safety policies around AI. While Trump described the agreement as “morally binding,” legal liability or enforcement measures were not explicit parts of the accord. The key takeaway from this handshake deal is that the people with the most amount of political power sit in Silicon Valley, not in Washington, D.C.

With the midterm elections just weeks away, it’s a good time to reflect on what Big Tech’s actions during this election season have revealed about its agenda and the larger context of the industry’s political influence. From CNN to The New York Times to NPR, there has been extensive news coverage of the hundreds of millions of dollars Big Tech has spent on the midterm elections. Months before Election Day, corporate spending this election cycle had already exceeded total disclosed corporate spending in the 2024 presidential election by 12 percent. The top two industries setting this record — with over half a billion dollars spent and counting — are crypto and AI. This unprecedented corporate spending on midterm elections is key to the tech industry’s plan to rig every level of government to work for the industry, from state legislatures to Congress.

The crypto industry is the largest political spender this election cycle, having spent over $200 million so far. The race it spent the most on was Felix Barry Moore’s campaign for U.S. Senate in Alabama. Crypto super PACs spent over $12 million supporting Moore, who has a pro-crypto track record; as the U.S. representative for Alabama’s 1st district, Moore co-sponsored a bill that prohibits the Federal Reserve from developing or issuing a central bank digital currency for U.S. monetary policy. This leaves digital assets under private control, away from federal scrutiny, which is what the industry wants.

In Illinois, crypto-related PACs spent over $10 million against former Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton, who is running for a seat in the U.S. Senate. Stratton has been vocal against the crypto industry. Politico reported that Stratton is endorsed by two prominent industry critics: Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Massachusetts) and Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker. Pritzker signed a digital assets law last year establishing regulatory oversight and protections for consumers against scams and fraud. In 2025, the FBI reported over $11 billion in losses related to cryptocurrency fraud in its Internet Crime Report.

Crypto corporations were also the dominant corporate political spenders in 2024 and gave $18 million to Trump’s 2025 inauguration. These contributions have paid off many times over the course of Trump’s second term. Trump removed Biden-era regulators and replaced them with crypto industry business partners or former industry insiders. In April 2025, the Trump administration shuttered the Department of Justice’s crypto enforcement team. Trump pardoned several crypto companies and billionaires that were under investigation for criminal money laundering and fraud, often after receiving investments in his own crypto empire. In June of this year, it was revealed that the Trump family has made at least $2.3 billion from crypto-related ventures during Trump’s second term.

Unprecedented corporate spending on midterm elections is key to the tech industry’s plan to rig every level of government to work for the industry.

This election season, Trump and the crypto industry were pushing for Congress to pass the Clarity Act, a bill essentially written by the crypto industry that locks in deregulation. From 2025 through August 2026, crypto companies Coinbase and Ripple spent a combined $18 million on lobbying Congress. Crypto donors gave Trump’s primary super PAC, MAGA Inc., over $88 million, more than any other industry. On September 15, the Clarity Act failed to advance through the Senate by a vote of 49-50. However, the attempt shed light on what the industry is seeking in terms of legislation: exemption from robust oversight, weak consumer and investor protections, and no prevention of conflicts of interest for self-enrichment and corruption.

author: Harriet Williamson
title: Sally Rooney’s Books Can No Longer Be Sold in the UK
content:
Bestselling Irish author Sally Rooney has announced that her books can no longer be sold in the UK due to the British government’s ban on Palestine Action. 


In a statement on Wednesday, the award-winning Normal People author said that due to her publicly-stated intention to go on supporting Palestine Action, including with

royalties from her work

, “the fulfilment of contracts to publish my work in the UK could now constitute a serious criminal offence”. 


Rooney added: “After a process of consultation and deliberation, and with my full agreement, my publisher Faber has therefore determined that it can no longer supply my work within the UK. I have made every effort to be honest with the public about my beliefs and intentions, and I am wholly prepared to accept the consequences.”


Palestine Action became the first direct action group in British history to be proscribed as a terror organisation under Keir Starmer’s Labour government last summer. 


Palestine Action is not proscribed or otherwise banned in the Republic of Ireland, where Rooney lives. 


Rooney’s

outspoken support for Palestine Action

 has previously disrupted her work in Britain. In September 2025, she was forced

to cancel a trip to the UK

 to receive the Sky Arts award for her latest novel, 2024’s Intermezzo, due to the risk she would be arrested under the Terrorism Act. 


She also submitted a statement to the High Court in support of the legal challenge to Palestine Action’s proscription in November 2025, arguing that the ban impeded free expression, including cultural and artistic expression, and warning that her works could disappear from UK booksellers altogether. 


Faber, Rooney’s UK and Ireland publisher, said: “Current legislation in the UK has led to circumstances where Faber cannot pass on UK earnings to Sally Rooney for her work. To sell a writer’s work and not be able to pass on earnings is an unconscionable situation for a publisher.


“As such, and in full agreement with Sally, we have taken the decision that we can no longer supply her works in the UK in any format. We remain the proud publisher of her remarkable body of work, which we will continue to sell in other territories.”


Since the ban on Palestine Action came into force, more than 3,700 people have been arrested for opposing the proscription, the vast majority for holding paper signs that read: “I oppose genocide. I support Palestine Action.”


According to the Home Office’s own data, terror-related arrests have risen by 1,553% in the last year, with 94% of them linked to support for Palestine Action. 


Palestine Action co-founder Huda Ammori is challenging the proscription in the Supreme Court, beginning on 4 November.

author: Redação
title: Big Problema
content:
O

Big Problema

 é uma conversa sobre o impacto das escolhas de quem está com a caneta na mão. Esse podcast narrativo foi idealizado pela primeira turma de

trainees da

 Agência Pública

 e procura entender como grandes empreendimentos têm impactado a cultura local das cidades brasileiras. Sabe quando bate um desespero porque a solução dos problemas ao seu redor não parece estar sob seu controle? Então, esse é um Big Problema.


A cada episódio, uma reportagem em áudio parte da vivência de um dos trainees para abordar como nossa relação com o espaço tem sido transformada com a chegada de gigantes da tecnologia e mais. Olhando as particularidades de cada cidade, esperamos mostrar que a distância não deve nos enganar: no fim, um problema local também é um problema coletivo. O nosso questionamento é: em nome dos interesses de poucos, o que temos deixado de fazer?

title: Gülsüm Elvan: Peace requires justice and women's struggle
content:
Eighty women from the women's movement, politics, academia, culture and the arts came together on 21 September under the appeal “Side by Side, Talking About the Future”, declaring that resolving the Kurdish question through democratic politics and negotiations would mark a new era for democracy in Turkey.


Gülsüm Elvan, the mother of Berkin Elvan, who was struck by a police-fired tear gas canister during the Gezi Resistance and died at the age of 15 after spending nine months in a coma, spoke to ANF about why she signed the appeal and what peace means for women.


‘Let no more mothers weep, let no more children be killed’


Gülsüm Elvan explained her reasons for signing the appeal, stressing her pursuit of justice and her determination to prevent other families from experiencing the same suffering. Elvan said: “The reason I signed this appeal is clear. I am a mother whose heart has been broken, whose child was taken from her, who has sought justice but has never been able to find it. At the same time, throughout my struggle for justice, whenever I speak about Berkin, I have always said, ‘Let no more mothers weep, let no more children be killed.’”


‘We will bring peace through struggle, women are rising up’


Elvan said that, as a mother who had lost her child, she believed genuine peace meant defending life. She drew attention to femicides and the deepening cycle of violence.


Elvan said: “A woman is killed every day. We are not safe on the streets. Just as marriage is natural, so is divorce by mutual agreement. Yet women are treated like property and murdered even for this reason. Women are being murdered, our nature is being destroyed, and journalists who report on these crimes are being killed. They killed Hakan Tosun. Even children are now killing one another in schools. Our struggle is for life, not death. Peace must be on the side of life.”


Elvan stressed that women must have an active say in the process and said: We will bring peace through struggle because women are rising up now. Real peace means living side by side democratically and in solidarity, in workplaces, on the streets and at home, producing and working together.”


‘We can see the future only by confronting the past’


Gülsüm Elvan stressed that confronting the past was essential to achieving lasting peace and that justice must be served. Elvan said, “If we confront who did what to whom and at what time, if the crimes committed are acknowledged and justice is served, only then can something genuine emerge. We will be able to see the future only when we confront the past.”


‘Prisoners are on hunger strike, trustees remain in place’


Gülsüm Elvan pointed to political prisoners, saying that practices contradicting the spirit of the peace process were still continuing. She said, “There are still government-appointed trustees. Many people, including my lawyers, are in prison. University student Taceddin Erol Şahin is being held in a pit-type cell simply for commemorating Berkin, and he is on the 163rd day of his hunger strike.”


Women to gather in Ankara on 31 October–1 November


The women-led struggle for peace and justice aims to bring fresh momentum to discussions on democracy in Turkey. The “Side by Side, Talking About the Future” appeal will be followed by a two-day conference scheduled to take place in Ankara on 31 October and 1 November, where possible paths towards a solution will be discussed in detail.

title: Iranian mountaineer and musician Ali-Sina Mustafavi executed
content:
According to Mizan News Agency, affiliated with Iran’s judiciary, Ali-Sina Mustafavi, a 38-year-old from Kerman, was executed on Wednesday. Human rights organisations had warned a day before the execution that it could be imminent after Mustafavi was placed in solitary confinement. Prison authorities were reportedly in contact with his family and had summoned them for a final visit.


Human Rights for Sports, an organisation that advocates for athletes’ rights, had also included Mustafavi, a mountaineer and musician, on its list of athletes at risk of execution. Human rights organisations said that Mustafavi had been forced to confess.


Mizan News Agency accused Mustafavi of carrying out armed attacks in Kerman in which civilians were injured. The report alleged that the attacks were carried out in support of Iran’s Crown Prince Reza Pahlavi and Israel.


Mizan also claimed that Mustafavi had filmed areas that were struck during the war. However, the agency provided no details about the trial proceedings or the evidence presented in court.


Iranian authorities systematically and arbitrarily use charges such as espionage, crimes against national security, armed rebellion, “enmity against God” and “corruption on earth” to prosecute dissidents and protesters. Human rights organisations say these charges are used to portray opponents as security threats and to justify death sentences.


Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch and United Nations experts have documented cases in which some death sentences handed down on the basis of such charges were carried out following proceedings involving serious violations of the right to a fair trial. In these cases, defendants were reportedly denied adequate access to lawyers, and confessions allegedly obtained under torture were used as the basis for verdicts.


Human rights organisations warn that many death sentences handed down under these circumstances may be arbitrary and politically motivated. They stress that the charges brought by Iranian authorities should not be accepted as independently verified facts.

title: Xebat Kobanê: A war veteran devoted to music and song
content:
Every war veteran who has sacrificed part of their body to protect their land and people in North and East Syria has a different story. Xebat Kobanê is one of them.


Xebat grew up in a patriotic family. One of his brothers was martyred, while one of his sisters joined the ranks of the revolution.


 


Xebat joined the People's Protection Units (YPG) with great enthusiasm and hope. He stood on the front lines of resistance in many areas against treacherous attacks targeting his land and people.


Xebat knew that martyrdom and injury were possibilities on this honourable path. Alongside his military training, he also developed himself ideologically. Conscious of following in the footsteps of Arîn and Rêvan, he took on all aspects of revolutionary work with great dedication.


Xebat Kobanê was wounded during a period of intense fighting, leaving both his legs paralysed. However, he has never regarded his injury as an obstacle. He follows Abdullah Öcalan's perspectives on war veterans and acts on the principle that “veterans are defenders of the revolution”.


Xebat has been interested in music for many years and plays the saz, a traditional long-necked string instrument, with remarkable skill. He also has a beautiful singing voice.


War veteran Xebat Kobanê takes his saz wherever he goes. He plays and sings songs for his fellow war veterans.

title: Martyr Welat wanted to be the voice of truth
content:
The early days of the Rojava Revolution saw many people living in Rojava seeking to become the voice of their society and expose the attacks, violations and suffering endured by their people. However, this was no easy task. Journalists who decided to document the realities faced by the people encountered numerous difficulties and dangers. Many lost their lives in pursuit of this mission. Many journalists seeking to document the atrocities committed during the Turkish state's occupation attacks on North and East Syria were targeted, particularly during the attacks on Serêkaniyê and Girê Spî in October 2019. One of them was martyr Vedat (Welat) Erdemci, who remained determined to be the voice of his people and bring the truth about the region to public attention until his final moments.


Journalist Zinar Cafer spoke to ANF about the life and work of journalist Vedat Erdemci, who was martyred during the attacks on Serêkaniyê on 11 October 2019.


Cafer said that a few words could never adequately convey the stories of the martyrs of the free press and added: “Writing books about the martyrs of the press or speaking about them in programmes is not enough on its own. At the beginning of the Rojava Revolution, many people in Kurdistan wanted to become the voice of their society because we witnessed numerous violations and attacks. The Rojava region of Kurdistan was experiencing attacks unlike anything seen elsewhere. Many people wanted to become the voice of this society. Of course, this was not work that everyone could easily undertake. Those capable of revealing the truth were mostly involved in journalism. However, whatever work a person undertakes, there is a price to pay. We take this opportunity to commemorate all the martyrs of the free press with respect. There were journalists in Rojava who succeeded in becoming the voice of truth and society through their pens and cameras until their final moments. When we speak of the martyrs of the press, we must particularly remember those martyred in October. The attacks on Serêkaniyê and Girê Spî took place in 2019. Welat Erdemcî was also martyred during those attacks.”


‘Martyr Welat wanted the world to hear the suffering of the Yazidi people’


Journalist Zinar Cafer said he had the opportunity to meet martyr Welat Ekinci in 2018 and continued: “I consider myself fortunate to have had the opportunity to meet martyr Welat in 2018. I first met him in the Deir ez-Zor region, during the operations to drive ISIS gangs out of the area. I was working in journalism at the time, particularly for Çira TV. The channel operated with the aim of becoming the voice of the Yazidi community. We were producing reports and covering developments, particularly the rescue of Yazidi women, children and other members of the Yazidi community. When I met martyr Welat, everyone was engaged in a race to deliver information as quickly and accurately as possible. Welat and I were almost competing with each other. We were both present when two Yazidi girls were rescued by fighters of the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF). The girls said, ‘We are Yazidis.’ Martyr Welat wanted to film the girls for a documentary he was planning to make. We also wanted to prepare a news report about what had happened. 


There was a competition over who could send their footage first and who could finish editing more quickly. We got to know each other through our work. Once we had filmed our footage, our relationship as comrades began to develop. Our comradeship with Colî and Suad also began during that period. Later, after filming together, we went to the Internal Security Forces headquarters. We sat together and talked. Martyr Welat wanted to make a documentary. His aim was to become the voice of the Yazidi community. He wanted to bring the suffering and hardships endured by the Yazidi people, particularly Yazidi women, and the 73rd Ferman (Shengal genocide) to public attention. Through his documentary, he wanted to show how ISIS had committed atrocities against the Yazidi community, what those atrocities involved and the immense suffering people had endured. His aim was to reveal all of this. We worked together on the documentary and completed part of it. Once the two Yazidi girls had been rescued, we travelled to Hasakah (Hesekê). Yazidis were living in the village of Gumer, south of Hasakah. We stayed there together for several days. Once we got to know each other, we began sharing the footage we had filmed and …

title: Two Iraqi soldiers killed in mine explosion in Kirkuk
content:
An officer and a soldier from the Iraqi army were killed in a mine explosion in Kirkuk on Wednesday. Two other soldiers were injured. The explosion occurred in Wadi Zixêtûn (Zghaitoun), near Reşad (Rashad), when a military vehicle belonging to the 11th Division triggered a previously planted mine.


Among those killed was Ahat Yasir, the division’s communications officer. The unit had been deployed to the area to investigate suspected positions and activities of remaining militants from the terrorist organization Islamic State (ISIS).


The previous day, the Iraqi Air Force had carried out airstrikes on ISIS positions in the valley south of Kirkuk. The soldiers involved had subsequently been dispatched on a reconnaissance mission.

title: YPJ: Attack on the images of our martyrs is an assault on the honour and values of our society
content:
The General Command of the Women’s Protection Units (YPJ) released a statement condemning the attacks against the images of fallen female fighters in Hesekê.


The YPJ statement on Wednesday said: “Recently, despicable attempts and attacks have targeted images of our martyrs and the sanctity they represent, which are among the most sacred values of our people and our revolution. These attacks, which directly target the dignity of our martyrs, violate the fundamental principles of humanity, moral awareness, and the inviolable red lines of society’s conscience.”


The statement stressed that: “Our martyrs are our identity, our honour, and the most sacred values underpinning our existence. Those who were defeated by the will and resistance of free women are now attacking our martyrs through inhumane methods that go beyond all standards of human morality. These immoral scenes and despicable acts are in no way befitting our people or our homeland. Such attacks constitute a direct assault on the honour and values of our entire society.”


The YPJ General Command called on the Damascus government to assume its responsibility, take immediate action against these inhumane acts, and hold those responsible fully accountable to the fullest extent possible. YPJ vowed that: “We will not remain silent in the face of these attacks, and no violation of the sanctity of our martyrs will go unanswered or unaccounted for.”


The statement concluded: “We call on all members of our nation, particularly women and young people, to remain vigilant against this psychological warfare, take a firm stand against these immoral scenes, safeguard our dignity, and stand united in solidarity with our martyrs. We will remain steadfast in defending the honour, dignity, and identity of our martyrs until the very end.”

author: Unknown
title: Families condemn the attack on the images of martyrs: We will continue on the path of our martyrs
content:
Rojin Mohammad, a founding member of the Martyrs’ Families Foundation in Kobanê, expressed her dismay at the attacks targeting images of martyrs in Hesekê, stating, “We will not accept such immoral acts.”


Rojin Mohammad explained that, for several days, certain groups have been systematically spreading chaos in the al-Khuwairan neighbourhood of Hesekê and attacking images of the martyrs.


“This is an attack on all peoples”


Speaking about the attacks, Rojin Mohammad said: “These martyrs sacrificed their lives for the freedom of Syrian soil and to protect all peoples from massacres. Attacking their images is not an attack on their families alone; it is an attack on all our values. This is a clear violation of the law.”


“The aim is to derail the integration process”


Mohammad pointed out that the aim of these attacks is to undermine the integration process in Syria. She continued: “This chaos and recklessness will not allow Syria to achieve integration or reach a positive outcome. On the contrary, these acts are an attempt to obstruct the integration process. The Syrian state must take notice of these attacks, put an end to these acts of sabotage, and hold those responsible accountable.”


“We will continue on their path”


Rojin Mohammad concluded her message by saying: “A democratic and free Syria must be built through the joint efforts of all its components. As mothers, we say that we will remain committed to the path of our martyrs until the very end. Martyrs never die.”

title: "Bogus": Minnesota State Senator Zaynab Mohamed on DHS Raid on Rep. Ilhan Omar's D.C. Home
content:
On Monday, federal agents from the Department of Homeland Security raided the Washington, D.C., home of Congressmember Ilhan Omar. Omar has faced years of racist targeting from President Trump over her ethnicity and immigrant background. She immigrated to the United States as a refugee from Somalia when she was a child. Omar is the first Somali American elected to federal office, the first woman of color to represent Minnesota and, along with Michigan’s Rashida Tlaib, one of the first Muslim women to serve in Congress.


“Congresswoman Omar has been under attack by this administration for the last decade. … She’s a symbol of everything that this administration hates: an immigrant who stands up for her community, who fought to be here in this country, and now is doing her job and her duty to serve her constituents,” says our guest Zaynab Mohamed, a fellow Somali immigrant who represents Minneapolis in Minnesota’s state Senate. As Trump spews racist invective against the Somali American community in Minnesota, Mohamed says, “We will continue to do everything we can to reject this type of hate and rhetoric from this administration.”

title: Orange Blossom Türkiye’ye geliyor: İstanbul ve Ankara’da sahne alacak
content:
Fransa çıkışlı elektronik müzik ve dünya müziği kolektifi Orange Blossom, ekim ayında İstanbul ve Ankara’da konser verecek. Elektronik altyapıları Orta Doğu ezgileri, Arapça vokaller ve geleneksel enstrümanlarla buluşturan grup, Türkiye’deki dinleyicileriyle bir araya gelecek.

1990’lı yıllardan bu yana müzik üreten ve Fransa’nın Nantes kentinde kurulan Orange Blossom, elektronik müzik ile farklı coğrafyaların geleneksel müzikal unsurlarını bir araya getiriyor. Trip-hop ve dünya müziği ekseninde üretim yapan kolektifin müziğinde Orta Doğu ezgileri, yaylılar, ritmik döngüler ve elektronik beat’ler öne çıkıyor. Meksika, Mısır ve Fransa gibi farklı ülkelerden müzisyenleri bir araya getiren grup, farklı müzik geleneklerinden beslenen bir sound oluşturuyor.

Orange Blossom’ın Türkiye’deki dinleyici kitlesiyle kurduğu bağda Türk müziğine ve sufi geleneğine duyduğu ilgi de etkili. Grup, özellikle Konya’da verdiği konserlerin ardından yaptığı açıklamalarda Mevlana’nın şehriyle kurduğu bağa ve sufi müziğin kendileri üzerindeki etkisine değindi. Ney ve saz gibi geleneksel enstrümanlara duydukları ilgiyi de dile getiren kolektif, bu müzikal unsurları kendi üretimlerinde elektronik altyapılarla bir araya getiriyor.

Grubun Türkiye’de geniş bir dinleyici kitlesine ulaşmasında “Ya Sidi” adlı parçası da etkili oldu. Parçanın “Çukur” dizisinde kullanılması, Orange Blossom’ın Türkiye’de daha fazla tanınmasına katkı sağladı.

Orange Blossom’ın müziğinde elektronik ritimler; Arapça vokaller, yaylılar ve farklı coğrafyalardan gelen geleneksel ezgilerle birleşiyor. Bu müzikal yapı, grubun canlı performanslarının da temelini oluşturuyor.

Kolektif, ekim ayında İstanbul ve Ankara’da vereceği konserlerde elektronik müzik ile dünya müziğini buluşturan repertuvarını dinleyicilerle paylaşacak.

Konserlerde kapı açılışı saat 20.00’de, performans başlangıcı ise saat 22.00’de yapılacak.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Διήμερη εκδήλωση της Κοινότητας Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών στο Πάντειο, 24 & 25/10
content:
Σύνδεσμος δημοσίευσης:

Διήμερη εκδήλωση της Κοινότητας Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών στο Πάντειο, 24 & 25/10


Οι εκδηλώσεις του διημέρου θα μεταδοθούν από το OmniaTV

:


YouTube


PeerTube


Facebook


Ανοιχτό κάλεσμα προς την κοινωνία


Χωρίς τη συλλογική δράση, οι ιδέες κοιμούνται στα κεφάλια και στις βιβλιοθήκες. Η γέννηση της πολιτικής ελευθερίας συμβαδίζει με τον αγώνα για τη συλλογική ιδιοποίηση της θεσμίζουσας αρχής.


— Eduardo Colombo


Ως Κοινότητα Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών καθ’ όλη τη διάρκεια του πολύμηνου και πολυεπίπεδου αγώνα ενάντια στα τελευταία σχέδια του κράτους και του κεφαλαίου βαδίσαμε και αγωνιστήκαμε πλάι πλάι με τους συντρόφους μας απεργούς πείνας μέχρι θανάτου Αριστοτέλη Χαντζή και Suzon Doppagne και από κοινού με όλους τους ανθρώπους των κινημάτων και της αλληλεγγύης. Ανθρώπους από ευρύτερες κοινωνικές ομάδες που αναγνώρισαν αυτόν τον αγώνα της Κοινότητας ως έναν συλλογικό αγώνα της κοινωνίας που αφορά όλες και όλους, συγκροτώντας ένα ευρύ κοινωνικό μέτωπο.


Και όπως αγωνιστήκαμε συλλογικά, νικήσαμε και συλλογικά!


Έχοντας κλείσει λοιπόν τον πρώτο μεγάλο κύκλο νικηφόρα, είναι ξεκάθαρο πως αυτό που έχουμε να υπερασπιστούμε δεν είναι μόνο αυτή η συγκεκριμένη νίκη ή μια ρωγμή που αποτέλεσε μια στιγμή στον χρόνο ή μια αυτοαναφορική συνθήκη εντός της οποίας βρίσκει τον εαυτό της η Κοινότητα Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών. Η παρακαταθήκη αυτού του αγώνα και της νίκης στο παρόν και το μέλλον απλώνεται μπροστά μας αναδεικνύοντας μια τεράστια δυνατότητα: Να ξαναχτίσουμε το συλλογικό φαντασιακό του κόσμου της αλληλεγγύης, της καθημερινής αντίστασης απέναντι στην εξαθλίωση, τον φόβο, την υποταγή, την εξατομίκευση, αντιτάσσοντας την αυτοθέσμιση των κοινωνιών μας και τη συγκρότηση κοινοτήτων, οπουδήποτε οι άνθρωποι αγωνίζονται, στις γειτονιές, σε πόλεις και χωριά, στους χώρους δουλειάς, στα σχολεία και τα πανεπιστήμια, στον δημόσιο χώρο.


Υπό αυτό το πρίσμα καλούμε σε μία διήμερη εκδήλωση στις 24 και 25 Οκτώβρη στις 17.00 στο Πάντειο Πανεπιστήμιο, (Νέο Κτήριο, Αίθουσα Σάκη Καράγιωργα Ι) για να συζητήσουμε πάνω στους κεντρικούς άξονες που δομήθηκε ο αγώνας αυτός, στις διαφορετικές μεθόδους και στα εργαλεία που χρησιμοποιήσαμε, καθώς και να δούμε συλλογικά και συνολικά τα σημεία που οδήγησαν στη νίκη αλλά και τις αδυναμίες, τις αστοχίες και τα λάθη που υπήρξαν. Αλλά κυρίως να εστιάσουμε στη συλλογική δυνατότητα που ανοίχτηκε μέσω αυτού του αγώνα και που πρέπει να διευρύνουμε. Να ενώσουμε τις αντιστάσεις μας για να δημιουργήσουμε τους όρους μιας κοινής δύναμης και να μετατρέψουμε την αλληλεγγύη από αντανακλαστικό σε σταθερή κοινωνική σχέση. Γιατί οι αγώνες κερδίζονται όταν συναντιούνται και όταν αναγνωρίζουν και συμπληρώνουν ο ένας τον άλλον.


Την πρώτη μέρα της εκδήλωσης, στο πλαίσιο ενός πρώτου απολογισμού, θα παρουσιαστεί από πλευράς της Κοινότητας η επιλογή του συγκεκριμένου αγώνα υπό τις συγκεκριμένες συνθήκες, οι πυλώνες πάνω στους οποίους οικοδομήθηκε, οι μέθοδοι και τα εργαλεία που χρησιμοποιήθηκαν, με αιχμή την απεργίας πείνας ως βασικό επαναστατικό μέσο για την επίτευξη της νίκης, καθώς επίσης και τα πρώτα συμπεράσματα και η προοπτική που ανοίγεται για το επόμενο διάστημα. Θα ακολουθήσουν διευκρινιστικές ερωτήσεις από τους παρευρισκόμενους, που θα απαντηθούν από την Κοινότητα, προκειμένου να προετοιμαστεί το έδαφος για την επόμενη ημέρα της εκδήλωσης.


Τη δεύτερη μέρα συλλογικότητες, οργανώσεις και ατομικότητες θα προβούν σε τοποθετήσεις, συμπεράσματα και απολογισμό του αγώνα, της στρατηγικής και των τακτικών του, καθώς και σε κριτικές αλλά και προτάσεις για τη συνέχεια.


Σας περιμένουμε όλες και όλους


—

Ή θα νικήσουμε ή θα νικήσουμε / Either we will win or we will win,

title: EMEP MDK Üyesi Şükran Doğan’a ‘NATO’ soruşturması
content:
Ankara — Emek Partisi (EMEP) MDK Üyesi Şükran Doğan, 7-8 Temmuz’da Ankara’da gerçekleşen 36. NATO Zirvesi’ne dair sosyal medya paylaşımları nedeniyle “halkı kin ve düşmanlığa tahrik” suçlamasıyla ifade verdi.

Emek Partisi İstanbul ve Ankara il örgütlerinin, Emek Gençliğinin ve gazetemiz Evrensel’in NATO Zirvesi’ne ve NATO gözaltılarına dair X paylaşımlarını yeniden paylaşan Doğan, Eryaman Karakolu’nda ifade verdi.

“Partimin paylaşımlarını retweet’lediğim için ifade verdim” diyen Doğan, Ankara’da uzun yıllar il yöneticiliği yaptığını da hatırlattı. “NATO zirvesinin üzerinden neredeyse 3 ayı aşkın bir süre geçti. Hâlâ NATO’yla ilgili sosyal medya paylaşımlarının soruşturma konusu yapılıyor olması ilginç. Cezaevinde onlarca NATO tutuklusu var” diyen Doğan, “Bu nasıl bir öfke” diye sordu.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

The midterm elections are in less than three weeks, on November 3. With Republican majorities in both chambers of Congress on the line, the Trump administration has thrown its time and resources into holding rallies in newly competitive states. We take a look at key Senate races in Georgia, Texas, Michigan and Maine with The Lever’s David Sirota. Ultimately, says Sirota, election results will hinge on voter turnout. “Will there be that surge of turnout based on how unpopular Trump is and how bad the affordability crisis is?” And, if they win, can Democrats then “deliver” on their promises?

David Sirotafounder and editor-in-chief of The Lever.

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now! I’m Amy Goodman.

With the midterm elections less than three weeks away, could the Democrats win back control of the House and the Senate? Election Day is November 3rd. Democracy Now! will be doing a four-hour broadcast from 8:00 to midnight Eastern Time that day. But at least 47 states and Washington, D.C., have early voting, with voters already casting ballots in some states. All 435 House seats and 33 Senate seats are on the ballot, in addition to some statewide races and ballot measures.

The list of battleground Senate states has been growing. As many as 10 Senate seats could be flipped, including several states that have been longtime deep-red Republican seats. Competitive races now include Ohio, Alaska, Texas and Kansas. Kansas has not sent a Democrat to the Senate in nearly a century. To win the Senate, Democrats need to flip four Republican seats and hold three of their own. They must hold Michigan, where Dr. Abdul El-Sayed is running against Republican Mike Rogers for an open seat.

President Trump’s been on the campaign trail. He spoke at a rally in Wasilla, Alaska, Tuesday, where incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan is facing off against Democratic challenger Mary Peltola, former congressmember and tribal judge. title: Eskişehir’de gazetecilerden dayanışma çağrısı: "Özgür basın susturulamaz!"
content:
Eskişehir’de gazeteciler ve Eskişehir Emek ve Demokrasi Platformu bileşenleri, Halk TV’ye yönelik müdahaleye tepki göstermek ve basın özgürlüğüne sahip çıkmak için Köprübaşı’nda bir araya geldi. Türkiye Gazeteciler Sendikası (TGS) Eskişehir Temsilcisi Şenay Bilik Yıldırım, burada yapılan basın açıklamasında, “Özgür basın susturulamaz, halkın sesi kısılamaz” diyerek gazetecilerle dayanışma çağrısında bulundu.

Platformu adına yapılan açıklamada, T24’e getirilen erişim engeli ile Halk TV’ye kayyum atanması ve kanalın yayınlarının durdurulmasının basın özgürlüğüne ilişkin kaygıları artırdığı belirtildi. Açıklamada, yaşananların yalnızca bir televizyon kanalının yayınını değil, orada çalışan gazetecilerin emeğini, iş güvencesini ve geleceğini de ilgilendirdiği vurgulandı.

Halk TV’nin Türkiye’nin en çok izlenen haber kanallarından biri olduğu ve Türkiye Gazeteciler Sendikasının örgütlü bulunduğu kurumda yaklaşık 200 basın emekçisinin çalıştığı hatırlatılan açıklamada, gazeteciliğin kolektif emeğe dayandığı ifade edildi. Muhabirlerden kameramanlara, editörlerden teknik ekiplere kadar çok sayıda basın emekçisinin gece gündüz çalışarak haber ürettiğine dikkat çekilerek Halk TV çalışanlarıyla dayanışmanın gazetecilik mesleğinin ortak değerlerine sahip çıkmak anlamına geldiği belirtildi.

Açıklamada, ülkede milyonlarca insanın geçim sıkıntısıyla mücadele ettiği, çocukların beslenme sorunlarının, gençlerin gelecek kaygısının, emeklilerin ve çalışanların yaşadığı ekonomik güçlüklerin giderek ağırlaştığı ifade edilerek, eğitimde laiklik, bilimsel eğitim ve fırsat eşitliği konularındaki kaygılara da dikkat çekildi. Kamu kaynaklarının kullanımı, yolsuzluk iddiaları ve kamuoyunu ilgilendiren soruşturmaların gazeteciler tarafından özgürce araştırılıp haberleştirilebilmesi gerektiği vurgulandı. Toplumsal sorunların görünür olması, tartışılması ve çözüm yollarının aranabilmesi için özgür basının önemine işaret edildi. Hiçbir toplumsal sorunun üzerinin örtülmemesi ve hiçbir gazetecinin kamu yararına yaptığı haberler nedeniyle baskı altında hissetmemesi gerektiği belirtildi. Hukuki süreçlerin gazetecilerin çalışma hakkını ve toplumun haber alma özgürlüğünü gözetmesi gerektiği ifade edildi.

Gazetecilerin farklı gazete, televizyon ve internet haber sitelerinde çalışabileceği, farklı düşüncelere sahip olabileceği belirtilen açıklamada, ortak mesleki kimliğe ve dayanışmanın önemine dikkat çekildi. “Biz gazeteciyiz! Birbirimizin rakibi olabiliriz ama birbirimizin düşmanı değiliz” denilen açıklamada, bir meslektaşın yaşadığı sorun karşısında sessiz kalmanın, benzer sorunlarla karşılaşıldığında yalnız kalma riskini büyüttüğü ifade edildi.

Dayanışmanın yalnızca gazetecilerin sorumluluğunda olmadığı vurgulanarak; işçiler, emekliler, öğrenciler, öğretmenler, esnaf ve toplumun bütün kesimleri özgür basının önemini görmeye çağrıldı. “Çünkü özgür basın herkes içindir” denilerek basın özgürlüğünün toplumun tamamını ilgilendirdiği belirtildi.

Açıklamada Anayasa'nın 28’inci maddesindeki “Basın hürdür, sansür edilemez” hükmü hatırlatılarak, gazetecilerin özgürce haber yapabildiği, basın emekçilerinin güvenceli koşullarda çalışabildiği ve herkesin farklı kaynaklardan haber alabildiği demokratik bir ortam istendi.

Türkiye Gazeteciler Sendikasının örgütlü olduğu Halk TV’deki meslektaşlarıyla dayanışma içinde olduklarını yineleyen açıklamada, gazetecilerin birbirini yalnız bırakmaması gerektiği vurgulandı. Açıklama, “Gazetecilik suç değildir! Basın hürdür, sansür edilemez! Yaşasın gazetecilerin dayanışması!” sloganlarıyla sona erdi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.
