author: Daron Letts
title: Nominations for KIA elections to open Oct. 26
content:
Nominations for five seats on the Kivalliq Inuit Association board of directors will open on Oct. 26.


The election is scheduled for Dec. 14, c

hief returning officer Penny Taylor announced Tuesday, in the association’s notice of election.


The roles include vice-president and secretary/treasurer, as well as the community director positions in Naujaat, Rankin Inlet and Whale Cove.


“This year’s election is more than a procedural milestone — it is an opportunity for Inuit across the Kivalliq region to help shape the future of their communities and strengthen Inuit-led governance,” Taylor said in an email on Tuesday. “

The voices of Inuit voters and nominees are essential to that work.”


The nomination period closes at 3 p.m. on Nov. 9.


Advance polls will be held on Dec. 7, Taylor said.


Mobile polls will also visit schools, elders’ centres, health centres, mine sites, boarding homes, healing facilities, and Winnipeg’s Uquutaq Medical Boarding Home. Schedules for each community will be posted by Nov. 30.


Eligible voters must be an Inuk enrolled under the Nunavut Agreement aged 16 years or older as of Dec. 14, 2026, and regularly reside in the Kivalliq region.


KIA is the designated Inuit organization under the Nunavut Final Agreement and one of three regional Inuit organizations associated with Nunavut Tunngavik Inc.

author: Unknown
title: Tupac cinayeti davasında Duane “Keffe D” Davis'e 40 yıl hapis
content:
ABD'de eski çete lideri Duane “Keffe D” Davis, rapçi Tupac Shakur’un 1996’da Las Vegas’ta öldürülmesini azmettirdiği gerekçesiyle 40 yıl hapis cezasına çarptırıldı. Eylülde jüri tarafından suçlu bulunan 63 yaşındaki Davis, kararı temyiz edeceğini söyledi.

Savcılar, Davis’in silahı ateşlememiş olsa da saldırıyı yönettiğini ve cinayette kullanılan silahı sağladığını savundu. İddia makamına göre ateş eden kişi, Davis’in yeğeni Orlando Anderson’dı. Cinayete karıştığını reddeden Anderson, 1998’de başka bir silahlı saldırıda öldü. Davanın temel delillerini Davis’in kendi anlatımları oluşturdu. Davis, saldırının düzenlendiği beyaz Cadillac’ın içinde bulunduğunu kamuoyu önünde defalarca kabul etmiş, 2019’da yayımlanan anılarında da silahı sağladığını anlatmıştı. Savunma ise bu açıklamaların kitap satmak ve para kazanmak amacıyla üretilmiş kurgu ve abartılar olduğunu ileri sürdü.

Davis, 2008’de rapçi Notorious B.I.G.’nin ölümüyle ilgili gizli bir polis görüşmesinde, kovuşturmadan korunmasını sağlayan anlaşma kapsamında Shakur cinayetindeki rolünü anlatmıştı. Daha sonra kitap ve röportajlarda yaptığı açıklamalar bu korumayı geçersiz kıldı; mahkeme polis görüşmesinin davada delil olarak kullanılmasına izin verdi.

Salı günkü ceza duruşmasında Shakur’un kardeşleri Sekyiwa ve Maurice, mümkün olan en ağır cezanın verilmesini istedi. Sekyiwa Shakur, ağabeyinin ölümünün ailelerini uzun süre derinden sarstığını söyledi.

7 Eylül 1996’da vurulan ve hip-hop tarihinin en önemli figürleri arasında gösterilen Shakur, hayatını kaybettiğinde 25 yaşındaydı. Davis’in mahkumiyeti, yaklaşık 30 yıl boyunca çözülemeyen cinayet dosyasındaki ilk mahkumiyet oldu.

author: Sicilia Libertaria
title: Attacco alle Idee!
content:
Reprimere il dissenso.


Il governo Meloni, dopo la batosta subita col Referendum sulla giustizia e le imponenti manifestazioni Pro-Pal, corre oggi ai ripari tentando di fare terra bruciata intorno ai movimenti di opposizione sociale che, finalmente usciti allo scoperto, ne hanno frenato le mire totalitarie e rivelato le collusioni genocidiarie, e minacciano in sovrappiù di farle perdere le prossime elezioni.


Contro questa vera opposizione che scende in piazza dimostrando di non temere i “decreti sicurezza” con i quali il governo avrebbe voluto silenziarla, rispolvera ora i metodi più duri ereditati dall’indimenticato Ventennio fascista, che non colpiscono più solo l’attivismo ma direttamente le idee di chi si oppone al governo. Non bastando più fogli di via, zone rosse, fermi preventivi, sanzioni onerose, “scudi penali”, minacce poliziesche e pressioni d’ogni tipo, si è deciso ad attaccare anche la libertà di espressione e di pensiero.


Due casi eclatanti

 sono venuti alla ribalta in questi giorni. Il primo riguarda tre esponenti del  movimento No Muos, tra cui un membro della Federazione Anarchica Siciliana, sottoposti a processo il 7 ottobre per istigazione all’occupazione della base MUOS di Niscemi. Il presunto reato sarebbe avvenuto a conclusione della manifestazione del 2 Agosto 2025, durante un serrato dibattito sulle future iniziative che il movimento avrebbe potuto intraprendere, tra chi era favorevole a ridiscutere la possibilità di una nuova occupazione della base (i compagni incriminati) e chi avanzava dubbi o ne contestava la proposta. Poliziotti aguzzini e magistrati, zelanti esecutori di ordini venuti dall’alto, scambiando surrettiziamente l’invito alla discussione per un invito all’azione, hanno pensato bene di ripescare un residuato del codice penale fascista, l’istigazione, reato a sé stante (perché non presuppone necessaria una successiva azione criminosa), infamante (perché prevede forme di prevaricazione della volontà altrui, subite specialmente da soggetti psichicamente labili e altamente influenzabili), che oltre a ledere la reputazione dei compagni accusati – impegnati da sempre nel creare autoconsapevolezza nelle persone – coinvolge l’intero movimento di cui fanno parte, le cui decisioni si fondano al contrario su pratiche assembleari e di condivisione politica.


È a tutti noto

 che a partire dagli anni ’80 del Novecento sono stati aboliti o fortemente ridimensionati reati similari all’istigazione, quali il plagio o l’apologia specialmente a mezzo stampa; che oggi, a costituire una vera emergenza sociale non sono gli attivisti contro le guerre e la militarizzazione dei territori, ma gli “influencer” e i “persuasori digitali” che governo e partiti politici incoraggiano e usano per i loro scopi elettorali; che appellarsi a un evanescente reato di istigazione, introdotto dal fascismo per tacitare definitivamente gli oppositori politici, se non strumentale e fazione appare quanto meno anacronistico.


Il secondo caso

 riguarda una ventina tra medici e psichiatri posti sotto inchiesta dalla procura di Ravenna con la speciosa accusa di aver redatto certificati falsi per impedire il trattenimento nei CPR (Centri di Permanenza per il Rimpatrio) di alcuni migranti irregolari. La procura ravennate entra nel merito della valutazione delle malattie e delle sofferenze patite in luoghi, come le carceri giudiziarie e i CPR, che molti dei medici indagati, aderenti in parte alla rete “Mai più lager – No ai CPR”, avevano definito come invivibili e disumani. L’accusa tende platealmente a denigrare l’azione di denuncia e di protesta portata avanti da questi medici, la cui vera colpa sarebbe quella “d’istigare alla cura”, come specificano le “Collettive Brigate Basaglia”, altra rete medica militante. Sono nuovamente le libertà di pensiero e di associazione a trovarsi sotto tiro.


Gli inquirenti vorrebbero asservire la medicina alle pulsioni repressive dello Stato, le cui strutture detentive provocano notoriamente gravi compromissioni della salute, danni mentali, autolesionismo e tentativi di suicidio in coloro che vi vengono trattenuti; e costringere a firmare falsi certificati di compatibilità carceraria anche quei medici che si rifiutano di tacere sulle inadempienze delle autorità e sottostare alle pretese del governo.


In entrambi i casi

, la presunta istigazione dei No Muos e l’ “istigazione alla cura” dei medici indagati, emergono in questi mesi palesi tentativi d’intimidire il dissenso, di creare …

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Rep. Delia Ramirez Introduces Landmark Bill to Abolish DHS, ICE, and CBP
content:
The Department of Homeland Security was established in 2002 as part of the Bush administration’s war on terror.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Rep. Delia C. Ramirez (D-Illinois) has introduced a bill that would abolish not just ICE, but the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) altogether, repealing the 2002 law establishing the agency and replacing it with one focused on protecting civil and human rights.

The wide-ranging legislation, dubbed the Reimagining Safety Act, would repeal the Homeland Security Act. Signed by President George W. Bush as part of his administration’s post-9/11 “war on terror,” the transformational bill created DHS and led to the establishment of Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

The bill would abolish DHS, CBP, and ICE — going further than the progressive call to abolish ICE. Other offices currently housed within the department, like Transportation Security Administration (TSA), the Coast Guard, Citizenship and Immigration Services, and the customs functions of CBP would be broken off into different authorities.

“We know that DHS was intentionally established with an overbroad mission and unchecked power. The last two years have made it visible what so many communities have actually been saying for decades: That DHS, frankly, is the single greatest threat to our public safety today,” Ramirez said in a press conference previewing the legislation last month. “We must strip away every single tool they are using to terrorize us.”

In DHS’s place, Ramirez’s bill would create a cabinet-level “Department of Community Safety,” which would address community concerns ranging from gun violence to disaster relief, using a public health-based approach. All immigration detention centers would be shuttered.

The legislation comes as DHS has ballooned into one of the largest agencies in the U.S. government in just 24 years of existence, with its authorities having been expanded by every subsequent presidential administration since its establishment.

Now, it has become central in executing President Donald Trump’s agenda, carrying out his administration’s fascist campaign of mass deportation, surveillance, and suppression of communities across the U.S.

The legislation is cosponsored by Representatives Adelita Grijalva (D-Arizona), Jim McGovern (D-Massachusetts), and Rashida Tlaib (D-Michigan), as well as over 40 advocacy and progressive groups.

“From its inception, those in power have wielded DHS as a weapon. Widespread illegal and abusive detention of immigrants, violent racial profiling, and state overreach — including domestic surveillance, civil rights violations via the USA PATRIOT Act,” Ramirez said.

“The bottom line is this: From its establishment, DHS has always been empowered to violate our rights, under the pretense of securing our safety,” Ramirez said. “Enough is enough.”

The administration has targeted hundreds of thousands of immigrants with arrests, detention, and deportations, often openly defying court orders and even constitutional safeguards to wreak havoc and invoke fear. At least eight people have been killed on the streets by DHS agents since the beginning of Trump’s second term, at least 57 have died in immigration detention, and thousands have been “disappeared” within the shadowy detention network or to places abroad. Meanwhile, journalists, activists, elected officials, and more, have repeatedly been caught in DHS’s ever-expanding dragnet.

Ramirez’s new bill also seeks to defang numerous other post-9/11-era policies and actions. It calls for the closure of the Guantánamo Bay military detention center, which Trump has used to imprison Somali immigrants. President Joe Biden pledged to and failed to close the center that became a notorious symbol of torture and indefinite detention under Bush, who once declared that the Geneva Conventions did not apply to the U.S.’s detainees at Guantánamo Bay and other CIA black sites established by the U.S. as it waged war on Iraq.

author: Unknown
title: Ameliyatı başarılı geçen Papa 14. Leo'ya akciğer kanseri tanısı kondu
content:
Vatikan Devlet Başkanı Papa 14. Leo'nun, akciğerinde tespit edilen kitle nedeniyle dünkü ameliyatının başarılı geçtiği ve öncesindeki testlerde şüphelenildiği gibi akciğer kanseri tanısının doğrulandığı bildirildi.

Vatikan'dan yapılan yazılı açıklamada, Papa'nın planlandığı üzere dün ameliyata alındığı belirtilerek, "Sağ akciğerin alt lobu, video destekli radikal cerrahi uygulanarak çıkarıldı. Ameliyat öncesi testlerde şüphelenildiği gibi, yapılan histolojik inceleme akciğer adenokarsinomu tanısını doğruladı" ifadeleri kullanıldı.

Papa'nın ameliyathanede yaklaşık 3 saat kaldığı, ameliyatın ise yaklaşık 90 dakika sürdüğü ve başarılı geçtiği aktarıldı.

Ameliyattan sonra Papa'nın normal bir şekilde uyandığı ve kısa bir gözlem süresinin ardından 10. kattaki odasına döndüğü kaydedildi.

Papa 14. Leo, dün öğle saatlerinde Gemelli Hastanesi'ne yatmıştı.

Vatikan'dan dün akşam saatlerinde yapılan ilk açıklamada da Papa'nın ameliyatının başarılı geçtiği vurgulanmıştı.

Vatikan, ameliyattan önce de Papa'nın iyileşmesi için 20 Ekim'e kadar bütün programlarının iptal edildiğini duyurmuştu. Tarihte ilk kez bir Papa, pazar duasında ameliyat olacağını açıkladı

Papa 14. Leo, 11 Ekim'de Vatikan'ın Aziz Petrus Meydanı'na bakan ofisinin penceresinden yaptığı geleneksel pazar duası sırasında, "Doktorlar, akciğerimde bir kitle (nodül) tespit etti. Doktorlar müdahalenin uygun olduğuna inanıyor ve bu nedenle onların tavsiyesi üzerine, nodülü aldırmak için ameliyat olmaya karar verdim. Ameliyat, önümüzdeki birkaç gün içinde yapılmak üzere planlandı. Manevi yakınlığınız için teşekkür ediyor ve kendimi dualarınıza emanet ediyorum" ifadesini kullanmıştı.

71 yaşındaki Papa'nın "sürpriz" olarak değerlendirilen bu açıklamasının ardından Vatikan Basın Ofisi de operasyon sonrasında iyileşme döneminin bir hafta sürmesinin beklendiğini duyurmuştu.

İtalyan basını da tarihte ilk kez bir Papa'nın, pazar duasında gelecek günlerde ameliyat olacağını şeffaflıkla açıkladığına dikkati çekti. Basındaki haberlerde, Papa'nın 6-17 Kasım'da Uruguay, Arjantin ve Peru'yu kapsayan Güney Amerika gezisini iptal etmemek için hemen ameliyat olma kararı aldığı belirtildi.

Vatikan'ın önceki devlet başkanı Papa Franciscus'un 21 Nisan 2025'te vefatının ardından Katolik Kilisesi'nin merkezi Vatikan'da 8 Mayıs 2025'teki Konklav'da (Papalık Seçimi) Papa olarak seçilen dönemin kardinali ABD'li Robert Francis Prevost, kendisine "Papa 14. Leo" ismini almıştı.

author: Unknown
title: Ecological destruction in the Zilan Valley continues
content:
Construction work on an irrigation canal in the Zilan Valley (Geliyê Zîlan), near the district of Erciş in Van province, is causing increasing damage to the region’s ecosystem. Since September 23, heavy construction machinery has been operating in the canyon as part of the so-called Pay Irrigation Canal Project. Excavation and construction work in the streambed and surrounding areas have altered the natural flow of water. Water levels have dropped significantly, and some sections of the stream have already dried up.


These developments threaten not only to have serious consequences for local wildlife and vegetation but also to exacerbate water supply problems in the region. Environmental activists have initiated legal proceedings against the project and requested a suspension of construction work. A court decision is still pending, while machinery continues operating in the valley.


Trees felled and riverside vegetation destroyed


The areas along the streambanks have been particularly severely affected. Trees have been felled and large sections of natural vegetation cleared within the valley. The grasses, shrubs, and trees growing in the area perform essential functions in maintaining the ecological balance: they stabilize the soil, prevent erosion, regulate water levels, and provide habitats for numerous animal species.


With the destruction of this vegetation, the streambanks are losing their natural protection. At the same time, wildlife habitats used for shelter, feeding, and reproduction are being destroyed. These interventions threaten the interconnected relationship between water, soil, and vegetation, which is crucial to the valley’s ecological stability.


The alterations to the streambed also have far-reaching consequences. Together with its banks, the stream forms a continuous habitat for fish, aquatic invertebrates, amphibians, birds, and other wildlife. Falling water levels and drying sections of the stream can destroy these habitats, reduce moisture in the surrounding soil, and make it more difficult for animals to access water.


Legal action against construction work


Environmental activists have filed an application with the Administrative Court in Van seeking a suspension of the project’s implementation. They have also filed a criminal complaint with the public prosecutor’s office in Erciş. No decision has yet been issued on the urgent application. Construction work continues despite the ongoing legal proceedings.


The controversial irrigation canal project dates back to 1993, when the Turkish State Hydraulic Works (DSI) initiated the project and issued a positive environmental impact assessment decision. After the project remained unimplemented for many years, it was put out to tender in 2016 and awarded to the company Günsay.


Zilan Valley threatened by large-scale projects for years


The irrigation project is not the only intervention threatening the natural environment of the Zilan Valley. For years, the region has been increasingly affected by state-backed energy and infrastructure projects. Particularly controversial is the development of geothermal resources, which has been pursued since 2020 and now threatens the livelihoods of several villages.


In Şorik, Karakilise, and Çaxirbeg, drilling and development activities are encroaching on agricultural land and residential areas. Residents now even fear that their villages may be evacuated. Environmental groups have also warned about the potential discharge of thermal waters contaminated with heavy metals into the region’s irrigation systems and waterways. However, publicly documented measurements are not yet available to allow a definitive assessment of the contamination levels.


The scale of the planned development is reflected in tenders issued in 2024, which offered licenses for the exploration and exploitation of geothermal resources covering approximately 8,860 hectares in total. The ongoing construction work on the Pay Irrigation Canal represents yet another intervention in an ecosystem already under pressure from energy projects.

author: Chris Walker
title: Report: Trump Is Having Second Thoughts About Livestreaming Military Execution
content:
Trump isn’t “particularly enthusiastic” about Pete Hegseth’s plan to livestream a military execution in December.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

President Donald Trump is reportedly asking advisors if he should go through with Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth’s plan to livestream a military execution later this year.

Trump has publicly indicated that he’ll make a final decision on the matter soon.

“There are two thoughts: don’t show it and show it,” Trump said. “Because, you know, by showing it, maybe other people won’t be doing what he did.”

“I’ll make a decision ultimately. I know what the military would like to do, but I’ll make a decision,” Trump added.

But according to reporting from Axios, Trump is questioning whether the execution of former Army Maj. Nidal Hasan should be televised, asking his advisers for their views on the matter.

Hasan was convicted of killing 13 soldiers at Fort Hood in Texas in 2009. He was shot during the rampage, and is now a paraplegic, paralyzed from the waist down. Hasan is set to be executed by a firing squad in December.

The president “didn’t sound particularly enthusiastic” about a live, national showing of the execution, a source close to Trump said to the publication, adding that “he’s calling around, doing the Trump thing, asking people what they think.”

The livestream event “might not happen,” another source confirmed.

Trump’s public statements about the death penalty reveal that he has errant views about capital punishment. Multiple studies have shown that there is no evidence supporting the idea that the death penalty can act as a deterrent, or that the threat of capital punishment somehow lessens violent crime. Indeed, several years of data demonstrate that the homicide rates in states with capital punishment are higher than in states without the death penalty.

Trump is also wrong about what “the military would like to do.” While there isn’t widespread data to demonstrate most servicemembers’ views one way or another, some officers have spoken out against the planned livestreaming of Hasan’s execution.

“It takes away everything America stands for when we do public executions,” one Army officer said in an anonymous comment to CNN. “The generational harm caused by allowing troops in uniform to stand in front of a man in a wheelchair and watch him get shot to death is irreparable.”

Several religious leaders, including Pope Leo, and a bipartisan cadre of lawmakers, have also spoken out against livestreaming the execution.

Despite Trump’s reticence about this specific event, he has been an outspoken proponent of expanding the death penalty, including for non-lethal crimes such as drug dealing. In his first week in office, he signed an executive order peddling the the false claim that the death penalty is “an essential tool for deterring” crimes, calling for the attorney general to seek the death penalty for crimes involving the killing of law enforcement officers, or when the defendant being charged is an undocumented immigrant.

In an op-ed published last week, Truthout’s board of directors president Maya Schenwar decried the death penalty in all of its forms, describing the botched execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee as an act of torture and Hegseth’s decision to livestream Hasan’s execution as part of a larger “pro-death penalty fervor.”

“The brutality is the point. The torture is the point. The murder, not only state-sanctioned but state-celebrated, is the very point,” Schenwar wrote.

A cohesive life-affirming agenda rejects not only executions, but also the inherent violence of incarceration, policing, deportation, imperial wars, and military aid to genocidal forces. It makes no excuses — let alone expansions — that prop up or prolong the existence of these institutions in ‘kinder, gentler’ forms.

“Let’s not allow ourselves to give in to the inertia of our brutal present, in which death by hanging is a mercy. Let’s envision the cohesive, life-affirming agenda that embraces a future for all of us, a world in which the torture of Christa Pike — or anyone — is unthinkable,” Schenwar concluded.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Trump Admin Is Reportedly Offering Children as Young as 5 $3,000 to Self-Deport
content:
The offers are meant to “coerce” the children into giving up on their immigration cases, an immigrant advocate said.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

ICE is offering children as young as 5 years old $3,000 “incentives” to voluntarily depart the country, legal advocates have reported, as the Trump administration works to separate immigrant families under the hammer of their mass deportation machine.

Bloomberg Law first reported on the offers, citing attorneys and immigrant advocacy groups who say that the offers are sometimes given to children who lack legal representation. The offers, they say, are a method of forcing children to take a deal so that they drop their legal challenges before they have gone through their time in the court system.

Shaina Aber, executive director for the Acacia Center for Justice, told Bloomberg Law that the tactic is “part of a larger pattern of really trying to coerce children, bully children, intensify pressure on children so that they abandon their cases.”

“It’s part of this deport-at-all-costs policy that seems to be in particular targeting children,” Aber went on.

The offer is being made by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) attorneys as well as immigration judges. In some cases, judges are telling children that it is a one-time offer and giving them no time to consider it, forcing them to make a decision “on the spot” even though “they might not understand what the longer term consequences are down the line,” Aber said.

Another group, the Amica Center for Immigrant Rights, said that it and similar groups have received the emails from ICE’s Office of the Principal Legal Advisor offering a “$3,000 incentive” for children. Michael Lukens, head of Amica, told Bloomberg Law that the latest offer came to his office this week for an 11-year-old.

The reporting shows that the Trump administration’s policies toward child deportations are even more extreme than previously thought. Last year, NBC reported that the Trump administration was offering children aged 14 and older $2,500 to self-deport or voluntarily leave the country, according to a Department of Health and Human Services memo.

Indeed, reports have since found that the Trump administration is carrying out this policy even in cases where the children were living with their families, in cases likened to President Donald Trump’s family separation policies from his first term.

The Department of Homeland Security didn’t confirm or deny the payments, saying that the administration is supposedly working to reunite children who come to the U.S. unaccompanied with their families.

According to a tracker maintained by the Marshall Project, as of August, the federal government has deported over 22,500 children since January 1, 2025. ICE arrests of children have only continued to escalate throughout Trump’s second term, with over 8,500 children having been arrested thus far — including 562 children and babies under 4.

author: Stephen Prager
title: Air Force Major Who Called for Trump’s Impeachment Held in Solitary Confinement
content:
Some legal experts say Jason Watson’s confinement for 24 hours a day could amount to illegal pretrial punishment.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Air Force Maj. Jason Watson was arrested July 1 on the steps of the US Capitol after calling for the impeachment of President Donald Trump. According to his lawyer, he’s now being held in solitary confinement 24 hours a day in what some legal experts say could amount to illegal pretrial punishment.

The Uniform Code of Military Justice (UCMJ) contains provisions barring officers from engaging in public political activities that are typically protected for civilians, including criticizing the president and other elected officials.

Prosecutors have charged Watson with violating them when he participated in a news conference calling for Trump to be removed from office over his launching of military actions against Iran, Cuba, and Venezuela without congressional authorization.

After the speech, Watson stood on the Capitol steps holding a sign that read “Impeach, Convict, Remove” and was arrested after he refused to move.

Before he was charged, Watson gave a CNN interview on August 17 in which he continued to criticize Trump, accusing him of “flagrantly violating the Constitution” and “breaking the law.”

He acknowledged that he could face severe consequences as a result of his speech: “We just have to be willing to accept that we can change what is happening in our country if we are just willing to pay a price for it,” he said.

One day later, he was arrested while on duty and taken into pretrial confinement. He now faces a general court-martial, the military’s most severe trial, which is capable of imposing lengthy prison sentences.

“Cruel and unusual form of punishment.” U.S. Air Force Maj. Jason Watson is headed to the most severe form of military trial — a general court-martial — after calling for President Trump’s impeachment while in uniform at the U.S. Capitol. His attorney reveals that Maj. Watson… pic.twitter.com/7izEA47Gh2

On Friday, Watson’s lawyer, Christopher Mutimer, told CNN that after nearly two months, Watson is “still in solitary confinement 24 hours a day,” which he said amounted to “cruel and unusual” punishment.

“Even if he gets an hour to eat or to exercise, he is alone,” Mutimer said. “He is literally by himself, with his thoughts, in a room where the light never turns off all day.”

In an essay published Sunday by writer Monte Mader, Watson himself acknowledged spending his days in isolation, revealing that his Bible had only recently been returned to him and that he had little access to news.

Watson described the conditions of his confinement as the reality one must accept when choosing to engage in nonviolent resistance.

“Walking this path,” he said, “means exposing oneself to violence while refusing to retaliate against it.”

Major Jason Watson is NOT a Democrat. His protest was NOT about party politics. It was about what he believes his oath requires of him—and the price he’s willing to pay for speaking out. Everyone has seen the arrest. Now hear the courageous powerful speech that came first: pic.twitter.com/MMRoiYPV7K

After his July 1 protest, Watson had been restricted to Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling in Washington. Though the base reportedly has a confinement facility, following his detention, he was instead moved to a county jail in Maryland.

During Watson’s September 18 preliminary hearing, Maj. Joshua Wendell, the hearing officer, said Watson could not be confined with civilians and was therefore kept in solitary confinement.

“He was placed in confinement because of the law, which puts him in solitary confinement,” Wendell said, according to Stars and Stripes.

Article 13 of the UCMJ “forbids punishing a service member before trial and forbids pretrial restraint more rigorous than the circumstances require.”

Mutimer has pointed out that solitary confinement is “usually reserved for individuals who are disobeying or are violent, and injuring other people,” and usually only for “a day or two, or a week.” Watson, he said, has “been in there for months now.”

author: Kourosh Ziabari
title: Trump’s Genocidal Rhetoric on Iran Deserves Legal Consequences, Scholars Say
content:
As Trump repeats annihilation threats against Iran, legal scholars implore other countries to step in.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

US President Donald Trump’s threats to destroy Iran have become so frequent that they often don’t make headlines. One recent exception, though, was during his 38-minute speech at the 81st session of the UN General Assembly on September 22, in which Trump mentioned Iran 17 times.

“Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever was before? Maybe one of the greatest in the Middle East, or even the world,” he blustered. “Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again?”

Using a mix of warnings and expletives to address Iranians, Trump falsely claimed that Tehran had refused to negotiate an agreement over its nuclear program. On both occasions when Iran was militarily attacked, in June 2025 and February 2026, it was in the middle of diplomatic talks with Trump’s envoys.

“Do I drive them into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness or generations?” he added during his speech at the international organization founded in 1945 to preserve global peace and security.

The U.S. military operations in Iran, an extension of the U.S.-Israeli aggression launched in February, have largely been on hold for the past few weeks as American voters gear up for the midterm elections in less than a month — with the unpopular war remaining a hot-button issue. But White House officials have sought to preserve momentum for the conflict through continued combative rhetoric, and Trump has led the charge with occasional social media outbursts and inflammatory monologues.

The UN address is far from the only time that Trump had resorted to annihilatory language to describe his intentions with Iran. “I have a big decision coming up,” Trump told Axios earlier in September. “Do I want to go in and annihilate them, or do I not?”

“My question is, if and when I want to destroy the entire country, when do I do it?” he told Fox News days after his speech at the UN. In October, TIME published an interview in which the publication asked him to clarify his annihilation comments. “Yeah, I would do that. It’s possible.… Because by annihilating Iran, we’ve created peace in the world. With Iran, I don’t think you could ever have peace.”

Most notably, in a widely criticized Truth Social post on April 7, he wrote, “a whole civilization will die tonight, never to be brought back again,” prompting calls from several members of the Congress for his impeachment under the 25th Amendment to the Constitution, including Rep. Steve Cohen (D-Tennessee), Rep. John Garamendi (D-California), and Rep. Jan Schakowsky (D-Illinois).

Different sections of the amendment have been invoked in the past when the sitting presidents were incapable of discharging their duties. For example, on November 19, 2021, former President Joe Biden invoked Section 3 of the 25th Amendment to undergo a medical surgery and his vice president Kamala Harris took charge as acting president for 85 minutes. Still, the fourth section of the amendment laying out the authority of the vice president and cabinet members to remove the president has never been invoked.

On April 30, a group of 30 psychiatrists and psychologists published a statement declaring that Trump was contending with a serious mental health impairment. The statement, which was entered into the Congressional Record by Senators Sheldon Whitehouse and Jack Reed of Rhode Island, argued that if the signatories were called to adjudicate the president’s fitness to fulfill the obligations of his office, they would confirm that “he lacks the capacity to do so.” Still, that option has not been raised by Vice President JD Vance or members of Trump’s cabinet.

“Trump’s statement was certainly genocidal in character, in the sense that it appears to demonstrate the intent to destroy the Iranian people as a protected national group, in whole or in part,” said Heidi Matthews, an assistant professor of law at York University in Toronto, referencing the U.S. president’s chilling Truth Social post.

“Direct and public incitement to genocide is considered an ‘other genocidal act,’ in that it is a crime independent of whether or not genocide is actually carried out,” she told Truthout …

title: Elon Musk Becomes the Largest Known Donor to This Year’s Midterms
content:
Alex Gibney, director of the new documentary Musk, discusses the rise of the world’s first trillionaire.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

We speak with the Academy Award-winning director Alex Gibney about his new documentary Musk, an expansive, nearly four-hour examination of the world’s first trillionaire and how he has amassed unprecedented power in business, technology and politics. The film traces Elon Musk’s early ventures and the rise of SpaceX and Tesla, examining the role of government support in their growth. It also explores his acquisition of Twitter, now X; his alliance with President Donald Trump and the MAGA movement; and his role in the Department of Government Efficiency, or DOGE, whose cuts devastated federal programs, including USAID.

Gibney says Musk has carefully crafted an image of a “polymath” who can solve the world’s most pressing problems, but that he is really “kind of a ruthless businessman” willing to do whatever it takes to succeed, including “a series of elaborate cons” to win government support for his companies.

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org, The War and Peace Report. I’m Amy Goodman, with Juan González.

The world’s richest man is pouring hundreds of millions of dollars into the November midterm elections in an effort to help Republicans hold on to their Senate majority. Elon Musk, the world’s first trillionaire, has reportedly funneled more than $366 million into Republican groups and his own super PAC, according to The New York Times. That makes him by far the largest known donor to this year’s midterms. Musk and President Trump have appeared together at three events over the past two weeks, praising one another, after a very public falling-out last year. And Musk is doing all this while overseeing a sprawling business empire that’s benefited enormously from federal contracts.

We spend the rest of the hour on a new documentary about Musk and the unprecedented power he’s amassed in business, technology, politics and beyond. The epic, nearly four-hour-long film by Academy Award-winning director Alex Gibney is called simply Musk. title: “Καμία δίωξη στον κόσμο του αγώνα” – συγκέντρωση την Τετάρτη 14/10, 09.00, στα δικαστήρια Χανίων
content:
Από την Ανοιχτή συνέλευση για την κρατική δολοφονία του Κώστα Μανιουδάκη:


Καμία δίωξη στον κόσμο του αγώνα


Τετάρτη 14 Οκτωβρίου & Τετάρτη 21 Οκτωβρίου | 09:00 | Δικαστήρια Χανίων


Από το καλοκαίρι του 2024, οι 4 μπάτσοι δολοφόνοι του Κώστα Μανιουδάκη έχουν κατηγορηθεί για ανθρωποκτονία με ενδεχόμενο δόλο σε ήρεμη ψυχική κατάσταση από κοινού. Μόλις τους τελευταίους 10 μήνες, η υπόθεση ξυλοδαρμού μέχρι θανάτου του Κωστή προχώρησε στην κύρια ανάκριση και ολοκληρώθηκε, επιβάλλοντας στους δολοφόνους απαγόρευση εξόδου από τη χώρα και εγγυήσεις 20.000€ για τους 2 μπάτσους και 5.000€ για τους άλλους 2. Οι μπάτσοι δολοφόνοι παραμένουν στις θέσεις τους, ένοπλοι, ενεργώντας μέχρι και σήμερα «τυχαίους» ελέγχους.


Η ανοχή και η επιβράβευση του κράτους στα δολοφονικά εγκλήματα των ένστολων φονιάδων του, έρχεται (και) μέσω του δικαστικού συστήματος: μέχρι και σήμερα, τους έχει δώσει το ελεύθερο να μηνύουν με κάθε τρόπο τον κόσμο που αγωνίζεται, από τους συγγενείς του Κωστή μέχρι τα μέλη της ανοιχτής συνέλευσης. Αντί, λοιπόν, να προχωράει ο προγραμματισμός της δίκης για ανθρωποκτονία από πρόθεση, προχωράνε οι μηνύσεις που κάνουν οι ίδιοι οι δολοφόνοι. Περιττό να πούμε πως στην περίπτωση που στη θέση των μπάτσων, κατηγορούνταν κάποιος «φτωχοδιάβολος», οι διαδικασίες θα κινούνταν με γρήγορους ρυθμούς.


Καλούμε σε συγκεντρώσεις αλληλεγγύης στα δικαστήρια: στις 14/10 για τον αδερφό του Κωστή, τον οποίο μήνυσε η Κ. author: Daron Letts
title: RCMP charge Chesterfield Inlet youth withfirst-degree murder
content:
Police have charged a Chesterfield Inlet youth with first-degree murder following the death of a man in the hamlet early Friday morning.


Nunavut RCMP issued a news release about the incident Tuesday.


Officers arrived on scene at 1 a.m. following a report of gunfire and located a man “with injuries consistent with a gunshot wound,” the release said.


The victim was transported to the local health centre, where he was pronounced dead.


Police arrested a youth and the Nunavut RCMP Major Crime Unit laid charges that same day.


The youth, whose identity is protected by law, is in custody and scheduled to appear in court in Iqaluit on Nov. 16.


It’s unclear what, if any, relation there is between the accused and victim.


RCMP are not providing any further details, the release said.

author: Dion Nissenbaum
title: Meet the Right-Wing Activists Urging Trump to Take Extreme Action in Elections
content:
“The president needs to completely declare a national emergency,” said longtime Trump ally Mike Lindell.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Since being released early from prison in June, former Colorado election clerk Tina Peters has been granted extraordinary access to the halls of power in Washington.

Peters said she has traveled to Washington seven times, visited the White House at least twice, and met with senior officials at the Justice and Commerce departments — remarkable access for someone on parole after a 2024 felony conviction for tampering with voting machines in an attempt to show that the 2020 election was rigged against President Donald Trump.

She’s a high-profile example of a group of Trump supporters and conservative activists trying to lay out a roadmap for the president to follow. They are urging him to take more extreme steps to try and influence the outcome of an election that many polls suggest could end Republican control of Congress. But as the election closes in, the activists are now voicing increasing concerns that the president and his administration aren’t going to act on their ideas.

Peters isn’t shy about what she wants. The 71-year-old activist is pushing the Trump administration to use emergency powers before the November election to scrutinize voting machines across America, though that’s something most experts and lawyers say it can’t legally do.

“A lot of people would say that we just need to go rogue and declare this radical emergency and we need to shut everything down,” Peters said last week on an election activist livestream on Rumble. “The encouraging part is that there are already orders and laws in place that allow them to do what they need to do.”

Other conservative activists pushing for changes to election administration include:

Cleta Mitchell, head of the Election Integrity Network and a Trump ally, who is pushing for the Commerce Department to examine foreign-made parts in voting systems as potential national security risks that should be addressed before November.

Mike Lindell, a longtime Trump ally who has spent years promoting claims that voting machines were used to manipulate U.S. elections, who wants Trump to declare a national emergency and prevent the use of electronic voting machines in November.

Peter Ticktin, a Florida attorney representing Peters and longtime Trump friend, who said Trump might have to declare martial law if the election results are in question.

Steve Bannon, a longtime Trump ally and former White House chief strategist who hosts the influential right-wing podcast War Room, who has repeatedly urged Trump to use emergency powers to require voter identification at the polls and send ICE agents to polling places.

James Mills, head of the Georgia State Election Board, who sent a letter last week urging the Trump administration to compel his state to make election software updates before the November election.

A wide array of lawyers, voting rights groups, civil rights leaders, and Democrats have denounced the ideas as an unconstitutional attack on the nation’s electoral process. But such criticisms haven’t deterred Trump from trying to advance a variety of proposals to impose more federal control over elections.

Federal courts have blocked Trump from advancing key pillars of two executive orders that would have transformed the U.S. Postal Service into a ballot regulation agency, eliminated grace periods for ballots arriving after Election Day, and required all people to provide documented proof of citizenship to register to vote.

With most of his efforts at election oversight blocked, Trump has left open the possibility he might heed the calls of supporters urging him to take drastic action before November.

“Let me just say that stranger things have happened, OK?” Trump said in an August interview with Wayne Allyn Root on Real America’s Voice, responding to a question about declaring a national security emergency as a way to assert more authority over elections. “I’ll leave it at that.”

The Trump administration has laid out an Election Day plan that includes dispatching 1,000 election monitors to look for any problems in key states, establishing FBI command posts across the nation, and military monitoring of potential cyber attacks from hostile nations. author: Chris Walker
title: US Measles Cases Top 4,200 as Pennsylvania Reports Sixth Death Related to Virus
content:
The CDC website has only recognized two of the six measles-related deaths recorded in Pennsylvania this year.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Health officials in Pennsylvania have announced another death related to measles, the sixth overall in the state and the U.S. since the beginning of this year.

Officials identified the person who died as a 39-year-old woman from Franklin County. The individual was reportedly not vaccinated against the virus. The county coroner described the cause of death as a “probable acute cardiac event due to possible complications of the measles.”

The state is facing a large measles outbreak, accounting for about a quarter of all measles cases identified across the country since January 1, 2026. As of Tuesday morning, over 4,260 measles cases have been reported in the U.S., 1,152 of them from Pennsylvania alone. Both South Carolina and Texas are also reporting close to 1,000 measles cases.

Notably, the vast majority of people who have tested positive for measles are unvaccinated, with only 3 percent of cases affecting a person who has received the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) shot.

Death from measles is rare but not unheard of, with about one to three deaths occurring for every 1,000 cases, some estimates show. The virus can also cause lifetime neurological and/or respiratory issues.

The vaccine is widely considered the best way to prevent measles infection. In rare instances where a “breakthrough” case occurs (where a person who was vaccinated still gets infected), the symptoms are generally less severe. The shot requires a higher threshold of vaccinated individuals in a given community than other vaccines to be highly effective at stopping the virus’s spread.

Despite a spate of deaths in Pennsylvania being recorded by state officials, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has so far only recognized two of those deaths on its website.

Measles was once considered “virtually eliminated” in the U.S., due to extremely low counts of infections identified yearly — in 2024, for instance, only 285 cases were documented. But anti-vaxxer and right-wing movements over the past couple of decades have decreased vaccine rates among the populace, resulting in much higher numbers of measles cases over the past two years.

The Trump administration has also gutted programs that have been successful in getting more people vaccinated in the past. Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., himself an anti-vaxxer, has placed anti-vaxxers on health advisory panels, and recently indicated to anti-vaccine groups that his work is not yet done.

“Let me be clear. You have a strong and steadfast friend at the White House,” Kennedy said during a gathering of anti-vaxxers last month.

Truthout is one of only a few platforms for justice-oriented, grassroots journalism. Today, we face an existential threat.

Due to Google’s launch of AI search, we’ve seen a drastic plunge in our site traffic and, as a result, our revenue. We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We are fundraising right now to meet our basic operating expenses. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference — we appreciate your support.

author: Mada Masr
title: State security prosecution renews detention of 6 Matsda2sh journalists for 15 days
content:
The detention of six journalists from fact-checking platform Matsda2sh was renewed for 15 days on Tuesday evening, pending further investigations, according to their lawyers. The renewal was ordered by the Supreme State Security Prosecution during today’s hearing in Case 8083/2026.


The journalists Mohamed Ashraf Abu Emaira, Abdallah Kadry, Islam Barakat, Mohamed Adel, Mohamed Mahmoud and Omar Helal are being investigated in the case, registered with the Supreme State Security Prosecution, and were questioned again by prosecutors in sessions on Tuesday.


The journalists’ lawyers told Mada Masr that questioning began around 1 pm and continued into the evening at the prosecution’s headquarters in the Fifth Settlement. The sessions revisited previous lines of questioning, including questioning about wages, the managerial structure of the platform and the way work was organized, with no new evidence presented to the journalists.


All six journalists have been held at Badr 1 Prison since they were brought before the prosecution early last week. Their lawyers said they are due to receive their first family visits starting Thursday, as well as to be granted dedicated time for exercise.


Security forces arrested the six Matsda2sh journalists in the span of24 hours

during a campaign

launched on September 28 which targeted the fact-checking platform’s team across several governorates. 


Their whereabouts remained unknown for five days, during which they were denied access to their lawyers and prevented from contacting their families, in

violation

 of the counterterrorism law under which they were detained, according to

EIPR

. They appeared before the Supreme State Security Prosecution on October 4 when investigations began.


The prosecution is investigating the six journalists for several offenses, including joining a terrorist group, spreading false news, misusing social media and receiving foreign funding.


Several journalists told prosecutors during their interrogations that they had been subjected to torture and forced to record video footage in custody of themselves reading fabricated confessions, according to the

Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights,

 whose legal team is leading their defense. The Journalists

Syndicate

 subsequently filed a complaint with the prosecutor general, calling for an investigation into allegations that the journalists were tortured at National Security Agency facilities before being brought before the prosecution. The

Interior Ministry

 denied the allegations two hours after the syndicate issued its statement.


Three of the detained journalists were referred to the Forensic Medicine Authority on October 6. The

prosecution

 said the following day that forensic reports found no injuries on their bodies or signs of violence having been used against them. 


EIPR

responded

 to the prosecutor’s statement by noting that prosecutors had refused to hear the journalists’ testimony as victims in the torture complaints they filed against the officers responsible for their detention at National Security Agency facilities. EIPR also said the prosecution had not summoned or heard testimony from the officers named in the complaints or witnesses to the incidents. It also noted that the journalists had not claimed to have visible injuries but had reported being subjected to torture, ill-treatment, threats and physical and psychological coercion.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Emergency Care for Christa Pike Was Delayed After Prison Botched 911 Call
content:
Emergency dispatchers were left scrambling after prison officials were unable to verify that the call was legitimate.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Newly released 911 calls show that prison officials neglected to provide basic details when calling for emergency care for Christa Pike after Tennessee officials botched her execution last week.

Emergency dispatchers were left scrambling after the prison official who made the first 911 call, roughly an hour after the lethal injection process began, was unable to provide the code for the prison facility, despite it being needed for confirmation by dispatchers.

This caused emergency care for Pike to be delayed by roughly half an hour as the chemicals wreaked havoc on her body. Her lawyer, at one point, made a call saying that she needed “immediate life-saving care” from first responders.

The revelations raise further questions about Tennessee prison officials’ protocol for executions. Witnesses present for the execution attempt on September 30 said that it was apparent during the procedure that officials were not prepared for the injections to fail, despite the high rate of failure for lethal injections.

The calls were released by Nashville’s Department of Emergency Communications (DEC) after information requests by news outlets, and posted online by the Nashville Banner. A transcript of the first call shows the caller, whose identity is redacted, being repeatedly asked for the verification code for the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution, which is needed for emergency dispatch to the prison. The prison official said they don’t know the code.

“I don’t have a code,” the caller said. When the dispatcher asked for a callback number, they gave the number for a cell phone, the transcript shows. The caller also seemed unsure about Pike’s age when asked, saying, “I believe 50.”

After that call, DEC placed a call to the Metro Fire Dispatch, where both the emergency dispatcher and the metro fire employee shared disbelief that the prison official didn’t know the procedure.

“How do they not have a code?” the fire dispatcher asked. “There’s nobody there that knows the process?”

“I guess since this is a special case, they may not know. But I don’t know why they don’t have the code…. [Riverbend] is the one place where you definitely need a code,” the emergency dispatcher said.

The lack of a code led officials to be unclear about whether or not the call was legitimate. The call also did not originate from Central Control for the state’s Department of Correction, as it would normally, leading to further confusion. As a result, dispatchers began reaching out to other prison officials in attempts to verify the call, while also trying to triangulate first responders.

Central Control was initially not even aware that that first call had happened. An employee told dispatchers not to send an emergency response because they “didn’t call anybody” and “would have been the one to call you guys.”

In another call, the DEC dispatcher expressed that they were “trying to find out if this is an actual thing that is happening … or if this is someone that is just basically prank calling or like swatting us.”

After the flurry of phone calls, and as a first responder was waiting at the gate of the prison to enter the facility, a Central Control employee was eventually able to confirm the legitimacy of the request — roughly half an hour after the initial 911 call. Medics later made sure to confirm that the prison officials knew where they were transporting Pike in the ambulance.

Pike was discharged from the hospital back to prison last week. She was initially unconscious and in critical condition after the execution, as the physician administering the procedure was seemingly unable to find a vein after going through at least seven needles. Ultimately, her lawyers said, they probably injected the drug into the tissue rather than into her bloodstream, causing her to be the first known person to survive a lethal injection attempt after the drugs had already been put into her body.

Pike has since regained consciousness, regained movement in her arms, and has been able to walk with some assistance. The horrific ordeal has sparked renewed calls for the abolition of the death penalty.

author: Alex Brown
title: At Least 39 Data Center Measures Will Be on the Ballot This Year in 8 States
content:
A recent poll finds 65 percent of respondents oppose the construction of AI data centers in their local community.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

In the course of a single election cycle, the backlash against data centers has grown from an issue at local planning commission and city council meetings to become a flashpoint in state and federal races across the country.

Candidates who once touted data centers as an economic boon have backtracked, and voters in at least three dozen cities, counties and townships will consider ballot measures in November that could ban data centers in their communities. Analysts say the opposition to data centers has come from Republican and Democratic voters alike.

“The people are speaking, and they’re speaking in one voice in opposition to this infrastructure,” said Tatishe Nteta, provost professor of political science at UMass Amherst. “It is not something that people desire in any shape, form or fashion. This potentially could be the issue that gives you the status of a former member of a city council or a former member of Congress.”

Last month, UMass Amherst published a poll, directed by Nteta, showing that only 11% of Americans would support the construction of an artificial intelligence data center in their local community. The poll found that 65% of respondents oppose the construction of such facilities.

Local and national activists have a long list of grievances against data centers, which tech companies are aggressively building to provide the computing power for artificial intelligence platforms. The rapid buildout of data centers is expected to strain the electrical grid and drive up energy costs, some forecasts show.

Opponents are also concerned about the facilities’ pollution, water use, noise and conversion of farmland and other open spaces. Many developers are also building private, “behind-the-meter” natural gas plants to power their data centers, increasing concerns about emissions and public health.

Some activists also object to the artificial intelligence technologies the sites will power, which threaten to disrupt the economy, replace workers, erode critical thinking skills and mental health and even — according to some tech executives — potentially kill all humans.

“For so many years, Ohio rolled out the red carpet to become a tech hub,” said Nick Owens, an attorney with Conserve Ohio, a campaign seeking to block data center development. “Unfortunately, what we’ve become is a tech dump.”

Activists across the country have lashed out at elected officials from both parties who have offered state and local tax breaks in order to entice data center developers. They’ve also called out local officials for negotiating deals behind closed doors and signing non-disclosure agreements with large tech companies.

“The politicians are chasing the grassroots, they aren’t leading on the issue,” said Anthony Elmo, public education defender with Good Jobs First, a policy group that tracks government subsidies related to economic development. “(Politicians) who were very pro-data center a year ago are now coming out against them due to political factors.”

Tech companies have launched their own political efforts to respond to the backlash. Industry leaders argue that artificial intelligence is key to the nation’s economic competitiveness. They note that the data center boom has created many construction jobs and increased property tax revenue in communities desperate for more money.

Leading the Future, a tech-backed Super PAC, has invested in federal and state campaigns in support of both Republican and Democratic candidates who support artificial intelligence. Josh Vlasto, the group’s co-leader, argued that the narrative around data centers has conflated the industry at large with its worst offenders — speculative projects that disregarded local opposition and failed to meet environmental standards.

“(Voters) want the jobs in their communities, they want the revenue, but they want the risks and downsides mitigated and addressed,” he said. “There is backlash in communities that don’t want them, but if you look to the states that are building and doing it right, these data centers are being welcomed and generating a massive amount of revenue. If this is done correctly, I could see this issue turning drastically in a different direction.”

author: Andrew Crocker
title: As Federal Court Rules ALPRs are Mass Surveillance, EFF Gets Disappointing Ruling
content:
In an extremely disappointing

ruling

, a California trial court dismissed

SIREN v. San Jose

, our case challenging the city of San Jose’s warrantless searches of its vast stores of automated license plate reader (ALPR) data. EFF and the ACLU of Northern California represent SIREN and CAIR California, two non-profits that serve San Jose residents, in this case.


Make no mistake: We believe this ruling is wrong on the law, and we will appeal. The ruling ignores the importance of landmark rulings from the U.S. Supreme Court regarding the invasiveness of aggregating collected data on an individual over time, including

one issued just months ago

. It also severely underestimates the harm that ALPRs cause, in San Jose and around the country. 


San Jose’s ALPR surveillance system is inescapable. It blankets the city’s streets in nearly five hundred cameras that continuously photograph every car that passes by and retains the collected data for a month or longer. In our briefs, we argued that law enforcement officers who warrantlessly search the resulting ALPR database are violating the California Constitution’s ban on unreasonable searches and its guarantee of privacy. The court disagreed, explaining that based on one California appeals court case involving individual streetlight cameras, people do not have a reasonable expectation of privacy when driving on a public road. This is wrong. Networked ALPRs are not individual streetlight cameras. Their net effect of tracking and mapping cars as they travel reveals patterns of life, intimate relationships, and much more.


Fortunately, there are signs that the tide is turning against ALPRs in the courts. Just a day before the ruling in our case, a federal district court in Oklahoma called ALPRs “a type of indiscriminate mass surveillance”

and decided

 that a law enforcement officer’s warrantless search of ALPR data violated the Fourth Amendment. The officer was observing traffic on an Oklahoma highway when he saw a woman driving a car with California plates. According to the court order, the officer began following the woman “for no apparent reason” other than her out of state plates. While following her, the officer decided to run the woman’s license plate number through

Flock’s ALPR system

 – again, with no apparent reason other than her California plates. The Flock search returned at least 30 days of data, allowing the officer to track the car across at least three states, over the span of a month, from a single search.


The facts of this case demonstrate how ALPRs allow law enforcement to grab a breathtakingly vast sweep of information about a car (and the driver within) with no more effort than a Google search. It’s true that when a person drives on public roads, they can be observed, including by police. But as the Supreme Court

has


explained

, we don’t expect law enforcement to be able to secretly track and store

every

 movement our cars while we’re driving. The federal court in the Oklahoma case aptly illustrated this difference in societal expectations:


We might reasonably expect our friends and family to tell us something like: “Hey, I saw you out driving by the store last week.” But we do not expect people we know—let alone strangers, and especially not law enforcement—to randomly approach us to say: “Hey, I have been following your car for the last 30 days, and here is a detailed log of every place your vehicle has been with supporting photographic evidence. I am also going to share this information with law enforcement throughout the country so they know your whereabouts, too.


This decision is the first of its kind, and EFF will continue working to ensure that it is the first of many. Outside the courts, we’ve seen people across the country step up to reject ALPRs at the

state

 and

local

 level. EFF will continue challenging this technology

on every front

 as well.

author: Joe Sandler Clarke
title: Scottish Government’s Deal With IDF-Linked Firm ‘Breaks Boycott Pledge’
content:
The Scottish government has been

accused of failing to live up to its Israeli boycott policy

, by agreeing to a multimillion-pound deal with a company linked to the country’s military.


GE Aerospace said on Monday it was

spending £30m

 to modernise Glasgow’s Prestwich Airport, as part of a partnership with Ayrshire Growth Deal, the National reported. The project is led by the Scottish and UK governments, as well as three local councils. 


The US firm’s jet engines are used by Israeli military planes in Gaza,

Campaign Against Arms Trade

 and other advocacy groups have said. In September, GE Aerospace

shareholders raised concerns

 that the

company had exported parts for military aircraft

 engines to countries accused of human rights abuses, including Israel. 


Scottish first minister John Swinney has said Israel is committing genocide in Gaza, and last year announced his government

would not give public money

 to companies supplying arms to the country.


“We will pause new awards of public money to arms companies whose products or services are provided to countries where there is plausible evidence of genocide being committed by that country,” he said at the time, “that will include Israel.”


The Scottish Green party have accused Swinney’s Scottish National Party (SNP) of failing to live up to this commitment with the airport renovation deal. Green MSP Laura Moodie told

the National

: “How can this possibly be reconciled with a policy of boycotting, divesting from and sanctioning companies that arm and support Israeli forces?”


The news of the GE Aerospace deal came just a few days after the Scottish government  partnered with Barclays on an

upcoming bond issue

. The bank has

come under pressure

 for its ties to firms doing business with the Israel Defense Forces (IDF). The Bureau of Investigative Journalism recently reported the bank had agreed to work with a firm that makes

parts for IDF drones

.


A Scottish government spokesperson defended the agreement with GE Aerospace.


“The primary market of GE Aerospace’s Scottish company is not defence,” they said. “Where this is the case, the Scottish company must complete a self-declaration confirming that it does not supply military equipment, technologies, or services to Israel or Myanmar.”

author: James Green
title: Trumponaro: como um governo de Flávio pode imitar a presidência de Trump no Brasil?
content:
Enquanto apoiadores do presidente Lula se

mobilizam

 para reverter os resultados do primeiro turno da disputa presidencial e garantir um quarto mandato liderado pelo Partido dos Trabalhadores, acho importante considerar que tipo de presidência o Brasil teria caso Flávio Bolsonaro fosse eleito em 25 de outubro.


Obviamente, todo cenário político nacional é único. Um eventual futuro governo Bolsonaro poderia ser bem diferente da forma como Donald Trump tem governado desde que retornou à presidência em 2025.

No entanto, dada a afinidade declarada da família Bolsonaro com o clã Trump — bem como com suas políticas e práticas —, vale a pena considerar em que medida um novo presidente, governando com uma forte base de extrema-direita no Congresso, poderia adotar elementos da cartilha política de Trump, caso suba a rampa em 1º de janeiro de 2027.


Observadores políticos vêm notando uma defasagem de dois anos entre os eventos políticos recentes nos Estados Unidos e no Brasil. Trump assumiu o poder em 2016; Jair foi eleito dois anos depois. Biden derrotou Trump em 2020; Lula venceu as eleições de 2022. Apoiadores de Trump invadiram o Capitólio em 2021; o exército de defensores de Bolsonaro invadiu Brasília dois anos depois, em 2023. Trump retornou ao poder em 2025; o Brasil poderá enfrentar uma nova presidência de Bolsonaro em 2027. Embora processos históricos distintos raramente apresentem uma relação de causa e efeito tão nítida, parece que os dois campos de extrema-direita mantêm um diálogo constante sobre a melhor forma de conquistar e consolidar o poder.


Trump rapidamente celebrou a vitória de Bolsonaro por uma margem de 1,9% em 4 de outubro, embora,

na mensagem publicada nas redes sociais

, tenha confundido o Brasil com a Índia: “125 milhões de pessoas votaram hoje no primeiro turno da eleição presidencial da Índia. Os resultados saíram logo após o encerramento da votação, no MESMO DIA!” Ele também aproveitou a ocasião para fazer comentários bombásticos sobre uma de suas principais obsessões: “Em Detroit, Filadélfia, Califórnia e em inúmeras outras cidades e estados dos EUA, os resultados — com números muito menores — frequentemente levam semanas para serem fraudados… digo, calculados. A votação na América é CORRUPTA!!!”


Enquanto Jair Bolsonaro baseou parte de sua campanha eleitoral de 2022 em críticas à confiabilidade do sistema brasileiro de votação eletrônica, o campo da direita manteve-se em silêncio sobre o processo de votação desta vez. Parece haver fraude eleitoral quando se perde, mas não quando se ganha. Ironicamente, Trump elogiou as eleições brasileiras por utilizarem procedimentos de votação que o próprio presidente dos EUA classificou como fraudulentos em seu próprio país.


Se os apoiadores de Lula reverterem o resultado do primeiro turno e vencerem por uma margem estreita no segundo turno, tanto Bolsonaro quanto Trump contestarão o resultado.

 A Casa Branca poderia insistir que o segundo turno das eleições brasileiras foi fraudulento e que Bolsonaro foi legitimamente eleito presidente, o que provocaria uma crise nacional e internacional sobre a legitimidade do novo governo de Lula.


Já se Flávio Bolsonaro derrotar o presidente Lula, provavelmente seguirá o exemplo de Trump, revertendo quase todas as políticas e programas do governo atual.

 A exemplo da ordem executiva de Trump emitida em 20 de janeiro de 2025 — seu primeiro dia no cargo —, concedendo perdão aos apoiadores que invadiram o Capitólio dos EUA na tentativa de anular os resultados da eleição presidencial americana de 2022, Flávio prometeu um perdão presidencial para seu pai (condenado por organizar uma insurreição contra o novo governo Lula) e para aqueles que invadiram a Praça dos Três Poderes em apoio ao plano de Bolsonaro.


Embora um perdão presidencial possa extinguir a pena de prisão restante de Jair Bolsonaro, ele não anularia a condenação do Supremo Tribunal Federal nem restauraria seus direitos políticos. Portanto, os aliados políticos de Bolsonaro poderiam buscar uma anistia legislativa que restaure plenamente a elegibilidade de Jair Bolsonaro.


Flávio pode governar pela vingança, assim como Trump 


Logo no primeiro dia de sua presidência, Trump anunciou uma campanha de vingança contra seus oponentes políticos, por meio de ações judiciais retaliatórias e de outras medidas administrativas. Flávio pode repetir essa estratégia.

title: Kurdish literature and cultural memory meet at Frankfurt Book Fair
content:
The 78th Frankfurt International Book Fair, which opened on 7 October in Frankfurt, Germany, concluded on Sunday evening, 11 October. The fair brought together publishing houses, writers, cultural institutions, journalists, academics and representatives of the publishing industry from around the world.


A total of 4,131 exhibitors participated in the fair, which hosted more than 3,600 events.


As one of the international meeting points for the book and publishing industry, the fair also provided a platform for discussions on literature, culture, freedom of expression, democracy, human rights and the future of technology.


‘Czechia was the guest of honour’


Czechia was this year's guest of honour at the Frankfurt Book Fair.


Under the theme “Ein Land an der Küste” (A Country on the Coast), Czechia established a 2,300-square-metre exhibition space at the fair. The Guest of Honour Pavilion hosted events covering various literary genres, with the participation of 75 writers.


The pavilion showcased Czech literature and the country's cultural heritage, incorporating artificial intelligence and interactive technologies. Visitors engaged with digital installations, while a live-drawing robot and interactive poetry applications attracted particular attention.


More than 40 publishing houses took part in Czechia's national presentation, showcasing their books and holding international publishing rights negotiations.


‘An international meeting point for publishers’


Publishing houses, literary agencies, distribution companies, cultural organisations and media representatives from around the world gathered across the Frankfurt Book Fair's exhibition halls.


Hall 3.0 stood out as one of the main areas for independent publishers and international literary circles. The hall also featured dedicated reading and event spaces for independent publishers.


Publishers not only presented their books but also discussed the future of the publishing industry through meetings with authors, rights negotiations, translation agreements and international partnerships.


‘Turkish publishing industry also represented in Frankfurt’


The fair also hosted events focusing on the publishing industry in Turkey.


A session titled “Publishing and Reading Habits in Türkiye” examined the current state of publishing in Turkey, changing reading habits and literary relations between Turkey and Europe.


‘Kurdish literature finds a place at Frankfurt Book Fair’


The fair's programme also featured works on Kurdish literature and history.


Writer Hasan Hayri Ateş presented his novel Şer Zamanıydı to readers at the Frankfurt Book Fair at the invitation of the Frankfurt Foreigners' Advisory Council.


The event was moderated by Hüseyin Çatal and attended by Rainer Vollmar, Chair of the Board of Darmstadt Literaturhaus, editor Jutta von Freyberg, and Gudrun Wörsdörfer and Marianne Koester, representatives of the Frankfurt Association for Solidarity with Rojava.


Discussions also addressed efforts to translate Ateş's novel into German and introduce it to German-speaking readers.


Kurdish politician and writer İdris Baluken gave a seminar on Kurdish literature at the fair, while Kurdish writer Musa Karbadağ also participated in events dedicated to Kurdish literature.


‘Baluken: I see politics and art as parts of the same resistance’


Kurdish politician and writer Idris Baluken emphasised the significance of his participation in the Frankfurt Book Fair, drawing attention to the repression faced by the Kurdish people in relation to their language, identity and culture.


Baluken said: “I consider it very important to be here at the Frankfurt Book Fair, one of the world's largest book fairs, as a Kurdish writer from Turkey.


We can say that this is a place where the pulse of the world's cultural, artistic and literary activities beats strongly. I am the son of a people whose language, identity and culture have been banned, who have been deprived of education in their mother tongue and whose very existence has been denied. I spent nearly seven years under conditions of aggravated isolation because I defended the rights of this people. I therefore find it significant to participate, through the literary works I produced during that time, in an event that brings together other peoples of the world and is hosted by important figures in the cultural sphere.


This is valuable both in literary and cultural terms and because it provides an opportunity to …
