title: Tosun: The case is not over until the third attacker is punished
content:
One year has passed since journalist, documentary filmmaker and environmental activist Hakan Tosun was beaten to death in the street in Esenyurt.


Tosun died after suffering a brain haemorrhage at the scene when he was assaulted by two people on the night of 10–11 October 2025 while on his way to visit his mother in the Mehmet Akif Ersoy neighbourhood of Esenyurt district.


Abdurrahman Murat and Adnan Şahin, responsible for Hakan Tosun's death, were summoned to the Esenyurt Mevlana Police Station to give statements and were arrested on charges of intentional injury. However, it was notable that Yusuf Özakdağ, a third person who had also participated in the attack, was questioned as a witness by the same police station.


Although a report by the Council of Forensic Medicine confirmed that Hakan Tosun had been severely beaten, the 17th High Criminal Court accepted the indictment for intentional injury prepared by the Büyükçekmece Chief Public Prosecutor's Office. Following months of proceedings, Abdurrahman Murat and Adnan Şahin were sentenced to life imprisonment for intentional killing. However, the verdict brought no sense of relief to the Tosun family.


Hakan Tosun's sister, Öznur Tosun, spoke to ANF and stressed that the case would not be over until Yusuf Özakdağ, who also participated in the fatal attack on her brother and has openly posed with firearms on social media while tagging gang names, is brought to trial and punished.


Continuing her brother’s legacy in the struggle for justice


Öznur Tosun joined the front ranks of the commemoration of the 10 October Massacre, an event her brother, journalist Hakan Tosun, had covered every year, and marched to demand justice for him, one year after he was beaten to death in the street.


Tosun, who experienced first-hand the difficulties of seeking justice in Turkey through the trial over her brother's murder, said: “I have always been someone who speaks out against injustice and unfairness, but the period following my brother Hakan's death made my sense of justice even more pronounced.”


Öznur Tosun, who experienced first-hand how far cruelty could go on the night of 10–11 October a year ago, recounted the events leading up to her brother's disappearance: “That day, my brother Hakan attended the commemoration of the 10 October Ankara Train Station Massacre in Kadıköy. At around 7 pm, he called my mother and told her he was coming home. She even asked him whether he was hungry. When Hakan did not arrive, my mother called him again. He told her, ‘I'm on my way, I'm coming.’ My brother was on the metrobus when he spoke to my mother. It was around 10 pm. My mother waited for a while, but when he still did not arrive, she called him again and realised she could not reach him. She did not tell me immediately because she did not want me to panic. At first, she thought his phone battery might have died. However, when Hakan still had not arrived by morning, she called one of his friends. After learning that his friend could not reach him either, she called me and told me what had happened.”


‘Mevlana Police Station concealed evidence with the killer’s family’


Öznur Tosun said she initially did not suspect anything serious but went to the nearest police station in Kağıthane to file a missing person report as a precaution. She said, “I thought perhaps my brother had been detained, or maybe he was exhausted because he had recently returned from the earthquake-hit region where he had gone to report.”


Tosun continued: “I was told that 24 hours had to pass before my missing person report could be processed. Even before those 24 hours had passed, Kağıthane Police Station checked hospital records but could not find any record of Hakan. I then contacted Esenyurt Mevlana Police Station, which was closest to where my mother lived, and filed another missing person report.


My brother's photograph was sent to them at 8 pm on Saturday. They knew that we, as his family, had been unable to reach him. Despite this, it was not until around 4 am that a police officer from Mevlana Police Station called me and informed me that Hakan was at Başakşehir Çam and Sakura City Hospital.


The incident took place on Friday evening. They knew by Saturday that we were searching for Hakan, yet they did not inform us. They had the documents and the missing person report in their possession, but they waited a full eight hours before notifying us.


During those eight hours, the killers were …

title: BaBa Zula: We stand for peace, the government must act
content:
Artists continue to share messages of peace through ANF. Members of the music group BaBa Zula said artists should take a political stance and called for Kurdish and all other languages spoken in the country to be free.


The musicians said: “The Justice and Development Party (AKP) does not inspire confidence. For peace to come, democracy, rights and the rule of law must come first. Thousands of our people from Anatolia and Mesopotamia have lost their lives. Peace is not a concession granted from above or a political favour. It means people being able to live freely, with their fundamental rights, mother tongues and cultures protected under a fair legal system.”


Murat Ertel, Esma Ertel and Levent Akman of the music group BaBa Zula answered ANF's questions.


‘Artists are being prevented from taking political positions’


Members of BaBa Zula said the group seeks to preserve the multicultural and multilingual heritage of Anatolia, Mesopotamia and Istanbul through its music. They said: “We are living under a cultural bombardment. There is a situation being created, particularly in the virtual world. It is as though the world is being shaped not by its seven billion people, but by the leaders of a population of just one billion. They are also trying to shape culture, but we are interested in the culture of the geography we live in. We eat the food of this region, listen to its music and try to reflect these influences honestly. Of course, we are also open to music from around the world. But what matters most to us is the music of our own geography. Istanbul is actually a beautiful example of this. It connects Asia and Europe, embraces Anatolia and has ties with the Balkans, Greece, the Mediterranean and Turkey. We find this much more appealing. For example, when we look at America, we see great power, but we also see distance.”


The group members stressed that artists should take political positions and shared the following views: “Unfortunately, efforts are being made today to prevent artists from being political and expressing political views. This is happening both in Turkey and abroad. Countries that present themselves as champions of democracy are doing this too. In Germany, for example, speaking about the massacre of Palestinians or criticising Israel provokes a strong backlash. In Britain, artists are also being prevented from speaking about these issues and are expected to remain apolitical. For example, the director Wim Wenders, who was in charge of this year's Berlin Film Festival, made the absurd claim that artists should not be political and should simply do their jobs. We also try to be political. We have our own style, which we have maintained from the very beginning, and we have no intention of ever abandoning it. Artists are very powerful because art and artists are among the most important forces shaping society.”


‘Mother tongues must be free’


The group members also defended freedom of the mother tongue, saying that while a common language could exist, different languages must be preserved. The group members said: “Different peoples have their own languages, and as long as those languages are spoken, they continue to live and their hearts continue to beat in those regions. But as a country, I think we are creating divisions over this issue too. When you look at Turkey, you are talking about a society that grew up with the idea of ‘72 nations’ in Anatolia and Mesopotamia. We believe that seven distinct ethnic communities live across the country's seven regions and that each of their languages should be able to survive.”


The musicians stressed that Kurdish should be free, but that linguistic freedom should not be limited to Kurdish alone. For example, when you travel to the east, you encounter Azerbaijanis. Azerbaijani should also be taught to their children. You go to Mardin (Mêrdîn) and encounter Assyrians; they should be able to receive education in their own language. Or you visit Arab Alevis in Adana; they should be able to continue learning Arabic as a second language. Laz should also be taught. Different languages enrich this country and make us more beautiful. We are very colourful, and we are beautiful together. Our beauty lies in multilingualism and multiculturalism. That is what makes us who we are. Children are taught English and Spanish, but they could also learn these languages. These are languages that should be integrated into our children's lives.”

title: The people of Shengal must decide their own future
content:
More than 6,000 people were abducted during the attack on Shengal by ISIS mercenaries on 3 August 2014, and around 2,500 remain missing. The Yazidis refer to the attack, in which thousands of people were massacred and abducted, as the 74th Ferman in their history.


Shengal was liberated from ISIS in 2015. In the aftermath of the Ferman (Shengal genocide), the Yazidis established their own administrative and defence mechanisms, forming a People's Council and defence forces such as the Shengal Resistance Units (YBŞ) and Shengal Women's Units (YJŞ). The autonomous administration, which has operated in practice in Shengal ever since, continues to exist as an expression of the people's determination to govern and defend themselves.


Turkey-Iraq trade-off in New York


Turkish President Tayyip Erdoğan and Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Zeydi met in New York on 23 September 2026 while attending the United Nations (UN) General Assembly. The joint statement issued after the meeting highlighted two main points: the full restoration of state authority in Shengal and the elimination of forces described in the statement as “prohibited foreign armed elements”, and the gradual transfer of the Turkish army's Bashiqa (Zilkan) base to the Iraqi federal government. The transfer process was made conditional on security measures to be taken by Iraq and a timetable to be agreed upon by both sides. However, no timetable has yet been announced.


The Turkish army established a presence at the Bashiqa base, approximately 30 kilometres northeast of Mosul, in December 2015. Around 600 Turkish soldiers are stationed at the base. Turkey's military presence in Iraq consists of five main bases, more than 2,000 soldiers and nearly 100 military positions. The transfer of the Bashiqa base, which accommodates fewer than a third of Turkey's total troops in Iraq, does not mean an end to Turkey's military presence in the country. Its other bases and military positions remain operational.


The agreement was interpreted in the Turkish press as an arrangement under which the Turkish army would end its presence at Bashiqa in exchange for the establishment of Iraqi state authority in Shengal. Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan also said at a press conference that these steps would be taken “after the terrorist group's presence in Shengal has been eliminated”.


Through this agreement, the Turkish state is seeking to position itself as a direct party to the Shengal issue. However, the administration and defence of a strategically important region such as Shengal have become a bargaining issue, traded against another state's military base in talks that excluded representatives of the people living there.


‘The solution lies in the constitution’


A meeting concerning the Yazidis was held in Baghdad on 1 September on the instructions of Ali Zeydi. All those attending the meeting on Shengal, which the Iraqi government held without Yazidi representatives, were military and security officials. Not a single Yazidi representative was invited. The appointment of a military district governor to Shengal was subsequently raised. However, the people of Shengal rejected the decision, stating that it had been made without their consent.


Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Zeydi later met with representatives of the YBŞ and the Yazidi community on 11 September. Sources familiar with the meeting reported that the Iraqi side had raised no serious objections to the Shengal delegation's demand to preserve its self-defence force, while the details of integration were left to a joint committee. The Iraqi Chief of General Staff visited Shengal with a military delegation on 22 September. The outcome of the visit was not disclosed, and the New York agreement was announced the following day.


This series of meetings demonstrates that Ankara was subsequently brought into the direct dialogue that Baghdad had established with Shengal. Baghdad has not ruled out the possibility of Shengal's self-defence forces continuing to operate within the Iraqi army under a recognised status. Keeping this possibility open, however, depends on continuing negotiations directly with Shengal.


Shengal's autonomy is, of course, another central issue in these discussions. Articles 122 and 123 of the Iraqi Constitution allow for extensive local autonomy without the establishment of a federal region. The constitution already provides for a degree of autonomy that would enable cultural and religious communities to …

title: PACE delegation meets with the DEM Party in Ankara, discusses the peace process
content:
Petra Bayr, President of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (PACE), held talks with the DEM Party during her official visit to Turkey on Monday. Accompanied by her delegation, she met with Co-Chair Tülay Hatimoğulları, Deputy Parliamentary Group Chair Sezai Temelli, and MP Sevilay Çelenk, who is a member of the Turkish delegation to PACE, at the Turkish Parliament.


The discussions focused on the role of Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan in the Peace and Democratic Society Process. Reference was made to the case law of the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) concerning the so-called “right to hope.” DEM Party representatives emphasized that Öcalan must be provided with living and working conditions that would allow him to participate freely in the peace process.


The discussions also addressed the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) rulings concerning imprisoned politicians Selahattin Demirtaş and Figen Yüksekdağ, as well as human rights activist and cultural philanthropist Osman Kavala, which have yet to be implemented. The Council of Europe delegation expressed its concern regarding these issues. Further meetings with political representatives in Turkey are scheduled as part of the official visit.

author: Battlescarred
title: The Founding Congress of the International Workers Association
content:
An account of the founding of the IWA in 1922

The founding of the International Workers Association at its constitutive congress in Berlin in 1922 was a long wished for goal of revolutionary syndicalists and anarchists around the world. The First International had been wound up at the congress in Philadelphia in 1875, and definitively dissolved in July of the following year. The end of the First International due to the clash between Marx and his followers and those who opposed him, including the grouping around Bakunin, Belgian socialists and British trade unionists, was a severe setback for the international workers’ movement. The so-called Anti-Authoritarian International founded at St Imier in Switzerland in 1872 had also foundered by 1877. Many revolutionary syndicalists felt the need for a new International, especially as the social-democratic parties had created their own international, the Second International, in 1889. This had been followed by the reformist trade unions creating their own international, The International Secretariat of National Trade Union Centres (ISNTUC) in 1901. When this collapsed because of the First World War, the reformist unions created the International Federation of Trade Unions (IFTU) at a congress in Amsterdam in July 1919. This united unions from United States, Belgium, Denmark, Germany, France, Great Britain, Holland, Luxemburg, Norway, Austria, Sweden, Switzerland, Spain, and Czechoslovakia. It represented 17.7 million workers and had a social-democratic orientation.

The first mass revolutionary syndicalist, anarchosyndicalist and industrial unionist unions had emerged at the end of the 19th century and beginning of the 20th century and included the Industrial Workers of the World (IWW) founded 1905, and the Federación Obrera Regional Argentina (Workers Regional Federation of Argentina-FORA) the Confédération Générale du Travail (General Confederation of Labour-CGT) founded in France in 1895, the Italian Unione Sindacale Italiana (USI), the Swedish Sveriges Arbetares Centralorganisation (SAC) founded in 1910 and the Dutch industrial federations, The Spanish CNT founded in 1910.

The International Syndicalist Congress of 1913

The first attempt to create a new international from these various unions took place in London in 1913. This, the International Syndicalist Congress, took place at Holborn Town Hall between September 27th to October 2nd, at the initiative of the Dutch Nationaal Arbeids-Secretariaat (National Labour Secretariat –NAS) and the British Industrial Syndicalist Education League (ISEL). Solidaridad Obrera (Workers Solidarity) in Catalonia, a precursor of the CNT, supported the move. However, the French CGT opposed the convening of such a congress. It was still within the ISNTUC and feared internal ructions as its reformist wing was strengthening at the expense of the anarchist and revolutionary syndicalist wing.

Thirty eight delegates representing sixty five organisations met and passed the following resolution:

The first International Syndicalist Congress recognises that the working class of all countries suffers the same repression by the State and the capitalist system. For this reason, it declares itself in favour of class struggle, international solidarity and independent organisation of the working class on the basis of the federative union. This tends to the immediate material and moral elevation of the working class until the total destruction of capitalism and the State. This declares, furthermore, that the class struggle is a necessary consequence of the private possession of the means of production and distribution, and that, therefore, this Congress tends to the socialisation of these means. In this sense, the constitution and development of trade union organisations should be oriented, since they are in the best conditions to ensure the production and distribution of products for the benefit of society as a whole. Verifying that the international unions cannot successfully carry out the class struggle if the workers continue to be divided by political and religious differences, the Congress declares that the class struggle, as such, can only have an economic character, for which the workers' organisations should not seek the stated goal through collaboration with the government or with its allies, and that they should rely solely on the power of the organisations and their direct action. title: Leaked Audio Features MI GOP Candidate Rogers Mocking Affordability Concerns
content:
Rogers minimized worries about rising costs due to Trump administration policies as “derangement.”

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

In newly unearthed audio, Republican candidate for U.S. Senate Mike Rogers (Michigan) appears to dismiss one of the top issues motivating voters in this year’s midterm races: affordability.

In a radio interview from January, Rogers blasted Democrats for highlighting the fact that Americans are facing higher consumer prices on myriad goods and services.

“They [Democrats] say, ‘Trump caused high prices’ — people go nuts, they lose their mind. I do believe there is this Trump derangement,” Rogers, a millionaire, said in the interview, minimizing legitimate concerns about rising costs.

Michigan GOP Senate Candidate Mike Rogers argues that concern over affordability is just 'Trump derangement': Rogers: They say, ‘Trump caused high prices’—people go nuts, they lose their mind. I do believe there is this Trump derangement. pic.twitter.com/VOfDhDYa3b

“[Democrats] have the gall to come out and say, ‘Guess what? We are the only ones that care about how expensive your life is,'” Rogers added.

In separate leaked audio featuring Rogers, the GOP candidate derides worries over higher costs for specific grocery items.

“Oh my gosh, coffee went up,” Rogers says on tape, mocking those concerns. “You know, horror!”

Rogers recently dismissed reporters who asked whether he should “provide an explanation” for those comments, belittling the query as “a couple of DNC talking points.”

Voters across the U.S. are, in fact, concerned about inflation, as prices are significantly higher on many staple items due in large part to President Donald Trump’s tariffs against other countries. Trump’s decision to launch a war on Iran has also resulted in rising fuel costs, which have increased costs of other goods, as diesel is needed to transport items for shipment across the U.S.

The Trump administration likely bears all of the responsibility for rising prices. According to a report from the New York Federal Reserve that was published last week, costs for many goods were actually decreasing before the president implemented an array of tariffs in his first year back in the White House. Because of that policy decision, prices are now increasing.

On a per capita basis, Michigan has been hit the hardest by price increases, with one estimate showing the total per-person household increase in costs being around $5,600 in the state.

Meanwhile, the latest polls show that Michigan voters are more supportive of the state’s Democratic Senate candidate, Abdul El-Sayed. In an aggregate of polling data from FiftyPlusOne, El-Sayed garners 48.2 percent of the vote while Rogers receives only 44.8 percent.

Truthout is one of only a few platforms for justice-oriented, grassroots journalism. Today, we face an existential threat.

Due to Google’s launch of AI search, we’ve seen a drastic plunge in our site traffic and, as a result, our revenue. We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We are fundraising right now to meet our basic operating expenses. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference — we appreciate your support.

content:
Le mouvement lycéen à se démarque depuis le 28 septembre par son intensité. Les lycéen·nes sur les blocages, et en particulier dans les différentes communes de banlieue, ont montré leur détermination avec des actions de blocus offensifs, barricades et manifs sauvages au rendez-vous. Iels ont également dû faire face à une intense répression orchestrée par la Préfecture et exécutée par les keufs et les chef·fes d'établissements. On a vu devant les lycées les flics faire massivement usage de gaz, mais aussi de

LBD

 et de

différentes grenades

, notamment les petites nouvelles, «

 

GL

», théoriquement assourdissantes et remplaçantes des tristement célèbres «

 

GM2L

 

». Les blocus ont également donné lieu à de nombreuses arrestations, des lycéen·nes comme de leurs soutiens, tandis que côté établissement, ont été prononcées des expulsions contre les élèves bloqueur·euses, ainsi que des conseils de discipline. Tout, pour mettre fin à la mobilisation.


Premières manifs


Dès la première semaine de mob', les lycéen·nes ont montré leur détermination dans la rue. Le mardi 29 septembre, les lycéen·nes rejoignent la manifestation nationale de la fonction publique. Le jeudi 1

er

 octobre, le rassemblement appelé à Jean Macé par les lycéen·nes débraye en manif sauvage avec dans le viseur le rectorat. Le vendredi, c'est le rassemblement à l'Hôtel de Région Montrochet qui part en sauvage. Les keufs, à chaque fois, s'en donnent à cœur joie. Le 29, on compte 41 interpellations. Le rassemblements de soutien aux interpellés qui a lieu le soir même est nassé et les soutiens contrôlés. Le 30, 17 nouvelles interpelations. Le 1

er

 octobre, les flics répriment salement la sauvage de Jean Macé, et arrêtent 38 personnes dans la journée, en comptant 14 lycéen-nes sur le blocage du lycée Colbert (Lyon 3

e

), aligné·es dans une mise en scène qui rappelle celle de Mantes-la-Jolie en 2018. Le 2 octobre, les flics arrêtent 31 personnes et en blessent de nombreuses autres, notamment dans les attaques de la manif sauvage qu'ils chargent et gazent abondamment jusque dans la gare Perrache. À la fin de la première semaine, on apprend que les keufs ont tiré

plus de 800 grenades lacrymogènes

 dans l'agglo' pour contenir la révolte, et arrêté 127 personnes.


@la_looutre


La deuxième semaine de mobilisation est marquée par deux grosses manifestations.


Le mardi 6 octobre, près de 30 000 personnes sont dans la rue avec les lycéen·nes. La tête du cortège, lycéenne et étudiante, avance rapidement. Le cortège arrivé à la place Guichard, plusieurs tentatives de sauvage ont lieu, les rues alentours sont retournées et plusieurs barricades enflammées sont dressée, ce qui aboutit à un face à face de près de 2h avec les flics, qui gazent abondamment la foule. Finalement, un cortège de plusieurs centaines de personnes part en manif sauvage dans le 7

e

 et se dirige vers le rectorat. La police, qui avaient perdu sa trace jusque là, occupée par les barricades de Guichard, finissent par gazer très largement les manifestant·es, et effectuent plusieurs charges.


Le 7 octobre, les lycéen·nes tentent de se rassembler à Jean Macé et sont contrôlés en masse par la police.


Le 8 octobre, la manifestation au départ de Bron réunit là encore plusieurs millers de personnes malgré la pluie. À la fin du parcours, une partie des manifestant·es part en sauvage dans le 8

e

, mais les flics interviennent rapidemment, en gazant et chargeant le cortège, le forçant à se disperser. Ils finissent par obtenir la dispersion complète des manifestant-es en quadrillant le quartier et le noyant sous les lacrymos.


On voit au fil de la mobilisation le dispositif policier changer. D'une repression brutale sur les blocus des lycéen·nes, à un dispositif relâché sur la manif des fonctionnaires, de l'usage abondant de gaz sur les premières manifs jusqu'au recourt à des charges policières sur le cortège...


Manif du 13 octobre


La manifestation de ce mardi change encore une fois le visage de la mobilisation et de sa repression. Rapidemment après le départ, un cortège de tête déterminé se forme. On peut célébrer les caméras défoncées et surtout les quelques onze banques et assurances du parcours dont les vitrines ont été éclatées, le mobilier et la paperasse sortis dans la rue.

author: Josh Richman
title: Privacy's Defenders Podcast: No Privacy Without Encryption
content:
When we communicate online today – from your personal emails and DMs to secure international commerce – we usually do so with encryption. Encryption converts readable data into unreadable gibberish to protect our privacy and security. This didn’t just happen organically. Three decades ago, the U.S government treated encryption like a weapon, and it took some unlikely heroes to set it free: a grad student, a junior lawyer, and a fledgling digital rights group who sued the federal government.

 


The ruling in

Bernstein v. Department of Justice

 held that code is speech and so is protected by the First Amendment – a precedent that underpins the internet as we know it today. This landmark case was led by Cindy Cohn, then a young pro bono lawyer working on behalf of EFF, who went on to become EFF’s legal director and then executive director.

 


Welcome to the second episode of “Privacy’s Defenders,” a podcast about the people – lawyers, journalists, hackers, and others – who’ve fought to secure your digital liberties since before most people even knew what the internet was.

Privacy info.


This embed will serve content from

simplecast.com


 

 

 


(You can also find this episode on the

Internet Archive

 and on YouTube.)


In this episode, Cindy – who left EFF in June – speaks with Dan Bernstein, who was a Cal Berkeley grad student when he developed a simple encryption algorithm called “Snuffle.” Because federal law classified encryption as a war munition, publishing Snuffle meant submitting it to the government for review, getting a license as an arms dealer, and being granted a license the government had no intention of granting. Bernstein felt this violated his free-speech rights and in 1995 he sued, represented by Cindy working with EFF.

 


Cindy also talks with Tony Coppolino, the Justice Department lawyer she battled in court – who admits she intimidated him from their very first phone call, and who offers a surprising perspective on the case all these years later.

 


The “Privacy’s Defenders” podcast (new episodes drop every other Tuesday!) is a follow-up to Cindy’s book, “

Privacy’s Defender: My Thirty-Year Fight Against Digital Surveillance

,” bringing to life pivotal moments in the voices of those who fought for your rights. Sales of “Privacy’s Defender” benefit EFF, so

pick up your copy today

!


Joanne Elgart Jennings co-produced and created this podcast.  

 


Jarod Sport co-produced, mixed, and mastered it.  

 


Corinne Ruff is our story editor.

 


We had additional help from Rachel Estabrook and Alison Broverman.

 


The original music was composed and performed by Nat Keefe of Hot Buttered Rum with Ben Andrews on the fiddle.

title: Δίκη των βασανιστών του Βασίλη Μάγγου: Το θέατρο των «δακρύων», οι 21 διακοπές και μια οικογένεια χωρίς φωνή
content:
Ανακοίνωση του

Δικτύου αλληλεγγύης και αγώνα Καρδίτσας

σχετικά με τις εξελίξεις στη δίκη των 6 βασανιστών του Βασίλη Μάγγου:


Δίκη Βασίλη Μάγγου: Το Θέατρο των «Δακρύων», οι 21 Διακοπές και μια Οικογένεια Χωρίς Φωνή


Με την ολοκλήρωση των απολογιών των έξι κατηγορούμενων αστυνομικών τη Δευτέρα, 12 Οκτωβρίου 2026, στο Μικτό Ορκωτό Δικαστήριο Καρδίτσας, ξεδιπλώθηκε πλήρως μια μεθοδευμένη και προκλητική υπερασπιστική τακτική.


Η διαδικασία σημαδεύτηκε από την ακραία στάση των συνηγόρων υπεράσπισης των αστυνομικών, η οποία εξελίχθηκε σε ένα δικαστικό περιβάλλον όπου στην οικογένεια του Βασίλη δεν επιτρέπεται καν να έχει πολιτική αγωγή (υποστήριξη κατηγορίας).


21 Διακοπές σε μια Δίκη χωρίς Πολιτική Αγωγή:


Όπως κατάγγειλε δημόσια ο πατέρας του Βασίλη, Γιάννης Μάγγος, η στάση της υπεράσπισης ήταν εντελώς απαράδεκτη.


Εκμεταλλευόμενοι το γεγονός ότι η οικογένεια έχει αποκλειστεί από τη διαδικασία και δεν εκπροσωπείται από δικούς της δικηγόρους για να τους αντιμετωπίσουν, οι συνήγοροι των αστυνομικών διέκοψαν τη ροή της δίκης συνολικά 21 φορές, προκειμένου να ελέγξουν πλήρως τις εντυπώσεις και να κατευθύνουν τη διαδικασία.


Το Θέατρο των Απολογιών:


Από τον «Τσαμπουκά» και την αλαζονεία της εξουσίας στα Κλάματα.


Η ίδια η διαδικασία των απολογιών των αστυνομικών έφερε στο φως μια προκλητική αντίφαση:


• Το πραγματικό πρόσωπο στον δρόμο: Όπως έχει καταγραφεί σε βίντεο, οι αστυνομικοί έξω από το δικαστικό μέγαρο Βόλου έδρασαν με απροκάλυπτo τσαμπουκά, ασκώντας άγρια βία και ξυλοκοπώντας τον Βασίλη Μάγγο μπροστά στα μάτια του κόσμου και των καμερών.


• Το αφήγημα του κρατητηρίου: Στον αντίποδα, οι αστυνομικοί στις απολογίες τους με όσα προκλητικά ισχυρίστηκαν , μέσα στο τμήμα μετατράπηκαν σε… «αρνάκια» , «μόνο φιλιά δεν του έδωσαν»του Βασίλη , σε μια απεγνωσμένη προσπάθεια να αρνηθούν τον βασανισμό που ακολούθησε.


• Στήθηκαν στις απολογίες τους: Μπροστά στους δικαστές, ο γνώριμος τσαμπουκάς και η αλαζονεία εξαφανίστηκαν και ορισμένοι από τους κατηγορούμενους έβαλαν μέχρι και τα κλάματα, σε μια προφανώς στημένη προσπάθεια να εκβιάσουν τη συμπάθεια της έδρας.


Επιστράτευσαν επίμονα το προφίλ του «καλού οικογενειάρχη» και παραπονέθηκαν ότι η κοινωνική κατακραυγή «διέλυσε» τη δική τους ζωή, αντιστρέφοντας πλήρως τους ρόλους θύματος και θύτη.


Πέρα από το ηθικό προφίλ, στο καθαρά υπηρεσιακό σκέλος οι αστυνομικοί τήρησαν μια στάση πλήρους άρνησης.


Δεν αποδέχθηκαν καμία ευθύνη για τα επιχειρησιακά λάθη και τη βαρβαρότητα της ημέρας εκείνης, στρέφοντας τα βέλη τους προς τις εντολές των ανωτέρων τους.


Η κοινωνία και οι αλληλέγγυοι ξέρουν πολύ καλά τι έκαναν και πώς τους αποκαλεί ο κόσμος. Η μνήμη του Βασίλη Μάγγου δεν είναι σκουπίδι για να παραγραφεί πίσω από υποκριτικά δάκρυα, δικονομικά τερτίπια και τον δικαστικό αποκλεισμό της ίδιας του της οικογένειας.


Τα αιτήματα της οικογένειας είναι και δικά μας αιτήματα:


• Να αποδοθούν πλήρως οι ευθύνες για τον βασανισμό και τον θάνατο του Βασίλη.


• Να υπάρξει πραγματικά δίκαιη δίκη χωρίς συγκάλυψη.


• Να καταδικαστούν οι 6 βασανιστές του Βασίλειου Μάγγου.


Η ακροαματική διαδικασία αναμένεται να συνεχιστεί εντός του μήνα, με τις επόμενες προγραμματισμένες δικασίμους να έχουν οριστεί για τις:


• 26 Οκτωβρίου 2026


• 29 Οκτωβρίου 2026


• 30 Οκτωβρίου 2026


Παράλληλα, για τις 16 Δεκεμβρίου 2026 έχει προσδιοριστεί η εκδίκαση της έφεσης των αστυνομικών σχετικά με την προηγούμενη καταδίκη τους από το Μονομελές Πλημμελειοδικείο Βόλου

ΣΤΟΥΣ ΔΡΟΜΟΥΣ ΑΝΑΠΝΕΕΙ ΤΟ ΔΙΚΙΟ


ΔΕΝ ΥΠΑΡΧΕΙ ΕΙΡΗΝΗ ΧΩΡΙΣ ΔΙΚΑΙΟΣΥΝΗ – ΔΕΝ ΘΑ ΞΕΧΑΣΤΕΙ ΤΙ ΚΑΝΑΝ ΣΤΟΝ ΒΑΣΙΛΗ


Δίκτυο αλληλεγγύης και αγώνα Καρδίτσας – Για υγεία, ζωή και ελευθερία

title: ‘Women, Justice and Memory Vigil’ against femicides in its second week
content:
The Amed (tr: Diyarbakır) Network for Combating Violence launched a “Women, Justice and Memory Vigil” against femicides and suspicious deaths of women last Tuesday, October 6. The vigil outside the Diyarbakır Courthouse will continue at the same location every Tuesday for 10 weeks.


Participants displayed a banner reading “Women Hold a Vigil for Justice and Memory,” along with photographs of women who had been killed.  Representatives of numerous political parties and civil society organizations attended the vigil in its second week.


Reading the statement on behalf of the Rosa Women’s Association, Ruşen Yakut said that during this week’s vigil, they were bringing together in collective memory the stories of women who were killed in different cities across Turkey between October 2 and 12 and whose information they had been able to obtain.


Emphasizing that the struggle for justice for murdered women is not limited to any particular period, Yakut stated that they would never abandon their demand for truth and justice. “For us, memory means remembering, leaving a trace, and ensuring that these women are not forgotten. The pursuit of justice means carrying the collective responsibility to protect women’s right to life into the present,” she said.


Following the statement, the stories of Füsun Yuluğkural, Gözde Çelik, Emel Bozkuş, Fadime Akbal, Gülşah Oktay, Sakine Y, Fikriye Cin, Mercan Kaplan, and Canan Bebek, who were murdered or died under suspicious circumstances, were read aloud.

title: Kurdish women’s movement participates in 39th Plurinational Gathering of Women in Argentina
content:
The 39th Plurinational Gathering of Women and Gender-Diverse People, held in Córdoba, Argentina from October 10 to 12, brought together hundreds of thousands of women from across Latin America. Organized by 300 local organizations, the gathering featured workshops, panel discussions, film screenings, and meetings.


 


A delegation from the Kurdish women’s movement participated in a meeting on internationalism, organized jointly with the Abya Yala feminist network, a panel titled “Revolutionary Practices,” and a screening of the film

In Search of Alina

. The events addressed the experiences of Kurdish women, the women’s revolution in Rojava, the struggle of women guerrillas in the mountains of Kurdistan, and the importance of international solidarity.


At the meeting on internationalism organized by the Kurdish women’s movement and the Abya Yala feminist network, discussions focused on the international dimension of Kurdish women’s struggle and the importance of the “Women Weaving the Future” network. Participants chanted the slogan, “Plurinational, plurinational; from Abya Yala to Kurdistan!”


During the panel titled “Revolutionary Practices,” the delegation spoke about the women’s revolution in Rojava, the struggle of women guerrillas in Kurdistan, and the role of internationalism. Following questions from participants, the delegation also addressed the Peace and Democratic Society Process.


Story of Alina Sánchez told


As part of the event, the film

In Search of Alina

, which tells the story of the life and struggle of internationalist revolutionary Legerîn Ciya (

Alina Sánchez

), who grew up in Córdoba and was martyred in Rojava in 2018, was screened.


In addition to the delegation from the Kurdish women’s movement, feminist, educator, and journalist Claudia Korol and Alina Sánchez’s mother also spoke at the screening. Her mother’s speech, in which she described her daughter’s life, joy, and determination, moved the participants.


The delegation also addressed an open assembly organized by the Abya Yala Feminists network on Sunday morning. The meeting, attended by representatives of Indigenous peoples and women’s organizations from different parts of Latin America, emphasized the importance of women’s organizing and leadership.


Throughout the gathering, the active participation of the Kurdish women’s movement brought international solidarity and opportunities for joint struggle to the forefront. The events concluded with discussions highlighting women’s liberation as one of the central struggles of the 21st century.

title: Conditions that gave rise to the Kurdish question and the conflict remain unchanged
content:
The conflict between the Turkish state and the PKK has been at a standstill for two years. The PKK has dissolved itself and decided to end its armed struggle against Turkey. The PKK disbanded and took significant steps in 2025 and 2026. All these steps were taken to enable free and unrestricted participation in democratic politics and to achieve a democratic resolution to the Kurdish question.


From the statement issued by the Kurdish Movement Leadership on October 8, we learn that the Turkish state has taken no steps apart from allowing meetings on Imralı Island every few months. More precisely, the Movement Leadership has conveyed this reality, which we have also witnessed, in the form of a polite warning. The statement emphasized that there is no longer any justification for the Turkish state’s failure to act following the significant steps taken by the movement.


The Movement Leadership stated that their leader must be freed and that legislation on freedoms, which would pave the way for a democratic resolution to the Kurdish question, must be enacted without delay. They specifically emphasized that if the Turkish state fails to take steps demonstrating such political will, they will interpret this as an intention to continue its previous policies.


The Movement Leadership made it clear that if the Turkish state takes no action and instead continues to demand further unilateral steps, it will no longer take such demands seriously. It also pointed out that the state’s failure to act would indicate that it is pursuing different objectives. They have thus taken a clear position against the state’s repeated demands to “take this step” or “take that step.”


It appears that the Movement Leadership harbors certain doubts about the Turkish state’s intentions. In short, their message was that they want to move the process forward, but the state is not demonstrating a similar commitment.


The statement issued by the Movement Leadership, along with assessments made to the press by some of its officials, deserves to be taken seriously. They have warned that if the Turkish state is playing a game, it would be the greatest miscalculation in Turkey’s history. Their statements constitute a call for the Turkish state to approach this process seriously. They would not have made such statements if they had not sensed uncertainty and delaying tactics, particularly in the attitude of the ruling AKP.


They consider it extremely important that the Kurdish People’s Leader be able to work under conditions of freedom. It is clear that if İmralı does not maintain continuous dialogue with journalists, intellectuals, politicians, and civil society organizations, they will regard this as a delaying tactic and another form of isolation. In the past, the state would occasionally allow a meeting or make a minor gesture, creating the impression that it was taking meaningful steps in the process. That policy, or game, has now reached its end.


Either this process will make substantial progress, or it will reach a deadlock. If the ruling AKP continues its current approach, it will demonstrate a lack of determination to move the process forward. This is not merely the view of the Movement Leadership; any Kurdish individual or democrat would think the same. After all, months and years are passing, yet the conditions that gave rise to the Kurdish question and the conflict remain unchanged!


The guerrillas are being told to lay down their arms and return, yet no changes have been made to the laws or the legal framework. Under the existing laws, not only returning guerrillas and Kurds but even ordinary democrats cannot freely engage in democratic politics. The prisons are still filled with political prisoners. In fact, even those who have already served the prison sentences imposed by Turkish courts are not being released! How can the guerrillas be expected to lay down their arms and return to Turkey unless the existing laws are changed? If the Turkish state expects them to simply “return home,” that is not going to happen. Indeed, officials from the Movement Leadership have already stated that such an approach is unacceptable.


On the other hand, although the guerrillas have withdrawn from Turkish territory and areas close to Turkey’s borders, the Turkish state is now demanding that they also leave the areas where they are currently stationed. In other words, it is telling them to go somewhere else and live as displaced people or refugees. If …

title: A new chapter in the heart of Paris: Kurdistan House of France
content:
The Kurdistan House of France, which aims to bring together the cultural, social, academic, and institutional activities of the Kurdish community in France under one roof, was officially unveiled to the public at a grand ceremony held at Paris City Hall.


The event, held on the evening of Monday, October 12, in the historic hall of Paris City Hall, located in the political and historical heart of the French capital, brought together politicians, institutional representatives, artists, academics, association leaders, and civil society figures from the Kurdish and French communities.


Three speeches were delivered during the evening. Paris Mayor Emmanuel Grégoire gave the opening address, followed by Baran Gürbüz, President of the Kurdistan House of France. Former French President François Hollande delivered the final political address of the evening.


Official launch at historic Paris City Hall


The decision to hold the official launch of the Kurdistan House of France (Maison du Kurdistan de France) at Paris City Hall itself was one of the evening’s most significant symbolic and political messages.


Relations between the Paris municipal administration and Kurdish institutions have become increasingly visible in recent months. In June, Grégoire received representatives of the Democratic Kurdish Council in France and the Kurdistan House of France at City Hall. Their discussions focused on the Kurdish community’s activities in France, youth initiatives, cultural and social programs, and potential joint projects with Kurdish institutions in Paris.


The event on October 12 marked a new stage in the development of these relations.


The official unveiling of an institution bearing the name Kurdistan at Paris City Hall, attended by hundreds of guests, is regarded as a powerful message reflecting the Kurdish community’s decades-long struggle, organization, and institutional development in France.


Baran Gürbüz: The beginning of a new era


Following the opening speech by Paris Mayor Emmanuel Grégoire, Baran Gürbüz, President of the Kurdistan House of France, addressed the participants.


Gürbüz emphasized that the Kurdistan House of France would not merely serve as a venue for events or gatherings but would operate as a permanent institution dedicated to meeting the needs of the Kurdish community in France.


Activities to be carried out in four key areas


The Kurdistan House of France will carry out its activities through four main departments; Culture, Sports and Youth, Social and Legal Affairs, Research and Academia.


Through this organizational structure, the Kurdistan House of France aims to contribute to preserving Kurdish culture, history, language, and collective memory while also building stronger ties with younger generations.


The Social and Legal Affairs Department will provide social, administrative, and legal support to those in need, while the Research and Academia Department will seek to strengthen academic studies on the Kurdish question, the history and culture of Kurdistan, and social developments.


The Sports and Youth Department will play a central role in strengthening ties with younger generations, increasing young people’s participation in social and collective activities, and implementing new projects.


Hollande: Solidarity with the Kurds should not be dependent on political circumstances


One of the evening’s most significant political messages came from former French President François Hollande.


Recalling the struggle against ISIS in Rojava during his presidency, Hollande highlighted the historic role played by Kurdish forces and said: “Victory against ISIS would not have been possible without the Syrian Kurds.”


The former Socialist president emphasized that France’s solidarity with the Kurds should not be dependent on changing regional circumstances or political agreements.


Hollande also recalled that during his presidency, he had received Kurdish women representatives and commanders involved in the fight against ISIS at the Élysée Palace.


‘420,000 Kurds live in France’


François Hollande also devoted particular attention to the role of the Kurdish community in France’s social and economic life.


Stating that approximately 420,000 Kurds live in France, he noted that Kurds have made significant contributions to the country in numerous fields, from science and culture to commerce and healthcare.

author: CMI Argentina
title: ¿Por qué sube el dólar?
content:
Nunca habían ingresado tantos dólares por la vía comercial y, sin embargo, desde abril la divisa ya subió $200. ¿Qué está pasando? ¿Va a seguir subiendo? Un informe de MATE aporta algunas respuestas.


Ilustración: Marcelo Spotti


Por Gladys Stagno


Desde mediados de abril, el dólar comenzó un movimiento ascendente luego de algunos meses de caída. El valor oficial de la divisa que por entonces cotizaba en torno a los $1.350, ya cuesta $1.540, lo que significa una apreciación del 14% en cinco meses, a razón de casi un 3% mensual,

muy por encima de la inflación registrada por el INDEC.


Las explicaciones oficiales del fenómeno no abundan, pero

el discurso que baja desde la cartera liderada por Luis “Toto” Caputo viene siendo la de patear la pelota afuera

 y atribuirles los índices antipáticos para el Gobierno a sucesos pasajeros, como la liquidación de divisas del agro.


Sin embargo, la suba sostenida del dólar puede –y quizá debe– explicarse por políticas propias del modelo libertario.


Fuente: MATE


Como vienen, se van


Según un informe del Mirador de la Actualidad del Trabajo y la Economía (MATE), la gestión de La Libertad Avanza tiene un comportamiento dual: mientras hay un récord de ingreso de dólares comerciales, estos no paran de irse.


“En 2026 ingresan, en promedio, 2.829 millones de dólares cada mes por el saldo favorable de la balanza comercial. Se trata de un récord absoluto para la economía que duplica o triplica registros de años anteriores”, sostiene el informe de MATE.


Sin embargo, así como llegan, se van. En números, y a pesar del incremento de las exportaciones, “en lo que va del año la economía perdió 1.582 millones de dólares mensuales”, plantea el estudio.


Barril sin fondo


La explicación de este déficit no tiene nada que ver con “factores estacionales”. “No alcanza el saldo comercial de la economía real para cubrir la salida de dólares de la economía financiera”, asegura el análisis de la investigación realizada por los economistas Diego Kofman, Lavih Abraham, Marco Kofman, Natalia Pérez Barreda y Sergio Arelovich.


Y es que, con el levantamiento de los controles cambiarios, la pérdida de reservas por dolarización de excedentes –más conocida como “fuga”– de personas jurídicas y personas físicas de alto poder adquisitivo “explotó”. “Se pierden más de 3.200 millones de dólares mensuales por este motivo”, detalla MATE.


Ahora bien, ¿quiénes fugan? Todos. Mientras que los hidrocarburos (petróleo y gas) llevan fugados 1.091 millones de dólares, el sector de los químicos ya sacó del mercado argentino otros 446 millones; alimentos, 399 millones; entidades financieras, 351 millones; y sigue la lista.


Desde que en diciembre se reactivó el envío al exterior de utilidades y dividendos, “ya se fueron 3.957 millones de dólares”, señala MATE. Desde noviembre de 2023, la fuga de excedentes ya suma 65.243 millones.


Más y más deuda


Así las cosas, la demanda de dólares de la economía financiera es superior a los que genera la economía real.


Mientras estos últimos fueron, de noviembre de 2023 a agosto de 2026, un total de 62.222 millones, la economía financiera consumió, en el mismo periodo, 97.606 millones de dólares.


Como consecuencia, el esquema solo sobrevive con más endeudamiento. En el detalle, desde la asunción de Javier Milei a la Presidencia la nueva deuda pública asciende a los 10.396 millones de dólares, y la nueva deuda privada a los 26.373 millones.


Pero más endeudamiento también implica más compromisos y, de acuerdo con el estudio de MATE, desde noviembre de 2023, los pagos de intereses por deuda pública y privada ya acumulan 32.364 millones de dólares.


Mensualmente, en tanto, egresan “más de 1.000 millones de dólares” por los pagos de intereses de la deuda externa pública y privada, detalla MATE. Y advierte: “En un contexto de crecimiento de estos pasivos, dicha pérdida de dólares se acentuará”.


Fuente:

https://canalabierto.com.ar/2026/10/08/por-que-sube-el-dolar/


La entrada

¿Por qué sube el dólar?

Indymedia Argentina Centro de Medios Independientes (( i ))

author: Afolabi Adekaiyaoja
title: Forward, but for whom?
content:
I have spent this week reflecting on African football. Qualifiers for the next Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) have begun, the identity of the reigning champions still awaits a ruling from the Court of Arbitration for Sport, and Nigeria begins its campaign without a federation board, after its president and executive committee

resigned in August

 — a rare case of Nigerian football administrators paying a price for failure, though, as I will argue, not quite the accountability it first appears. None of it can be separated from the politics and money that will shape next year’s FIFA presidential election.

Weeks after the 2026 World Cup in North America, FIFA unveiled a plan to sell a stake in the tournament’s commercial rights to private investors. The proposal would have seen a new entity, FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), take over FIFA’s broadcast, sponsorship, ticketing, and licensing operations. FIFA would keep control and sell minority stakes to outside investors, raising up to $4.2 billion against a $20 billion valuation. The lead investor was reportedly

Thrive

, a firm founded by Joshua Kushner, whose brother Jared is US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law. To win the member associations’ approval, FIFA promised to raise each one’s development allocation for 2027–2030 from about $8 million to $20 million, with an optional further $20 million paid up front. But the backlash, largely led by UEFA, the European confederation, was swift and relentless. Within days, FIFA president Gianni Infantino

withdrew the plan

 and has spent the weeks since trying to salvage his presidency and avert a challenge that previously seemed impossible.

During this period, Africa’s confederation stood firmly with Infantino. Several federation presidents backed him publicly, and Samuel Eto’o, the Cameroonian legend who now runs his country’s federation,

went further

, arguing that the plan could have done a great deal for smaller federations. FIFA’s crisis meeting was held in Rabat rather than Zurich, and the executive committee of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) later met there and

unanimously reaffirmed its support

 for him. Much of the commentary has cast this as a deferential, even subservient, relationship, with Africa as a continent unable to stand up for “true footballing values” once money is on the table.

But Africa’s relationship with FIFA did not begin in deference. UEFA may have threatened a boycott this summer, but in 1966 it was African federations, led by Ghana’s Ohene Djan and Ethiopia’s Yidnekatchew Tessema, that boycotted World Cup qualifying ahead of England ’66 because they had been made to share a single qualifying place with Asia and Oceania, while Europe had 10 of the 16 spots. The boycott worked: Since the next tournament, in 1970, Africa has had at least one guaranteed place. In 1974, the same bloc helped the Brazilian João Havelange defeat Stanley Rous for the FIFA presidency. Rous had spent years trying to keep apartheid South Africa, already shut out by CAF, inside world football.

However, Havelange’s victory set the terms of the bargain that has governed FIFA-Africa relations since. He campaigned on the promise of expanded tournaments and development for the Global South. He delivered them, but he also brought a culture of patronage that defined his 25 years in power. Sepp Blatter, his long-serving general secretary, inherited the same structure when he succeeded him in 1998, and used it to peel away African federations even though CAF officially backed UEFA’s Lennart Johansson. In 2002, when CAF’s own president, Issa Hayatou, contested the presidency, he was beaten heavily, deserted by members who preferred the patron they had to the African they might have had.

Under Infantino, FIFA has become even more involved in Africa’s management. In 2017, Madagascar’s Ahmad Ahmad unseated Hayatou as CAF president, a result Infantino reportedly supported, and in 2018 Ahmad declared Africa’s support for Infantino’s re-election a year early. In 2021, Infantino cast a long shadow as rivals stood aside and endorsed Patrice Motsepe, the South African mining billionaire, as new CAF president, after FIFA had sent its own secretary-general, Fatma Samoura, to run CAF’s affairs for six months in 2019, and after Ahmad was banned by FIFA’s ethics committee. Motsepe’s tenure has recorded successes, but critics still cast him as Infantino’s puppet in Cairo.

title: Tuncer Bakırhan: Müzakere masasından kalkmayacağız
content:
DEM Parti Eş Genel Başkanı Tuncer Bakırhan, Irak Kürdistan Bölgesel Yönetimi'nin başkenti Erbil’de Ortadoğu Araştırma Enstitüsü (MERI) tarafından düzenlenen uluslararası forumda konuştu.


Bafıl Talabani: Türkiye’deki süreci desteklemeliyiz, İran’da da benzer bir süreç başlıyor


Bugün  12:23


Kürt meselesinin barışçıl ve demokratik yollarla çözülmesi gerektiğinin altını çizen Tuncer Bakırhan, şunları söyledi:


“Müzakere masasından kalkmayacağız, çünkü çıkarımız bundadır. Çözüm sürecini biz başarıya ulaştıracağız. Kendimize güveniyoruz, devrimcilere güveniyoruz, bizimle yan yana duran halkımıza güveniyoruz. Yüzyıllık bir meseleyi birkaç ayda çözmek çok zor, biraz sabırlı olmak gerekiyor. Kürtler 100 yıldır demokrasi arayışı içinde. Devletin işin içinde olmadığı yerde Türkiye toplumunu ikna etmeye çalışıyoruz. Yüzyıldır ilk defa TBMM ‘bizim de bir Kürt sorunumuz var, bu sorunun çözülmesi için bir çerçeve yasaya ihtiyacımız var’ dedi ve ilk defa bir çerçeve yasa çıkardı. Bu çerçeve yasanın uygulanması için daha çok mücadele edeceğiz. Kürtlerin geleceği masadadır, diyalogdadır, demokrasidedir.”


İlham Ahmed: Suriye’de ilk kez Kürt dili ve kültürü tanındı ancak uygulama eksik


12 Ekim 2026


"Büyük sorumluluk üstlendiler"


Bakırhan sözlerine şöyle devam etti:


“Bu barış sürecinde Sayın Mesud Barzani’nin büyük katkısı oldu. Buradan kendisine teşekkür ediyoruz. Bu sürecin ilerlemesinde gerekli olan bütün sorumluluğu ortaya koydu. Bu sürecin ilerlemesi için emin olun o kadar çok çaba ortaya koydu ki… Aynı şekilde Neçirvan Barzani’ye çok teşekkürler, bu süreçte çok büyük bir rolü oldu. Gerçekten bu süreçte büyük bir sorumluluk üstlendi. Kürdistan Bölgesi’nde bulunan bütün siyasi partilere teşekkür ediyorum. Türkiye barışını sağlarsa Kürdistan Bölgesi daha çok güvende olacak. Türkiye’de barış olursa Irak Kalkınma Yolu projesi de iyi sonuç verir."


Tülay Hatimoğlulları: Neden somut adım atılmıyor?


Bugün  14:37


“Kürtlerin anadili seçmeli olamaz”


Bakırhan, “Bizim amacımız sadece Türkiye’ye demokrasinin gelmesi değil. Suriye’deki kardeşlerimizin de refah içinde yaşamasını istiyoruz. Suriye’ye bu yeni yol arayışında başarılar diliyoruz. Provokasyonlara gelmemek ve yüzyıl önceki politikalardan vazgeçmek lazım; çünkü Suriye yeterince bedel ödedi" dedi.


MERI nedir?


Orta Doğu Araştırma Enstitüsü'nün (MERI), büyük ölçekli uluslararası forumlar da dahil olmak üzere çok çeşitli konferans ve toplantılar düzenliyor. Bu etkinlikler, yerel ve uluslararası paydaşları bir araya getirmeyi, Irak, Kürdistan Bölgesi ve daha geniş Orta Doğu'yu etkileyen önemli konuları tartışmak ve ele almak için bir platform sağlamayı amaçlamaktadır.


Orta Doğu Araştırma Enstitüsü (MERI), önde gelen bağımsız politika yapıcı bir kurum olarak konumunu, geniş bir yelpazedeki konularda yapıcı diyaloğu teşvik etmek için kullanmaktadır.


Bu etkinliklerde, MERI, Irak Cumhurbaşkanı, Irak Parlamentosu Başkanı, Kürdistan Bölgesel Hükümeti Başbakanı, hem Irak hem de Kürdistan Bölgesi'nden çeşitli bakanlar ve çok sayıda uluslararası şahsiyet de dahil olmak üzere birçok seçkin konuşmacıyı ağırlamıştır.

title: Fon soruşturmasında 29 isim malvarlığı tedbiri listesine sehven yazıldı
content:
İstanbul Başsavcılığının nitelikli dolandırıcılık, Sermaye Piyasası Kanunu’na muhalefet ve bu suçlardan elde edildiği değerlendirilen malvarlığı değerlerinin aklanması iddiaları kapsamında yürüttüğü soruşturmada, 141 kişinin malvarlığına tedbir uygulanmasına yönelik yazı ilgili kurumlara gönderildi.

Gazeteci Bahadır Özgür’ün aktardığına göre, söz konusu listede bulunan 29 kişinin adının sehven yazıldığı, daha sonra resmi makamlar tarafından ilgili birimlere yazılı olarak bildirildi.

Hatalı olduğu belirtilen 29 kişinin kimler olduğu açıklanmazken, ilk listede adının bulunduğu öne sürülen eski AKP'li bakan Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya'nın durumu da gündeme geldi.

Cumhuriyet’in resmi kaynaklardan edindiği bilgiye göre, Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya, düzeltmenin ardından tedbir uygulanan kişiler arasında bulunmuyor.

Kaya ve eşi İlyas Kaya, daha önce soruşturma kapsamında şüpheli sıfatıyla ifade vermiş, hisse işlemlerinde herhangi bir yönlendirme yapılmadığını ve kendilerine özel bilgi verilmediğini savunmuştu.

İlyas Kaya’nın düzeltilen listedeki durumuna ilişkin ise net bilgi bulunmuyor.

Tedbir uygulanan kişiler arasında TERA yöneticisi Emre Tezmen ile şarkıcı Mustafa Sandal’ın eşi Melis Sütşurup Sandal’ın da bulunduğu bildirildi.

Başsavcılığın Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK) ile Türkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankasına (TCMB) gönderdiği yazıda, tedbir kapsamındaki kişilere ait şüpheli işlemlerin gecikmeksizin savcılığa bildirilmesi istendi. Tedbir kararının kişilerin emekli maaşlarını kapsamadığı belirtildi.

Tapu ve Kadastro Genel Müdürlüğü, Denizcilik Genel Müdürlüğü ve Sivil Havacılık Genel Müdürlüğünden de listede bulunan kişiler adına kayıtlı taşınmaz, gemi ve hava aracı olup olmadığının tespit edilmesi talep edildi.

Savcılığın yazısının ardından Tasarruf Mevduatı Sigorta Fonunun (TMSF) da tedbir kapsamındaki bazı kişilere elde edilen tutarların iadesine yönelik tebligat gönderdiği bildirildi.

TMSF’nin tebligatlarda Sermaye Piyasası Kanunu’nun 107. maddesi kapsamında işlem yapılabileceğine ilişkin uyarıya yer verdiği aktarıldı. Fon soruşturması kapsamında daha önce bazı yatırımcılara gönüllü iade imkanı tanınmıştı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Hoffenheim-Beşiktaş maçı ne zaman, saat kaçta, hangi kanalda? Cerny oynayacak mı?
content:
Beşiktaş, UEFA Avrupa Ligi’nin 2. haftasında Hoffenheim deplasmanına çıkacak. 15 Ekim Perşembe günü oynanacak karşılaşmanın başlama saati ve yayın kanalı merak ediliyor. Kocaelispor maçında sakatlanan Vaclav Cerny’nin karşılaşmada forma giymesi beklenmiyor.

UEFA Avrupa Ligi’nde heyecan 2. hafta karşılaşmalarıyla devam ediyor. Beşiktaş, Almanya temsilcisi Hoffenheim’a konuk olacak. Siyah-beyazlılar, Avrupa Ligi’nde üst üste ikinci galibiyetini almayı hedeflerken Hoffenheim karşısında deplasmanda puan arayacak.

Kocaelispor’u 2-1 mağlup ederek moral bulan Beşiktaş’ta gözler, Avrupa Ligi mücadelesine çevrildi. Peki Hoffenheim-Beşiktaş maçı ne zaman, saat kaçta ve hangi kanalda? Vaclav Cerny karşılaşmada oynayacak mı?

title: Fatmanur Çelik ve Hifa İkra için adalet arayışı sürüyor: İstismar davasının karar duruşması yarın
content:
Kızı Hifa İkra’nın Kuran’a Hizmet Vakfıyla ilişkili olduğu iddia edilen Ayhan Şengüler tarafından istismar edilmesine karşı adalet mücadelesi yürüten Fatmanur Çelik ve kızı istismar davasından yalnızca iki ay önce Zeytinburnu sahilinde şüpheli şekilde ölü bulunmuştu. Çelik’in ve kızının hayatını kaybetmesi kadınlar ve kamuoyu tarafından öfkeyle karşılanmış ve 5 Mayıs günü Hifa İkra’nın istismar edilmesi üzerine görülen duruşmaya da kadınlar çağrı yapmıştı. Ayhan Şengüler’in istismardan yargılandığı bu davanın karar duruşması ise 14 Ekim Çarşamba günü saat 10.00’da İstanbul 2. Ağız Ceza Mahkemesinde görülecek.

Duruşma öncesi konuştuğumuz, Fatmanur Çelik ve Hifa’nın avukatı, Önce Çocuklar ve Kadınlar Derneğinden Av. Serenay Yaman yargılama sürecini, gerçekleşen ihmalleri hatırlatırken bir yandan da Fatmanur ve Hifa’nın şüpheli şekilde ölü bulunmasına ilişkin soruşturmanın gizli yürütüldüğünü ve yedi aydır soruşturmanın ne aşamada olduğunun ise bilinmediğini aktardı.

Ayhan Şengüler’in yargılanması başladıktan itibaren çeşitli hak ihlalleri Fatmanur Çelik ve avukatları tarafından gündeme getirilmişti. Av. Yaman, yargılama sürecinde Hifa İkra’nın yaşadığı hak ihlallerine dikkat çekti. Mahkeme başkanının çocuğun davranışlarını ve mimiklerini görmek gerekçesiyle Hifa’yı mahkeme salonunda dinlemek istediğini öğrendiklerini belirten Av. Yaman, “Çocuk küçük yaşta olduğundan CMK m. 236 uyarınca adli görüşme odasında dinlenmesini talep ettik. Duruşma öncesinde mahkeme kalemiyle AGO'nun hazır edilmesi için görüşmeye gittiğimizde kalem tarafından mahkeme başkanının cinsel istismar dosyalarında mağduru mahkeme duruşma salonunda dinlediği ve bu duruşmayı da bu şekilde gerçekleştireceği tarafımıza iletildi. Bu duruma itiraz ettik, mahkeme başkanıyla görüşmek istedik, başkanın koruması olduğunu öğrendiğimiz kişi tarafından bizlere başkanın avukatlarla görüşme yapmadığı söylendi” dedi.

Av. Yaman, mahkeme başkanının Hifa İkra dinlenirken sanık Ayhan Şengüler’i salondan çıkarttığını ancak çocuğun birçok kişinin ortasında yaşadığı istismarı yeniden anlatmak zorunda kaldığını söyledi: "Çocuk hukuka aykırı bir şekilde, çocuğun üstün yararı ilkesi hiçe sayılarak mahkeme salonunda onlarca kişinin içinde dinlendi.” Kanun uyarınca çocuğun ifadesi alınırken bir uzmanın orada bulunması ve çocuğun örselenmemesi için soruları çocuğa uzmanın yöneltmesi gerektiğini belirten Av. Yaman, “Mahkeme usule aykırı şekilde uzman yerine geçip çocuğa sorular yöneltti. Doğrudan çocuğu yargılar gibi davrandılar. Olayın detaylarına ilişkin üst üste ve tekrarlı sorular soruldu. Çocuğun duruşmadan sonra günlerce yataktan çıkmadığı ve ağladığı müvekkil tarafından dile getirildi" dedi.

Av. Yaman, tüm bunlara rağmen sanığın o duruşmada da tutuklanmadığını belirtti:

“Dava konusu olaya ilişkin soruşturma aşamasında başta takipsizlik kararı veriliyor. Sonra hak savunucuları itiraz ediyor, iddianame düzenleniyor ve dava açılıyor. Bundan sonraki süreçte yaşananlar, sanki hukukun üzerinde bir dokunulmazlık varmış izlenimi yaratıyor. Hiç kimse hukukun üstünde değildir, hiçbir süreç de hesap sorulamaz olmamalıdır.”

Mahkemenin bu keyfi yargılaması karşısında HSK'ya şikayette bulunduklarını da söyleyen Av. Yaman, şikayetin de reddedildiğini, hakim hakkında hiçbir soruşturma yürütülmediğini belirtti.

Duruşmalar devam ederken Fatmanur Çelik’in sanık tutuksuz yargılandığı için adalet nöbetine başlamak istediğini belirten Av. Yaman, “Fatma Nur kendi iradesiyle adalet nöbeti tutmaya karar verdi. Yaşadıklarını duyurabilmek için, kızının sesi olmak için her gün adliyeye gitti” ifadelerini kullandı.

Fatmanur Çelik ve Hifa’nın ölümü gerçekleşmeden önce Çelik’in kendisini güvende hissetmediğini söyleyen Av. Yaman, Hifa’nın ve Fatmanur’un ölümüne ilişkin soruşturma dosyasının mart ayından itibaren açık olduğunu ve soruşturmanın gizli yürütüldüğünü aktardı, Av. Yaman, “Biz dernek olarak katılma talebinde bulunduk ama savcılık tarafından talebimiz reddedildi. Dosyada gizlilik kararı olduğu için ne gibi işlemler yapıldığını, hangi aşamada olduğunu bilmiyoruz. Soruşturma tamamlanmadan ölümün nasıl gerçekleştiğine dair kesin bilgiye ulaşmamız mümkün değil. Ancak bunun doğal bir ölüm olmadığını biliyoruz, ihmaller araştırılmalı"” dedi.

Av. Yaman, “Büyük ihmaller var. Bunların soruşturulması gerekiyor ancak soruşturulmuyor. Tam tersine, hak arayan avukatlar soruşturuluyor. ‘Neden bunları sorguluyorsunuz, neden üzerilerine gidiyorsunuz?’ diye biz sorgulanıyoruz. Geçmişte Hifa mahkeme …

author: Unknown
title: A lot of people seem to mix up ‘community’ with ‘friend group’ so when they read ‘no one should be…
content:
A lot of people seem to mix up ‘community’ with ‘friend group’ so when they read ‘no one should be abandoned by the community. No matter what they did’ they think it means ‘you have to be friends with abusers’. When in reality it means ‘no matter what someone does they shouldnt be left to go homeless and be denied financial, housing, medical, etc aid’

You don’t have to be friends with these people, no one is saying that. It’s just saying that you should support rehabilitative justice, support programs that help homeless people, support funding for free medical services, and make sure they don’t turn away anyone who needs help.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Denuncian perjuicios para los detenidos provocados por el traslado de la cárcel de Devoto a Marcos Paz
content:
Empezaron a trasladar a los detenidos que están en la penal de Devoto a los nuevos módulos carcelarios que construyeron en Marcos Paz, dependientes del Servicio Penitenciario Federal (SPF). Denuncian destrucción de vínculos y la interrupción de trayectorias académicas.


Por Jesús Cabral @CabraAbelardo


Con un amplio operativo de las fuerzas de seguridad, este domingo empezó a cumplirse el acuerdo firmado entre el gobierno de Jorge Macri y el gobierno de Javier Milei. El que estipula trasladar a los detenidos que en la actualidad están en la penal de Devoto a los nuevos módulos carcelarios que construyeron en Marcos Paz, dependientes del Servicio Penitenciario Federal (SPF).


En ese contexto, querellantes, sobrevivientes, familiares de víctimas de la Masacre del Pabellón Séptimo y un amplio arco de organizaciones sociales, enfatizan en la destrucción de los vínculos de los detenidos y la interrupción de sus trayectorias académicas que produce el movimiento de un penal a otro.


Denuncian la destrucción del Centro Universitario Devoto (CUD) del Programa UBA-XXII, de la Universidad de Buenos Aires (UBA), con más de 40 años de funcionamiento. Explicaron que es considerado “un símbolo de la democracia argentina”. Fue inaugurado el 17 de diciembre de 1985, tras la firma de un convenio marco firmado entre la UBA y el SPF.


“Desactivar el sistema democrático”


Se trata de un espacio que fue creado luego de que el país atravesara la última dictadura cívico-militar, “con el objetivo de restituir los derechos históricamente vulnerados a las personas detenidas”, apuntaron los demandantes. “No es casualidad, es parte del plan de Milei para desactivar el sistema democrático”, remarcaron.


Una vez que terminen con los traslados, el plan es urbanizar el predio del penal de Devoto con espacios verdes. Y un sector será destinado para mantener viva la memoria por la Masacre del Pabellón Séptimo, que ocurrió el 14 de marzo de 1978, donde fallecieron 65 detenidos en un incendio. La querella reclama que todo el predio -no solo una parte- sea declarado Sitio de Memoria.


Claudia Cesaroni es la abogada fundadora del Centro de Estudios en Política Criminal y Derechos Humanos

(CEPOC)

. La letrada luchó -junto a su estudio jurídico- para desarchivar la causa de la Masacre y a fines de 2025 logró que dos exjefes del SPF sean condenados.


Trayectorias académicas interrumpidas


“Están avanzando contra todos los acuerdos y lo previamente conversado con organizaciones sociales y entidades públicas, en cuanto cómo iba a hacer el traslado de detenidos. Sin embargo, lo primero que hicieron fue sacar a los referentes del CUD”, criticó Cesaroni.


Y completó: “Recuerdo que habíamos quedado con que esos detenidos serían llevados a Ezeiza, porque en Marcos Paz no están dadas las condiciones para el desarrollo académico que mantenían en Devoto”.


La letrada detalló que se llevaron a los detenidos que estaban alojados en los pabellones 50 y 52; que son los están más avanzados en la progresividad de la penal. También expresó su preocupación por la poca repercusión pública sobre la destrucción de una sede académica de la UBA, que es una experiencia modelo en el mundo. Explicó que el CUD es un espacio lleno de colores y posibilidades para las personas que transitan el encierro punitivo como castigo.


También destacó el compromiso de los equipos de docentes que trabajaron en el lugar durante décadas transformando las vidas de las personas en situación de encierro. “El CUD fue dinamitado, todo empezó cuando este Gobierno prohibió el funcionamiento de los centros de estudiantes en las cárceles federales. Son traslados intempestivos”, apuntó la abogada.


Cesaroni concluyó: “Es lamentable, porque hay una parte de la sociedad que no mira esto que está pasando, parece ser que no le importa, es algo que lamento mucho. Todas las Universidades Públicas deberían pronunciarse en defensa del Centro Universitario Devoto”.


Por su parte, la Procuración Penitenciaria de la Nación (PPN), presentó un habeas corpus colectivo y correctivo. Lo hizo en el marco de su misión de velar por los derechos de las personas detenidas en instituciones de encierro de la órbita federal.

author: anred
title: Ley de Tierras: organizaciones celebran el fallo y llaman a seguir movilizando
content:
La Corte Suprema de Justicia dictó el pasado viernes 9 de octubre una medida cautelar interina que restituye provisoriamente la Ley de Tierras Rurales, suspendiendo así el artículo 154 del DNU 70/2023 que la había derogado. La medida, que salió con el voto de conjueces y con el de Rosenkrantz como único voto en contra, responde a una presentación oportunamente planteada por la Asociación Civil Árbol de Pie, que ayer fue respaldada a través de un Amicus Curiae presentado conjuntamente por el SERPAJ, la CTA Autónoma y la Asociación Argentina de Juristas ante la Corte Suprema. La Corte restituyó la norma, pero todo el DNU 70/23 sigue en jaque. El jueves 15, cuando Diputados lo trate, las organizaciones marcharán al Congreso para exigir su derogación completa.

Por Canal Abierto.


Redacción Canal Abierto |

La Corte Suprema de Justicia dictó hoy, viernes 9 de octubre, una medida cautelar interina que restituye provisoriamente la Ley de Tierras Rurales, suspendiendo así el artículo 154 del DNU 70/2023 que la había derogado. La medida, que salió con el voto de conjueces y con el de Rosenkrantz como único voto en contra, responde a una presentación oportunamente planteada por la

Asociación Civil Árbol de Pie

, que ayer fue respaldada a través de un

Amicus Curiae

 presentado conjuntamente por el

SERPAJ

, la

CTA Autónoma

 y la

Asociación Argentina de Juristas ante la Corte Suprema

.


Los demandantes originales del caso Árbol de Pie son la asociación ambientalista homónima, dos comunidades mapuches (Lafkenche y Lof Fvta Anecon) y la exlegisladora de Río Negro Magdalena Odarda. A diferencia del caso CECIM, que la semana pasada fue rechazado por falta de legitimación, esta demanda se apoya en la

protección del ambiente

 y los

derechos indígenas

, no en la «soberanía».


A través de un comunicado, las organizaciones revelaron que en sus presentaciones, “advirtieron sobre

la gravedad institucional de eliminar, mediante un DNU

, un régimen legal de protección de la tierra rural, con consecuencias para el ambiente, los recursos naturales, la integridad territorial y los derechos de los pueblos indígenas. Asimismo, sostuvieron que la medida

vulnera garantías constitucionales y convencionales, además de las obligaciones internacionales

asumidas por el Estado argentino”.


En el mismo escrito, difndieron la solicitud a “que se convoque a una audiencia pública para ampliar el debate, garantizar la participación de las comunidades indígenas involucradas y aportar elementos relevantes para la resolución de una cuestión de profundo interés público y trascendencia institucional. Las organizaciones reafirmaron su compromiso con la defensa de los derechos humanos, la soberanía sobre los recursos naturales y la protección de los territorios”.


El martes 29 de septiembre, la Corte había fallado en el caso «CECIM» rechazando su legitimación para demandar.

El argumento fue que la «soberanía» no es un interés colectivo protegido por el artículo 43 de la Constitución

. Ese fallo, en la práctica, dejó la ley de tierras derogada y sin restricciones la venta de territorios argentinos a extranjeros.


La reacción no se hizo esperar. El martes 6 de octubre hubo

una fuerte movilización a Tribunales para repudiar el fallo que había suspendido la cautelar

lograda por los excombatientes. Las organizaciones sociales salieron a la calle, los diputados opositores anunciaron

una sesión especial para el 15 de octubre,

 no solo para rechazar el artículo 154 sino para

voltear todo el DNU 70/2023

.


En paralelo, el Gobierno sufrió otro revés en el Congreso: tuvo que bajar los capítulos de

Ley de Tierras

 y

Manejo del Fuego

 de la Ley de Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada, que se discutía en el Senado. Esos dos capítulos pretendían convalidar legislativamente lo que el DNU 70/2023 había hecho por decreto: abrir la compra de tierras rurales a extranjeros y flexibilizar las restricciones sobre el uso del suelo después de incendios. Sin los votos suficientes, el oficialismo optó por retirarlos para salvar el resto de la ley.


La Corte se reunió de urgencia y dictó la cautelar interina que restituye la ley de tierras hasta que el juez federal de Bariloche resuelva el fondo del caso Árbol de Pie. La votación fue 4 a 1. Rosenkrantz fue el único voto en contra: sostuvo que a algunos sectores de la sociedad les disguste lo resuelto la semana pasada no puede ser motivo para adoptar medidas que la Constitución y la ley no permiten, y …
