title: Botan: Disarmament is a precondition for peace, not peace itself - Part Two
content:
Politician Lezgin Botan spoke to ANF about how the process is viewed by the Kurdish public, political and legal expectations, the relationship between disarmament and democratisation, and possible developments in the coming period.


The first part of this interview can be read

here

. 


Botan said strengthening local governments and ending the practice of appointing trustees were among the important issues in the process. He stressed that strengthening local democracy should be considered not only in relation to the Kurdish question but also in the context of Turkey's overall democratisation.


Botan also said: “Local democracy is an important issue in the democratic resolution of the Kurdish question. The constant supervision of local governments by the central administration, and their being rendered ineffective when deemed necessary, create serious problems for the political will of the people. The practice of appointing trustees, in particular, means that the central administration appoints officials to replace elected representatives. Overriding the will expressed by the people through elections poses a serious problem for democratic representation. Strengthening local governments should not be seen solely as a demand of Kurds. This is an issue concerning Turkey's overall democratisation. The European Charter of Local Self-Government, which Turkey has signed, should also be reconsidered in this context.”


‘Freedom of expression and association is essential for democratic politics’


Lezgin Botan said a democratic solution cannot be achieved without freedom of expression and association, stressing that political normalisation requires guarantees for these rights. Botan said: “If we are talking about political normalisation, people must be able to express their views, organise and engage in political activities. Democratic politics cannot be strengthened as long as restrictions on political party activities, the right to assembly and demonstration, freedom of expression and freedom of association remain in place. The implementation of rulings by the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) and the Constitutional Court is also important. Under Article 90 of the Constitution, implementing international conventions and relevant court rulings is essential to strengthening the rule of law.”


‘Lasting social peace cannot be achieved without confronting the past’


Botan said the current dimensions of the Kurdish question cannot be considered separately from the past, drawing attention to the consequences of previous policies for collective memory.


Lezgin Botan continued: “We cannot assess the Kurdish question solely in terms of what is happening today. In the past, policies were implemented restricting the use of Kurdish identity and language in the public sphere. These policies had serious consequences for collective memory. The period of the Law on the Maintenance of Order must also be examined from this perspective. The Law on the Maintenance of Order was essentially a typical system of ethnic cleansing, particularly through demographic change. It is not easy to establish lasting social peace without confronting what happened in the past. A democratic solution also requires confronting historical memory.”


Botan said that alongside high expectations, a cautious approach persists among the Kurdish public, adding that this is also reflected in opinion polls. He said: “There are both considerable expectations and caution among the Kurdish public. People attach importance to the beginning of a process, but they do not want it to remain at the level of rhetoric, as happened in the past. A survey conducted by SAMER between 14 and 21 June 2026 among 908 people in 18 provinces found that 84 percent of respondents expected legal measures. This finding shows us that expectations among the Kurdish public are not limited to ending the conflict.


The findings of KONDA's 2025 surveys are also important to this discussion. We see that perceptions and expectations concerning the Kurdish question have changed among different sections of society. However, high expectations also increase the risk of disappointment. For this reason, concrete steps rather than rhetoric are needed in the process.”


‘Disarmament and democratisation must advance together’

title: Whereabouts of 5 Kurdish men arrested in Baneh remain unknown
content:
The fate of Hesen Mistefayî, Şerzad Çawşînî, Şahîn Reşîdzade, Xusrew Kerempûrî, and Muhyedîn Banerîzî, who were arrested by Iranian intelligence forces in Baneh, in Kurdistan Province, remains unknown.


According to information reported by the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN), Iranian intelligence forces raided the family home of Muhyedîn Banerîzî, a resident of Baneh, in the early hours of 9 October 2026, and arrested him.


Xusrew Kerempûrî, who also lives in Baneh, was detained on October 7 during a raid on his family’s home.


Hesen Mistefayî, a well-known philanthropist in the city, was arrested by Iranian intelligence forces on October 6 while taking his child to the hospital. It was reported that, following Mistefayî’s arrest, intelligence agents left his child alone on the street.


Şerzad Çawşînî, originally from Sardasht and residing in Baneh, and Şahîn Reşîdzade were also arrested by Iranian intelligence forces on October 3 and September 26, 2026, respectively.


According to the KHRN, all five men were arrested without court warrants. Since their arrests, no information has been made available regarding their whereabouts, health conditions, or legal proceedings.

title: Kariane Westrheim: A democratic solution to the Kurdish question would also benefit Turkish society
content:
Prof. Kariane Westrheim, President of the European Union Turkey Civic Commission (EUTCC), said that one of the most critical issues to be addressed at the 20th Kurdish Conference at the European Parliament this year would be the ongoing process in Turkey, stressing that this opportunity must not be missed.


We spoke with Prof. Kariane Westrheim of the University of Bergen in Norway about the 20th Kurdish Conference, which will take place at the European Parliament on 14–15 October. Westrheim explained the need that led to the establishment of the conference and reflected on developments over the past two decades. She also outlined the main topics of the 20th conference, identifying the Peace and Democratic Society Process underway in Turkey as the most critical issue. “We need to make use of this process. We must not miss this opportunity,” the EUTCC President said.


Drawing attention to Europe’s declining influence on and interest in Turkey, Westrheim emphasised: “Europe has often refrained from using its influence consistently on issues of democracy, human rights and the rule of law. This is regrettable.”


Professor Westrheim, this year you are organizing the 20th Kurdish Conference in Europe. Why and how did you feel the need to initiate and sustain such a conference?


First, I am not organising the conference alone, we are a good team of volunteers and friends who have been working all these years to keep the Kurdish question on the international agenda and particularly within the EU system and Europe. The idea came in 2004 with the foundation of the EU Turkey Civic Commission (EUTCC), four organisations decided to organise an international conference which became the annual International Conference on EU Turkey and the Kurds held in the European Parliament. It emerged from an obvious conviction: the Kurdish question is not only a question of human rights, democracy, and peace in the Middle East; it is also a European question. For decades, the situation of the Kurdish people has been characterised by conflict, repression, displacement, and political exclusion. At the same time, there has been a serious lack of understanding of the historical and political dimensions of the Kurdish question in Europe.


We felt that there was a need for a forum or a platform where politicians, academics, journalists, human rights defenders, and representatives of Kurdish civil society could meet, exchange views and discuss the situation openly. With these conferences we wanted to bring the Kurdish question into the European political debate. 


The fact that we have now reached the 20th conference is significant. It shows that the need for such a platform has not disappeared. On the contrary, despite all the changes in Turkey, Europe and the wider Middle East, the fundamental questions concerning democracy, human rights and a peaceful solution to the Kurdish question remain unresolved.


Since we are touching on this subject, what is the source of your own commitment to the Kurdish cause? How did you first become acquainted with the Kurdish people and their struggle?


My commitment to the Kurdish cause developed through my first encounters with the Kurdish freedom movement in 2002. Through that experience, I began to understand more deeply the complexity of the Kurdish question.


This eventually also became an academic subject for me. I wrote my PhD thesis on PKK and education, under the title

Education in a Political Context: a study of knowledge processes and learning sites in the PKK

. Through this work, I had the opportunity to study not only the political context in which the movement developed, but also the importance it placed on education, political consciousness through transformation and change, the development of individuals and society.


Over the years, I have worked closely with the movement and with people connected to it. That has given me an opportunity to learn a great deal - not only about the Kurdish question itself, but also about politics, education, organisation and the experiences of a people, in particular women, who have struggled for recognition and democratic rights under extremely difficult circumstances. 


My commitment has therefore developed through both academic work and personal experience. I have not simply studied the Kurdish question from a distance; I have had the opportunity to meet people, listen to their experiences, and follow their political and social struggle over the years …

title: Μικροφωνική συγκέντρωση για το κύκλωμα εμπορίας βρεφών στα Χανιά, Τρίτη 13/10, στις 19.00, στη πλ. Αγοράς
content:
Κάλεσμα από

Αγκίδες,

συλλογικότητα ενάντια στις έμφυλες καταπιέσεις & σε κάθε μορφή εξουσίας

:


Λίγα λόγια για το κύκλωμα εμπορίας βρεφών & εκμετάλλευσης ατόμων με μήτρα


Το χρονικό…


Τον Αύγουστο του 2023, αποκαλύπτεται ένα κύκλωμα «εμπορίας βρεφών, παράνομων υιοθεσιών και εκμετάλλευσης ατόμων με μήτρα» στην Κρήτη, με τη σύλληψη σχεδόν 10 ατόμων και την προφυλάκιση 4 εξ αυτών ως μέλη του. Στο επίκεντρο βρίσκεται η κλινική γονιμότητας και υποβοηθούμενης αναπαραγωγής «

Mediterranean Fertility Institute

», στην οδό Ζυμβρακάκηδων στο κέντρο των Χανίων. Μεταξύ των προφυλακιστέων βρίσκονται ο μαιευτήρας-γυναικολόγος και ιδιοκτήτης της κλινικής, Ιωάννης Γιακουμάκης, ο οποίος κατέχει αρχηγική θέση στο κύκλωμα, καθώς επίσης και ο εμβρυολόγος Διαμαντής (Danny) Δαφνής. Στο κύκλωμα εμπλέκονται ακόμα εργαζόμενοι του κέντρου, καθώς και γυναίκες που είχαν τον ρόλο των «μεσιτριών». Τόσο ο ιδιοκτήτης της κλινικής όσο και ο εμβρυολόγος αποφυλακίστηκαν στις αρχές Νοεμβρίου του 2025.


Τον Ιανουάριο του 2025, συλλαμβάνονται για την εμπλοκή τους στο κύκλωμα και ο διευθυντής της γυναικολογικής κλινικής του ΠΑΓΝΗ και καθηγητής του Πανεπιστημίου Κρήτης στο Ηράκλειο, Αντώνιος Μακρυγιαννάκης, και ακόμα ένας γυναικολόγος χειρούργος στα Χανιά. Μετά την απολογία τους αφήνονται ελεύθεροι με περιοριστικούς όρους και εγγυοδοσία 50.000 και 100.000 αντίστοιχα. Ο Μακρυγιαννάκης έκτοτε συνεχίζει να βρίσκεται στη θέση του και να εργάζεται κανονικά.


Η δράση του κυκλώματος ξεκινάει τουλάχιστον από το 2018, ενώ δεν περιορίζεται μόνο στην Κρήτη. Όπως διαπιστώνεται, το κύκλωμα διατηρούσε τρία γραφεία σε Χανιά, Θεσσαλονίκη και Ρουμανία που είχαν τον ρόλο της διαμεσολάβησης. Μέσω αυτών, δηλαδή, εντόπιζε και μετέφερε στην Ελλάδα φτωχές γυναίκες από την Ουκρανία, τη Ρουμανία, τη Βουλγαρία, τη Γεωργία, τη Μολδαβία και Ρομά, με σκοπό να τις εκμεταλλευτεί ως παρένθετες μητέρες ή δότριες ωαρίων. Καθ’ όλη τη διάρκεια της κύησης, οι γυναίκες ήταν έγκλειστες, υπό αυστηρή παρακολούθηση και αποκομμένες από το οικογενειακό-φιλικό περιβάλλον τους σε σπίτια-τρώγλες που μίσθωνε το κύκλωμα. Μετά τη γέννα, τα βρέφη δίνονταν παράνομα για υιοθεσία έναντι υψηλής αμοιβής. Υπολογίζεται ότι κοντά στις 200 γυναίκες έζησαν σε αυτό το καθεστώς, ενώ οι μισές περίπου είναι θύματα trafficking.


Παράλληλα, το κύκλωμα εξαπατούσε συστηματικά άτομα με μήτρα που απευθύνονταν στους συγκεκριμένους γιατρούς για εξωσωματική. Φαίνεται να προκύπτουν περίπου 400 περιπτώσεις, στις οποίες οι γιατροί ισχυρίζονταν ότι είχαν προχωρήσει σε εμβρυομεταφορά, ενώ στην πραγματικότητα ήταν απολύτως εικονική και το γενετικό υλικό που λάμβαναν το πουλούσαν σε άλλα ζευγάρια. Για να είναι, όμως, ακόμα πιο πειστικοί δεν δίσταζαν να τους χορηγούν βαριές ορμονοθεραπείες που συνιστώνται σε αυτές τις διαδικασίες.


Στις

14 Οκτωβρίου

 αναμένεται να ξεκινήσει η δίκη σε ειδικά διαμορφωμένη αίθουσα στο

ΜΑΙΧ

 (Μεσογειακό Αγρονομικό Ινστιτούτο Χανίων), με 33 κατηγορούμενους για 17 συνολικά κατηγορίες κακουργηματικού χαρακτήρα. Κάποιες από αυτές τις κατηγορίες αφορούν τη συγκρότηση και συμμετοχή σε εγκληματική οργάνωση, την εμπορία ανθρώπων, τις παράνομες διακινήσεις γενετικού υλικού (ωαρίων), τις παράνομες υιοθεσίες, τη μεσολάβηση σε υιοθεσία ανηλίκου, τις δωροληψίες και δωροδοκίες, τις παραβάσεις του νόμου περί υποβοηθούμενης αναπαραγωγής, την πλαστογράφηση, τις ψευδείς ιατρικές πιστοποιήσεις κ.α. Έχουν σημειωθεί 75 περιπτώσεις κλοπής ωαρίων και 592 εικονικές εμβρυομεταφορές -αριθμοί που προκύπτουν μόνο από τις καταγγελίες όσων τόλμησαν-, με τα κέρδη από τη δράση τους να ξεπερνούν τα 8,5 εκατομμύρια ευρώ.


Η υπόθεση του κυκλώματος εμπορίας βρεφών και εκμετάλλευσης ατόμων με μήτρα που αποκαλύφθηκε στα Χανιά δεν μπορεί να ιδωθεί μόνο ως μια υπόθεση οργανωμένου εγκλήματος, παράνομων υιοθεσιών ή παραβίασης της νομοθεσίας για την υποβοηθούμενη αναπαραγωγή. Αν σταθούμε μόνο εκεί, κινδυνεύουμε να δούμε την υπόθεση σαν μια εξαίρεση, ένα «άρρωστο» κύκλωμα που παραβίασε ένα κατά τα άλλα «ουδέτερο» σύστημα. Αντίθετα, πρόκειται για μια ιστορία που αναδεικνύει πώς συναντώνται η πατριαρχία, η ταξική ανισότητα, οι κρατικές-εθνικές πρακτικές, η βιοϊατρική, η τεχνολογία της αναπαραγωγής και η εμπορευματοποίηση του σώματος.


Ας ξεκινήσουμε από τα βασικά…


Ο καπιταλισμός βασίζεται, εκτός των άλλων, στην αναπαραγωγική εργασία των θηλυκοτήτων. Καθώς η καπιταλιστική οικονομία δεν στηρίζεται μόνο στην εργασία που παράγει εμπορεύματα, οι θηλυκότητες όχι μόνο πρέπει να παράγουν ανθρώπινο δυναμικό, αλλά είναι αυτές που θα πρέπει να …

title: Prosecution drops 3 articles vs Sara; impeachment narrows to ‘unexplained wealth’
content:
Bagong Alyansang Makabayan, however, said the denial of the chance to convict the Vice President on her misuse of confidential funds is a great disservice to the Filipino people, and a huge missed opportunity.


The House of Representatives (HOR) prosecution panel in the impeachment trial announced it is no longer pursuing alleged misuse of confidential funds, bribery, and grave threats charges against Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte.


In concluding their case on Tuesday, lead prosecutor and Representative Gerville Luistro asked the Impeachment Court it is only retaining the unexplained wealth case against alleging she amassed P817.87 million (Dh47.81 million) in undeclared assets and unexplained wealth from 2022 to 2025.


Dropped charges:


Article I (alleged misuse of confidential funds)


Article III (bribery)


Article IV (grave threats)


Retained charge:


Article II (accuses Duterte of amassing P817.87 million in allegedly undeclared assets and unexplained wealth from 2022 to 2025)


Luistro said the decision to drop the articles of impeachment was made to expedite the trial and narrow the scope of the proceedings, claiming that the prosecution panel is completely confident that the evidence presented for alleged unexplained wealth is substantial, compelling, and strong enough to stand on its own to secure a conviction and warrant removal from office.


Lead defense counsel Sheila Sison described the prosecution’s surprise move as “very strange,” adding it is unfair on Duterte to have been impeached under three charges only to be denied the chance to dispute the allegations on alleged misuse of confidential funds and grave threats in open court.


“It is too late for the prosecution to claim it just wants to save time when it has already spent 38 days [in open court],” Sison said.


Senator-Judge Alan Peter Cayetano manifested his support to the defense’s opposition, saying the respondent vice president should be given a chance to counter the allegations that have been made public.


Senator-Judge, meanwhile, Francis Pangilinan reminded that the Presiding Officer ruled as early as last July 15 that withdrawal is an option.


In his ruling, Presiding Judge and Senator-Judge Francis Escudero allowed the dropping of the three complaints, acknowledging it is the prosecution’s prerogative to do so.


He ordered the defense counsels to prepare for their arguments against charges of Duterte’s illegal wealth when the trial resumes on November 9.


What does this mean?


 

Bagong Alyansang Makabayan president Renato Reyes Jr., a complainant to one of the several impeachment charges against Duterte, said the withdrawal of three articles of impeachment and the retention of just one is obviously a way to shorten the impeachment proceedings and arrive at a judgement at the earliest time this year.


“If the Prosecution prefers a shortened trial, it probably means they are confident that the votes needed to convict have been somehow secured or that they are confident of securing such votes soon,” Reyes said.


Reyes, however, expressed regret that the impeachment court could no longer convict on Duterte’s misuse of public funds.


“[It is] a great disservice to the Filipino people, and a huge missed opportunity, that the Senate impeachment court will not rule on the Vice President’s misuse of confidential funds,” Reyes said.


Reyes said the complaint on misuse of public funds is where corruption is clearly established. With confidential funds still in use under the Ferdinand Marcos Jr. government, Duterte’s conviction on the issue would have been a blow against government corruption.

author: Wanessa Celina
title: Bancada indígena diminui no Congresso e lideranças se preparam para desmonte e retrocesso
content:
Investigamos o que importa para os brasileiros além do que passa na campanha eleitoral. Leia mais reportagens como essa clicando

aqui

.


Os cinco partidos com políticos que mais atuaram em pautas consideradas contrárias aos povos indígenas, segundo a plataforma do Conselho Indigenista Missionário (Cimi), vão ocupar 53 cadeiras no Senado Federal a partir de 2027. São eles o PL, o PP, o Republicanos, o União Brasil e o MDB. O PL conseguiu ocupar a maior bancada do Congresso Nacional, com 121 deputados e 28 senadores eleitos pelo partido. 


Como a

Agência Pública

 já

noticiou

, entre 2019 e 2026,

o PL foi o partido que mais votou e propôs propostas legislativas que ameaçavam os direitos dos povos originários

, segundo levantamento do Cimi. Luis Ventura, secretário-executivo do Conselho, vê a nova formação do Congresso Nacional como um perigo direto aos povos indígenas. 


Na avaliação de Ventura, no Senado, cinco partidos vão poder aprovar sozinhos alterações da Constituição que podem afetar diretamente os indígenas. Na Câmara dos Deputados, entretanto, mesmo em menor número, ainda se espera um campo de resistência, ainda que minoritário. “Há muitos outros parlamentares não indígenas que já aderiram, de forma sistemática, às pautas indígenas. Existe uma frente parlamentar mista de defesa dos direitos dos povos indígenas desde 2019 […] era uma frente parlamentar mista de mais de 150 parlamentares entre senadores e deputados”, explica Luís Ventura.


No Senado, nenhum dos 54 senadores eleitos se autodenomina indígena. Atualmente, na Casa, só dois parlamentares se identificam como indígenas: Wellington Dias (PT-PI) e o ex-vice-presidente de Jair Bolsonaro, Hamilton Mourão (Republicanos-RS), que adotou essa identidade nas eleições de 2022. 


Ventura explica que a presença de indígenas no Senado sempre foi mais difícil. “O Senado sempre foi uma Casa totalmente hermética para os povos indígenas e isso porque o sistema eleitoral no Brasil torna muito difícil conquistar uma vaga nesse lugar. As formas de colonialismo político nos estados são muito herméticas e,

se você perceber, dos 54 [senadores eleitos], salvando algumas exceções do campo da esquerda, estamos falando de pessoas que pertencem a um espectro político reacionário, conservador, fundamentalista, militarizado”

, acrescenta o secretário. 


Um Senado com baixa representatividade de povos indígenas, na visão do secretário executivo da Cimi, reforça um movimento que deve retroceder nas pautas centrais para essa população. “O objetivo deles vai ser impedir as demarcações, impor o Marco Temporal e abrir os territórios para a exploração econômica de terceiros. Esses são os grandes três objetivos dessa grande bancada reacionária que entrou no Senado”, prevê.


Indígenas ocuparão menos do 1% do Congresso Nacional


Ex-ministra dos povos indígenas do governo Lula, Sônia Guajajara se reelegeu deputada federal pelo PSOL


Os resultados do primeiro turno mostram que a presença de povos indígenas no Congresso Nacional ficará abaixo de 1% em 2027. Apenas duas das 45 candidaturas indígenas lançadas pela “Bancada do Cocar” foram eleitas no primeiro turno. 


A bancada é um movimento iniciado no Acampamento Terra Livre em 2017 e tentou eleger deputados e senadores indígenas para defender suas pautas. Para a

Pública

, a deputada federal Célia Xakriabá (PSOL-MG) reeleita para mais um mandato, afirma que o objetivo era eleger entre seis a oito parlamentares federais. Entre os 45 candidatos, apenas Sônia Guajajara (PSOL-SP), com 54.207 votos, e Juliana Cardoso (PT-SP), com 111.904 votos, conseguiram uma cadeira na Câmara. 


Outros 21 nomes, de vários locais do país e que participaram do projeto, conseguiram cargos de suplente. Entre todas as candidaturas, o único candidato da bancada do cocar que disputou um cargo majoritário, Isael Munduruku (Rede-AM), não conseguiu se eleger a governador do Amazonas. Ismael (Rede-AM), único candidato a senador do projeto, também não foi eleito.

author: radical.guide
title: What ICE watching actually involves
content:
ICE watching goes beyond standing on the street and observing where ICE is. Hotlines verify rumors ("Is ICE here or not?"), in Spanish and in other languages. Emergency cash assistance reaches families of the detained because a day or two or three in jail can derail someone's life. Education programs explain judicial warrants and when ICE needs a signed one to go into a place. Community watches sit alongside all of it.

title: Rede de Sementes da Teia dos Povos – no Quilombo da Ponte
content:
👉 Apoie pelo link: [apoia.se/teiadesementes]


Durante o 11º Encontro de Mulheres Negras e Quilombolas do Quilombo Engenho da Ponte, a Rede de Sementes da Teia dos Povos realizou mais uma entrega de sementes crioulas, fortalecendo a corrente de solidariedade entre territórios quilombolas da Bahia. Marinalva, que representava a comunidade anfitriã, agradeceu ao grupo do Apoia-se por fazer chegar às mãos do povo aquela semente que vai engrandecer a agricultura local. Ela destacou que quem deseja fazer parte e apoiar esse grupo será sempre bem-vindo.


As sementes foram entregues ao companheiro Mário Guerreiro, membro da associação quilombola, situada em Cachoeira, território vizinho da mesma região. Ele contou que estava sendo contemplado pelos contribuintes, pelas pessoas que participam doando sementes e doando o seu trabalho voluntário. Mário ressaltou que a doação serve tanto para ele quanto para toda a comunidade, porque planta quem tem vontade de cultivar o milho, e que a semente é saborosa, nutritiva e gostosa, um verdadeiro pertencimento partilhado.


Com esse apoio, a rede garantiu combustível para tratores, tratoritos e roçadeiras, manteve o calendário de plantio, produziu insumos para adubação agroecológica, assegurou a alimentação dos militantes que trabalham na ponta e garantiu os recursos necessários para levar sementes até os territórios em luta.


Graças a cada apoiador e apoiadora, mais de 1 tonelada de sementes crioulas foi produzida e distribuída para mais de 100 territórios de luta em todo o Brasil. Cada real doado germina em transformação real. Quem ainda não contribui pode se juntar a partir de R$ 2 por mês e ser um elo fundamental nessa corrente. Quem tem terra, semeia. Quem não tem, apoia. Ninguém fica para trás.

author: Leonardo Fernandes
title: Brazilian election exposes geopolitical struggle and US interference in Latin America
content:
The results of the first round of Brazil’s presidential election, which sent ultra-conservative Senator Flávio Bolsonaro of the Liberal Party and incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva of the Workers’ Party to a runoff scheduled for October 25, had immediate repercussions across Latin America.

The Brazilian election, in which Flávio Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of valid votes against Lula’s 45.16%, has become the epicenter of a regional geopolitical struggle that exposes the alignment of far-right leaders with Washington’s agenda versus the progressive governments defending continental sovereignty.

Leaders from Latin America’s progressive camp reacted with both caution and resolution, denouncing the risks of social regression and submission to US interests.

Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum emphasised the need to wait for the final runoff results before offering any definitive assessment of regional geopolitics. When asked if a potential victory for Bolsonaro would leave the Mexican government without allies in Latin America, Sheinbaum downplayed the potential friction with the ultraconservative figure.

“Our main ally is the people of Mexico; as long as we remain close to the people, representing them and governing by and for the people, there will be no problem whatsoever,” Sheinbaum said during her daily press conference.

Meanwhile, former Colombian president Gustavo Petro criticised the rhetoric of local right-wing factions and denounced interference by the Donald Trump administration in Latin America. Petro emphasised that the brief periods of progressive and humanist governments reduced the region’s historic social inequality. He said that Washington’s strategy seeks to destroy sovereignty and foster political instability.

“President Donald Trump decided to accept [Secretary of State] Marco Rubio’s proposal and prioritise an agenda of destroying progressivism over the agenda of combating drug trafficking; it is worth remembering that progressive ideas lie at the origin of all American republics, including that of the USA,” Petro wrote.

“The consequence of Donald Trump’s policy will be increased social and economic inequality, as well as a rise in drug trafficking, violence, and northward migration. For the people of Latin America whose elections have been rigged by the direct interference of a foreign government, there is no alternative but rebellion,” Petro argued.

Among conservative and far-right leaders, the vote was met with an atmosphere of euphoria and celebration.

Argentine President Javier Milei took to social media to celebrate the results in Brazil, describing the election as historic and calling Lula a “communist leftist”. Milei once again championed the US ultraconservative movement by citing the acronym MAGA, shorthand for Trump’s slogan “Make America Great Again”.

“A communist leftist loses to a right-winger, and the markets celebrate with sharp gains … Impoverishing leftists, get out of the way, for we are trying to make the continent shine,” Milei wrote on X.

In another post, the Argentine president stated that “freedom is advancing in Brazil”.

“Congratulations, dear friend Flávio Bolsonaro, on this historic election against the communist Lula,” posted Milei, who is facing a severe crisis of popularity amid the skyrocketing poverty rate among the Argentine population.

In the same vein, Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella stated that the true meaning of change lies in defeating the left, publicly expressing his support for the pro-Bolsonaro candidate.

“Today my heart is with Brazil; may God have mercy on this sister nation, just as He did with Colombia. True change is defeating the left,” wrote Espriella. “A big hug, my friend Flávio Bolsonaro. Stand firm for the Fatherland!” posted the Colombian president, concluding his message with a salute to Cristo Rey.

Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado also celebrated the election results, linking Bolsonaro’s performance to the effort to defeat communism in the region. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu joined in the congratulations and expressed a desire to restore priority diplomatic ties with Brazil under a potential right-wing government.

“My respect and affection go to the people of Brazil for an exemplary democratic process, in which they were able to proudly exercise popular sovereignty through the vote. My recognition goes to Flávio Bolsonaro, the winner of this first round,” the Venezuelan …

author: dev
title: Cinéastes de notre temps
content:
C'est visible partout, la jeunesse a pris la rue et la parole. Une nouvelle génération rejoint celle de 2016 dans la détestation de la police et sur les chemins de la révolte. L'époque est toujours aux acharnés. Pour ce premier épisode de

Cinéastes de notre temps

 nous passerons

l'Époque

 de Matthieu Bareyre (2019) dans une version un peu différente de ce qui a été diffusé au cinéma et en festival. Bref, le vrai « director's cut » comme on dit.


Il est parfois difficile d'extraire ce qui mérite d'être vu parmi les milliers de productions cinématographiques dont nous sommes abreuvés. Les films sont jetables comme n'importe quelles autres marchandises. Le cinéma peut être une place forte contre le spectacle seulement si nous sommes en mesure de défendre une culture critique.


« Je voudrais que

Cinéastes de notre temps

 soit une émission de laboratoire pour la création d'un nouveau langage ... Pour moi, cette émission poursuit un ensemble de réflexions sur le matériau filmique et sur la manière dont le sens peut ou non s'en emparer ».


(André S. Labarthe.

Cinéma 69

, 140, novembre 1969.)


Régulièrement, nous proposerons sur

lundimatin

des films


gratuits et en streaming pendant une semaine,


accompagnés d'un entretien avec leurs cinéastes.


« L'idée était de mettre un réalisateur face à un autre réalisateur, qu'il soit mort ou vivant – même si on s'est vite aperçus que la rencontre avec les vivants présentait un plus vif intérêt. » (

Entretiens avec André S. Labarthe,

Thierry Lounas, Capricci 2011)


Notre époque est riche en soulèvements, en bouleversements, en évènements. Elle se caractérise par la mise en images et en sons, en cinéma, de ceux-ci. Nous irons à la rencontre des cinéastes qui ont été fidèles à un événement et qui ont fait du cinéma un lieu de son expression. Nous chercherons des films qui vont vers la rencontre et le dehors. Un cinéma dans lequel la vie se multiplie et qui invente de nouveaux désirs.


A rebours de la tyrannie de l'actualité et de la publicité, mais aussi contre toute nostalgie, nous essayerons de proposer ici une sélection de films « actuels » qui font l'épreuve du temps. C'est à dire que par leur puissance visionnaire, nous parions qu'ils ne s'useront pas.


Episode 1 :

 L'Époque

 de Matthieu Bareyre (2019)


Entre l'après-Charlie de 2015, Nuit debout en 2016 jusqu'aux élections présidentielles de 2017, des jeunes de tout horizons prennent la parole au hasard des rencontres nocturnes dans Paris. Sous-titre : « regarde ta jeunesse dans les yeux ». Un film en hommage à « ceux qui ne dorment pas : leurs rêves, leurs cauchemars, l'ivresse, la douceur, l'ennui, les larmes, la teuf, le taf, les terrasses, les vitrines, les pavés, les parents, le désir, l'avenir, l'amnésie. »

L'époque

 c'est une génération qui se raconte à travers des visages en gros plans, autant de pairs d'yeux, à travers une multitude de mondes hétérogènes et communicants réunis par le film dans leur confrontation commune avec le monde

tel qu'il est

. L'époque c'est une communauté temporelle, un cocktail Molotov de sensibilités connectés ensemble par la parole, l'intelligence collective et le montage.


A venir lundi prochain :


Épisode 2 :

Boum Boum,

Laurie Lassalle, 2022. (En streaming).


Entretien croisé - Matthieu Bareyre & Laurie Lassalle


@Marion Siéfert


Pour toutes propositions, écrire à

dimanchepm@riseup.net

title: La Palestine en procès. Autour du livre de Rafik Chekrat
content:
Rendez-vous le 18 octobre à 15h à Ivry-sur-Seine (2 rue Robespierre)


Présentation du livre «

 

La Palestine en procès

 

» par l'auteur Rafik Chekkat, suivie d'une vente-dédicace du livre qui paraît le 16 octobre et d'un repas.


Rafik Chekkat est notamment avocat spécialisé dans les questions de discrimination et des libertés fondamentales.


Il vous présentera son ouvrage et répondra à la question : «

 

Peut-on encore défendre la Palestine librement en France

 

?

 

».


Il vous fera part de son témoignage et de son analyse sur la répression juridique et la criminalisation de la solidarité envers la Palestine, à partir de son expérience des deux dernières années, période durant laquelle il a eu à plaider pour défendre les droits des militants de la cause palestinienne, et notamment des militants d'Urgence Palestine


Depuis qu'il a repris le chemin des prétoires en 2024, les dossiers s'accumulent en effet. Les convocations pleuvent. Les procédures se multiplient. À chaque audience, ce sont les mêmes infractions qui reviennent : apologie du terrorisme, incitation à la haine. À chaque fois en cause : la dénonciation des bombardements à Gaza ou l'expression d'une solidarité.


Ce livre s'appuie sur les affaires, les visages et les trajectoires qui font la réalité de cette Palestine en procès. On y voit se dessiner l'avenir de nos démocraties : la restriction des libertés publiques, la banalisation des dispositifs d'exception et la difficulté croissante à tolérer des formes de dissidence qui remettent en cause les récits établis.


L'écrasement de Gaza au miroir de la justice française.


Ce qui nous amène à lui poser la question : «

 

Pourquoi la dénonciation des crimes commis en Palestine suscite-t-elle aujourd'hui autant de controverses, de pressions et de tentatives de répression

 

?

 

»


Ce débat sera clôturé par un repas.

author: Unknown
title: LE SOLARISME COMME PRATIQUE DE COHÉRENCE
content:
Le Solarisme parle d'émerveillement. Le moment où un photon devient électron dans un panneau n'est pas seulement technique : c'est le moment où l'étoile qui soutient la vie devient travail humain sans destruction.


Per Lubio Lenin Cardozo


Le Solarisme n'est pas une technologie. C'est une pratique de cohérence.


Nous vivons dans une culture fossile. Même quand nous posons des panneaux solaires, nous continuons de penser en mode fossile : énergie centralisée, propriétaire, consommée sans limite, administrée par quelques-uns.


Le Solarisme propose de changer non seulement la source, mais la géométrie du pouvoir qui se cache derrière la source.


1. De la géométrie concentrée à la géométrie distribuée


La culture fossile est une géométrie concentrée : quelques puits, quelques mines, quelques raffineries, quelques propriétaires qui contrôlent la captation, la propriété et l'administration de l'énergie de milliards de personnes.


La culture solaire est une géométrie distribuée : des millions de points de captation, de réparation, de réutilisation, de propriété communautaire. Des toits, des balcons, des jardins agrivoltaïques, du verre solaire transparent.


La question n'est pas seulement «

 

d'où vient l'énergie

 

?

 

» mais «

 

qui possède le panneau

 

? Qui le répare

 

? Qui décide

 

?

 

»


2.

INTERLUDE

 : Objection - Le solaire n'est-il pas lui-même extractiviste

 

? De la première à la seconde géométrie


Un panneau solaire et une batterie lithium ne tombent pas du ciel. Ils nécessitent silicium, lithium, cuivre, cobalt. Donc, oui, dans sa première géométrie, le solaire peut reproduire de l'extractivisme. C'est ce que nous appelons la culture fossile avec des panneaux solaires.


Le Solarisme ne dit pas : «

 

posez des panneaux et le problème est résolu

 

». Le Solarisme dit : L'extractivisme n'est pas une technologie, c'est une géométrie.


Géométrie concentrée = quelques mines au Congo/Chili, quelques usines en Chine, quelques propriétaires en Europe qui contrôlent la captation. Peu importe si c'est du pétrole ou du soleil, si la géométrie est concentrée, le résultat est extractif.


Géométrie distribuée = des millions de points de captation, de réparation, de réutilisation, de propriété communautaire.


Un panneau propriétaire Tesla + batterie propriétaire qui finit à la décharge en 8 ans = extractivisme solaire.


Un panneau en open hardware, réparable localement, en propriété communautaire, couplé à une culture de la suffisance et non de la consommation illimitée = pratique de cohérence.


Ce n'est pas le panneau qui change la société, c'est le passage de consommateur à producteur-administrateur-décideur d'une partie de son énergie.


Et c'est là que la critique de la question nous aide : comment produire des panneaux à faible extractivisme, durables 30 ans, réparables, recyclables

 

? C'est le vrai chantier de la seconde géométrie.


3. Le Sujet Énergétique : de consommateur à Solarian


Le passage central du Solarisme est de devenir Sujet Énergétique.


Le consommateur achète de l'énergie qu'il ne comprend pas, produite ailleurs par d'autres.


Le Solarian (Sujet Énergétique) capte, administre, partage et décide d'une partie de son énergie.


C'est une pratique de cohérence entre ce que nous pensons et ce que nous faisons avec l'énergie.


4. Quelle humanité pouvons-nous devenir

 

?


Si l'énergie devient un bien commun comme un jardin, que faisons-nous du temps libéré

 

?


Le Solarisme répond : Cuidar (prendre soin), Crear (créer), Contemplar (contempler).


Une communauté intergénérationnelle qui peint avec la lumière holographique solaire, qui répare ses outils, qui partage son pain, qui médite.


L'énergie n'est plus une marchandise. Elle redevient ce qu'elle a toujours été : la condition de la vie.


Lubio Lenin Cardozo - Toronto


Solarisme : pratique de cohérence pour une seconde géométrie.


Si le Solarisme aide l'humanité à vivre en paix avec elle-même et avec la Terre, c'est une bonne pratique. Le soleil n'attend pas, et les pauvres non plus.

title: Une île et une nuit : un film qui donne envie de lutter et de faire des films
content:
Retour à Paname du film des Pirates des Lentillères, la fiction collective fabriquée entre 2021-2023 par les occupant-es et passagèr-es du Quartier Libre des Lentillères à Dijon.


Parce qu'on a besoin de créer nos propres imaginaires des luttes,


parce que le cinéma de fiction n'est pas réservé à l'industrie,


parce que la lutte peut être joyeuse malgré les tempêtes...


que vivent les films pirates et collectifs

 

!


Une île et une nuit


Un film des Pirates des Lentillères : 2021-2023, 1h40, onze langues différentes, sans sous-titres, tous publics


Projection vendredi 16 octobre 2026 à 20h


au Shakirail : 72 rue Riquet 75018, M° Marx Dormoy, Riquet, La Chapelle


prix libre


La projection sera suivie d'une discussion qui sera notamment l'occasion de parler de l'actualité pas forcément réjouissante des Lentillères, des menaces qui pèsent sur elles, et de questionner la volonté de «

 

péréniser

 

» des lieux à tout prix et de ses conséquences sur la lutte.


Synopsis

 : Autour du feu, voyageurs et pirates se racontent leurs souvenirs, leurs rêves, leurs batailles. D'une langue à l'autre, de récit en récit se font entendre le grondement de la tempête et le bruissement des feuilles, les sirènes menaçantes et les danses endiablées, le choc des sabres et le chant des oiseaux. Jusqu'à l'aube se dessinent mille et un chemins de cette île imaginaire mais pourtant bien réelle.


Contexte

 : Une île et une nuit est un film de fiction réalisé collectivement entre 2021 et 2023 par les habitant-es et usagèr-es du Quartier Libre des Lentillères, lieu squatté et autogéré s'étendant sur les dernières terres maraîchères de la ville de Dijon.


Ces 8 hectares ont été occupés et remis en culture depuis 2010, en résistance à un projet d'«

 

écocité

 

» en béton qui les menace encore aujourd'hui. Au milieu de la ville, ces espaces en friche et ces maisons abandonnées se sont transformées en un quartier autogéré aux multiples usages, faisant s'entremêler habitat collectif, maraîchage, jardinage, auto-construction, événements festifs et culturels, etc. C'est un lieu de luttes et de solidarités en tous genres ainsi qu'une véritable réserve de biodiversité.


Dans ce film nous utilisons le prisme de l'imaginaire pour parler du réel, de ce que nous vivons ici, de comment nous y sommes arrivé-es, de ce que nous y cherchons et de contre quoi nous nous battons chaque jour. C'est une fiction musicale et dansée, sans héros ni héroïne, avec des maisons qui sont des bateaux (et inversement), des pirates de toutes sortes et tout plein de langages différents... Bref, le Quartier Libre des Lentillères c'est une île aux trésors à travers le regard du cinéma

 

!


Auto-produit, auto-diffusé, basé sur la participation bénévole, ce film tourné sur pellicule argentique 16mm s'est construit au fil de la vie du lieu, en corrélation avec celle-ci, au rythme des événements et des saisons. De l'écriture au montage en passant par le tournage, chaque étape a été collective et participative, dans une démarche de partage de savoir-faire ouverte à tou-tes.


NB

 : le film est uniquement visible lors de projections publiques accompagnées.


 Site du film :

https://www.piratesdeslentilleres.net/

author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: Groups decry military threats vs activist, media worker in Palawan
content:
Catagupan, Balabac, Palawan. Screengrab from Google Earth.

A network of alternative media organizations denounced the alleged intimidation experienced by a student leader and a media worker while conducting fieldwork at the Indigenous Molbog community in Barangay Catagupan, Balabac, Palawan.

In a statement, the People’s Alternative Media Network (Altermidya) stressed that no journalist or media worker should face intimidation, surveillance, or threats to life for doing their work. “These reported threats are grave and unacceptable.”

On October 8, Brent Sumague of the League of Filipino Students (LFS) Southern Tagalog and Marky Casaquite of Southern Tagalog Exposure, a member-organization of Altermidya, allegedly received threatening remarks from a certain Xyron Aliño who reportedly introduced himself as a personnel of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) Western Command.

The alleged intimidation happened after local authorities trooped to the focus group discussion and consultation activity of Sumague and Casaquite with Molbog community members. The two went to the area as part of a documentary they wanted to produce about the possible effects of Super El Niño on Indigenous peoples, as well as the impact of alleged land grabbing linked to the establishment of the military site in Balabac town under the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA) between the Philippines and the United States.

The Philippine National Police (PNP) Balabac was reportedly part of the operating team. It released a statement debunking the allegations of harassment.

Sumague told Bulatlat that two individuals who introduced themselves as administrative staff of the Barangay Catagupan government brought them and other Molbog community members to the barangay hall, questioning the activity’s objective. The said barangay staff, he said, told them that the gathering of Indigenous peoples requires prior notice to the barangay.

“This was not new to Indigenous peoples since they have been told several times that gathering has been prohibited,” Sumague said in Filipino.

Julius Abubakar, administrative staff of the Barangay Catagupan government, said in a public Facebook post that the barangay’s action, in coordination with AFP and PNP, stemmed from the lack of coordination by Sumague and Casaquite as they conducted a meeting without prior notice.

He said that it is prohibited to conduct a pagtitipon (gathering) in the barangay, especially if the initiators are from other provinces.

“A prior notice from the barangay is not needed. A focus group discussion is a legal activity and covered by the constitutional right to free expression. The barangay has no power to impose such a requirement,” human rights lawyer Ephraim Cortez told Bulatlat when asked for a comment.

Sumague said that the activity was conducted at the Molbog Tribal Hall and it was attended by around 20 community members.

Human rights alliance Karapatan criticized local authorities for not allowing Sumague and Casaquite to stay in the community overnight. The LFS member told Bulatlat that they were on board the police mobile patrol and brought to a boarding house allegedly recommended by the police.

“It is equally unconscionable for the police and military to harass and threaten people who want to get the facts on the ground about the impact on the masses of both natural disasters like El Niño and man-made disasters like militarization to protect US interests,” Cristina Palabay, Karapatan secretary-general, said in a statement.

Altermidya expressed concerns about the situation of the concerned Indigenous community. “Communities must be free to speak to journalists, raise grievances, and express their views without fear of retaliation, surveillance, or harassment.”

The group called for an immediate and transparent investigation of the alleged threats attributed to AFP Western Command personnel, urging government authorities to guarantee the safety of journalists.

For Southern Tagalog Exposure, these alleged acts of intimidation violate the right to inform the public on issues faced by local communities and are attempts to stifle press freedom. (DAA)

author: Dominic Gutoman
title: US intensifies sanctions vs. ICC
content:
Philippine-based and international human rights organizations condemned the sanctions imposed by the United States (US) against the International Criminal Court (ICC), citing adverse impacts to poor countries.

The US sanctions, declared on October 9 by State Secretary Marco Rubio, bans transactions with the court to paralyze its resources and its ability to operate. The sanctions impose legal, financial, and travel restrictions to certain individuals and institutions.

“The Court will continue to fully discharge its mandate, with independence and impartiality, acting only on the basis of the law and the evidence, for the sake of the countless victims of grave crimes” said ICC President Tomoko Akane, urging state parties and the international community to stand against the obstruction of justice.

The administration of Donald Trump has previously sanctioned 13 prosecutors and judges of ICC, three Palestinian human rights organizations, and the United Nations special rapporteur on human rights in the Occupied Palestinian Territory Francesca Albanese. The sanctions escalated after the ICC looked into war crimes committed by US troops in Afghanistan in 2018 up to the ongoing genocide of the US and Israel in Palestine.

Read: US sanctions vs. ICC hinders victims’ quest for justice

“Such attacks on institutions that prosecute US and Israeli officials and troops committing war crimes and genocide are utterly condemnable,” said Cristina Palabay, secretary-general of Karapatan.

Former ICC Judge Raul Pangalangan, who chairs the independent Philippine Truth Commission, said that the Filipino families who suffered in Rodrigo Duterte’s so-called “drug war” will feel the impacts directly. “Victims’ lawyers have to be paid, and witnesses who fly to The Hague need protection when they come home. None of that happens if the money stops. A mother from a poor neighborhood in Manila, who has waited years to tell the court what happened to her son, may never get the chance.”

The ICC is prosecuting the case of former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte. The ICC Pre-Trial Chamber I found reasonable grounds to believe that Duterte is responsible as an indirect co-perpetrator for the crimes against humanity of murder when he was Davao City Mayor and, later on, President of the Philippines. His trial will start on November 30.

Read: Timeline: ICC case against Rodrigo Duterte

“The governments that pushed for these sanctions will hardly notice them. Victims in poorer countries, for whom this court is often the only place left to turn, will feel the impact right away,” Pangalangan added.

On October 8, The ICC Trial Chamber III released the public redacted version of their decision, declaring that Duterte is fit to stand trial based on the assessment of independent medical experts. The ICC also adopted measures for his participation in his trial.

Palabay condemned the Marcos Jr. administration for its repeated refusal to re-ratify the Rome Statute, calling the position an opportunistic stance.

“Although Ferdinand Marcos Jr. is so far benefiting from the ICC’s detention, investigation and prosecution of his political rival Rodrigo Duterte, the ICC’s task of going after war criminals puts Marcos Jr. in danger of being in the ICC’s crosshairs someday,” Palabay said. “He has not issued any strongly worded statements in support of the US position, but being a US lackey, it is only a matter of time before he echoes Trump’s vociferous attacks on the ICC.”

Human Rights Watch, Open Society Institute, American Friends Service Committee, and Center for Constitutional Rights filed a lawsuit in the US federal court seeking to have the sanctions struck down.

“The Trump administration has made clear its aim to destroy the ICC to shield US and Israeli officials from facing charges before the court. The ICC was created to ensure that no one, no matter how powerful, is above the law,” said Philippe Bolopion, executive director of Human Rights Watch. “Governments that value human rights and accountability should condemn this outrageous move and take swift action to protect the ICC, its staff, and all those who cooperate with it, starting with the European Union using its laws to mitigate the sanctions’ impact in the region.” (RTS, DAA)

author: Brian Hioe
title: Why Would Chiang Wan-an Propose Replacing Songshan Airport with an “AI Park”?
content:
IN AN UNUSUAL proposal, Taipei mayor Chiang Wan-an has proposed replacing Songshan Airport with an AI park. Chiang claims that this AI park would involve not only technological facilities, but also greenery and residential areas.

This is not the first time such a proposal has been made. In the past, DPP political candidates such as Lee Ying-yuan in 2002, Frank Hsieh in 2006, and Enoch Wu in 2022 have made similar proposals to move Songshan Airport and to replace it with a park.

Nevertheless, the central government has rejected such proposals in the past, citing security concerns. High-level officials usually travel from Taiwan to other countries through Songshan Airport, as do foreign dignitaries. Songshan Airport also serves some functions for the Taiwanese military, as it is guarded by it because of the view that the Chinese military would seek to capture it in the event of an invasion. Located in downtown Taipei, Songshan Airport is the smaller airport that serves Taipei besides Taoyuan International Airport. Unlike Taoyuan International Airport, it is located inside the city rather than outside of it.

Flights to Taiwan’s outlying islands are usually serviced outside of Songshan Airport. In recent years, short-range flights to Japan and South Korea have also operated from Songshan Airport. Indeed, it is hard to imagine that residents of Taiwan’s outlying islands would be pleased about having to travel outside of Taipei in order to travel from and to home.

Ironically, Chiang’s proposal runs counter to the interests of other KMT candidates. KMT New Taipei mayoral candidate Lee Shu-chuan currently calls for increasing connections between New Taipei and Songshan Airport. When asked about the impact on Kinmen residents, KMT legislator Chen Yu-chen downplayed the potential conflict between the interests of her constituency and Taipei residents. Apart from facilitating travel, Songshan Airport plays an important role in medical evacuations from outlying islands of Taiwan that lack the medical capacity that the Taiwanese mainland has.

Chiang would probably be reaching for proposals to make his campaign appear as though it has more vision, instead of seeking reelection. Though Chiang was expected to handily win the Taipei mayoral race, it has proved surprising that he has faced an upstart challenge from legislator Puma Shen of the DPP. Shen has distinguished himself with his number of policy proposals, while attacking Chiang as lacking any vision for governance.

Nevertheless, the proposal may be short-sighted and ultimately open him to the criticism that he is simply grasping for ideas. For one, an AI park in the middle of Taipei would be costly and consume significant water and electricity resources, as well as increase real estate prices, even if it proves common for politicians to call for the establishment of tech parks in their constituencies, with the claim that this will create high-tech jobs.

Chiang has also been accused in the past, in a conspiratorial manner, of cutting trees across the city so as to make it easier for Chinese drone incursions. That dismantling the Songshan Airport would have security concerns for Taiwan will likely lead to further allegations against Chiang that he makes political proposals that could benefit a Chinese invasion.

title: 15 de octubre. Florentino Iglesias presenta ‘Gastón Leval. Una visión heterodoxa del anarquismo’
content:
CAMBIO DE FECHA

 (iba a ser el viernes 16)


El investigador

Florentino Iglesias

 estará presentando, en la sede de la FAL en Madrid, el libro

Gastón Leval. Una visión heterodoxa del anarquismo

. Será el

jueves, 15 de octubre, a las 19:00

, en compañía de

Juan Merino

, presidente de la Fundación Anselmo Lorenzo.


Charlaremos con Florentino, quien nos sumergirá en esta

figura clave en la historia del anarcosindicalismo español

, responsable, entre otras tareas, de viajar al congreso fundacional de la

III Internacional de Sindicatos en Moscú en 1921

, donde coincidiría con

Emma Goldman y Alexander Berkman

 para exigir a

Lenin

 la

liberación de los anarquistas rusos encarcelados

.


GASTÓN LEVAL, seudónimo de Pierre Robert Pillar (1895 – 1978), fue un anarcosindicalista francés, combatiente e historiador de la Revolución Social española. Hijo de un comunero francés, huyó a España en 1915 para evadir el servicio militar ingresando en la CNT, organización por la que luego sería nombrado delegado adjunto al congreso fundacional de la III Internacional de Sindicatos en Moscú en 1921. Allí coincidiría con Emma Goldman y Alexander Berkman para exigir a Lenin la liberación de los anarquistas rusos encarcelados. Posteriormente, la CNT se pronunciará por la ruptura de los lazos con los bolcheviques.


Más tarde se retiró a Argentina durante la dictadura de Primo de Rivera, donde viviría de 1923 a 1936, retornando a España para documentar la revolución y las colectividades anarquistas urbanas y rurales.


Ideológicamente, destacó en la década de los veinte como anarquista intransigente y puro, pero con el tiempo modulará sus planteamientos, proponiendo un anarquismo que ponga en valor el aspecto económico, defendiendo la superioridad de las federaciones de industria sobre la comuna. Durante las jornadas de Mayo del 68 participó activamente en los debates universitarios, defendiendo las posiciones libertarias contra las marxistas. Siempre mantendrá un fuerte contacto con los círculos libertarios del exilio español.


Leval propondrá una «interpretación libertaria de la historia» como contrapeso al materialismo histórico marxista. Iniciará una revisión sobre los grandes problemas que plantea el anarquismo, rechazando encuadrar a éste dentro de esquemas cerrados, y alejándose de interpretaciones simplistas.

¿Horario?

¿Dónde?

 Sede de la FAL en Madrid

author: Alfredo Seguel
title: Masiva movilización global en apoyo a Palestina exige poner fin al genocidio
content:
La Jornada Global por Palestina movilizó a decenas de miles de personas en más de 60 países al cumplirse tres años del inicio de la ofensiva en Gaza. Londres concentró 250,000 asistentes; Santiago marchó por la Alameda con miles de personas. Argentina, México, Perú, Francia,  Uruguay,  también fueron parte, como referencias de los países movilizados, de la protesta mundial.


Una jornada mundial contra el genocidio


Miles de personas salieron a las calles en más de 60 países entre el 9 y el 11 de octubre para exigir el fin de la ofensiva israelí en Gaza, al cumplirse tres años del inicio del conflicto.


La Global Alliance for Palestine (GAFP) convocó la jornada internacional bajo la consigna “Poner fin al genocidio, defender la tierra”, con marchas, protestas estudiantiles y acciones en lugares de trabajo que involucraron a más de 200 organizaciones. Las demandas centrales incluyen el embargo de armas a Israel, el endurecimiento de sanciones y la suspensión de acuerdos comerciales.


Londres: 250.000 personas y al menos 20 detenidos


En el centro de Londres, miles de personas se congregaron para expresar su apoyo a los palestinos tras tres años de “genocidio”, según consignó The Guardian en crónica de Sammy Gecsoyler.


Los manifestantes, muchos con kufiyas y banderas palestinas, marcharon hacia el Parlamento con pancartas de «Fin al genocidio» y «Palestina libre». La policía metropolitana informó de al menos 20 detenciones.


Los organizadores cifraron la asistencia en 250.000 personas. El embajador palestino en el Reino Unido, Husam Zomlot, compartió un video de la marcha: «Tres años después, las atrocidades de Israel en Gaza y Cisjordania continúan, al igual que la solidaridad del pueblo británico. Más fuerte, más grande y para siempre. Gracias a todos».


The Guardian detalla que es la primera marcha nacional desde que el canciller Ed Miliband anunciara sanciones al comercio con los asentamientos israelíes y declarara que la ocupación israelí de Cisjordania es ilegal en su totalidad. Aimee Shalan, directora de la Palestine Solidarity Campaign, declaró a AFP: «Estamos aquí hoy para conmemorar tres años del genocidio en curso en Gaza», y pidió «sanciones plenas contra Israel».


La movilización puede verse aquí:


Santiago: la Alameda se llena de solidaridad


En Santiago de Chile, organizaciones estudiantiles, sociales y sindicales convocaron una marcha que partió pasado el mediodía desde Metro Universidad Católica y avanzó hasta Los Héroes. La manifestación fue organizada por Solidaridad por Palestina Universidad de Chile y la Federación de Estudiantes de la Universidad de Chile (FECh), con adhesión de agrupaciones sindicales, organizaciones sociales y la comunidad palestina en Chile.


La presidenta de la FECh, Laura Mlynarz, señaló: «La solidaridad internacional es relevante en un contexto como el que nos encontramos hoy día, un contexto donde EEUU quiere que Latinoamérica vuelva a ser su patio trasero».


Algunas imágenes de las movilizaciones en Chile (TRT)


Otras ciudades del mundo se suman a la protesta


Previamente a la jornada global, también tuvo expresiones en Argentina, donde cientos de personas marcharon bajo la lluvia en Buenos Aires con banderas palestinas, según un reporte de HispanTV conducido por Sebastián Salgado:


En México, la convocatoria partió del Ángel de la Independencia hacia la Plaza Palestina Libre, frente al Hemiciclo a Juárez.


En Perú, colectivos estudiantiles y organizaciones de derechos humanos marcharon en Lima para presionar al Gobierno a romper relaciones diplomáticas y comerciales con Israel, según Wayka Perú. Los organizadores peruanos advirtieron: «No queremos que el Perú siga el camino de Argentina, donde Milei ha llegado al extremo de declarar a Argentina como ‘la nueva tierra prometida de Israel’, poniendo al país al servicio de un proyecto genocida». Estas expresiones se sumaron a las movilizaciones de Londres y Santiago como parte de una misma jornada global.


Ver manifestaciones en Montevideo


Manifestación en Lima 


Un alto el fuego frágil y una crisis humanitaria persistente

author: Alfredo Seguel
title: Chile: Alertan que las nuevas Reglas del Uso de la Fuerza “no cumplen estándares de derechos humanos” y advierte “margen excesivo”
content:
Amnistía Internacional Chile advirtió que las Reglas del Uso de la Fuerza (RUF), aprobadas el 7 de octubre tras la muerte de dos policías, no cumplen estándares internacionales de derechos humanos. Su director, Rodrigo Bustos Bottai, criticó la ausencia de proporcionalidad, rendición de cuentas y prohibiciones esenciales, advirtiendo un mayor riesgo de abusos, especialmente en manifestaciones.


“Dejan a la ciudadanía en mayor desprotección”: Amnistía cuestiona la RUF aprobada  y advierte un “margen excesivo”


El reciente fallecimiento de dos policías aceleró la aprobación del proyecto de ley sobre las Reglas del Uso de la Fuerza (RUF) que llevaba en tramitación desde hace más de tres años.

 El 7 de octubre,  el texto fue aprobado por la Cámara de Diputados y Diputadas y posteriormente por el Senado. Al respecto, Rodrigo Bustos Bottai, director ejecutivo de Amnistía Internacional Chile, ha dicho:

“Las reglas tal como han sido aprobadas no cumplen con los estándares internacionales de derechos humanos.

Es preocupante que no contemplen adecuadamente principios fundamentales como la proporcionalidad y la rendición de cuentas, y que se hayan debilitado referencias esenciales a la prohibición de la tortura y de protección de grupos de especial protección como niñas, niños y adolescentes. Estas deficiencias abren la puerta a que puedan repetirse graves violaciones de derechos humanos, otorgando un margen excesivo de actuación a las policías y las Fuerzas Armadas y dejando a la ciudadanía en una situación de mayor desprotección

”.


Las Reglas del Uso de la Fuerza establecen las condiciones y límites bajo los cuales las policías y las Fuerzas Armadas pueden ejercer sus funciones

. El proyecto de ley busca entregar un marco común para determinar cuándo, cómo y con qué intensidad puede utilizarse la fuerza, así como establecer deberes y responsabilidades asociados a su empleo.


El Estado tiene la facultad de utilizar legítimamente la fuerza para proteger a las personas y mantener el orden público. Sin embargo, esta facultad debe ejercerse dentro de límites estrictos y de acuerdo con las obligaciones internacionales de derechos humanos.


Chile, como Estado parte de la Convención Americana sobre Derechos Humanos y del Pacto Internacional de Derechos Civiles y Políticos, está obligado a respetar y garantizar, entre otros, los derechos a la vida e integridad personal. Estos tratados se complementan con estándares específicos de Naciones Unidas sobre el uso de la fuerza y las armas de fuego, así como con la jurisprudencia de la Corte Interamericana de Derechos Humanos.


Una regulación adecuada debe establecer, entre otros elementos, los principios de legalidad, necesidad, proporcionalidad y responsabilidad. Esto significa que la fuerza debe perseguir un objetivo legítimo, utilizarse solo cuando sea necesaria y recurrir a medios e intensidad acordes con la amenaza o resistencia enfrentada.


“Durante el estallido social pudimos ver las graves consecuencias del uso desproporcionado y abusivo de la fuerza, que dejó a miles de personas heridas y con lesiones de por vida. En ese momento, recomendamos con urgencia establecer reglas y protocolos más precisos y acordes con el derecho internacional. Sin embargo, esto aún no se ha cumplido, lo que abre la puerta, especialmente en contextos de manifestación, a que estos abusos puedan volver a ocurrir”, expresa Bustos Bottai.


Contar con reglas claras también es relevante para las propias instituciones encargadas de hacer cumplir la ley: permite entregar certeza sobre sus facultades y, al mismo tiempo, establecer mecanismos para prevenir abusos y determinar responsabilidades cuando la fuerza se utiliza fuera de los límites establecidos.


“Una regulación adecuada no debe entenderse como un obstáculo para la labor policial o militar. Por el contrario, reglas claras, compatibles con los derechos humanos y acompañadas de mecanismos efectivos de supervisión y rendición de cuentas permiten entregar mayor certeza a quienes ejercen funciones de seguridad y fortalecer la protección de todas las personas”, afirma Rodrigo Bustos Bottai.


Aspectos como la ausencia del principio de proporcionalidad, la falta de una prohibición expresa de apuntar armas menos letales al rostro, cabeza o torso y la eliminación del principio de rendición de cuentas; sumado a las disposiciones que amplían las circunstancias en que podría utilizarse fuerza potencialmente letal, incluida aquella destinada a impedir …

author: Alfredo Seguel
title: Comunidad Kawésqar recuerda al Estado chileno los siete mil años de vida marítima como pueblo: ¿Usos consuetudinarios o lo que significa vivir el mar?
content:
La Comunidad Indígena Kawésqar Grupos Familiares Nómades del Mar publicó un artículo de opinión en el que reivindica más de 7,000 años de vida marítima, rechaza la salmonicultura por destruir el ecosistema del que dependen y advierte que el Estado verificará sus usos consuetudinarios en las próximas semanas. Exigen que ese reconocimiento no sea contradictorio.


“Vivir el mar no es folclore”: la comunidad kawésqar reivindica 7.000 años de vida marítima y advierte que la salmonicultura “rompe el círculo”


La Comunidad Indígena Kawésqar Grupos Familiares Nómades del Mar publicó un artículo de opinión titulado “Usos consuetudinarios o lo que significa vivir el mar”, en el que reivindica más de 7.000 años de vida marítima y advierte que la salmonicultura “rompe el círculo” ecológico del que depende su cultura. El texto, firmado por la propia comunidad, sostiene que para el pueblo kawésqar un uso consuetudinario “no es un dato que se anota en un formulario”, sino “la manera en que hemos vivido el mar durante más de siete mil años, y que seguimos viviendo hoy”. Y aclara: “

No es folclore que se muestra en una fecha, ni una costumbre del pasado que se recuerda con nostalgia

“.


El artículo describe las prácticas que sostienen esa forma de vida: navegar como pueblo canoero, pescar “lo justo, cuando hace falta, para seguir camino”, recolectar en la marea baja, bucear en apnea “como bucearon nuestras abuelas”, tejer el junquillo, tomar del bosque alimento y medicina, levantar el At y encender fuegos “donde hubo campamentos antiguos” para transmitir a los niños la memoria de quiénes son. “Cada una de estas prácticas es una hebra; ninguna se entiende sola, así son nuestras economías”, subraya la comunidad, que enfatiza que en su cosmovisión “todo está conectado” y que “el mar y la tierra no son dos cosas: son un mismo cuerpo del que formamos parte”.


La comunidad aclara que su forma de vivir el mar “es compatible con casi todo lo que ocurre en el borde costero” —pesca artesanal, pesca recreativa, navegación, turismo respetuoso e investigación científica— y desmiente que un Espacio Costero “expulse a alguien” o “levante un cerco sobre las aguas”: “Quien diga que pedir nuestro reconocimiento es cerrar el mar, miente, y lo sabe”.


La única actividad con la que no pueden convivir, afirman, es la salmonicultura, porque “carga el agua de materia orgánica hasta dejar el fondo sin oxígeno, vuelca antibióticos que alteran la vida marina, y sus escapes de salmones golpean a las especies nativas de las que dependemos”. Te invitamos a leer el artículo completo a continuación.


Usos consuetudinarios o lo que significa vivir el mar


Para nuestro la comunidad kawésqar, un uso consuetudinario no es un dato que se anota en un formulario. Es la manera en que hemos vivido el mar durante más de siete mil años, y que seguimos viviendo hoy. No es folclore que se muestra en una fecha, ni una costumbre del pasado que se recuerda con nostalgia. Es lo que hacemos cuando navegamos nuestros canales, al bajar a las riveras, sumergirnos en el agua o en el bosque. Vivir el mar, para nosotros, es todo eso junto, y no se puede separar en partes sin dejar de ser lo que es.


Navegamos, como lo hizo siempre un pueblo canoero, y mientras navegamos pescamos lo que necesitamos: no una faena industrial, sino lo justo, cuando hace falta, para seguir camino. Recolectamos en la marea baja, entre las rocas, el erizo y el marisco que el mar deja al descubierto. Buceamos en apnea, como bucearon nuestras abuelas, para alcanzar lo que la orilla no da. Recogemos el junquillo y lo tejemos, y en ese tejido —cestería, adornos— se sostiene no solo un oficio sino un bienestar del espíritu. Del bosque tomamos alimento y medicina, y los materiales con que se levanta el At, nuestra vivienda. Encendemos fuegos donde hubo campamentos antiguos, y alrededor de ellos traspasamos a los niños, hablando, la memoria de quiénes somos. Cazamos, también, como parte de esta vida. Cada una de estas prácticas es una hebra; ninguna se entiende sola, así son nuestras economías.


Porque en nuestra cosmovisión todo está conectado. De lo humano se pasa a lo animal, y de lo animal al territorio, en un círculo que no se puede romper. El mar y la tierra no son dos cosas: son un mismo cuerpo del que formamos parte. Por eso cuidar el territorio no es para nosotros una política ambiental, sino una forma de cuidarnos a nosotros mismos. Dañar el agua es dañar al pez, y dañar al pez es dañarnos. Esa es …

author: Alfredo Seguel
title: Histórica alianza trasandina: Madres del Silencio firman acuerdo con Abuelas para buscar bebés apropiados por la dictadura en Chile
content:
La Fundación Hijos y Madres del Silencio, de Chile, firmó en Buenos Aires un convenio con Abuelas de Plaza de Mayo para buscar bebés sustraídos durante la dictadura de Pinochet. Registros oficiales identifican más de 23.400 niños enviados al extranjero. La unidad de búsqueda creada el 2025, fue desmantelada de inmediato con el Gobierno de Kast.


Las madres chilenas a las que dijeron que su bebé había muerto buscan a sus hijos con las Abuelas de Plaza de Mayo


Las otras víctimas de Pinochet:


En febrero de 1974, cinco meses después del golpe de Estado liderado por Augusto Pinochet, Amelia Flores dio a luz a su hijo Fernando en el Hospital Parroquial de San Bernardo. Dos horas después, el personal médico le dijo que había muerto, no le mostró el cuerpo y le aplicó una inyección que la dejó dormida tres días. A su esposo le entregaron un ataúd cerrado y un servicio fúnebre ya pagado. Así lo relató el periodista Manuel Barrientos en Página 12 de Argentina.


En 2020, Amelia vio por televisión el testimonio de una mujer con una vivencia idéntica y comprendió que su historia no era única, sino un patrón. Se acercó entonces a la

Fundación Hijos y Madres del Silencio (FHMS),

 nacida en 2014 como un grupo de Facebook. Según

Página 12

, junto a madres que buscaban a sus hijos escribían adultos desde Estados Unidos, Italia, Australia o los países nórdicos intentando descifrar su origen, lo que reveló una red de sustracción forzada y tráfico de niños a gran escala.


Los registros oficiales consolidados a partir de denuncias ante la justicia chilena identifican a más de 23.400 niños enviados al extranjero, aunque los investigadores creen que la cifra real podría duplicarse

. La fundación detectó chilenos apropiados en veinte países: unos 8.000 en Estados Unidos, más de 2.200 en Suecia y 500 solo en Cerdeña, además de cientos en Francia y Dinamarca. Según el reportaje, el despojo afectó a mujeres en situación de vulnerabilidad, muchas de comunidades originarias, y en él habrían operado congregaciones de la Iglesia Católica como intermediarias.


Cerca del 80% de los integrantes de la FHMS son mujeres

. Su presidenta y fundadora,

Marisol Rodríguez, busca un hermano o hermana que a su madre le dijeron que nació muerto; la periodista Ana María Olivares logró encontrar a una sobrina. La relación con el Estado ha sido de desidia y promesas incumplidas

: en 2019, una comisión investigadora de la Cámara de Diputados reconoció violaciones a los derechos humanos y la Corte Suprema designó un equipo para la causa penal.

Hacia el cierre del gobierno de Gabriel Boric se creó una unidad de búsqueda, desmantelada de inmediato tras la asunción de José Antonio Kast.


La semana reciente,

cuatro integrantes de la fundación viajaron a Buenos Aires para firmar un convenio de cooperación con Abuelas de Plaza de Mayo

. Por Abuelas firmaron la vicepresidenta Buscarita Roa, nacida en Chile, y el secretario Manuel Goncalves, nieto restituido; por la FHMS, Marisol Rodríguez, Ana María Olivares, María del Carmen García Castro y Amelia Flores. García Castro destacó que Abuelas es un referente mundial y que “nosotros no podemos inventar la pólvora”. Amelia, de 72 años y matemática, ve en el trabajo de Abuelas la clave para que la búsqueda de su hijo continúe en sus hijas y nietos.

author: Ian Angus
title: Ecosocialist Bookshelf — October 2026
content:
Climate and Capitalism editor Ian Angus introduces eight left-wing books on the rise, ideas and goals of the new far right.

First, an apology: I’ve been working flat out on my next book — Social Murder: Capitalism’s Assault on Human Health in the Anthropocene — so this the first Ecosocialist Bookshelf since July. I will try not to miss any more.

Second, an explanation: Usually I include titles on a variety of subjects in science, politics, theory, history etc. But recently, my shelf has been crowded with new books on the rise and nature of the radical right, so I am introducing eight of them at once. I’ll return to the normal mix next month.

End Times Fascism and the Fight for the Living World By Naomi Klein and Astrid Taylor Farrar, Straus and Giroux A new iteration of the far right is on the march. Klein and Taylor explore the alliance of religious fundamentalists, Silicon Valley technologists and ethno-nationalists that aims to make the world unliveable while protecting themselves from the consequences by hiding on luxurious private islands, rocketing to Mars, or deploying massive military force to keep the ‘bad’ people out.

Backlash: The Global Rise of the Radical Right Edited by Don Kalb and Walden Bello Pluto Press We live in an age of counterrevolution. Liberal elites around the world are weaponising their fascistic narratives, creating political enemies and consolidating even more power and wealth. This collection of essays from leading researchers reveals new forms of the radical right, neo-nationalism, authoritarian neoliberalism, illiberalism and democratic backsliding.

Muskism: A Guide for the Perplexed By Quinn Slobodian and Ben Tarnoff Harper Collins Elon Musk promises sovereignty through technology: plug in, power up and become self-reliant. Slobodian and Tarnoff cut through the hype to reveal what Musk really represents: a new political economy, where to be “free” means to serve a Techno-king. Muskism isn’t about the man. It’s about the machine that made him — and the world he’s trying to make.

Country of Lords: Neo-Aristocrats, Social Darwinists, Tech Utopians, and the Long Fight Against Equality in America By Kim Phillips-Klein WW Norton United States history is often told as a hard-won march toward the promise of equality, but there has always been a countertrend. Again and again, influential Americans have argued that the social, economic and racial hierarchies in which some groups of people rule over others are not only natural but good.

The Nerd Reich: Silicon Valley Fascism and the War on Democracy By Gil Durán Simon & Schuster Durán explains the origins, strategies and ambitions of Silicon Valley’s war on democracy. From San Francisco’s weaponised elections and secret billionaire projects to the White House, Durán exposes how the world’s richest men aim to replace elected governments with corporate rule.

The Right-Wing Idea Factory: From Traditionalism to Trumpism By Donald F Kettl Oxford University Press Kettl traces the rise of a revolutionary political force that has redefined the United States right. Fuelled by soft money and amplified by social media, a network of determined activists and organisations aims to dismantle traditional free-market conservatism and replace it with a populist agenda rooted in cultural and social issues.

Gilded Rage: Elon Musk and the Radicalization of Silicon Valley By Jacob Silverman Bloomsbury An essential dispatch from the frontlines of the billionaire revolution in which Musk is just the beginning. Silverman maps a sprawling network of radicalised elites — from Peter Thiel and JD Vance to the financiers bankrolling Donald Trump — who are using their power and their money to drive a political revolution.

The Cultural Marxism Conspiracy: Why the Right Blames the Frankfurt School for the Decline of the West By AJA Woods Verso “Cultural Marxism” is one of the far right’s favorite buzzwords. Woods uncovers the bizarre story of the cult leaders, right-wing intellectuals and White House officials who believe a coterie of left-wing scholars and students is plotting to undermine Western civilisation.

[Reprinted from Climate and Capitalism. Inclusion of a book does not imply endorsement.]
